Decide and apply: correct the doc, or restore the account deliberately. **Whether that login works on the demo today is NOT established** — the row may persist from an earlier seeding era with its old hash. Answering it needs a DB read that was outside this seat's authorisation.
- [ ] **2. Turning seeding back on now suspends the platform admin.** The moment anyone sets `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` on the demo to restore seeding, `requiredSeedPw('ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD')` returns null (`userRepo.ts:1039,1075`), and the null branch writes `status='suspended'` plus an unusable hash — **actively suspending a pre-existing row, not merely skipping it**. `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` must be set in the *same* change. This is a trap for whoever next tries to re-seed, and nothing warns them at the point of the switch.
- [ ] **3. Consider making the trap loud rather than documented** — the seeder could refuse to start (or log at `error`) when `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` is combined with a `requiredSeedPw` account whose variable is unset, instead of silently suspending it.

## Why this is filed and not fixed

Wednesday's ANSWER, 2026-09-08: *"Do not edit USER_TESTING/CREDENTIALS-AND-PORTALS.md yet… the fix depends on which way Q1 goes. File it as a ticket now so it cannot be lost."* Setting a credential on a running system is Kam's signature class and collides with his own `rotate-properly` ruling on the admin credential (2026-09-07).

**Q1 came back in a way that DE-ESCALATES the deploy:** the `632f16dfe..400517aaf` deploy does **not** suspend `admin@secuura.com`, because the seeder never runs. Item 2 is the residual risk that outlives the deploy.

## Not blocking the deploy

The 19-commit deploy is unaffected by this ticket. Recorded here so the finding cannot be lost when the deploy card closes.

title: A deploy that rsyncs the OpenAPI spec and does not restart api-gateway ships a silently stale published contract — rsync breaks the bind mount by inode
description:
## BLUF

**The demo redeploy runbook can ship a stale published API contract with every check passing.** `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` is a **file-level** bind mount into `api-gateway` (`docker-compose.yml:542`, `:ro`). `rsync` **writes a temp file and renames it, so the updated file gets a NEW INODE** — and a Docker file bind mount resolves to the inode at container-create time. The container goes on serving the **old** file indefinitely.

It is not stale cache. The container is looking at a **different file on the same path**.

## Measured during the 2026-09-08 deploy (632f16dfe → 400517aaf)

After the rsync, before any restart:

|  | md5 | bytes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| host `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` | `7e43a8d89afb…` | 1332983 (new) |
| inside `api-gateway` `/app/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` | `c014b2fce71c…` | 1329831 (**old**, dated Sep 7 03:45) |
| served `GET /api/docs/openapi.yaml` | — | 1329831 = the container's copy |

After `docker compose restart api-gateway`: container md5 `7e43a8d89afb…`, identical to the host; served bytes 1332983; the new text `BOUND TO THE` went **0 → 1** and `DIFFERS FROM the ACTING` **0 → 2**, with `organizationUuid` **1 → 2** as a control and an impossible string at 0.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note

**The failure mode is exactly KS-978's**, which this same deploy shipped the fix for: *the published contract says something the route does not do*. KS-978 was a wrong sentence in the source. This is the **delivery mechanism** producing the same outcome from a correct source — and it is quieter, because every signal an operator would check looks right:

* `rsync` exits 0 and reports the file transferred ✅
* the file on the VM disk **is** correct ✅
* rebuilding the image does nothing (the spec is mounted, not baked) — so "I rebuilt it" feels like the fix and is not ✅
* the container is healthy, the endpoint returns 200 ✅

Nothing surfaces the divergence except comparing the md5 **inside** the container against the host.

## Items

- [ ] **1. Add the gateway restart to the runbook as a required step**, not an optional one — `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md` §Redeploy runbook. Wording should carry the mechanism (inode), because "restart to pick up the spec" reads as cargo-cult and gets dropped.
- [ ] **2. Correct the existing guidance.** The current understanding recorded in project notes is "a rebuild does not publish it, a restart does" — true but incomplete, and it does not say the container will serve the old file *forever* until something re-resolves the mount.
- [ ] **3. Add a post-deploy assertion** that fails loudly: compare `md5sum` of the host spec against `docker exec api-gateway md5sum` of the mounted path, and refuse to call a deploy complete when they differ. This is the check that would have caught it with no human judgement involved.
- [ ] **4. Audit for other file-level bind mounts with the same exposure** — `nginx-demo.conf` is the known sibling. Directory mounts are not affected; only single-file mounts are.

## Not a live defect right now

The 2026-09-08 deploy restarted `api-gateway` and the served spec is verified correct. This ticket is about the **next** deploy, by whoever does not know.

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, from the deploy itself.

title: Archiving a ticket silently archives its sub-issues, including NON-TERMINAL ones — and the parent-side check cannot detect it
description:
## BLUF

`issueArchive` **cascades to sub-issues.** Archiving 23 terminal tickets on 2026-09-08 also archived **KS-918 (Backlog)** and **KS-920 (In Progress)** — children of **KS-490**. Neither was in any target list. **In Progress is live work.**

**And the obvious verification cannot catch it:** once archived, the parent's `children` connection returns **nothing**. Asking the parent what it took with it reads clean.

Both were restored the same session. This ticket is about the mechanism, which is still live.

## Measured

```
child -> parent    KS-918.parent = KS-490      ✅ reveals the link
                   KS-920.parent = KS-490      ✅
parent -> children KS-490.children = 0         ❌ shows NOTHING
```

**The timestamps are what identified it as a cascade rather than a concurrent actor:**

```
KS-490  (mine, targeted)      archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z
KS-921  (mine, targeted)      archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z
KS-918  (NOT targeted)        archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z   <- identical ms
KS-920  (NOT targeted)        archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z   <- identical ms
```

Identical to the millisecond = one batch = one cause. **My own first diagnosis blamed a concurrent actor and was wrong; the timestamp disproved it.**

**Full accounting for the pass:** 33 intended + 2 collateral = 35 archived, measured 35. Only KS-490 had children, so the blast radius was bounded at exactly two.

## Why it went unnoticed until arithmetic caught it

The only reason anyone knows is the **census delta: −25 against an expected −23**. That is the shape most easily rationalised as a stale count. Every other signal looked clean:

* the archive calls all returned `success: true` — and they had, for the 23 asked;
* the parent-side `children` query returned **0**;
* no error, no warning, nothing in any response mentioning the children.

## The rule this produces

**Before archiving, query** `child → parent` **for the target's children and record the count. After, take a full paged census.**

```
expected delta = |targets| + |children found|
```

**If the delta is not exactly that, stop.** Asking the parent side for `children` is *the check that cannot fail* here — it reads zero both when there are none and when they have just been archived.

## Items

- [ ] **1. Make the children pre-check part of any archive procedure**, with the delta equation above as its pass condition.
- [ ] **2. Decide whether a cascade onto a NON-TERMINAL child should be refused outright.** Kam's standing ruling is that non-terminal work stays visible on the board; a cascade violates that silently.
- [ ] **3. Measure the historical population — see the sibling ticket** on the 95 pre-existing archived non-terminal tickets. This mechanism would produce exactly that.

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, from the archive pass that hit it.

title: 95 archived tickets sit in NON-TERMINAL states — measure whether a cascade put them there
description:
## BLUF

**97 archived tickets on the KS+PS boards are in non-terminal states.** Two were archived today (mine, restored the same session). **The other 95 predate this session and nobody has established how they got there.**

```
Backlog     83
Todo         6
In Progress  4
In Review    3
Blocked      1
```

**This is a hypothesis with evidence, NOT an asserted cause.** [KS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-995) established that `issueArchive` cascades onto sub-issues — including non-terminal ones — and that the parent-side check reads clean afterwards. **That mechanism would produce exactly this population, silently.** It may also be that some were archived deliberately.

## The measurement that would settle it

For each of the 95: **is its parent archived, and does the parent's** `archivedAt` **match the child's to the millisecond?**

That is the same discriminator that disproved a wrong third-party attribution during today's pass, applied backwards:

* **match → decisive for cascade.** One batch, one cause.
* **mismatch → closes nothing.** It was archived separately, which is consistent with a deliberate act.

One-directional, and that limit should be carried into whatever the measurement concludes — a mismatch is not evidence of intent.

## 🔴 Do NOT unarchive anything on the strength of this ticket

**83 tickets reappearing in Backlog changes what the team sees.** A restoration is as much a board change as an archive, and it is Kam's call on a measurement — not a tidy-up. **Measure first, report, then ask.**

## Items

- [ ] **1. Run the parent/timestamp measurement** across all 95 and report the split.
- [ ] **2. For any confirmed cascade victim, establish whether the work is still live** — an In Progress ticket archived by accident is different from a Backlog item nobody was going to do.
- [ ] **3. Only then** put a restoration proposal to Kam, with counts by state.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

Every count taken with a default query has been wrong on this board today — *twice*. `Tested Not Deployed` read 24 when it was 29, and a Duplicate census read 4 when it was 5 because the query capped at 250. **If 95 live-state tickets are invisible, every "what is open" number anyone has quoted is short by some part of 95.**

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, alongside KS-995.

title: The OAuth token endpoint is outside the credential-stuffing rate-limit zone — /api/oauth/ is not keyed in $secuura_auth_limit_key
description:
## BLUF

`/api/oauth/` **sits OUTSIDE the credential-stuffing rate-limit zone that** `/api/auth/` **sits inside.** The OAuth token endpoint — the one that exchanges codes and redeems refresh tokens — gets only the aggregate `/api/` ceiling, not the 5 r/s + burst 10 bound the config itself calls *"the credential-stuffing bound"*.

**True whether or not** [KS-823](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-823) **is fixed**, which is why this is its own ticket rather than a sub-item of it: KS-823 is about the refresh grant's missing client authentication; this is about the rate-limit zone configuration. Different logical path, per Kam's one-ticket-per-path rule.

## Measured

`Blockchain/Dev/docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf`, read at the demo VM's SHA `400517aaf`:

```nginx
map $request_uri $secuura_auth_limit_key {
    "~^/api/auth/"     $secuura_limit_key;
    "~^/api/v1/auth/"  $secuura_limit_key;
}
limit_req_zone $secuura_auth_limit_key zone=secuura_auth:10m rate=5r/s;
```

The map keys **two** prefixes. `/api/oauth/` is neither. The file's own comment describes the zone as *"auth at 5 r/s + burst 10 is the credential-stuffing bound"* — so the intent of the zone is explicit, and the token endpoint is outside it.

**The endpoint is reachable:** `nginx-demo.conf` `location /api/` → the gateway; `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:317` `router.use('/api/oauth', proxy('auth', …))` with no `authenticateToken` and no scope gate (deliberately — the section header reads *"AUTH / USER / SESSION (no gateway auth — handled by auth service)"*).

**Control that the map's silence is real and not a grep artefact:** the same map DOES key `/api/auth/` and `/api/v1/auth/`, and neighbouring gateway mounts in `proxy.ts` ARE guarded (`/api/webhooks` carries `authenticateToken(true), attachScopes, requireScope('webhooks:manage')`). So both instruments can produce a positive, and the negative on `/api/oauth/` means something.

**No request was made against the demo, valid or invalid.** This is a read of code and configuration only.

## Why it matters

`POST /api/oauth/token` accepts credential-bearing material — an authorization code, a refresh token, and for confidential apps a client secret. It is a guessing surface of the same class as `/api/auth/login`, and it is the one the zone was written to bound. Anything that brute-forces or sprays against it meets only the aggregate `/api/` ceiling shared with every other API path, rather than the per-key 5 r/s bound.

## Not claimed

* **No exploitability measurement.** Whether the aggregate `/api/` ceiling is in practice tight enough has NOT been measured, and doing so needs a probe that has not been authorised.
* **No claim about the local or production configs.** `nginx-demo.conf` was read; `nginx.conf` and `nginx-production.conf` were not, and they may differ. Whoever picks this up should check all three before changing one.

## Fix shape

Add `"~^/api/oauth/" $secuura_limit_key;` to the map, or widen the existing keys — then confirm the other two nginx configs and decide whether the same gap exists there. A rate-limit change wants its own verification that legitimate token exchange is not throttled.

Discovered 2026-09-08 during KS-1001's disposition pass over the P2 In Review queue, while reading KS-823's reachability.

title: e2e: "CIP-30 API availability check" calls a route that does not exist, and its assertion passes on the 404
description:
## BLUF

`tests/e2e/.../happy-path-wallet.spec.ts:255` **calls a route that does not exist — and its assertion**
**is written so that the 404 PASSES.** The test is named *"CIP-30 API availability check"* and asserts
only `expect(response.status()).toBeLessThan(500)`, with a comment saying *"may return 404 if not*
*implemented"*. **404 < 500.** It has never been able to fail for the thing it names.

**This is not one line.** The same shape runs through the recruitment e2e suite: **13**
`toBeLessThan(500)` **assertions and 33** `if (response.ok())` **guards across 62 tests in 5 files.** An
`if (response.ok())` wrapper means that when the endpoint is absent, **zero assertions execute and the**
**test passes.**

Surfaced by @PeterObeden's `wallet/status` question on PR #802 (see KS-1009). It is a
**check-that-cannot-fail**, which is this board's most-repeated family.

## Measured

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| service-side references to `/api/wallet/status` | **0** — the route does not exist |
| service-side references to `/api/wallet/supported` | **0** — nor does this one |
| **CONTROL —** `/api/auth/wallet/challenge`**, used correctly in the same file** | **6** |

The control is what makes the zeros mean something: the same search over the same tree finds the route
that does exist, so the zeros are real absences rather than a search that cannot match.

**And the correct path is already known inside the same directory.** `fixtures/recruitment-data.ts:291`
defines:

```
walletStatus: (address: string) => `/api/auth/wallet/status/${address}`
```

The test does not use it. So this is a mistake, not a deliberate second route.

### The family, per file

| file | `toBeLessThan(500)` | `if (response.ok())` | tests |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `admin-config.admin.spec.ts` | 4 | 11 | 21 |
| `alternative-paths.spec.ts` | 4 | 7 | 16 |
| `happy-path-nft.spec.ts` | 1 | 13 | 6 |
| `happy-path-wallet.spec.ts` | 3 | 2 | 11 |
| `happy-path-web.spec.ts` | 1 | 0 | 8 |

Not every one of these is wrong — `< 500` is a legitimate assertion for *"this must not 5xx"*, and
`if (ok())` is legitimate where the test genuinely is conditional. **What is not legitimate is a test**
**whose NAME claims to check availability and whose assertion passes when the thing is absent.** The
count is the search space, not the defect count.

## ⚠ OPEN QUESTION — do not change any route until this is answered

**It is not established what these tests were meant to cover.** Two readings, and they lead opposite
ways:

1. **The path is a typo** — the intended route is `/api/auth/wallet/status/:address`, the fixture proves
   the author knew it, and the fix is to use the fixture and assert a real outcome.
2. **The route was planned and never built** — `/api/wallet/status` and `/api/wallet/supported` were
   meant to be a `wallet-connector` service surface, and these are placeholders deliberately written to
   tolerate absence.

Reading 2 is not far-fetched: the test's own comment says *"Test that wallet connector service is*
*running"*, and `wallet-connector` is a real service in this repo.

**Changing the route under reading 2 would silently delete the record that something was never built.**
So: establish the intent first, then fix. Do not repoint the URL as a tidy-up.

## Suggested shape once intent is known

* If typo: use `fixtures/recruitment-data.ts`'s `walletStatus()` and assert the actual contract
  (`exists` true/false), not a status band.
* If unbuilt: mark the tests `test.fixme()` with the ticket reference, so the gap is visible rather
  than green.
* Either way, **a test whose name asserts availability must fail when the thing is unavailable.**

*Filed by s152 from PR #802's open question, on Wednesday's instruction. Measured on* `origin/develop`
*merged into the KS-732 worktree. Nothing changed.*

title: The `require-pr-gates` ruleset survived the Actions retirement: 7 required checks that can never report, 0 required approvals, and ALWAYS bypass for admins
description:
## BLUF

`develop` **and** `main` **carry an ACTIVE ruleset that enforces nothing for an admin and is unsatisfiable for everyone else.** It requires seven status-check contexts whose workflows no longer exist, requires **zero** approving reviews, and grants `ALWAYS` bypass to org and repo admins.

The retirement of Actions is well tracked ([KS-789](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-789/contributingmd-justifies-the-hooks-degradation-and-its-no-verify), [KS-910](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-910/preflight-leg-12-executes-zero-suite-cells-it-is-a-reachability-check), [KS-926](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-926/17-of-20-check-sh-guards-run-from-no-live-entry-point-including-sql)). **What is not tracked is the ruleset left pointing at it.** A branch that looks protected in the settings UI, and in the API reports `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN` on a PR with no reviews and no checks, is worse than one that is plainly unprotected — the reassurance is the problem.

Found while reviewing [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#805](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-726-write-ahead-the-cardano-tx-hash-so-a-lost-submit-reply-cannot-48dbfe970108), after asking the ordinary question "could this merge without an approval?". It can.

## What the ruleset actually says

`require-pr-gates` — `target: BRANCH`, `enforcement: ACTIVE`, conditions `refs/heads/develop` + `refs/heads/main`.

| rule | setting |
| -- | -- |
| `PULL_REQUEST` | required |
| — `requiredApprovingReviewCount` | **0** |
| — `requireCodeOwnerReview` | false |
| — `requireLastPushApproval` | false |
| — `requiredReviewThreadResolution` | false |
| — `dismissStaleReviewsOnPush` | false |
| `REQUIRED_STATUS_CHECKS` | 7 contexts (below) |
| — `strictRequiredStatusChecksPolicy` | false |
| `DELETION` / `NON_FAST_FORWARD` | both on — these two DO work |

Required contexts: `Code Security Gates` · `Standalone locks pass clean-room npm ci` · `build / Build + push platform images (fresh)` · `Schemathesis suite` · `Playwright suite` · `Performance suite (k6 smoke)` · `Akto suite (PR)`.

Bypass actors, **both** `bypassMode: ALWAYS`: organization admins, and repository role `5` (admin).

## The three problems, separately

**1 — Seven required checks that can never report.** Every recent workflow run is `startup_failure` at **0s** (`gh run list`). The workflows producing these contexts were retired. So for a contributor without admin the ruleset is not strict, it is **unsatisfiable** — nothing they push can ever go green, and the failure reads as "waiting for a check" rather than "this check no longer exists".

**2 — Zero required approvals.** A PR is required; an approval is not. On `main` as well as `develop`, which is the part I would not have guessed. `main` is meant to be the releasable branch (CLAUDE.md → Branching Model), and it currently asks for no human sign-off at all.

**3 —** `ALWAYS` **bypass for admins hides both.** Anyone who could notice problems 1 and 2 is exactly the population the ruleset never applies to. GitHub computes `mergeStateStatus` for the viewer, so an admin sees `CLEAN` and no warning of any kind.

## The demonstration

[Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#805](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-726-write-ahead-the-cardano-tx-hash-so-a-lost-submit-reply-cannot-48dbfe970108), read 2026-09-08:

```
mergeable:         MERGEABLE
mergeStateStatus:  CLEAN
reviewDecision:    null      (no reviews of ANY kind ever submitted)
statusCheckRollup: 0 checks
```

Mergeable right now, by any admin, with no approval and no green check — and nothing on the PR page says so. That PR happens to be under active review, so no harm is in flight; it is the state that is the finding, not the PR.

## Reproduce

```
gh api graphql -f query='{ repository(owner:"Secuura", name:"Distributed_Secuura") {
  rulesets(first:5){ nodes{ name target enforcement
    conditions{ refName{ include exclude } }
    bypassActors(first:20){ nodes{ bypassMode organizationAdmin repositoryRoleDatabaseId } }
    rules(first:30){ nodes{ type parameters{ __typename
      ... on PullRequestParameters { requiredApprovingReviewCount requireCodeOwnerReview requireLastPushApproval requiredReviewThreadResolution dismissStaleReviewsOnPush }
      ... on RequiredStatusChecksParameters { strictRequiredStatusChecksPolicy requiredStatusChecks{ context } } } } } } } }'
```

Note the REST endpoints (`/branches/develop/protection`, `/rulesets`) answer **403 "Upgrade to GitHub Pro"** on this private repo, which is why this is easy to miss — the obvious check reports nothing rather than reporting the truth. GraphQL answers fine.

## Suggested shape — not a decree, and deliberately not one change

These are three decisions, not one, and they belong to different owners:

1. **Drop the seven dead contexts** from the ruleset, or repoint them at whatever replaced Actions. Leaving a required check that cannot report is the worst of the three states. *(Cheap; no policy decision.)*
2. **Decide the approval count deliberately**, for `main` and `develop` separately. If 0 is intended on a 4-seat team, say so in CONTRIBUTING and this ticket closes on that; if it is a leftover, 1 on `develop` and 1 on `main` is the obvious floor.
3. **Reconsider** `ALWAYS` **bypass.** `pull_request` mode instead of `ALWAYS` keeps admins able to unblock an emergency while still surfacing the state to them.

**(1) is worth doing regardless of how (2) and (3) land.**

## Relationship to what is already tracked

* [KS-412](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-412/ci-require-all-systemtest-all-tools-pr-suites-pre-merge-to-block) (Todo, High, Peter) — *"require all systemTest PR suites + pre-merge to block merges on failure (branch protection + sign-off)"*. Points **forward** to the gate we want. This ticket is the **residue behind us**: the ruleset that already exists and no longer means anything. They should probably be sequenced — clean this up, then build [KS-412](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-412/ci-require-all-systemtest-all-tools-pr-suites-pre-merge-to-block) on the cleared ground.
* [KS-789](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-789/contributingmd-justifies-the-hooks-degradation-and-its-no-verify) — CONTRIBUTING justifies the hook's `--no-verify` bypass with *"CI is the hard gate"*. This is the same sentence, one layer down: the ruleset also asserts a gate that is not there.
* [KS-910](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-910/preflight-leg-12-executes-zero-suite-cells-it-is-a-reachability-check), [KS-926](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-926/17-of-20-check-sh-guards-run-from-no-live-entry-point-including-sql) — the Actions retirement itself and its orphaned guards. Cause; this is effect.

## Not claimed

I have not checked whether any merge to `develop` or `main` has actually gone in unreviewed — only that nothing prevents it. Nor have I touched the ruleset; changing it needs org-admin rights and is a decision, not a fix.

*Raised by Peter's session, 2026-09-08, from the #805 review. Read via GraphQL against the live repo, not from documentation.*

title: Eight containers ran images their own tag no longer pointed at — "the stack is up" says nothing about what it is running
description:
## BLUF

**Eight containers in a stack everyone called "up" were running images that were not the image their own tag pointed at.** `docker compose up -d` moved them onto their current `:latest` — an image dated as far back as **2026-07-19** — which means they had been running something older still.

**The finding is not the drift. It is that "the stack is up" carried no information about what the stack was RUNNING.** That is the same hole KS-1011 records from the other side: the stack marker built to answer *"what is this stack running?"* reads `unknown` for branch, commit, owner and started_at. Between them there was no way to tell, and nobody could have noticed.

## Recommendation

Make "up" mean something checkable. Either close KS-1011's marker so the stack states its own provenance, or add a preflight/boot check that compares each running container's image id against the id its tag currently resolves to, and says so loudly when they differ. Cheap, and it converts an invisible condition into a printed line.

Not built in this session — filed while the evidence existed.

## Detail — measured 2026-09-08 during the s153 rebuild-and-delta

Container image ids recorded **before** the swap and **after**, on develop `5ffaaf396`:

| container | tag | was (image id) | now (image id) | now built |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `secuura-admin-frontend` | `2_project_files-admin-frontend` | `1ccb569c333c` | `ae9dc7c99b50` | 2026-09-05 |
| `secuura-issuer-frontend` | `2_project_files-issuer-frontend` | `acaf87948f1a` | `5f5ab1858e02` | 2026-08-12 |
| `secuura-nginx-gateway` | `2_project_files-nginx-gateway` | `1a88d7c62acf` | `da61354d1455` | 2026-09-02 |
| `secuura-pgbouncer` | `2_project_files-pgbouncer` | `fb7bc96531ca` | `fff0c069d941` | 2026-07-29 |
| `secuura-status-frontend` | `2_project_files-status-frontend` | `30912434c7ee` | `cabba2bce603` | 2026-09-02 |
| `secuura-tokenomics-website` | `2_project_files-tokenomics-website` | `25a649012e13` | `8b2bc0c41da4` | 2026-07-29 |
| `secuura-verifier-frontend` | `2_project_files-verifier-frontend` | `3e771b8687a1` | `167864b4b09c` | 2026-08-06 |
| `secuura-website-frontend` | `2_project_files-website-frontend` | `a8f694884e17` | `3245fa82b505` | 2026-07-19 |

These eight rebuilt **byte-identical** (fully cached, so the tag never moved and the image kept its old creation date). The container still changed image — which is what establishes that it had not been on the tag's image to begin with.

For contrast, in the same swap **22** containers moved onto images genuinely built that day, and **3** did not move at all (`postgres`, `redis`, `stack-marker` — image-only services that are never built). 30 + 3 = 33.

## ⚠ The evidence was perishable and is now mostly gone

Re-checked immediately after recording: **7 of the 8 prior images are no longer resolvable on this host** — only `secuura-pgbouncer`'s (`fb7bc96531ca`, 2026-07-29) survives. The ids above are the durable record; the images behind them are not.

Control for that claim: `docker inspect` **by full id** resolves correctly for a currently-running image, so the failures are genuine absences and not a broken lookup.

## What is NOT established

* **How long** each container had been drifted. The prior images' creation dates were not captured before they were pruned, so the age of the drift is unknown and is not claimed.
* **Why** they drifted — whether from a partial `up`, an interrupted rebuild, or a `restart: unless-stopped` recovery that reattached an older image. Not investigated.
* Whether the demo VM has the same condition. **Not measured** — nothing on the demo was touched this session.

## Related

KS-1011 (the stack marker reads `unknown` for everything it exists to report) — the same gap seen from the other side.

title: Test-estate CLASS: a fixture that cannot discriminate certifies the bug — unmintable values, and fixtures satisfying both arms of a guard (3 instances: auth x2, originate x1)
description:
## BLUF

**A fixture whose values the PRODUCT could never produce tests the mock, not the product — and it fails in the direction nobody watches.** We are trained to look for tests *stricter* than reality, which manufacture false findings. The opposite — a suite **looser** than the product — is worse: it does not raise a false alarm, it issues a **certificate for the live bug**.

**This is not hypothetical. A cell named after the behaviour it was failing to test was green over KS-1013 for as long as that defect existed.**

## The instance that proves the class

`services/auth/src/__tests__/ks467-user-admin-isolation.test.ts`, the cell `'unknown target id is 404'`, requested `PATCH /admin/nope` — a **malformed** id, not an unknown one — and asserted `404`.

It passed. It could only ever pass:

| layer | answer to a malformed id |
| -- | -- |
| the repo **mock** (`getUserByIdPlatformScope` → `state.users.get(id) ?? null`) | `null` → route answers **404** ✅ green |
| **real Postgres** | `22P02 invalid input syntax for type uuid` → route answered **500** |

So the suite asserted the not-found path while the product was returning a 500, and the test's own name — *unknown target id* — describes a case it never exercised.

## The tell is FIXTURE SHAPE, not assertion logic

Both suites that drive `PATCH /api/users/admin/:id` used ids the system can never mint:

| file | fixture ids |
| -- | -- |
| `ks467-user-admin-isolation.test.ts` | `'user-a'`, `'user-b'`, `'user-c'`, `'sysadmin-1'`, and `/admin/nope` |
| `usersAdminStatus.test.ts` | `'u1'` (target), `'admin1'` (caller) |

Real user ids are UUIDs. **Every one of those fixtures describes a request shape the product never receives**, so every assertion built on them is a statement about the mock's behaviour.

Fixed for these two files in **KS-1013 / PR #910** — necessary there, because the new format guard broke them. **The class was deliberately not swept in that PR** (one logical path per PR); that sweep is this ticket.

## Recommendation

1. **Sweep the auth suites for fixture values the product cannot produce** — ids, tenant ids, org ids, emails. The cheap high-signal filter: any id-shaped fixture that is not a UUID.
2. **Where a mock stands in for a typed column, make it reject what the column rejects.** A `getUserById` mock that returns `null` for a non-UUID is *more forgiving than Postgres*, which is exactly how the KS-1013 cell went green. It does not need a full type system — refusing a non-UUID id would have failed that cell honestly.
3. **Treat "the existing suites that break when I add a guard" as the signal.** When KS-1013's guard landed, the suites that broke were the honest ones. **The ones that did NOT break are the ones to read.**

## 🔴 The same failure one layer up — my own sweep, recorded because the next person needs it

While fixing this I enumerated the route's callers with `grep "call('PATCH', '/admin/"` and declared them found. That pattern **cannot see a URL built as a template literal inside a helper**, which is exactly how `usersAdminStatus.test.ts` does it:

```
return fetch(`${baseUrl}/admin/u1`, { method: 'PATCH', … })
```

Result: the first full-suite run came back **7 failed**, all caused by me. **The complete instrument (the full suite) was available the whole time and I reached for the cheap one first.**

**It is the same defect as the class above, one layer up: a search whose SHAPE assumes how the callers were written.** A grep for a call convention is a fixture too — it tests the convention, not the code. Where a suite exists, run the suite; use grep to *locate*, never to *enumerate*.

## Scope / not-scope — WIDENED 2026-09-09, deliberately, so the title matches what this closes on

**Filed as the auth suites. Now scoped to the test estate, because a third instance turned up in** `originate` **and the class is one class, not two.**

The call, stated rather than drifted into: splitting it would leave two tickets with overlapping sweeps and neither owning *"can this fixture discriminate?"*. One sweep looks for both costumes in the same pass. **Retitled to name the CLASS rather than the auth instance, so the headline and the closing condition are the same thing.**

* **In scope:** the test estate. **Measured so far in TWO services** — `auth` (fixture values the product cannot mint) and `originate` (a fixture satisfying both arms of a disjunction).
* **Not claimed:** whether the other 13 services share it. **Still unswept** — two services is not a platform-wide finding, and this ticket does not imply one.
* **Closing condition:** the sweep across the test estate with both filters below applied, and what it finds filed or fixed. NOT "the three known instances are patched" — those are already fixed in #910 and #912.

### The two cheap filters the sweep runs on

1. **Fixture VALUES the product could never mint** — highest signal: an id-shaped fixture that is not a UUID.
2. **Fixtures that satisfy MORE conditions than the assertion isolates** — find guards that are a disjunction (`A || B`) and check whether any cell isolates each arm. Where none does, that arm is unpinned however many green cells surround it.

* **Not this ticket:** the KS-1013 fix itself (done, PR #910) and the doc-wording correction about `docker restart secuura-auth`, which is a separate finding from the same session.

## Provenance

Found by s154, 2026-09-09, while building KS-1013 on `develop` `5ffaaf396`. The mock/Postgres divergence was measured, not reasoned: the live route returned 500 for `id=0` before the fix and 400 after, while the ks467 cell returned 404 in both worlds because it never reached a database. Class framing commissioned by Wednesday, who ruled it a separate logical path that must not travel inside a P2 fix.

---

## Instance 4 — `action-pins-labelled.sh`: a self-test line that never reaches the mechanism it names (added 2026-09-09, Peter)

Found reviewing PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#921](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-778-the-pin-label-gate-could-not-see-two-legal-shapes-and-its-guard-0ba71ba302a2) / [KS-778](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-778/preflight-leg-10s-pin-label-parser-is-blind-to-a-quoted-uses-and-an). Same class, **a third costume**: not a value the product cannot mint, and not a fixture satisfying both arms — a fixture that **does not reach the mechanism its own comment claims it exercises**.

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/action-pins-labelled.sh` (preflight leg 11) gained a completeness guard: every line the *finder* (`git grep`) returns must yield a row from the *parser* (`sed`), or the gate fails. The guard is the headline of that PR — it closes a partial-blindness hole where an unreadable pin read as a clean tree.

The self-test written to cover it, at `:97-106`, says:

> *"Prove the completeness comparison can fail, using a line the finder shape matches and the parser deliberately cannot"*

**Measured — the finder does not match that line.** The fixture is:

```
z.yml:1:        uses: actions/checkout@0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456g # v7
```

That ref is 39 hex plus a `g`. The finder regex requires `[0-9a-fA-F]{40}`, so it fails *first* — I ran the finder pattern against the line directly: **no match**. The assertion that remains is only "the parser rejects a non-pin", which is true but is not the finder/parser divergence the comment names. **The completeness guard therefore ships with nothing pinning it.**

### Why it belongs to this class rather than being a lint nit

The file's own header states the principle this violates, at `:67`: *"the assertion below is that a set is empty, and an empty set is worth nothing unless the instrument can produce a non-empty one."* The other two assertions in that gate each earned red-proofed fixture rows — I reverted them and watched them go red (8/1/1 and 9/1/1 against an expected 9/1/2, exit 2 both times). Assertion 3 is the only one with no such row, and its cell returns a **confident green** either way.

It also has no net underneath: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/` holds 12 shell suites and **none tests this gate's parser** — the sole reference, `preflight_deps.test.sh:291`, stubs the gate to `exit 0` to test the runner's wiring. So the embedded self-test is the entire test estate for that file.

### The fix, measured

Either of these matches the finder and is refused by the parser, and both produce `could not read 1 of 67 pinned reference(s)`, exit 2:

```
uses: actions/cache@5555555555555555555555555555555555555555 with:
uses: actions/cache@5555555555555555555555555555555555555555f
```

A one-line swap. Flagged to Kamil on PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#921](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-778-the-pin-label-gate-could-not-see-two-legal-shapes-and-its-guard-0ba71ba302a2); the change itself is correct and was approved rather than held for this.

### A related, smaller one in the same file

`:87` computes the self-test's conflicting-SHA count across **all** rows, while the production check at `:152` excludes `(none)` rows. The fixture has one unlabelled SHA appearing once, so the two agree — **by coincidence, not construction**. The self-test is not validating the expression the gate actually runs.

### A third filter for the sweep

The two filters above catch values and disjunctions. This instance suggests a third:

3. **Fixtures whose input never reaches the code path the test names.** Where a test drives a two-stage pipeline (finder → parser, producer → consumer, guard → handler), check that the fixture actually clears stage one. A fixture rejected at stage one exercises stage one's rejection, not the interaction the test is named for — and reads green forever.

*Note: this is a fourth instance, so the title's "3 instances: auth x2, originate x1" is now understated. Left as-is deliberately — it is your ticket and your framing; retitle if you want it to track.*

*Provenance: read and executed at* `dbe7ba6b3` *(PR* [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#921](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-778-the-pin-label-gate-could-not-see-two-legal-shapes-and-its-guard-0ba71ba302a2) *head), 2026-09-09. Finder/parser divergence, both red-proofs and the completeness guard's behaviour all measured by running the script, not inferred. Review:* [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#921](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-778-the-pin-label-gate-could-not-see-two-legal-shapes-and-its-guard-0ba71ba302a2)

title: CLASS: the id-format contract seam — 79 of 83 path params are untyped and ~15 siblings answer 404 for a malformed id; needs a structural guard, not per-route .uuid()
description:
## BLUF

**KS-1013 fixed one route. The seam it sat on is a class, and the class is a CONTRACT seam rather than a per-route omission.**

A read-only sweep of 17 sibling `GET` routes found **NO 500s** — so the 500 variant is not broadly exposed and **KS-1013 was genuinely narrow.** That is the good news and it is the reason this is not urgent.

**But ~15 siblings answer** `404` **for a malformed id** — which is the exact wrong answer KS-1013's own commit message argues against: telling a caller "not found" about an id that could never name anything in any tenant.

## The numbers

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| path params named `id` in the published spec | **83** |
| carrying `format: uuid` at base | **3** |
| carrying it at head (after KS-1013) | **4** |
| sibling GETs swept | 17 |
| 500s found | **0** |
| answering 404 for a malformed id | **~15** |

**So "KS-1013 matches its three siblings" is literally true and is 4 of 83.** Worth stating plainly, because the PR body's phrasing invites a reader to think the spec is broadly typed. It is not.

## The fix shape — structural, NOT per-route

**Do not solve this by adding** `.uuid()` **to routes one at a time.** That is a convention nobody can enforce and the sweep above is the evidence: 79 of 83 params never got it.

**A structural guard at the router, keyed off the spec's declared format**, is the shape. The spec already knows which params are `format: uuid`; the runtime should refuse what the contract declares illegal, without a per-route edit.

## Folded in — two more findings on the same seam

**F-2 (MINOR, measured).** `format: uuid` and the enforced zod regex **describe different sets**: `urn:uuid:<uuid>` is spec-legal and gets **400**. 1 of 13 candidates tested; both controls behaved. So KS-1013's "runtime-is-truth" claim holds for 12 of 13 — true, and not universal. **A structural guard derived from the spec would close this by construction, which is why it belongs here rather than as its own ticket.**

**F-3 (MINOR, forward-looking, measured).** A zod **v3 → v4** bump silently NARROWS this guard on **5 of 10** candidates, while `format: uuid` keeps declaring them legal. The repo pins `^3.22.4`, so it needs a deliberate major bump to bite.

🔴 **F-3 is a landmine attached to a future upgrade, and that is why it is in this ticket rather than a separate one** — whoever does the zod major bump needs to meet it, and they will be reading the id-format ticket, not a MINOR filed six months earlier.

## Aggregation note

F-4, F-2 and F-3 are **one logical path** — the id-format contract seam — per Kam's aggregation rule. They are not three tickets that arrived together; they are three symptoms of the spec and the runtime disagreeing about what an id is.

## What is NOT established

* **The sweep was read-only and covered 17 GETs.** Not all 83 params, and no non-GET verbs. The `0 500s` result is bounded by that.
* **Whether a structural guard would break any existing caller** — unmeasured. Some of those 79 params may legitimately not be UUIDs.
* **The ~15 count is approximate**, as the gate reported it.

## Provenance

Found by the QA gate during the KS-1013 / PR #910 tier-1 pass, 2026-09-09, sweeping outward from the route under test. Relayed via Wednesday; all counts are the gate's measurements. Related: KS-1013 (the instance), KS-663 (contract drift).

title: Substrate: data_subject_requests is defined in THREE files that disagreed about processed_by's foreign key — and after KS-754 they agree for two different reasons
description:
## BLUF

**Three files define** `data_subject_requests`**, and before KS-754 they disagreed about whether** `processed_by` **carried a foreign key.** Two had `REFERENCES users(id)`; one never did.

**That disagreement is evidence a question was open, and it has NOT been reconciled.** Filed rather than fixed, deliberately.

🔴 **After KS-754 the three now AGREE — for two different reasons. That looks like convergence and it is not.** One file never had the constraint; the other two lost it because widening the column to `TEXT` forced the drop. **A future reader sees three files agreeing and stops asking.** This ticket is the record that they arrived there by different routes.

## The three definitions, as they stood

| file | before KS-754 |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:468` | `processed_by UUID REFERENCES users(id),` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql:473` | `processed_by UUID REFERENCES users(id),` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docker/init/01-schema.sql:495` | `processed_by UUID,` ← **no FK** |

## The real question, which is bigger than one column

**Why do three files define the same table at all, and which is authoritative?**

That is the substrate shape: a schema defined in more than one place drifts silently, and the drift is only ever noticed when someone changes one of them. **This one was noticed because a migration forced a read of all three.** Nothing else would have surfaced it.

**Not established, and this ticket does not guess:**

* **Which file is authoritative.** The migration chain is what an existing database actually ran, but both init files are used for provisioning paths of their own.
* **Whether the docker file's missing FK was deliberate or an omission.** No comment, ticket or commit message explains it. It could be either.
* **Whether other columns or tables disagree across the same three files.** **NOT SWEPT.** `processed_by` was read because a change forced it; nobody has compared the three definitions as wholes. **That sweep is the valuable part of this ticket and it is unstarted.**

## Recommendation

1. **Sweep the three files against each other** — the whole schema, not this column. That is the finding this ticket exists for.
2. **Then decide which is authoritative**, and make the others derive from it or be deleted.
3. **Do NOT close this by noting that the three now agree on** `processed_by`**.** They do, and it means nothing: see the BLUF.

## What KS-754 did and did not do

**Did:** dropped the FK on the two files that had it, because `users.id` is `uuid` and Postgres refuses a `TEXT` column under an FK to a uuid PK. Forced by the change, not a reconciliation.

**Did NOT:** add the FK to the docker file, align the files to each other, or touch `migrations/001` at all (it is applied history; the runner keys on filename with no checksum, so editing it would make a fresh replay differ from what every existing database ran).

## Provenance

Found by s154, 2026-09-09, during the KS-754 consumer enumeration on `develop` `f9296f9e` — the three definitions turned up in a frame-1 sweep for the column name. Wednesday ruled it a finding to file unreconciled. Related: KS-754, KS-949 (the multiple-SQL-source class).

title: Reshape the advisory gate: it is NON-DETERMINISTIC on an unchanged tree — 8 advisories in 30 min, one appeared then vanished. Warn-then-fail, keyed on REACH and SEVERITY (window length is Kam's)
description:
## BLUF

**The advisory gate is NON-DETERMINISTIC ON AN UNCHANGED TREE.** Two runs of the same commit, minutes apart, give different verdicts — because it hard-fails on a dataset that a third party edits continuously and we do not control.

**That is a correctness problem, not a throughput one.** A gate that answers differently on identical input cannot distinguish *"this commit is unsafe"* from *"you ran it at the wrong minute"*.

**Kam ruled the reshape on 2026-09-09 (**`both`**): warn for a window, then hard-fail. The WINDOW LENGTH is explicitly reserved for him and is an open question at the foot of this ticket — it is not proposed here as a number.**

⚠ **And the design must be REACH- AND SEVERITY-AWARE, or it weakens the gate in the one case it exists for.** Detail in *The design constraint* below.

## The evidence — measured across three runs in about half an hour, 2026-09-09

```
run 1  ~21:4x   audit-locks  31 advisories match, 29 baselined   ->  2 missing
run 2  ~22:0x   audit-locks  32 advisories match, 31 baselined   ->  1 missing
run 3  ~22:15   audit-gate   37 reported,         34 baselined   ->  5 missing
```

**The arithmetic is closed, which is what makes this a measurement rather than an impression.** Between runs 1 and 2 exactly **two** baseline rows were added — 29 + 2 = 31, so the *baselined* count is fully explained. **The MATCH count still moved 31 → 32.** Nothing in the repo's dependencies changed: one JSON file was edited, touching zero `package.json` and zero lockfiles.

**Eight distinct advisories touched this repo in half an hour. Three were baselined. The gap widened while it was being closed.**

### 🔴 And one went the OTHER way — this is the part that makes it non-determinism

Between runs 2 and 3, `GHSA-2wm5-q62r-hmrv` (colord) **stopped being reported by the root gate entirely**. Its own output:

```
CLEANUP (advisory): 1 baseline entry is no longer reported — remove:
  - GHSA-2wm5-q62r-hmrv (colord, KS-1024)
```

**An advisory that blocked every push fifteen minutes earlier was no longer reported at all** — with no change on our side. **The dataset does not only grow. It churns.**

## Why the obvious fix is a trap

Baselining the current five turns the preflight green **now**. Run 3 proves that says nothing about run 4. **A green preflight after a triage round is evidence that the external set was quiet for one run, not that the tree is clean** — and the same three runs above show how long "quiet" lasts.

**Triage cannot outrun publication.** That is the loop this ticket exists to break.

## ⚠ The design constraint — a FLAT window would weaken the gate

Written flat, *"warn for a window, then hard-fail"* lets a **production-reaching** advisory sit unblocked for the whole window.

**That is not hypothetical, and the counter-example arrived the same morning the option was drafted:** `GHSA-8m3c-c648-2xjj` — nodemailer's `resolveContent()` bypassing `disableFileAccess`/`disableUrlAccess` on the legacy signature — is a **production dependency of** `services/auth` **and** `services/originate`, the two services that send mail. It survives `npm ci --omit=dev` and reaches a runtime image. **A flat window would have left that unblocked.**

**So the window must key on the same discriminator that has decided every one of these triages:**

| class | behaviour |
| -- | -- |
| measured NOT to reach a shipped tree, **and** moderate or below | **WARN** for the window, do not block |
| reaches a shipped tree | **HARD-FAIL immediately**, no window |
| **HIGH or CRITICAL**, wherever it lives | **HARD-FAIL immediately**, no window |

**This preserves the property Kam wants — nobody blocked for changing nothing — without buying it with the property the gate exists for.** It is deliberately the same test as the standing authority's own clauses: *what does this reach* is the only question that discriminated all morning.

**A necessary consequence, stated so it is designed rather than discovered:** the warn path needs the reach measurement to be **automatic**. Today it is done by hand, per advisory, by whoever is blocked. A gate that warns-or-fails on reach must derive reach itself, or the window just moves the manual step earlier.

## 🔴 OPEN QUESTION FOR KAM — the window length

**He ruled the shape, not the number, and it is not being chosen here.**

Recommendation offered as a recommendation only: long enough that a normal working day is not interrupted by a third party's publishing schedule, short enough that a warn cannot be ignored into permanence. **The data point this ticket can contribute is that eight advisories arrived in half an hour, so any window shorter than that is indistinguishable from no window at all.**

## What is NOT claimed

* **No root cause for the churn.** Whether the 31→32→37 movement is newly-published advisories, a registry re-index, or an `npm audit` dataset refresh is **NOT measured**. The *effect* is measured; the mechanism is not, and the reshape does not depend on which it is.
* **Whether we actually call the vulnerable nodemailer signature** — see the linked note; unmeasured at filing.
* **No claim that any current advisory is exploitable here.** Reachability has not been measured for any of them; that has been true of this baseline since KS-470.

## Provenance

Measured by s154, 2026-09-09, on `develop` `f9296f9e` while blocked from pushing KS-754 — the three runs are its own, and the arithmetic was closed before the conclusion was drawn. Ruled by Kam 2026-09-09 08:12 (`both`), confirmed *"Okay, go ahead with your recommendation."* The reach/severity split is Wednesday's design constraint. Related: KS-1024 (the triage that produced this), KS-470, KS-531.

title: KS-754 gate F-3 (MINOR): migration 048 ships with ZERO automated coverage — test:migrations is hard-wired to 044, so a migrations/ change fires a gate about a different migration
description:
**Source:** tier-1 QA gate on PR #914, 2026-09-09.

## The gap

048's new suite **mocks** `$executeRaw` **outright and never touches a database** — its name claims the column widening it does not exercise.

The repo's only migration-behaviour gate, `npm run test:migrations`, is **hard-wired to one file**:

```
MIGRATION="$HERE/../044_vault_entries_repair.sql"
```

The CI job gated on *"did this change touch* `migrations/`*?"* therefore runs the **044** scenarios. So a `migrations/` change fires a gate about a **different migration** — and Actions is retired for this repo anyway.

The gate driver ran 048 by hand and it holds. **Nothing will drive it again.**

## Why it matters

KS-667's own argument applies verbatim: 048's claimed behaviours are behaviours of **Postgres executing it**, which a mock cannot assert.

## The fix

Make `test:migrations` take the migration(s) under test rather than a hard-wired path, and add 048's scenarios (FK drop forced; constraint name; idempotency — all three already driven by hand in the gate report §5).

## Family

This is a **check that cannot fail** in the KS-926 sense — the gate runs and asserts something other than the change that triggered it.

Report: `.../2026-09-09-qa-gate-ks754-pr914/report.md`

title: tests/e2e auth-exhaustive races its OWN lockout — same commit gives 1 or 11 failures, so the suite cannot gate anything
description:
## BLUF

`tests/e2e/tests/auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` **is non-deterministic against an unchanged product.** It brute-forces logins, `playwright.config.ts` sets `fullyParallel: true`, and every run leaves **4** `lockout:*` **keys** in redis — so its own ordinary login cells race its own lockout. Until this is fixed the suite cannot be used as a gate, because a failure count carries no information.

## Measured — 2026-09-09, `develop` `b6884888d`, `lockout:*` cleared before EACH run

| run | command | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| A | three specs | **23 failed / 54 passed** |
| B | three specs | **11 failed / 71 passed** |
| C | `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` alone | **1 failed / 52 passed** |
| D | `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` alone | **11 failed / 42 passed** |

**Nothing about the product changed between any of them.** Lockout keys were counted after every run: 4 each time, so the suite reliably creates them and unreliably outruns them.

**The flapping cells move as ONE block** — both 23-failure runs carried exactly the same 23, which is what rules out twelve independent flakes and points at a single shared cause. They are all in `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts`: 2.1.1–2.1.5, 2.2.8, 2.2.9, 2.8.1, 2.9.1, 2.9.2, 2.9.4, 2.9.5.

**The deterministic remainder is 10 recruitment/wallet cells** (red in 5 of 5 runs) plus `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts:734`, whose assertion is wrong rather than the app — filed separately.

## Suggested fix (not prescribed)

Either serialise this file (`test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` or a dedicated non-parallel project), or give the brute-force cells a **dedicated account** so they cannot lock the fixture persona the rest of the file logs in with. The second is likely better: it keeps the parallelism and removes the coupling.

## Class

This is the **KS-724** family — a harness that stops testing while still producing results. There, a scan evicted its own bearer; here, a suite locks out its own persona.

## Provenance

* the four runs, lockout counts, and the identical 23-cell block | measured live on the local stack, recorded in `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/BASELINE.md` | 2026-09-09
* Filed from KS-734's baseline work (s160), which made the suite installable and could then measure it.

title: tests/e2e 2.4.6 'SQL injection in registration name is sanitized' asserts against an ECHO — a permanent red carrying no signal
description:
## BLUF

`auth-exhaustive.spec.ts:734` **fails on an echo, not an injection, and the assertion cannot tell them apart.** It is red in **5 of 5** measured runs and will stay red for any application that stores and returns a user-supplied display name.

## Measured

`POST /api/auth/register` with `name = "Robert'); DROP TABLE users; --"`:

* returns **201**
* body carries `"displayname":"robert'); drop table users; --"` back **verbatim**
* **the injection did not execute** — no SQL error, no `syntax error`, no 5xx. The sibling assertions on `'sql'` and `'syntax error'` both **pass**. Parameterised SQL held.

The only failing line is:

```js
expect(body.toLowerCase()).not.toContain('drop table');   // line 751
```

**Control that it is not simple unfiltered input:** sibling **2.4.7 (XSS in name) passes**, so the field is not merely echoed unfiltered everywhere.

## Suggested fix

Re-aim it at what it means to assert: no SQL error **and** `status < 500` (both already true), or assert the stored value equals the exact input. **The output-escaping question is separate** and needs frontend evidence — deliberately UNMEASURED here: I measured the echo, not the renderers.

## Provenance

* the 201 + verbatim echo + passing siblings | recorded on KS-734's 2026-09-02 comment, which asked for this ticket; re-confirmed red in 5 of 5 runs 2026-09-09
* **Attribution, measured not assumed:** not #745's — its three hunks all sit in `2.8 MFA / TOTP` (lines 1207–1352); this is line 734.

title: No independent liveness signal for our own VMs — kintsugi was dead for 53 h and Azure health read `Available` the whole time
description:
## BLUF

`secuura02-kintsugi-vm` **was down for 53 hours and nothing told us. The first signal was Stuart's tooling — a person, not a monitor. And Azure's own platform health read** `Available` **for the whole 53 hours, which is why the one alerting surface we do have would not have fired either.**

Both halves are one logical path — *we have no independent liveness signal for our own VMs* — so they are one ticket per Kam's 2026-09-06 aggregation rule, not two.

## What happened

* Azure live-migrated the VM at **2026-09-07T03:56:13Z** (`PlatformInitiated`, *"paused 0.993s, memory-preserving"*). The guest did not survive it.
* The workload died at ~**04:00Z**. On-disk logs **stop at 03:55:01Z** with **zero** entries for 53 h (control: **53** entries in the same hour).
* It came back only because a person went looking on **2026-09-09**, and was force-reset at **09:31:45Z**.

## Half 1 — no liveness signal

Nothing watches whether kintsugi is serving. There is no uptime check, no synthetic request, no alert on absence of logs. Detection was **incidental**.

⚠ This is the same shape as **KS-670** (demo's on-chain verification down **6 days**, found by a person). Two incidents, same missing control. That is the argument for fixing the class rather than the instance.

## Half 2 — the alerting surface we DO have was lying

Azure marked the box **Available at 03:59:30Z** and said *"no additional action is required"* — while the guest was dead and stayed dead for 53 hours. `memory-preserving` migration means **no reboot**, so Caddy survived in memory and kept answering at the edge while sshd, the guest agent and dockerd were all gone.

**So a health check that trusts either Azure resource health OR a naive port-200 on the front door would have reported green throughout.** Any monitor built here has to make a request that actually traverses the app, and has to alert on **silence** (no logs / no successful synthetic) rather than on an error, because a dead guest produces no errors at all — it produces nothing.

## Why this is due now

The incident record is closed (`5_Project_History/HANDOVER-kintsugi-outage-CLOSED.md`). **Recurrence is not** — Azure live-migrates this box as routine platform behaviour and the guest does not survive one. Boot diagnostics / serial console is now **ENABLED**, so a repeat leaves evidence; nothing currently tells us the repeat *happened*.

## Suggested shape (not a decision — the approach is open)

1. An external liveness check per VM (demo + kintsugi) that traverses the app, not just the edge — the front door answered while the box was dead.
2. Alert on **absence** — no successful synthetic in N minutes, or no new log lines — not on error responses.
3. Do **not** key anything off Azure resource health alone. This incident is the counter-example, in our own record.

## What is NOT established

* Whether the demo VM has the same exposure — **not measured**; it is the same subscription and region and probably does, but I did not check.
* The remount-read-only theory for the guest's death is **strongly supported, not proven**: no kernel message survived, because it could not be written to the disk it was about.

## Provenance

Azure activity log (read in slices — the API truncates silently at 50), the guest's own journal, `df` 37% and a clean `fsck` refuting ENOSPC and corruption from inside. Recorded by s160, filed by s161.

title: CLAUDE.md's "rebuild local after any merge to develop" needs its written exception — a merge with zero buildable surface is a measured no-op
description:
## The ask

**Give** `CLAUDE.md`**'s "rebuild local after any merge to** `develop`**" rule its own written exception**, so the next seat does not have to re-derive it — or, worse, skip it without measuring.

Current wording (project `CLAUDE.md`, "Local + new-Azure sync workflow" §1):

> *"After any merge to* `develop`*, rebuild local so it stays current."*

## Why

On 2026-09-09 (s161) #904 was merged to `develop`. Measured before spending ~30 min of image builds:

```
2 files:  systemTest/__tests__/pre_suite.test.sh            +26/-1
          systemTest/__tests__/quarantine_call_sites.test.sh +27/-1
files with a buildable/deployable surface: 0
```

No service, frontend, package, migration, Dockerfile or compose file. **An image rebuild could not have changed anything** — so the local `develop` ref was synced and the images left alone, and the report said so plainly rather than claiming "local rebuilt".

That was the right call, but it is the **second** time in one session a written rule needed a measured departure. **A rule with a legitimate exception that every seat rediscovers is a rule someone will eventually skip without measuring** — and the departure is invisible unless the operator volunteers it.

## Suggested wording

> *"After any merge to* `develop` *that touches a **buildable surface** (*`services/`*,* `frontend/`*,* `packages/`*,* `migrations/`*, a Dockerfile or a compose file), rebuild local so it stays current. A merge touching only test scripts, docs or CI config is a **measured no-op** — say so, name the file count, and sync the ref instead of rebuilding."*

The load-bearing half is **"say so"**: the exception is only safe while the operator states which branch they took and on what measurement.

## Scope note

⚠ **There are TWO copies of this file** — the project-root `CLAUDE.md` and the repo copy at `2_Project_Files/CLAUDE.md`. Both need the edit or they drift, which is its own recurring trap here.

## What is NOT established

Whether the rule has ever actually been skipped *without* a measurement. **Not swept** — this is filed on the near-miss shape, not on an observed incident.

Filed by s161 on Wednesday's instruction, 2026-09-09.

title: develop is RED on the services/originate jest suite and NOTHING catches it — the suite is a blocking gate nowhere automated
description:
## BLUF

`develop` **is RED on the** `services/originate` **jest suite right now, and no instrument in this repository objects.** Measured tonight: 2 of 4 cells in `ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard.test.ts` fail on develop's own blob. **The suite is a blocking gate NOWHERE automated**, so the mainline can be red indefinitely and nothing says so.

Filed on Wednesday's ruling as a **new** ticket rather than folded into KS-961, because KS-961 is In Review and adding scope to an in-review ticket either reopens reviewed work or buries the new scope under a review that never covered it.

## The measurement

```
npx jest src/__tests__/ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard.test.ts   (in services/originate)
  2 passed   the two NEGATIVE cells (400s an object, 400s a null)
  2 FAILED   both POSITIVES - expected 201, received 500
  EXIT=1
```

Run on blobs verified byte-identical to develop: the test file is `229a3ccde` at both `origin/develop` and `b6884888d`; `routes/webhooks.ts` is `c88eb97db` at both. **PR #926 is the fix and it is open and unmerged**, blocked on an approval.

**Scope of the redness, which the QA gate did not measure:** the full service run is **48 suites / 509 tests, 1 suite / 2 tests failed** — the ks444 positives are the *only* failures in the whole service. ⚠ That run covers **48 of develop's 49** originate suites: it was executed on a tree missing `ks754-processed-by-widened.test.ts`, which is **unswept and named rather than rounded away**.

## Why nothing catches it — four instruments, each checked with a control

| instrument | originate/jest | control on the same file |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` (13 legs, 428 lines) | **0 hits** | `step` -> 18 hits |
| `.githooks/pre-push` (244 lines) | **0 hits** | `preflight` -> 18 hits |
| 17 GitHub workflows | only `ci.yml` + `deploy-demo.yml` invoke workspace tests, **both** `workflow_dispatch`**-only** | 17 mention `test` |
| the 7 `pull_request`-triggered workflows | **none runs any service unit suite** | read their `run:` steps individually |

**This conclusion does not depend on the Actions billing state.** Even with Actions fully funded, no PR-triggered workflow invokes this suite. Actions being retired (Kam, 2026-08-27) is a second, independent reason.

## The actual gap

**The only instrument that would ever catch a red mainline is a human filling in a Test Evidence line — and it only fires if a PR happens to touch that service.** `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` requires `**Unit suites (touched services):** run/result | not run + why`. A suite that is red on develop and untouched by the current PR is invisible to that, by construction.

## The precedent that makes this concrete

`DEV-PROCESS.md` **has already made this exact argument once, for a different subject, and acted on it.** Cross-cutting guards get their own Test Evidence line specifically because, under "run `npm test` in the touched service", they *"execute only when someone touches* `shared`*, which is the change least likely to add a fifteenth service error handler"* — and it concludes **"A guard on no path that runs is not a guard."**

**The same argument applies to a red mainline suite, and nothing currently makes it.**

## Fix shapes (not a ruling - the cheapest is probably the third)

1. A preflight leg that runs the touched service's unit suite, so a red mainline blocks the next push that goes near it.
2. A periodic mainline run whose only job is to answer "is develop green" - no PR coupling.
3. A **baseline-diff** rule in the Test Evidence block: the author records develop's own result for the suites they ran, so "2 failed" is visibly pre-existing rather than silently attributed to the change. This is the same shape KS-660 already applies to Schemathesis ("the failing SET ... + its diff vs the develop baseline set, never a bare count").

## Related

* **KS-961** - the aggregate workspace suite never runs on a PR. Adjacent, In Review, deliberately not extended.
* **KS-1046** - `PREFLIGHT PASSED` printed identically whether 13 legs ran or 10. Same family: a claim whose check did not run.
* **KS-927 / PR #926** - the fix for the red itself.

## Ask

**Kam or Wednesday to pick a fix shape** (or rule that the red simply waits for #926 and no instrument changes). Nothing here is urgent in the sense of a live outage - it is urgent in the sense that the next person to read a green board about `originate` will be reading a false one.

*Filed by s162 (Platform K), 2026-09-09, on Wednesday's ruling. Measurement is mine and reproducible from the commands above.*

title: FLAKE (3rd occurrence, first with a name): ks949 seed-site enumeration fails ~1 in 7 full auth runs and passes alone — timeout hypothesis refuted
description:
## BLUF

`ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts` **fails intermittently in the FULL** `services/auth` **suite and passes on every re-run.** This is the **third** occurrence of a self-healing auth failure. It is the first one with a **name**, which is the only reason it is a ticket rather than a memory.

**Cell:** `the real person is gone from every EXECUTABLE seed site › the enumeration actually finds seed sites, including the one the gate planted in`

## The measurement, 2026-09-09

| run | scope | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | full `services/auth` suite | **FAILED** — `Error: STACK_TRACE_ERROR` at `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts:314` |
| 2, 3 | full suite, identical tree | 642/642 green |
| 4, 5 | full suite, after an unrelated mock fix | 641/642 then 641/642 (a *different*, deterministic failure, since fixed) |
| 6, 7 | full suite | **642/642 green** |
| — | that file ALONE | **30/30 green, 2.73 s** |
| control | full suite on clean develop `d4cf7e3cf`, separate worktree | **635/635 green** |

## Hypothesis TESTED and NOT SUPPORTED — do not re-propose without new evidence

**Timeout under full-suite parallelism.** The failing cell walks the whole `Blockchain/Dev` tree reading every `.ts/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.sql/.sh` file, which is the slowest thing in the suite, and `STACK_TRACE_ERROR` is a shape vitest produces for a task-level abort. **Refuted by the same instrument:** it passes under *identical* parallelism on runs 2, 3, 6 and 7. A timeout that fires once in seven identical runs is not explained by the walk being slow.

**Mechanism therefore UNESTABLISHED.**

## 🔑 How this was caught — the part worth keeping

`HANDOVER-s161.md` **§3 records two earlier occurrences (**`api-gateway` **1/293,** `auth` **2/633) whose test names were NEVER captured.** Without a name there is nothing to pick up, which is precisely why s161 declined to file them and why that was the right call at the time.

That handover shipped an instrument for the next occurrence:

```bash
npx vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=/tmp/vitest-run-$(date +%s).json
```

…with the standing instruction: **capture the name FIRST, before re-running, because a re-run destroys the evidence** — and both earlier events were lost to exactly that.

**It was used on the third occurrence and it produced the name. The instrument paid inside one day of being written.** That is the difference between *"we keep seeing flakes"* and *"we caught the third one because the second one left us a tool."* This ticket exists to make that fact survive the handover it came from.

## Why this is now closeable when the first two were not

It carries a **named subject**, a **reproduction attempt with its result** (7 full runs + 1 isolated + 1 clean-develop control), and a **refuted hypothesis** so the next person does not spend the hour re-proposing it. Mechanism-unestablished is a fine state for a ticket; *unidentified* was not.

## Where to start

1. Re-run the full suite in a loop capturing JSON per run until it reproduces (it took 1 in 7 here) — **do NOT pipe through** `tail`**/**`head`, which is how the first two names were lost.
2. When it reproduces, read `failureMessages` from the JSON rather than the terminal: `STACK_TRACE_ERROR` is what the JSON reporter emitted, and the human reporter may carry more.
3. `ks949…test.ts:314` is the tree-walk control cell — `expect(sites.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3)`. Worth logging `sites` on failure, since an enumeration that transiently returns fewer sites is a different defect from a timeout, and both would present this way.

## Related

* **KS-1052** — found during that work; carries the same record.
* `5_Project_History/HANDOVER-s161.md` §3 — the two earlier occurrences and the instrument.

*Filed by s162, 2026-09-09, on Wednesday's ruling.*

title: Per-tenant databases never receive the file migrations — CORE_MIGRATIONS FORCEs RLS with ZERO policies, so a per-tenant DB is dark on 5 core tables from boot 1 (permanent)
description:
## BLUF

**Per-tenant databases receive** `CORE_MIGRATIONS` **and NEVER the file migrations — not on any boot.** Measured, not read. The consequence is not "039 is missing": `CORE_MIGRATIONS` **enables and FORCEs** row-level security on five core tables while **every policy for them lives only in** `migrations/*.sql`, so a per-tenant DB lands with **FORCE RLS and ZERO policies**. A non-superuser runtime role then reads **zero rows** from `documents`, `certifications`, `audit_logs`, `custody_events` and `shares` — unconditionally, with no GUC able to fix it — and the boot log reports `{migrated: N, skipped: 0}`.

**Latent today, live the moment** `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB=true` — i.e. the moment KS-160 Path A (per-tenant-DB isolation) ships. This is a landmine directly under that roadmap item.

## The defect, in source

`services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`

* **:932** `applyFileMigrations(pg, dbUrl, 'main', fileMigrations)`
* **:939** `applyFileMigrations(pg, platformDbUrl, 'platform', fileMigrations)`
* **:1108** `migrateDatabase(pg, tenantConnStr, tenantDbName, CORE_MIGRATIONS)` ← the tenant loop, **no** `applyFileMigrations` **call anywhere in it**

`applyFileMigrations`' own signature makes it structural, not an oversight in one call: `dbName: 'main' | 'platform'`. A tenant database is not a value that type admits, and the routing inside it (`if (dbName === 'main' && m.isPlatform) continue`) has no third branch.

**The trap is the split:** `CREATE POLICY` appears **0 times** in the whole of `startup-migrations.ts` (control: the same grep finds **19** in `migrations/*.sql`), while CORE_MIGRATIONS runs `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` + `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` at :439-440 (`custody_events`), :485-486 (`shares`), :551-552 (`documents`) and a `format()` loop at :633-634. **Enforcement ships in the array; permission ships in the files. Tenant DBs get only the array.**

The second path that can seed a tenant DB does not close the gap either: `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:62` `createTenantDatabase()` applies `INIT_SCRIPTS_DIR` (`docker/init`, bind-mounted at `docker-compose.yml:2038`) — **12 .sql files, 0** `CREATE POLICY`**, 0** `tenant_scope_bypass` (control: `migrations/` has 17 files with `CREATE POLICY`, 3 with `tenant_scope_bypass`).

## Measurement

Disposable `postgres:15-alpine`, SSL enabled with a locally-signed CA so the product's hard-coded `?sslmode=require` tenant connection could genuinely succeed. Product's own `runStartupMigrations()` driven from source; `startup-migrations.ts` blob verified **identical on** `origin/develop` **and HEAD** (`6a1b53bafa1ad707e663814f95ed92a668e96280`), `migrations/` identical too. Platform DB + main DB + one genuinely separate tenant DB (`tenant_alpha`). Four boots.

| read on `tenant_alpha` after 3 boots | value |
| -- | -- |
| public tables (**connection proof**) | **27** — `documents`, `users`, `anchor_store` all present |
| `_secuura_migrations` table exists | **0 — the file stage never ran, once** |
| `pg_policy` rows | **0** |
| tables with RLS **enabled** | **5** — all also `FORCE` |

**Same reader on the main DB (positive control):** `_secuura_migrations` **48 rows**, `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` **recorded**, `pg_policy` **28**, RLS tables **25**.

### The consequence, measured as an action (not asserted)

`secuuraadmin` is a superuser and bypasses RLS, so the owner read proves nothing. Re-measured as `s163_app` — `LOGIN NOBYPASSRLS`, non-superuser, the KS-109 runtime-role shape:

```
tenant_alpha  documents / certifications / audit_logs   ->  0 , 0 , 0
tenant_alpha  documents WITH both GUCs the product sets ->  0    (no policy exists to satisfy)
tenant_alpha  organizations (non-RLS table, 1 row)      ->  1    <- NON-ZERO CONTROL: login + grants work
superuser, row_security=off, tenant_alpha documents     ->  1    <- the row DOES exist
secuura       documents, NO GUC set                     ->  0
secuura       documents WITH app.tenant_scope_bypass    ->  1    <- DISCRIMINATION CONTROL
secuura       documents WITH app.current_tenant_id      ->  1
```

The zeros on `tenant_alpha` are real zeros, not an unreachable database: the same role, in the same database, reads 1 from a non-RLS table.

## Scope — honest in both directions

**REFUTED for the configuration running today.** `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` defaults false (`services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:245`), so every `tenant_config` row points at the shared app DB — which *does* get the file migrations via the `'main'` path. Confirmed in my own run: the 6 seeded tenants all carried `db_name = secuura`. **5 occurrences of the flag repo-wide, all code/comment, ZERO config sites** (control: `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` appears in `docker-compose.yml`).

⚠ **NOT measured against demo or UAT** — both are held. The above is source + a local reproduction.

**CONFIRMED for per-tenant DBs.** Set the flag — or provision any tenant whose `db_name` differs from the app DB — and that tenant is dark on its five core tables from its first boot, permanently, with a success line in the log.

## Fix shape (not implemented here)

Give `applyFileMigrations` a tenant arm and call it from the loop before `migrateDatabase`, with the file corpus filtered the way `'main'` filters it. The `'main' | 'platform'` union is the thing to widen — an omission should stop compiling rather than be remembered. Any fix must also address the **ordering** KS-1054 documents (039 needs tables CORE creates), or a tenant DB simply reproduces the boot-1 window instead of the permanent one.

## Provenance

QA gate finding **F-928-3**, read-from-source and explicitly UNMEASURED, carried inside KS-1054. Measured here by s163 on 2026-09-09, local disposable containers only, removed at close. Demo, UAT and every shared database untouched.

---

## TLS: the tenant connection is VERIFY-FULL, and that is what makes F-928-4's counter load-bearing

**The product hard-codes** `?sslmode=require` **on the tenant connection string** (`startup-migrations.ts:1105`), and `pg-connection-string` **2.12.0 treats** `require` **as** `verify-full` — it says so itself at runtime: *"The SSL modes 'prefer', 'require', and 'verify-ca' are treated as aliases for 'verify-full'."* So the tenant loop does not merely want TLS; it requires a **CA-verifiable certificate chain and a matching hostname**.

**Proved both ways before any of the measurement above was trusted**, against the same container and the same connection-string shape:

```
no trusted CA   ->  "unable to verify the first certificate"
trusted CA      ->  connected, current_database() = tenant_alpha
```

That is why this ticket's zeros mean something: had I not stood the CA up, the tenant DB would have been unreachable and I would have measured my own container instead of the product.
