title: revoke answers 400 "already revoked" where 404 belongs if the document is deleted mid-race
description:
**Pre-existing, and narrowed rather than introduced by the KS 1278 change.** Found while building PR #1393.

`updateDocument` in originate's document repository returns `null` for **two** different outcomes:

1. the document was not found — the inner `getDocument` read came back empty (the pre-existing path, `documentRepo.ts:538`);
2. the guarded write changed no row — the KS 1278 `ifStatusIsNot` guard refused it because the row was already in the target status.

The revoke route maps `null` to **400 BAD_REQUEST "Document is already revoked"**. For the ordinary case that is right, and deliberately so: the route 404s and 403s before the write, and 400s on the read, so by the time the guarded write runs the document exists and was not revoked at read time — a `null` can only mean the row became revoked in between, which is exactly the race KS 1278 closes.

**The residual:** if the document is **deleted** between the route's read and the guarded write, outcome 1 fires instead, and the caller is told **"Document is already revoked" with a 400** when the correct answer is **404 Document not found**. The window is narrow — it is a race, not a reachable sequential path — and nothing here is a security or data-integrity problem: no write happens, no provenance row is recorded and no anchor is emitted in either case. It is a response-classification defect only.

**Before KS 1278** the route did not read the write's result at all, so this particular confusion could not arise there; the same single `null` was already ambiguous for every other caller of `updateDocument`, which is why this is recorded as pre-existing in shape and merely surfaced at a new call site.

**What a fix would need.** Separate the two meanings rather than overload one `null` — for example a discriminated result (not-found vs guard-refused vs updated), or a cheap existence re-read on the `null` path before choosing the status code. Both touch every caller of `updateDocument`, which is why it was explicitly left out of KS 1278's scope rather than bolted on.

**Not measured.** No live sweep and no two-session test ran against a real PostgreSQL. The claim above is read off the control flow in `documentRepo.ts` and `routes/documents.ts` plus the mocked cells in PR #1393, not reproduced against a running stack.

Refs KS-1278

title: gate63 minors on the KS-1404 trust-anchor wiring (PR 1388): six Minors carried forward, and the image proof was never run
description:
gate63 returned **GO** on #1388 (KS-1404, the trust-anchor wiring) with six Minor findings, none
blocking and none Major. The PR has merged; this ticket carries the findings forward with the
fix-shape the gate gave for each. Report `a68b1497f421c496…`, 276 lines.

Refs KS-1404

## The six findings

**N-1388-1 — the tsc figure does not reproduce, and no host is named.** The claim "a single
pre-existing tsc error (`rfc3161-verify.ts` TS2345), its line moving 344→349" appears in the commit
message, the PR body and flow 11.4. The gate measured TypeScript 5.9.3 on standalone member
installs and got **rc 0, zero** `error TS` **lines at both** `f01c1da5717f` and `3ce575eeb63c`; the brief
expected 59. Three different counts for one figure, none with a host. The substance holds — **0 NEW**
**errors either way** — but it sits in a client-facing doc with nothing that lets a reader
re-measure it. *Fix-shape:* name the host and install recipe beside each figure, or restate as
"0 new tsc errors (base N / head N on <host>, <recipe>)". The "1937 packages" figure in the PR body
is the same class (the gate measured 349+267 standalone, 346+311 as workspace members; I measured
1,393 package directories in the worktree — three units, one number).

**N-1388-2 — the cheat sheet's corrected note points the wrong way.** The note after the KS-1404
table (`:3776-:3779`) says the wiring row is "below"; it is at `:3748`, **above**. "is now covered"
also reads as though some environment already has the anchor in effect — none does, because no
deploy has happened. *Fix-shape:* "below" → "above", and say "this change wires every
compose-launched box; in effect once deployed". This could not be fixed in the merge-in: Q-M's M1
pins the head's section byte for byte.

**N-1388-3 — cell A does not bind the default's variable name.** Tamper T-NAME
(`${OTHER_VAR:-/app/config/tsa-trust-anchors-dtrust.crt}`) stays **6/6 green**. The default still
pins D-Trust so verification is unaffected; what breaks silently is the documented override path.
*Fix-shape:* anchor the regex to `^\$\{TSA_TRUST_ANCHORS_PEM:-(.*)\}$`. *Regression test:* T-NAME
must red cell A.

**N-1388-4 — no PR cell parses the REAL per-provider file inside the verifier.** C1 hashes the PEM
with the test's own decoder; C2 uses a synthetic root. At the base C1 reds only through A's
precondition, so its own conjunct has no independent red-first. The gate's probe P1/P2 closes the
gap at runtime for this head, as does pre-existing cell 17 (the bundle's block 1 is byte-equal to
this file). *Fix-shape:* commit P1 and P2 as cells —
`parseTrustAnchors(readFileSync(<real file>)).length === 1` at the digest, and a synthetic token with
the real file by path refused "does not chain", never "no trust anchor configured".

**N-1388-5 — a missing anchor is silent until a verify, and** `/health` **carries no anchor state.**
Fail-closed is the safe direction, but a wiring failure reproduces today's "everything refused"
state behind a green `/health`. *Fix-shape:* an `anchors: {configured, count, sha256[]}` block in
`/health`, or a boot-time log line. **Operational consequence now:** the deploy sweep must use the
in-container checks in the gate's C7(a), never `/health`.

**N-1388-6 — the image also ships the two-root bundle** (DigiCert included) at
`/app/config/tsa-trust-anchors.crt`. Q-SCOPE holds and no new privilege is created.
*Fix-shape (optional):* COPY only the per-provider file, or note it in `config/README.md`.

## OWED to the kintsugi deploy round, not done here

**C6, the local image proof, is NOT RUN — the Docker daemon was unreachable (c6 rc 20).** So the
claim that the built image actually contains `/app/config/tsa-trust-anchors-dtrust.crt` is
unverified. It is owed to the deploy round, which is a separate seat on its own GO. Nothing in
#1388 has been deployed: `TSA_URL` is present-but-empty on both live boxes, which resolves to
D-Trust by code default, and `TSA_TRUST_ANCHORS_PEM` is absent on both, so every real RFC 3161
token is still refused with `no trust anchor configured` until a deploy happens.

## Also worth recording, found while merging

`merged8.py` requires nine `targets` as (blob, mode) pairs that the gate's `## MERGE ADDENDUM` line
does not publish. I sourced each by reading `ls-tree` at the head so the mode comes from git rather
than from me, but the gap between what the gate publishes and what the merge tool demands is an
invitation to guess at a value that lands on `develop` permanently.

title: pre-push: when local develop is behind, the gate's changed set comes from a stale origin/develop and refuses a push for systemTest files the author never touched
description:
## BLUF

**The pre-push hook refuses a push for** `systemTest/` **files the author never touched.** When local `develop` is behind, the hook falls back to the shared checkout's `origin/develop` ref for base selection. That ref is stale, so the computed push range includes every `systemTest/` change merged since — and the KS 989 formatting gate then selects a package the author did not touch, finds no deps in a fresh worktree, checks **0 packages** and fails closed. Measured on PR #1394.

This is **not** the same as KS 998 item 1. That item was the gate failing **OPEN** on missing deps (exit 0 when prettier is absent). It now fails **CLOSED**, which is correct and is the discipline working. The defect is upstream of it: the *changed set* names a foreign package in the first place. KS 998 anticipated exactly this tension — "hard-failing presents an environment condition as a gate failure, which is precisely KS 991's" concern — and this is that case arriving.

## Measured

| Range | Paths | of which `systemTest/akto/` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| stale `origin/develop` (`32e058975d4e`) .. head `a94ec8f6a2c6` | 38 | **21** |
| the commit alone (`d784b613c81e` .. `a94ec8f6a2c6`) | 5 | **0** |

The 21 `systemTest/akto/` paths come from KS 1411's merged commits `a964e962c` and `ffca61a3d`, already on develop.

Refs at the time, in the shared checkout:

* local `develop` = `c56dd7c32edf` (2026-10-01)
* local `origin/develop` = `32e058975d4e` (two develops behind)
* the commit's real parent = `d784b613c81e`

No local ref knows `d784b613c81e` as develop, so the fallback is taken.

## Why it had not been seen before

The previous seat's push passed this gate because **its base WAS** `32e058975d4e`, identical to the stale ref, so its range was exactly its own 6 files with 0 `systemTest/` paths and the gate selected no package at all. Every seat whose base is newer than that ref hits this, and each merge into develop widens the range further. It gets worse with time rather than being a one-off.

## The misleading line

On refusal the hook prints:

```
[pre-push] systemTest formatting gate FAILED — fix the files named above.
```

It names **no file**. The gate's own preceding output is explicit that nothing was examined — `NOTHING CHECKED — every selected package was skipped, so no file's formatting was examined. This is NOT a formatting failure: the gate could not run.` The hook line contradicts it and sends the author looking for a formatting defect that does not exist.

## The gate already has what it needs

When the gate does run and fails, it labels the offending file `(NOT in this push — inherited red)`. So the information required to avoid charging an author for a foreign package is present at the point of the message.

## Remedies, in order of narrowness

1. **Derive the gate's changed set from the push's own range** — the real parent, or develop by SHA — rather than a fallback base. Narrowest, and the gate already computes the distinction for its message.
2. **Refresh** `origin/develop` **in the shared checkout.** Fixes the symptom for all seats but is a ref write in a checkout other sessions assert byte-identical across their rounds, so it needs a window with no live seat.
3. **Have each fresh worktree install the four gated** `systemTest` **packages** before its first push. Works, but it is four installs per worktree for a gate that should not have selected them.

## Reproduce

```
git -C <worktree> diff --name-only 32e058975d4e a94ec8f6a2c6 | grep -c '^systemTest/akto/'   # 21
git -C <worktree> diff --name-only d784b613c81e a94ec8f6a2c6 | grep -c '^systemTest/'        # 0
bash systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh < <the first range>   # 0 checked, 1 skipped, FAIL
```

After `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in `systemTest/akto` the same command reads `1 package(s) checked, 0 skipped, 0 failed`, rc 0 — and a planted formatting defect in an akto file still returns rc 1, so that green is a measurement and not an install that silenced the gate.

Four `systemTest` packages declare `format:check` (akto, api-explorer, performance, playwright) and all four have `node_modules` absent in a fresh worktree, so any of them can be the one selected.

Discovered 2026-10-05 raising PR #1394 (Refs KS 723). Host Kamil's Mac Studio (2).

title: gate64 minors on the KS-1330 runner re-land (PR 1389): six findings carried forward, and the gate kit's key reader goes blind on a split <h2>
description:
gate64 returned **GO** on #1389 (KS-1330, re-landing the round-2 signal handling) at head `a7f5965a7b3f`. The PR has MERGED as squash `22b268143a6377c9a82cd03379daa596cd26d644` on develop. This ticket carries the non-blocking findings forward with the fix shape the gate gave for each, plus one defect in the **gate kit itself** that will hit every lane merging on top of PR 1390. Refs KS-1330 ## The six carried findings **N-1389-1 — Minor, MEASURED.** Leg 14 is no evidence for item 1, and the PR body says it is. Leg 14 sends no signal to the runner, so both INT arms are unreachable there. Fix: drop the leg-14 sentence from any future Test Evidence for this work; the arm's evidence is the suite, not the push. **N-1389-3 — Minor, MEASURED.** The interrupt cell cannot tell a re-raise from a plain exit 1 — the tamper stays 61/0. Fix: assert the signal-death exit status (128+SIG) rather than just non-zero, so a runner that exits 1 instead of re-raising reddens. **N-1389-4 — Minor, PROBED.** A false grep sentence and an absent file. The conclusion holds, the figures do not. Fix: re-measure per file against a must-hit control before restating it anywhere. **N-1389-5 — Minor, PROBED.** The coupling figures are wrong: 16 read-heads measured, not 2; 9 trap-INT, not 10 of 10. The conclusions hold. Fix: same as N-1389-4 — the sentence survives, the numbers must be re-taken. **N-1389-6 — Minor.** Item 3 has no pinning cell; its explanatory comment sits mid-loop rather than in the header; and there is a re-indent artefact. Fix: add one pinning cell, move the comment to the header, drop the re-indent. **N-1389-7 — Polish, MEASURED.** An interrupt under a short TMPDIR leaves the in-flight `rss-suite.*` log behind. Pre-existing, not introduced by this PR. Not in scope here: **N-1389-2** belongs to KS 1331 (the untrapped background grandchild), and **N-1389-8** / **N-1389-9** are Info. ## The gate-kit defect — the one worth acting on `c4_docs_gate64.py:61` **finds doc sections with a SAME-LINE reader, and PR 1390 split** `

` **across** **lines, so the key list silently loses half its entries.** The reader is `h2 = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if '

' in l]` followed by a key match against `lines[i]`. Both key regexes require the closing tag on the opening tag's line: cheat `— KS-(\d+)

`, flow `\(KS-(\d+)\)`. Measured on the real doc bytes, read by the GitHub contents API at each ref: | flow doc | `

` lines | same-line keys | multiline-tolerant keys | split `

` | | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | | develop `d784b613c81e` | 16 | 8 | 8 | 0 | | develop `c5101866e` (after PR 1390) | 16 | **4** | 8 | **5** | Keys LOST by the same-line reader: KS 1015, KS 1345, KS 1388, KS 1210. Keys kept: KS 666, KS 1404, KS 1333, KS 1005. The split `

` lines are 1671, 1790, 2504, 2618 and 2734, and the shape is ```

9. Auth surface — connector tokens on the users routes (KS 564, KS 1402)

``` The cheat sheet is unaffected (6 `

`, 6 same-line keys, 6 tolerant, 0 split, at both develops). **Why it matters.** The kit README calls the key-anchored predicted tree "the authority". The predicted TREE was in fact sound here, because it comes from `merge-tree`, not from this reader. What degrades is the gate's judgement: the D5 key census and M8's "every doc at M equals develop's doc, key for key" ran over a 4-of-8 key list and would **PASS while blind to four sections**. A gate that passes blind is worse than one that fails. The coordinator set M1 and the M8/D5 key census aside for this merge by name and replaced M8 with blob byte-equality, which needs no reader and is strictly stronger for a PR carrying no doc hunk. Note that `flow_numbers()` at `:81` uses `re.findall(r'

\s*(\d+)\.', text)` over the whole text, and `\s*` crosses a newline — so that reader survives a split while `sections()` does not. The two readers disagree on the same document. **Fix shape.** Match the key against the whole `

` element rather than its opening line: join from `

` to the next `

` before applying the key regex, or apply the regex to the full text with `re.S`. Then add a fixture with a split `

` so the arm cannot go vacuous again, and a control proving the pre-fix reader loses a key on it. **Also measured, already filed elsewhere — not duplicated here.** The push for this merge needed `npm ci` in `systemTest/akto` first, because the stale shared `refs/remotes/origin/develop` (`32e058975d4e`) widens the format gate's selection to 21 `systemTest/akto` paths that the merge-in range itself does not contain (`f0179806..M` is 0). That is **KS 1422**, measured there on PR 1394. ## Evidence * Squash `22b268143a6377c9a82cd03379daa596cd26d644`, tree `c25213614a52e3ce018855ed61c27cbf4558734f`, one parent `f0179806494e42df254b9580168be3cd4a35f307`, subject 75 chars, 0 trailers. * Merge-in `677750a8d48c7f7533171f888598f6e1494fa288`; gate64 `qm` M1-M8 PASS twice, 0 FAIL, with the head-as-merge-in-head control returning 5 FAIL. * Push preflight, verbatim and NOT a pass: `PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 12/15 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.` Legs 3, 4 and 8 skipped — local stack not up. Leg 14: `shell suites: 67 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (of 67)`. * Not tested, named rather than implied: a live sweep, a real PTY ^C, the whole push preflight, and any bash other than 3.2.57.

title: updateDocument: a UUID-addressed update matches 0 rows and silently writes nothing for the 12 unguarded callers
description:
A `updateDocument(id, ...)` call whose `id` is the platform UUID (the primary key) resolves the row on the READ but matches **0 rows** on the WRITE, because the UPDATE keys on `external_id`. For the one guarded caller this surfaced as a wrong 400 and is fixed under KS-1278. **For the other 12 production callers there is no guard, so the function returns the updated record and the caller reports success while the database was never written.**

Instrument for the mechanism: read of `documentRepo.ts` at `4a1620588819` (blob `e29ebcdd79c2`) plus the caller census below. The silent-success behaviour for the unguarded callers is **inferred from the same code path, not separately probed — unmeasured against a live database.**

## Why a UUID reaches these callers

`fromDbRow` returns `id: row.external_id || row.id` and `documentUuid: isValidUuid(row.external_id) ? row.external_id : row.id`. When `external_id` is not UUID-shaped, `documentUuid` IS the primary key, and the API hands clients that value. `getDocument` accepts it via its uuid fallback. The UPDATE does not.

## Caller census

Measured with `git grep -n 'updateDocument(' <sha> -- Blockchain/Dev`, read from a file. 24 lines at `4a1620588819`, 23 at the branch base `32e058975d4e`. Controls: a must-hit token returned 2 files; a nonsense token returned rc 1 with 0 lines.

Breakdown: **13 production calls**, 1 definition, 1 comment line, 9 test-file lines.

| file:line @ 4a1620588819 | id expression | where the id comes from | can carry a platform UUID | opts | base behaviour on a UUID id |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| routes/documents.ts:800 | `id` | `:639` create path, `documentUuid ?? doc-<ts>` | no in practice | none | row inserted with that external_id, so the key matches |
| routes/documents.ts:881 | `id` | same as 800 | no in practice | none | matches |
| routes/documents.ts:913 | `id` | same as 800 | no in practice | preserveTerminalStatuses | matches |
| routes/documents.ts:928 | `id` | same as 800 | no in practice | none | matches |
| routes/documents.ts:1224 | `id` | `req.params` at `:1188` | **YES** | none | **0 rows, returns the record, reports success** |
| routes/documents.ts:1408 | `id` | `req.params` at `:1327` | **YES** | none | **0 rows, returns the record, reports success** |
| routes/documents.ts:2398 | `id` | `req.params` at `:2353`, route `/:id/revoke` | **YES** | ifStatusIsNot | 0 rows, returns null, wrong 400 — FIXED under KS-1278 |
| routes/verification.ts:396 | `String(docId)` | `persistHealedAnchor` at `:389` | **YES** | preserveTerminalStatuses | **0 rows, silent** |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:183 | `documentId` | parameter, threaded from the create path | no in practice | preserveTerminalStatuses | matches |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:258 | `documentId` | `opts.documentId` | no in practice | preserveTerminalStatuses | matches |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:295 | `documentId` | `opts.documentId` | no in practice | preserveTerminalStatuses | matches |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:376 | `document.id` | a DocumentRecord | **YES when external_id is NULL** | preserveTerminalStatuses | **0 rows, silent** |
| services/anchorStateSync.ts:414 | `document.id` | a DocumentRecord | **YES when external_id is NULL** | preserveTerminalStatuses | **0 rows, silent** |

So **12 of the 13** keep `WHERE external_id` unchanged under KS-1278, and **5 of those 12** are reachable with a value that matches no row. The NULL-`external_id` case is already in gate65's own NOT TESTED list.

This census **corrects the figure of 14** used while ruling KS-1278: 14 counted the 13 production calls plus one non-call line. The measured count is 13 production callers, 1 opted in, 12 others.

## What was searched before filing

Linear team KS titles, case-insensitive: `updateDocument` 0 hits, `documentRepo.ts` 0 hits, `external_id` 0 hits. Must-hit control: `revoke` returned 18. Inverted control: a nonsense symbol returned 0. So the filter discriminates and this class was genuinely unfiled. `searchIssues` was not used as an absence instrument.

## Not fixed here

KS-1278's round 2 narrows the fix to the single opted-in revoke path on purpose, so the blast radius is one caller. Changing the other 12 needs its own decision: for an unguarded caller a 0-row update is currently indistinguishable from a successful one, so simply re-keying them would change what several callers report. Refs KS-1278.

title: unhandledRejection posture as shipped differs from KS-546's: setupGracefulShutdown has no callers, and originate survives rejections while the gateway's comment cites it as fail-fast
description:
## Summary

[KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) ruled that the api-gateway **survives** unhandled rejections and that *everything else stays fail-fast*. On `develop` `f556373b9`, two things don't match that ruling. First, the shared wrapper that would make every other service log and apply its mode, `setupGracefulShutdown`, has **no callers**, so [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything)'s Verify step can't be observed. Second, **originate survives** unhandled rejections: it registers its own listener, which logs and does not exit. The gateway's own comment cites originate as an example of fail-fast. Either originate is a second, undocumented `survive` service, or it's a bug. That's a ruling for you, not something to settle in systemTest.

These came up while scoping [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture), the systemTest ticket that pins the [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) posture. They're outside systemTest, so they're filed here for you.

+++ Evidence (read at source, `develop` `f556373b9`, 2026-10-06)

### 1. `setupGracefulShutdown` has no callers

* It's defined at `packages/shared/src/utils/gracefulShutdown.ts:99` and re-exported at `utils/index.ts:10`. No service imports it: `git grep setupGracefulShutdown -- Blockchain/Dev` finds only the definition, the re-export, a JSDoc example and the comment below.
* The code now says so: `packages/shared/src/index.ts:22-23` reads *"the gateway consumes these directly (the setupGracefulShutdown wrapper itself has no live consumers today)."*
* So the line [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything)'s Verify section says to check, `Graceful shutdown handlers registered (unhandledRejection mode: X)` (`gracefulShutdown.ts:177`), never prints. *"All other services log* `exit`*"* can't be observed on any stack.
* The only live path is the gateway, which wires `resolveUnhandledRejectionMode` + `createUnhandledRejectionHandler` itself (`services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:1161-1171`) and logs `unhandledRejection mode: <mode>`.

### 2. originate is not fail-fast for unhandled rejections

* `services/originate/src/index.ts:72-77` calls `process.on('unhandledRejection', …)`, which logs, calls `trackError`, and **returns**. It never exits.
* Registering any listener disables Node's fatal default, so originate keeps running after an unhandled rejection. Its `uncaughtException` handler just below it *does* exit.
* The surrounding comment ([KS-294](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-294/perfscalability-originate-service-crashes-under-write-pressure)) explains why it logs: so a crash leaves a trace. It doesn't say surviving is intended.
* `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:1159-1160` says *"Every other service keeps fail-fast (originate's own handler, or Node 20's fatal default)"*. That's backwards for originate. It also names Node 20, but the images are `node:24-alpine` (`services/originate/Dockerfile`).

### 3. Scope check

Only two `process.on('unhandledRejection'` registrations exist under `services/`: the gateway ([KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything), intended) and originate. Every other service has no listener, so it falls back to Node 24's fatal default and does fail fast. The `routes/verification.ts:1367` hit is a comment, not a registration.

### Not checked

Nothing was run against a stack. This is a code read only. No Platform S code is involved.

+++

## What's needed (your call)

1. **originate:** decide whether it should **survive** or be **fail-fast**.
   * If survive: say so in [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything)'s terms. Ideally declare `UNHANDLED_REJECTION_MODE=survive` for originate too, so the posture lives in config rather than an inline listener.
   * If fail-fast: wire originate through `createUnhandledRejectionHandler` (mode `exit`) so it still leaves the [KS-294](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-294/perfscalability-originate-service-crashes-under-write-pressure) trace before exiting.
2. `setupGracefulShutdown`**:** either have the services call it, so every service logs its mode, or delete the wrapper and amend [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything)'s Verify step to what can actually be observed.
3. **The gateway comment** at `api-gateway/src/index.ts:1159-1160`: correct it to match whatever (1) decides, and fix the Node version.

## How systemTest will use the answer

[KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture)'s boot-posture assertion checks that the gateway logs `survive` and a sampled non-gateway service does not. Today the only service that logs a mode at all is the gateway. [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) will assert the posture as shipped and cite this ticket. When you rule on (1) and (2), that assertion moves with your ruling, red→green.

Refs: [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) (the ruling, Done) · [KS-529](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529/gateway-intermittent-502-bad-gateway-to-healthy-upstreams-under-sweep) (outage class) · [KS-294](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-294/perfscalability-originate-service-crashes-under-write-pressure) (originate's logging rationale) · [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) (systemTest pin). Raised by agent on Peter's behalf.

title: systemTest: SSRF regression for POST /api/teams/webhook-config (split from KS-502 §3b) — waits on KS-784's validation order
description:
## Summary

This is [KS-502](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-502/systemtest-schemathesis-skipped-security-regressions-needing-a-proper) §3b, split out on 2026-10-06 so that [KS-502](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-502/systemtest-schemathesis-skipped-security-regressions-needing-a-proper) can close on the parts we can do now (§1 billing idempotency, §2 seed-demo gate, §3a). This part waits on Kamil.

`POST /api/teams/webhook-config` carries the [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487/review-b-input-validation-injection-upload-xssssrf-and-crypto) B-1 SSRF guard on `webhookUrl`. But `requireM365` answers **503** before validation whenever `ENTRA_*` is unconfigured, which is the case on every developer stack and slot. So `tests/test_webhook_ssrf.py::TestWebhookSsrfResidual` can never reach the guard, and has been a documented skip since July (`test_webhook_ssrf.py:207` on `develop` `f556373b9`).

## Waiting on

[KS-784](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-784/post-apiteamswebhook-config-fails-the-schemathesis-pr-sweep-on-every) (Kamil, Backlog). The 2026-09-14 requirement and its 2026-10-06 follow-up ask whether `webhookUrl` will be validated **before** `requireM365`. Neither has an answer yet.

* **If option 1 (validate first):** this becomes a plain red→green regression on any slot. Internal, metadata and rebinding hosts → 400 regardless of `ENTRA_*`.
* **If option 2 (a local test mode):** the test enables that mode and makes the same assertions.
* **If neither:** recategorise the skip as out of scope (the [KS-519](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-519/schemathesis-systemtest-register-non-passing-tests-coverage-gaps-and) category) with this ticket as the reason, instead of leaving a bare skip.

## Done looks like

The skip is removed. The test is shown red against the current ordering and green after [KS-784](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-784/post-apiteamswebhook-config-fails-the-schemathesis-pr-sweep-on-every) lands. It appears on all three surfaces (console, Schemathesis results, HTML report), the [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage) coverage row flips, and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` plus the QA cheat-sheet are synced.

title: systemTest: the pre-rotation key is dead after rotate:true (split from KS-568 row 4) — waits on KS-577 revoke-on-rotate
description:
## Summary

[KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks) row 4 proves that read-back survives key rotation. Kam ruled on 2026-08-07 that rotation must also **revoke the prior key**. As shipped, `rotate: true` mints a new key and leaves the old one valid with identical scopes. So a row-4 test that checks only the new key passes while the compromised credential stays live.

This ticket is the fourth assertion, **the old key is dead after rotation**. It's split from [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks) on 2026-10-06 so that [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks) can close on what holds today: rows 1–3, row 4's read-back half, rows 5–8 (row 5 is unblocked by [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578/cross-tenant-api-key-revoke-misses-the-db-row-when-the-cache-is-cold), Deployed to UAT), and the two-tier key provisioning.

## Waiting on

[KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577/rotate-true-mints-a-new-key-but-never-revokes-the-old-one-implement) (Kamil, **In Review** as of 2026-10-06): implement revoke-on-rotate and agree the cutover window. The cutover window decides the assertion's timing: immediately dead, or dead after N seconds.

## Test

* Anchor under an operational key → `rotate: true` → the **old** key gets an auth error on read and on write, and the write creates no row (no 2xx-with-no-effect).
* Run with a warm and a cold key cache, the [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578/cross-tenant-api-key-revoke-misses-the-db-row-when-the-cache-is-cold) lesson.
* Red on `develop` today, green once [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577/rotate-true-mints-a-new-key-but-never-revokes-the-old-one-implement) merges. It could land early as `xfail(strict=True)` citing [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577/rotate-true-mints-a-new-key-but-never-revokes-the-old-one-implement), so it flips loudly. Peter's call once [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks) is in review.
* Appears on all three surfaces (console, Schemathesis results, HTML report).

## Also gated by [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577/rotate-true-mints-a-new-key-but-never-revokes-the-old-one-implement)

[KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks)'s conditional bulk re-key extension waits on [KS-576](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-576/bulk-re-key-one-admin-authorised-rotate-across-a-named-set-of) (Todo, Kamil), which is blocked on [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577/rotate-true-mints-a-new-key-but-never-revokes-the-old-one-implement) by ruling. title: Connector keys are minted `anchors:read` and `documents:revoke`, but neither scope is enforced anywhere — anchor reads are scope-ungated and revoke has no scope check
description:
## Summary

`register-connector` mints Platform S connector keys with nine scopes, including `anchors:read` and `documents:revoke`. Neither scope is checked anywhere in the request path. So a connector key's anchor reads are not scope-gated at all: a key minted WITHOUT `anchors:read` would still read anchors. And `documents:revoke` has no effect: the revoke route checks ownership only. That breaks the deny-by-default rule ([KS-539](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-539/k-define-governing-rules-for-document-operations-by-agents) R2: scopes are the authority) for these two scopes. This is a code read; nothing has been probed live yet.

+++ Evidence (read at source, `develop` `f556373b9`, 2026-10-06)

**Minted:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:485-489` (`S_CONNECTOR_SCOPES`) includes both `'documents:revoke'` (:486) and `'anchors:read'` (:487). Vocabulary: `packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts:42` and `:76`.

`anchors:read` **— enforced nowhere:**

* `api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` gates only the two anchor WRITES: `POST /api/anchors` and `POST /api/anchors/batch` carry `attachScopes, requireScope('anchors:write')` (:852-863).
* The catch-all `router.use('/api/anchors', authenticateToken(true), proxy('anchoring', …))` (:865-868) has no `requireScope`, so every anchor read reaches anchoring with authentication only.
* A search of `services/*/src` and `packages/shared/src` (tests excluded) finds `anchors:read` only in the minting list and the vocabulary — no check in anchoring either.

`documents:revoke` **— enforced nowhere:**

* The other document verbs check their scope through `isAllowedByRoleOrScope(...)`: create and version `documents:write` (`documents.ts:372`, `:1983`), transfer `documents:transfer-custody` (`:1599`), share `documents:share` (`:2172`).
* The revoke route (`documents.ts:2344` onward) has no scope check. It gates on `document.owner?.id !== user.id` → 403. A connector principal is never the owner, so connectors cannot revoke at all. Your own [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) finding, 2026-08-26, verbatim: *"A connector principal cannot revoke at all"*.

### Not verified

* No live probe yet with a connector key minted without `anchors:read`. Whether anchoring further limits reads per tenant was not checked.
* Severity therefore not asserted beyond "the scope is not checked".

### Related, deliberately not duplicated

* Whether connectors should be able to revoke at all is the open question you put to Stuart on [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) (2026-08-26, Kam's ruling "ask Stuart to reconcile [PS-616](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-616/s-shipped-ps-569-ahead-of-ks-566-so-lifecycle-event-and-flat-anchor) first"). This ticket does not reopen that. It only records that the minted scope is dead either way: if the answer is "no", stop minting it; if "yes", the route needs the scope check plus an owner-gate change.
* Duplicate check, Platform K + Platform S, 2026-10-06: no ticket names either scope's enforcement. [KS-71](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-71/q6-scope-aware-rbac-in-originate-sk-connector-role-can-post) (Done) built scope-aware RBAC for create. [KS-858](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-858/security-class-a-scope-gate-mounted-as-an-exact-route-above-a-catch) (Deployed) is a different class: scope-gate bypass by path spelling.

### Suggested direction (your call)

1. Gate anchor reads with `requireScope('anchors:read')` for key callers (as `/api/documents` does with `documents:read`), or stop minting the scope.
2. Resolve `documents:revoke` per the [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) answer.

systemTest coverage follows on Peter's side: [KS-571](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-571/systemtest-schemathesis-ks-539-agent-document-operation-rules) item 3 (R2, deny-by-default) / [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks).

+++

Refs: [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480/sk-k-side-support-consistent-userorg-ownership-credential) / [KS-539](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-539/k-define-governing-rules-for-document-operations-by-agents) (rules R2) · [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) (revoke question) · [KS-571](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-571/systemtest-schemathesis-ks-539-agent-document-operation-rules) / [KS-568](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-568/systemtest-schemathesis-sk-connector-identity-regression-coverage-ks) (systemTest) · [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) (Review A). Raised by agent on Peter's behalf.

title: Akto full scan reports three LOW HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES results (wallet-status ×2, GET /api/settings/notifications) that no ticket or allowlist covers — classify them: by-design or a finding
description:
## BLUF

The one `test:security` run on 2026-10-07 reported three **LOW** results from `HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES` on two public routes. No ticket covers them and no allowlist mechanism can express them. They are probably expected for public routes that ignore request headers, but that is **not established**, and today they fail the Full OWASP workflow on their own because the gate fails on any severity, LOW included.

## Measured (slot 1, Mac, Akto 2.37.1, 2026-10-07, run `security`, full OWASP summary `6ac60a95a141e9203079d8bf`, 50,450 result docs)

| Result |  |
| -- | -- |
| Template | `HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES`, category INPUT, severity LOW, CWE-20, nature INTRUSIVE |
| Docs for the template | 350; **90 executed** (a captured exchange); **3 flagged** (raw `vulnerable: true`); 347 not |
| Flagged 1 | `GET /api/auth/wallet/status/dt-seed-7` |
| Flagged 2 | `GET /api/auth/wallet/status/STRING` (the `{walletAddress}` placeholder) |
| Flagged 3 | `GET /api/settings/notifications` |

**What the template does** (read from the library file): it selects a 2xx, non-error response, replaces **every request header value** with invalid values, and flags the result when an attempt still returns 2xx with a body more than 90% identical to the original and the same schema.

**What the data shows.** Each flagged result has 4 attempts. Attempts 0–2 returned **400** (102-character body, 0% match). **Attempt 3 returned 200** (50 characters for wallet-status, 83 for settings/notifications) with a **100% match** — that attempt is what tripped the template. The altered request carried 3 headers for wallet-status (`host`, `x-akto-ignore`, `authorization`) and 2 for settings/notifications (`host`, `x-akto-ignore`). Which values attempt 3 used was **not examined**.

## Why this needs a ticket

* The two routes are already known to be public: `wallet/status` is public by necessity and cannot be allowlisted ([KS-1009](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1009/security-get-apiauthwalletstatus-returns-userid-role-to-any-anonymous); Kamil, PR #802, quoted in `endpointFalsePositives.ts`: "the registry has no representation for a parameterised route"), and `GET /api/settings/notifications` keeps optional auth by ruling ([KS-719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-719/security-put-apiprivacysettings-and-apisettingsnotifications-accept), quoted in the same file from `routes/admin.ts`: "The GET above keeps optional auth so anonymous readers still get the documented defaults").
* No existing allowlist mechanism fits. `KNOWN_FALSE_POSITIVE_ENDPOINT_TESTS` admits two ruled kinds with compile-time bounds (`public-by-design` only for `REMOVE_TOKENS`; `similarity-undiscriminating` only for three templates — Kamil's [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) bound), and a LOW from an INPUT template is neither. The wallet-status URL also carries a path parameter the registry cannot express.
* The gate (`assertNoVulnerabilities`) fails on any severity. So even after [KS-1009](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1009/security-get-apiauthwalletstatus-returns-userid-role-to-any-anonymous)'s HIGH is fixed, any of these LOWs that recurs will keep the Full OWASP workflow red.

## Not established

* **Whether it is a real input-validation gap (CWE-20) or expected** for routes that never read the headers being altered. For `settings/notifications` the altered headers do not include `authorization`, so "it ignores a bad token" does not explain it.
* **Why it was not reported before.** The 2026-10-05 full runs on slots 2 and 4 listed only the nginx LOW ([KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low)). This stack's collection also carried authenticated samples for these URLs (a `feed-har` added them, 343 → 349 endpoints). Not shown to be the cause.
* Related, not claimed: [KS-1207](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1207/security-an-unknown-sk-key-on-an-optional-auth-mount-skips-the) (In Progress, Kamil) covers an unknown key on an optional-auth mount skipping the Bearer check.

## Proposed next steps (smallest first)

1. Re-run **only** this template on those three URLs with a targeted Akto `CUSTOM` run (`apiInfoKeyList`; the technique used for [KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low)) and read attempt 3's actual request: which headers, which values.
2. Classify each: by design, or a finding. Kamil's call for the platform side.
3. If by design: accept it by a **narrow** rule with the ruling quoted verbatim (the [KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low) pattern), and a control showing another endpoint or template still fails. Extending the allowlist's compile-time bound needs Kamil's ruling first. If a finding: a platform ticket for Kamil.

## Done means

1. Each of the three results has a recorded classification, with the attempt-3 evidence.
2. If by design: the Full OWASP workflow no longer fails on them, a control still fails, and Console = Akto = HTML agree on the known-FP and vulnerable counts.
3. If a finding: it is ticketed for the owner and the test keeps failing honestly.

title: start-secuura.sh --rebuild leaves ~30 untagged images per slot per rebuild (and interrupted rebuilds pin them)
description:
Raised from platform-s ([PS-1012](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1012/dep-ssd-local-systemtest-make-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox>)) rather than fixed from there, because `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` is platform-k's.

## What happens

`docker compose` names each built image `<compose project>-<service>`: `platform-k-*` for slot 1, `secuura_slot2-*` for slot 2, and so on. `start-secuura.sh --rebuild` builds every service again (the serial per-service `docker compose build` from [KS-345](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-345/start-secuurash-rebuild-hangs-on-the-full-33-service-compose-bake)). Each rebuild moves those tags to new images, and the previous image of each service is left untagged as `<none>`. That's about 30 images per slot per rebuild, some of them 0.6–2.2 GB. Nothing in the script prunes images or the build cache. A grep of `start-secuura.sh` for `prune`, `rmi` and `image rm` finds nothing.

**The worse case is an interrupted rebuild.** On 2026-10-02 the Pro had 29 `<none>` images, every one held by a container in K slot 1's project (`platform-k`) that was `Created` **but never started**: `secuura-auth`, `secuura-api-gateway`, `secuura-originate` and others. Docker won't prune an image a container uses, so those stayed until someone removed them by hand (Stuart did).

## Measured (MacBook Pro, Docker Desktop, 2026-10-07)

* `docker system df`: images 20.7 GB, of which 1.76 GB is reclaimable. The **build cache is 39.6 GB, of which 22.65 GB is reclaimable**, mostly entries last used in the previous two days by slot rebuilds.

## Suggested fix (for Kamil's judgement)

The platform-s side is doing this in [PS-1012](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1012/dep-ssd-local-systemtest-make-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox) / [Secuura/platform-s#909](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1012-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox-synced-machines-994c737d0439):

* **Label every build with its owner:** for compose, a `labels:` entry under each service's `build:` such as `com.secuura.slot-image=<project>-<service>`, or one label per project.
* **Before rebuilding,** run `docker image prune -f --filter label=…` scoped to this compose project. Without `-a`, this removes only dangling, unused images from earlier builds of this slot. It never touches another slot, platform-s, a tagged image, or an image a container still uses.
* **After an interrupted rebuild,** remove that slot's `Created`-but-never-started containers, so they stop pinning old images.
* **Don't prune the build cache automatically.** It's shared by every slot on both platforms, so pruning it makes everyone's next build cold. Documenting a manual `docker builder prune --filter until=168h -f` is enough.

title: Renovate cannot bump base-image-watch.sh EXCLUDED_BASES — Blockchain/Dev/** is in ignorePaths (split from KS-1367; needs Kamil's agreement)
description:
## BLUF

Split from [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not) at Peter's request (2026-10-07). [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not)'s branch (`feature/ks-1445-…`, shared with [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is)) makes Renovate see `systemTest/performance/config/observability.yml` `k6Image`. The remaining part needs a change to the repo's `ignorePaths`, which sits in Kamil's work-stream E ([KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490/review-e-deployment-containers-and-cicd-supply-chain)). **This ticket waits on Kamil's agreement.** He has not commented on [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not), so there is nothing of his to quote yet.

## Re-verified from source (2026-10-07, worktree at `origin/develop` 652cf5f6e)

* `renovate.json:4` has `"ignorePaths": ["Blockchain/Dev/**"]`. Renovate skips every manager, including a `customManagers` regex, under that path.
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/base-image-watch.sh` `EXCLUDED_BASES` names `grafana/k6:2.3.0` and every `observability/docker-compose.yml` image tag.
* Two tests fail when that list disagrees with the files Renovate does bump:
  * `systemTest/performance/tests/unit/config/k6ImagePinParity.test.ts` (k6)
  * `observability/test/compose-image-pins.test.mjs` (observability, added in [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is))
* So a Renovate PR is red until a person edits the list by hand. That is safe, because nothing slips through, but it is noise.
* Renovate app: `gh pr list --state all --author app/renovate` returns no PR ever. That is consistent with the app not being installed. The installation itself could not be read with the available token.

## Options for Kamil

1. Narrow `ignorePaths` so `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/base-image-watch.sh` is visible, and add a regex `customManagers` entry for its quoted `"image:tag"` lines, grouped with `k6 runtime` and `observability stack images`.
2. Leave it as a hand edit. The red parity tests are the prompt, and that is documented in `systemTest/performance/docs/quick-start.md`.

## Done when

- [ ] Kamil has chosen 1 or 2. Quote his reply verbatim here.
- [ ] If 1: the config passes `renovate-config-validator --strict`, and a dry run shows one grouped update covering all three k6 sites.

title: packages/shared: one test imports services/demo-service and needs cors, so the suite cannot pass on a member-only install
description:
**BLUF:** one test file in `packages/shared` needs another workspace member's dependency, so the package's suite cannot pass on an install that provides only `packages/shared`'s own closure. It passes on a full `npm ci` at `Blockchain/Dev`, where `cors` is hoisted from `services/*`.

**Measured** (2026-10-12, Seat F 17th; clean-room copy of develop `a31b77577` with no `node_modules`; node v24.7.0):

* `npm ci` run inside `packages/shared` is an implicit-workspace install from the root lock (npm's prefix there is `Blockchain/Dev`). A stock one has no vitest at all, so to see this I made vitest resolvable in that install (a variant lock carrying the KS-1317 vitest declaration). Then `npm test`: `Test Files  1 failed | 48 passed (49)`, `Tests  945 passed | 4 skipped (949)`.
* The one failing file is `src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts`: `Error: Cannot find package 'cors' imported from .../services/demo-service/src/app.ts` (`app.ts:14`), thrown from the file's `KS-832 ACCEPTANCE BAR` suite, whose 4 tests are then skipped.
* Control, same develop on a full `npm ci` at `Blockchain/Dev`: `node_modules/cors` present, `Test Files 48 passed (48)`, `Tests 945 passed (945)`, `tsc --noEmit -p packages/shared` rc 0. In the member-only install `node_modules/cors` is absent.
* `cors` is declared by 21 of the `services/*/package.json` files (`demo-service` among them) and not by `packages/shared`, so nothing in `packages/shared/package.json` tells a reader the suite depends on it.

**Why it matters:** the dependency is invisible and works only through hoisting, so the failure appears only when someone runs the package's tests without the full install. It is lower urgency than it looks: since the KS-1317 guard, a member-only `npm test` stops early with a message naming the full install, so this is reached only when someone supplies vitest another way.

**Suggested shapes (not prescribed):**

* Move the test to where its dependency is declared (`services/demo-service`), or to a root-level guard suite that is only run after a full install.
* Do not declare `cors` in `packages/shared`: the 25 service Dockerfiles (of the 29 that reference `packages/shared`; the other four are frontends) copy `/shared` (with its `node_modules`) from the `shared-builder` stage into the runtime image, so any new dependency there ships in every image. That is the cost that made the Spark's vitest declaration for KS-1317 the wrong shape.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts` (the boot of the demo-service app, around line 5601), `Blockchain/Dev/services/demo-service/src/app.ts` line 14.

Found while raising KS-1317. Filed unassigned in Backlog on Wednesday's instruction, 2026-10-12.

title: api-gateway: an untyped create never meets the catalogue's DOCUMENT rules (enforcement.ts:101), plus two KS-1203 follow-ups (PR #1465 gate notes)
description:
## BLUF

Three notes from the Opus QA gate on PR #1465 (KS-1203 option A, merged as `a2f575a642638d64493997d0f68747a1d1f03dc6`), left out of that PR on purpose because a change to the gated head would have voided the GO. **Note 1 matters most:** an untyped `POST /api/documents` never meets the type catalogue's `DOCUMENT` rules, so the type's own requirements are skipped for exactly the body KS-1203 is about. It is pre-existing and outside the ruled scope. The gate graded it Minor; I filed it at Medium because it is an authorization-shaped gap.

## Recommendation

One small tier-1 PR, test first:

1. **Resolve an untyped body to the default type in** `enforceDocumentTypeRules`**, not just in the connector allow-list.** `services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts:101` still resolves a body with no type to `''`, so the function returns `docType: {}` and enforces nothing. The catalogue's `DOCUMENT` entry (seeded at `routes/admin.ts:316-336`, described as "the default when a creation request names no documentType") is never applied to an untyped create: `isActive`, `creatorVerificationLevel`, `requireMFA`, `metadataSchema` and `requiresApproval` are all skipped. Use the shared `DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_TYPE` there. **Measure first** (read-only): what the stored `DOCUMENT` entry requires on each environment, because enforcing it on untyped creates can newly refuse callers who rely on the gap, the same lockout risk KS-1190 names.
2. **Behavioural cells for the two sites that are only source-pinned.** `originate/src/routes/documents.ts:584` and the gateway workflow gate (`enforcement.ts:264`) are covered only by a regex over the source text; the gate's three mutations turned only that cell red. Add a cell asserting that originate stores `DOCUMENT` for each of the eight untyped shapes. Note that after item 1 the workflow-gate site becomes reachable for an untyped body, and can finally be tested behaviourally.
3. **Tell operators about the new 403.** `MCP Deployment/troubleshooting.md:119-123` does not say that an untyped create from a restricted connector is checked as `DOCUMENT`. A connector operator who hits the new 403 has no hint.

## Detail

* **Source:** Opus gate on PR #1465, verdict `GO WITH NOTE`, no Major. Verdict file sha256/16 `8d8a2c2d745d81c5` (Wednesday's `reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1465/verdict.md`).
* **What PR #1465 did and did not claim:** it made the allow-list apply to the resolved default type. It did not claim the catalogue rules apply, and its comment "the check and the stored type cannot drift apart again" is true for the allow-list only.
* **Related:** KS-1203 (the parent; stays In Progress until deployed), KS-1190 (a different gap in the same enforcement code: an unknown required level fails open).

title: The developer portal page documents POST /api/verification/verify-batch, which no service and no spec implements (CSRF carries exclusions for it)
description:
## BLUF

`services/api-gateway/src/docs/developer-portal.html:294` lists `POST /api/verification/verify-batch` ("Verify mul\[tiple documents\]") as a public endpoint. **Nothing serves it.** The OpenAPI spec (310 paths) declares `verify` and `verify-file` for the unversioned and v2 families but no `verify-batch`; no router in `services/originate` or any other service registers `/verify-batch` under verification (the only `verify-batch` code is the separate MCP server's own root-level `/verify-batch` in `services/mcp-server`). So a developer who follows the portal gets a 404, and `csrf.ts` carries CSRF exclusions for `/api/verification/verify-batch` and `/api/v2/verification/verify-batch` that cover a route nothing implements.

## Recommendation

Owner decision, then one of: (a) implement the route and add it to the spec, so the page and the exclusions are true; (b) remove the row from the portal, and drop both CSRF entries in the same change (a dead exclusion is a latent hole: a future route at that name would be silently CSRF-exempt). Priority Low. Until then the two CSRF entries are PINNED by cells (KS-1469) so they cannot vanish or change unnoticed; that pin is deliberately not a statement that the route exists.

## Detail

* Found while resolving the m1 note from the Opus gate on PR #1466 (the `/api/v2/verification/verify-batch` exclusion was pinned by no cell). Evidence, from a repo-wide search at develop `b4a245fba1ca`: spec path scan (310 paths, none `verify-batch`); `git grep` for verify-batch in non-test code finds only the portal row, the two `csrf.ts` entries, and the MCP server; a control with the same grep shape finds the real `/verify` and `/verify-file` routes.
* Other rows on that page were NOT checked against the code.
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, literal title and description): `developer-portal`, `developer portal`, `verify-batch`: no ticket about this page's rows.

Related: KS-1469, KS-1461, KS-1165.

title: No gate executes the DB-backed integration suites: the default test run ignores them and CI is retired
description:
## BLUF

**No gate executes the DB-backed integration suites.** Five `*.integration.test.ts` files exist at develop `65d7722f83a6` (originate: `ks597-issuer-organization-id`, `ks597-b-caller-org-externalref`, `ks1263-multi-write-rolls-back`, `rightsHolders.tenant-scope`; auth: `auth.integration.test.ts`). Each is red-proved, and none runs unless someone types `npm run test:integration` against a Postgres. The cells that pin RLS attribution and multi-write atomicity therefore protect nothing automatically.

## Recommendation

Add one opt-in-but-loud step to the author's final check: run each service's `test:integration` against a throwaway Postgres built the repo's documented way, and list it in `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` under the manual CI-gate equivalents. It must print a visible SKIP line with the reason when no database is reachable, never a silent pass. A faithful local recipe that needs no Docker is in `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-2nd/RECIPE-faithful-local-postgres.md` (init SQL, then all main-DB migrations, then the `secuura_app` role).

## Detail

* **Why none runs:** `services/originate/jest.config.js:8` ignores `\.integration\.test\.ts$` by pattern ("the default run stays unit-only + mock-DB"); the pre-push preflight runs each workspace's `test` script, which is that default run; GitHub Actions is retired for this repo; `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` §Manual CI-gate equivalents does not list the integration config. `grep` for `test:integration` finds it only in `services/originate/package.json`, the jest configs and `docs/TESTING.md`.
* **Found while:** verifying KS-980 and KS-1306 (the RLS integration suite), where the merge comment already said the config "still runs only on demand".
* **Not in scope:** KS-1307 (a PR body that quoted a subset as a full run) is about reporting, not about whether the suites run at all.
