*Filed by Seat J 9th on Wednesday's instruction. Not fixed here.*

title: Cockpit: statusline.sh:85 does shell arithmetic on rate_limits.seven_day.resets_at, so an ISO-8601 value kills the whole statusline — the lane-V pane renders none and ctx% is unreadable from inside a session
description:
Filed on Wednesday's instruction of 2026-10-13 11:39:04Z, after Seat V 9th could not satisfy a context-based wrap threshold because its pane shows no statusline. **This is a root cause with a one-line fix, not just a symptom report.** The file is at the workspace root (`Setup and System/statusline.sh`), outside any project folder, so this seat read it and did not edit it.

## The defect

`Setup and System/statusline.sh:85`

```sh
week_resets=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.rate_limits.seven_day.resets_at // empty')   # :79
...
secs_left=$((week_resets - now_ts))                                                       # :85
```

`:85` performs **shell arithmetic directly on** `resets_at`, which assumes the field is epoch-seconds. When Claude Code supplies it as an **ISO-8601 string**, the arithmetic aborts:

```
/Volumes/DevMASTER/Setup and System/statusline.sh: line 85: 2026-10-17T00: value too great for base (error token is "17T00")
```

The script then exits **rc 1 having printed nothing**, so Claude Code has no statusline to render — and `ctx:NN%`, computed 30 lines earlier at `:54`, is lost with it.

## Truth table, measured by piping synthetic JSON to the real script

| `rate_limits.seven_day.resets_at` | rc | rendered |
| -- | -- | -- |
| ISO string `2026-10-17T00:00:00Z` | **1** | **nothing** |
| epoch integer | 0 | `[Secuura/Blockchain] Opus 5 \| Ultrathink \| ctx:37% \| 7d:89% renews:3d 11h \| azure:-` |
| field absent | 0 | `… ctx:37% \| 7d:89% \| azure:-` |
| `rate_limits` absent entirely | 0 | `… ctx:37% \| azure:-` |

So three of four shapes are fine and exactly one kills it. **The same ISO input against the global fallback** `~/.claude/statusline-command.sh` **returns rc 0** and renders `Opus 5 | ctx:200k used:37% | 7d:89%`, so the defect is specific to the project script.

## The observable effect, measured across panes

`tmux capture-pane -p -t <pane> -S -` and a count of lines matching `ctx:[0-9-]`:

| pane | cockpit name | `ctx:` lines | last value |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `%0` | wednesday | 1 | `ctx:74%` |
| `%83` | Secuura/Blockchain-K | 1 | `ctx:26%` |
| `%84` | Secuura/Blockchain-J | 1 | `ctx:21%` |
| `%82` | **Secuura/Blockchain-V** | **0** | **none** |
| `%1` | fleet-monitor | 0 | none (not a session pane) |

Three session panes render a figure and lane V's renders none, so the instrument discriminates. Wednesday read K at 23% and J at 16% about ten minutes earlier and this seat read 26% and 21%, so those are live values rather than stale screen text. **Which shape of** `resets_at` **a given pane receives is what decides it; that is not established here, and the fix makes it moot.**

## Why it matters beyond one cosmetic row

`ctx:NN%` is the **only** instrument for the context window. A seat whose statusline dies has no way to read it:

* both statusline scripts take the JSON on **stdin** and persist nothing (`statusline.sh:54` and `statusline-command.sh:7` both read `.context_window.used_percentage`; the only cache in the project script is `/tmp/.claude_azure_user_cache`, for `az account show`);
* the rendered line is not in the pane's scrollback — zero `ctx` hits over the full history;
* nothing under `~/.claude` holds it.

A seat in that state either guesses or substitutes a different number. This one substituted the **session token budget** ("\~2.6% of 15M remaining") for the context window, which is a different quantity entirely, and Wednesday had to correct it. Her words: *"A seat once read the budget as 3% and died at 100% of its window hours later."* So a dead statusline row removes the guard against a seat dying mid-merge.

## Fix

Convert before subtracting, and never let this block the render. Both halves matter:

1. Parse `resets_at` as a date when it is not numeric — e.g. `date -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$week_resets" +%s` on macOS — or skip the countdown when it does not parse.
2. **Guard the arithmetic** so a future field-shape change degrades the countdown rather than deleting the statusline: test `case $week_resets in (*[!0-9]*) ... esac` before `$(( ))`, and have the script emit its base line regardless. A statusline is a diagnostic; it must not be the thing that fails silently.

A self-test with the four rows of the truth table above would have caught this.

## Proposed and NOT done

A project-local `statusLine` wrapper in `.claude/settings.local.json` that tees stdin to a file, making `ctx%` readable from inside a session. **Wednesday ruled against it for now** (11:39:04Z): that file is shared by every seat in the project folder, and J 10th and K 10th were live in it at 89% weekly usage. It is recorded here as the option, not as a pending action. Fixing `:85` is the smaller and better change and needs no shared-settings edit.

## Priority

Filed **Medium** as instructed. An argument for higher exists and is recorded rather than acted on: the failure is silent, it disables the only context instrument, and it is latent for every seat whose harness sends an ISO `resets_at`. That call is not this seat's.

## Provenance

* Measured by Seat V 9th, 2026-10-13, pane `Secuura/Blockchain-V` `%82`. Everything above is a reading, not a quotation, except Wednesday's sentence about the earlier seat, which is quoted as hers.
* Deduped before filing: 327 distinct issues over 5 search terms with comments and archived included; 0 near hits. `statusline.sh`, `resets_at`, `value too great for base` and `context_window.used_percentage` each → 0. Fresh-nonce negative control `v9c-f4d2b8ff74cb` → 0; positive control `cockpit` → 2 (KS-939, KS-907).

title: Akto suppressions and exclusions: one cites the wrong ticket (KS-442 → KS-510), and two coverage trade-offs (VOLATILE_PATH_RE, 8 built-in data-exposure templates) have no ruling or owner
description:
**BLUF:** the [KS-1478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1478/akto-image-2371-2383-release-v2383-2026-10-13-testing-image-has-no) audit of every rule that stops an Akto result from counting checked each one against the ticket it cites. Most stand and are no wider than their ruling: [KS-308](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-308/akto-scans-report-100percent-skipped-tests-testing-container-cant), [KS-323](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-323/akto-after-ks-314-drive-connectivity-skip-bucket-to-0-confirm-mongo)/324, [KS-397](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-397/are-apidocument-types-and-apioauthscopes-intentionally-public-or)/364, [KS-719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-719/security-put-apiprivacysettings-and-apisettingsnotifications-accept), [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) (narrower than the ruling), [KS-1397](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1397/the-gateway-answers-every-request-with-server-nginx-aktos-unwanted)/1421 (narrower, fails closed, **seen firing live on 2026-10-14** on `POST /api/certifications/issue`), [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709/akto-reports-a-pass-for-a-test-that-executed-nothing-clean-0-not), [KS-417](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-417/akto-spec-consistency-guard-for-the-endpoint-scoped-known-fp-allowlist)/425/524 and [KS-1416](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1416/akto-the-three-code-injection-sqli-scans-run-0-sqlnosql-templates-akto). **Three do not.** The citation fix was made and then **backed out at Peter's instruction (update the app only, log issues)**. Re-verified against `develop` 3c0a52221 on 2026-10-14.

## 1. Wrong citation: `/api/identity-credentials/types`

`systemTest/akto/src/core/endpointFalsePositives.ts:148` (and the docblock at `:117-119`) suppresses `REMOVE_TOKENS` on this endpoint, citing [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424). [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424)'s ruling (Kam, 2026-07-11) covers **only the five verify operations** and says *"reference reads stay protected"*. The ticket that actually registered this endpoint as public by design is [KS-510](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-510/akto-register-get-apiidentity-credentialstypes-as-by-design-public) (Done, 2026-07-23), resting on the spec's `security: []`. The test comment `tests/unit/core/endpointFalsePositives.test.ts:34` carries the same citation.

## 2. `VOLATILE_PATH_RE` drops whole paths from HAR replay with no ruling

`src/setup/harSpec.ts:26`: `/\/(analytics|dashboard|realtime|metrics)\b/i` means those endpoints get **no real HAR sample**, so authz templates skip them for **every** template, not just the similarity ones ([KS-357](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-357/akto-drive-authz-precondition-skips-0-complete-attacker-role-auth)). Today's feed excluded **19** volatile endpoints of 141 GET endpoints. Kamil's [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) analysis (2026-08-28) warns that this exact mechanism *"removes the audit log from the scan"* and that the `analytics` paths *"already make"* that trade, *"worth asking whether they should be making it either"*. No ticket reviews it, and its scope is wider than any ruling.

## 3. 8 Akto built-in data-exposure templates are loaded but never selected

`tests/aktoSetup.test.ts:329-338` (`KNOWN_CATALOG_DRIFT.loadedNotInCatalog`): `SENSITIVE_DATA_EXPOSURE_{ADDRESS,CREDIT_CARD,EMAIL,IP_ADDRESS,JWT,PHONE_NUMBER,SSN,VIN}`. Its own comment calls this *"a REAL, previously-unrecorded coverage observation … a coverage decision … deliberately not folded into* [KS-717](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-717/akto-test-id-catalog-and-the-loaded-template-library-drift-silently)*'s drift fix"*. Today on 2.38.2 the library is again 208 = 199 bundled + 9 built-ins, so it is unchanged. No ticket owns the decision.

## Also stale

`endpointFalsePositives.ts:206` quotes `routes/admin.ts:1437`; the quoted code is now at `:1487` / `:1523`. Staleness detection for similarity entries is already [KS-761](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-761/similarity-undiscriminating-fp-entries-have-no-staleness-detection-a), so it is not duplicated here.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The `/api/identity-credentials/types` entry and its test cite [KS-510](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-510/akto-register-get-apiidentity-credentialstypes-as-by-design-public) (with "spec `security: []`, no Kam ruling"), not [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424). **A test demonstrates it:** a unit test that every `public-by-design` entry's cited ticket is one whose text names that endpoint (or a recorded reason), red on the [KS-442](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-442/make-the-verify-family-public-5-ops-gateway-relax-spec-security-ks-424) citation.
2. `VOLATILE_PATH_RE`: a recorded decision (Kamil's input sought, per the [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) discussion): narrow it, scope it to the similarity templates as [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) Option B did for the tolerance, or accept it with a reason. Report the number of endpoints it excludes in the run's coverage section so the trade is visible.
3. The 8 data-exposure templates: enable them (and measure the tier-budget cost and any false positives on a platform that legitimately returns emails and addresses), or record why not, with the decision recorded where the catalog selection lives.
4. The stale `admin.ts:1437` pointer is corrected or replaced by a symbol reference.

title: package_format_gate.test.sh: five REAL-npm cells INTERMITTENT - red once in the full shell run (430/5), green twice run alone (435/0, develop and a branch)
description:
## BLUF

Five `REAL npm` cells in `systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate.test.sh` went **red once** inside a full `npm run test:shell` run (**430 passed / 5 failed**), then **passed in both of two direct runs** (**435 passed / 0 failed**), one on develop and one on a branch. So the defect, if there is one, is **intermittent**, not "on develop". No harm today: these cells fail closed (a red refuses a push, it never lets one through). They are filed rather than dismissed because one red in three runs is not "flaky, proven", and a cell that reds without a code change will be read as a regression by whoever hits it next.

Filed by Seat R 45th (raise lane), 2026-10-15, on Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER 02:31:25Z, Q2 (ii)).

## The three runs

All three ran in one clone of `Secuura/Distributed_Secuura` on the same machine, with the same `node_modules` (`npm ci` rc 0, 1937 packages). Run 1 left `TMPDIR` to the runner's own handling; runs 2 and 3 set a short `TMPDIR=/tmp/r45ab` and unset git's local env.

| run | tree | how | package_format_gate |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | branch `762d044b0` (KS-1547: a one-line `preflight.sh` change; this suite does not read `preflight.sh`) | inside `npm run test:shell`, all 89 suites back to back, 02:15–02:24Z | **430 passed, 5 failed** |
| 2 | same branch, `762d044b0` | `bash systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate.test.sh` alone, 02:25Z | **435 passed, 0 failed** |
| 3 | develop `e67e0dc1916b954a53c40db68ea81f0f905de641` | same, alone, 02:27Z | **435 passed, 0 failed** |

So the five did not reproduce on either tree when the suite ran on its own.

## The five cells, verbatim from run 1

```
FAIL REAL npm with a hanging postinstall: REFUSED as a timeout
       want "1/1", got "0/0"
FAIL ...no node_modules in the package, no stage
       want "no/0", got "yes/0"
FAIL ...so the listener was contacted and the script ran (the earlier 0 was the gate, not the fixture)
       want "1/yes", got "1/no"
FAIL the install's npm userconfig is the stage's private HOME, not the developer's ~/.npmrc
       want "1/0", got "0/0"
FAIL ...while it does see what npm and the shell need (PATH, npm_lifecycle_event, npm_config_cache)
       want "yes/yes/yes", got "no/no/no"
```

All five read `ok` in runs 2 and 3.

## What is and is not established

* **Established:** the five reds are not caused by the KS-1547 change. Runs 2 and 3 give the same result on its branch and on develop.
* **Not established:** the cause. Three readings fit, and I have not separated them:
  1. **Load or timing.** Every one of the five spawns a real `npm` and reads a timeout, a listener, or the staged env. Run 1 ran it as suite 60-something of 89 back to back, and the J-lane seat was live on the same machine.
  2. **Interference between suites.** Something an earlier suite leaves behind in run 1, such as a lingering listener, a port, an npm cache entry, or a leaked env var, could make the later suite misread.
  3. **The KS-1396 change.** KS-1396 (merged into develop as `e67e0dc1`) moved `systemTest` to TypeScript 7.0.2 and oxlint and removed ESLint there. It is the most recent change to this tree. **Named as a candidate only, not measured.** Runs 2 and 3 were on trees that already contain it and were green, so it is not enough on its own.

## What would settle it

Run the full `npm run test:shell` N times (N ≥ 5) on an idle machine and count the five cells. Then run `package_format_gate.test.sh` alone N times under a synthetic CPU load. If it reds only in the full run, the cause is interference between suites. If it reds alone under load, it is timing, and the fix is the cell's timeout margin.

## Related, not duplicates (searched first)

The search covered title and description, archived issues included, and was controlled: a fresh nonce returned 0 hits and `preflight_test_types_ratchet_leg` returned 3. `systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate`, `hanging postinstall`, `REFUSED as a timeout`, `npm userconfig is the stage`, `npm_lifecycle_event`, `listener was contacted`, `no node_modules in the package` and `REAL npm` all returned **0**. `package_format_gate` returned **KS-1063** (Done, a different defect: a gate that examined nothing exits 0). `FORMAT_GATE_INSTALL` returned **KS-1583** (Backlog, the KS-998 item 1 gate's six Minors, a different defect).

title: Declared Node floor (engines.node >=18.0.0 in 5 packages) contradicts what the repo needs (22.13+) and runs on (24) - decide the floor
description:
## BLUF

**The repo declares a Node floor it cannot run on.** Five `package.json` files declare `engines.node >=18.0.0`, but a shell suite on the push path already requires **Node 22.13+**, every Docker image builds on **Node 24**, and the preflight assumes a **Node 24** host. Nothing breaks today — the real runtimes are all 24 — but the declared floor tells a developer Node 18 or 20 is fine, and on either one that suite stops with a FATAL. **This ticket records the measurements and asks for a decision. It is deliberately NOT a fix:** the floor is a choice, not a defect with one right answer.

Filed by Seat R 48th on Wednesday's instruction (ANSWER of 2026-10-18T15:24:54Z), after it surfaced while raising PR #1580 (KS-1624 F1). All measurements at `develop` `6184eaa0af75c1e27eb69bbff67a7790ef494b5f`.

## Measurement 1 — what the repo DECLARES

A census of all **50** tracked `package.json` files:

| `engines.node` | files |
| -- | -- |
| `>=18.0.0` | `Blockchain/Dev/package.json`, `connectors/whatsapp-bot`, `services/mcp-server`, `services/tenant-provisioning`, `services/tokenisation` (**5**) |
| `>=24.11.0` | `systemTest/akto`, `systemTest/oxlint`, `systemTest/performance`, `systemTest/playwright` (**4**) |
| none | **41** |

There is **no** `.nvmrc`, `.node-version` or `.tool-versions` anywhere in the tree (0 files). So the only machine-readable statement of the platform's floor is `>=18.0.0` — and the repo's own test tooling already contradicts it with `>=24.11.0`.

## Measurement 2 — what the repo actually NEEDS

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks812_whatsapp_bot_default_api_target.test.sh` strips TypeScript types with `module.stripTypeScriptTypes`, available from **Node 22.13**. It says so in its header (line 24) and is guarded: the helper is at line 25, its first call at **line 40**, and on an older Node it exits **2** at **line 44** with `FATAL: this suite needs node 22.13+ (module.stripTypeScriptTypes)`. It runs in the full shell-suite runner. By grep it is the only script under `Blockchain/Dev/scripts`, `systemTest` or `.githooks` needing a Node newer than 18 — so 22.13 is the measured real minimum *for the tooling*, and it is above the declared floor.

## Measurement 3 — what the repo actually RUNS ON

* **Docker:** all **13** `FROM node:` lines in the tree are `node:24-alpine`. Every shipped service builds and runs on 24.
* **Preflight:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/lockfile-cleanroom.sh:49` and `:58` assume a host Node **>=24** on the CI path ("Host node >=24 lets us skip docker", "CI always runs node>=24 (host path)").
* KS-355 (Done) moved CI to Node 24.

## The decision this needs (options, not a recommendation)

1. **Raise the five floors to** `>=24` — matches every runtime and the systemTest packages; Node 18 and 20 are past end-of-life. This is the value KS-1398 already suggests (see below).
2. **Raise them to** `>=22.13` — the measured minimum for the tooling, the least restrictive honest value; leaves a gap between declared and shipped runtimes.
3. **Add a pin file** (`.nvmrc` / `.node-version`) as well as or instead of (1)/(2), so local tooling picks the right version automatically.
4. **Leave** `>=18.0.0` and accept that a developer on 18/20 gets a FATAL from one suite.

Whichever is chosen, `ks812`'s guard can stay as it is — it already fails loudly and names the version.

## Related, and why this is a separate ticket

**KS-1398** (Backlog) carries the same value as one row of a TypeScript 7 migration *suggestion*: `engines.node | >=18.0.0 ×5 | >=24 (Node 18 and 20 are past EOL)`. That row is the same field and the same direction as option 1. It is split out here because the floor is a decision that stands on its own today — it is a live contradiction on the push path, and it should not wait on whether a TypeScript 7 move is ever approved. If the TS 7 work goes ahead and settles the floor, this ticket closes with it.

## How this was searched before filing (dedupe)

Over **1,613** issues including archived, by symbol: `engines` (6 hits), `>=18` / `Node 18` (1: KS-1398), `stripTypeScriptTypes` / `strip-types` / `NO-STRIP-TYPES` (1: KS-355), `22.13` (0), `node:24` / `24.11` (39, broad), `nvmrc` / `node-version` / `tool-versions` (1: KS-355), `Node floor` / `Node version` / `engines.node` (5: KS-1427, KS-1398, KS-1102, KS-464, KS-355). Controls: `preflight` 169 hits, a nonsense token 0. Read KS-1398, KS-355, KS-1427, KS-1102 and KS-464: only KS-1398 records the declared floor, as noted above.

title: anchor_store.created_at is bound from the anchoring PROCESS's clock, not the database's — move it to a DB-side default (prerequisite for the #1568 gate's option (i))
description:
**Filed on Wednesday's instruction (2026-10-18T20:14:35Z), which ruled this OUT of #1568 round 3 and into its own ticket. Measured at develop** `83ed01af70fd5ed6cca9ac66f28ddcb8a1034105`**.**

## What

`anchor_store.created_at` has a DB default of `NOW()` (`migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:725`), but the main upsert **binds it explicitly** as parameter `$21` from `anchor.createdAt`, a `new Date()` taken in the anchoring service's own process (`Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1372`, the `INSERT INTO anchor_store … VALUES ($1…$22)`).

`documents.created_at` by contrast is the **database's** `NOW()` (`services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts`, the `INSERT INTO documents (… created_at, updated_at) VALUES (… NOW(), NOW())`).

So the two timestamps most likely to be compared with each other come from **two different clocks**.

## Why it matters

1. **It is the prerequisite for the #1568 gate's option (i)** — "the guard refuses when the stored anchor predates the claiming document". That rule is a direct comparison of these two columns, so under any skew it refuses legitimate updates. Round 3 deliberately avoided the comparison (migration 051 is an existence test at insert time, no clock), which is why this is not blocking — but option (i) cannot be made sound without this.
2. **Migration 051's one-off apply-time census does use the order**, and so inherits the caveat. A skew-induced false positive there costs a human one look at a listed row (the census is read-only and human-resolved), never a refused legitimate write — stated as narrowing in 051's header and in #1568's PR.
3. Any future reporting that orders anchors against documents has the same exposure.

## Scope

Stop binding `$21` and let the column's own `DEFAULT NOW()` apply (or capture `now()` inside the same statement). Roughly one line in the upsert plus its parameter list, and a cell asserting a freshly inserted `anchor_store` row's `created_at` comes from the server (e.g. it sits between two `now()` readings taken around the insert, and is unaffected by a skewed value supplied by the caller).

## Measured, and not

**Measured:** the `$21` binding and the `documents` `NOW()`, both read at the SHA above. **Not measured:** actual skew on any deployment. On compose the containers share the host kernel clock, so skew is expected to be \~0 (J 12th's reading); across hosts — the Container Apps shape — nothing guarantees it.

*Seat J 13th. Related: KS-1612, KS-1603, KS-1384.*

title: tests/e2e callers of the retired POST /api/documents/:id/verify: rewrite against /api/verification/verify once the e2e package can run (KS-1628, KS-734)
description:
**KS-1628 retires** `POST /api/documents/:id/verify`**. These** `tests/e2e` **callers of that route will fail against a stack that has the change, and none of them was run** — `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e` is a separate Playwright package that needs a live stack, which no preflight leg provides (KS-734 is the ticket for making it runnable). Wednesday ruled (b) on KS-1628 PR 2: leave them, name them, and file this ticket, because an unrun rewrite of assertions is a guess presented as a fix.

## The callers (at develop `83ed01af70fd`)

**Will fail when run:**

* `tests/e2e/tests/integration/full-certification-flow.api.spec.ts:62` — POSTs `requestedFields` / `purpose` / `legalBasis` to the retired route and asserts `result.verified`, `result.issuer.verified` and `result.blockchain.anchored`. Those are the retired gateway handler's response shape: the successor `POST /api/verification/verify` answers `checks.isAnchored`, and its `blockchain.anchored` is usually absent.
* `tests/e2e/tests/recruitment/alternative-paths.spec.ts:54, :134, :198` and `tests/e2e/tests/recruitment/fixtures/recruitment-helpers.ts:82` — call it through the endpoint map `API_ENDPOINTS.documents.verify(...)`, defined at `tests/e2e/tests/recruitment/fixtures/recruitment-data.ts:254` (and the twin map at `tests/e2e/tests/fixtures/test-data.ts:82`).

**Degrade cleanly, no action needed:** `tests/e2e/tests/holder-exhaustive.prelaunch.spec.ts:278` and `tests/e2e/tests/verifier-exhaustive.prelaunch.spec.ts:292` try the old route inside a fallback chain and move on at status ≥ 400.

## What "done" looks like

Once the e2e package can run (KS-734): rewrite each "will fail" caller against `POST /api/verification/verify` (`{ documentId }` or a content hash in the body), assert the successor's own shape (`verified`, `checks.isAnchored`, the honest `blockchain` blob), point the two endpoint maps at it or drop their `verify` key, and **run them**.

## After KS-1628, what the old path answers

The request meets the auth-gated `/api/documents` proxy mount: **401** unauthenticated (before any route is looked up), **originate's 404** when authenticated with a documents scope.

## Dedupe

`description: contains` over all issues: `API_ENDPOINTS.documents.verify` 0, `recruitment-helpers` 0, `full-certification-flow` 0, `holder-exhaustive` 0, `tests/e2e/tests/fixtures/test-data` 0, `alternative-paths.spec` 2 (KS-1010, a CIP-30 check that passes on a 404 — a different defect; KS-734, the runnable-e2e ticket this one depends on). Control: a nonsense literal returns 0.

Filed by Seat R 49th from KS-1628 PR 2. Not built.

title: verifierVerificationLevel is still seeded, stored, served and admin-editable but enforced nowhere after KS-1628
description:
**After KS-1628, a document type's** `verifierVerificationLevel` **is still seeded, stored, served and admin-editable, but enforced nowhere.** Wednesday ruled (a) on KS-1628 PR 2: retire the gate with the route, and file this ticket. **The options below are for the owner to choose between; this ticket does not choose.**

## What happened

The only place the per-type verifier level was enforced was api-gateway's own handler for `POST /api/documents/:id/verify` (`routes/verification.ts`, the level check at develop `:596-608`): it read the document type's `verifierVerificationLevel` and refused a caller below it with 403 `INSUFFICIENT_VERIFICATION_LEVEL` (pinned by `ks1176` section E). KS-1628 retires that route.

**Still present, measured at develop** `83ed01af70fd`**:**

* seeded: `api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts`, nine document types each carry a `verifierVerificationLevel`;
* stored and edited: originate `routes/adminConfig.ts:202`, `:234`, `:1768`;
* served: api-gateway `routes/platform.ts:895` and the document-types route (`routes/verification.ts`).

**Enforced:** nowhere. `meetsVerificationLevel` survives in `services/enforcement.ts:153`, but that is the CREATOR level on document create. The successor `POST /api/verification/verify` is public by design (KS-442).

**Real effect today:** none — the one enforcement point had 0 calls at the edge on kintsugi (\~30 days) and demo (\~38 days), measured read-only 2026-10-19. The risk is a **misleading control**: an administrator who sets a verifier level will reasonably believe it restricts who can verify a document of that type.

## Options for the owner

1. **Remove the setting** — drop `verifierVerificationLevel` from the type catalogue, the admin UI and the stores.
2. **Label it inert** in the admin UI ("not enforced since KS-1628") and leave the data.
3. **Re-introduce a verifier-level gate on a non-public verify route** (the public successor is public by design, so a gate there would contradict KS-442).

## Related

* **KS-1190** ("meetsVerificationLevel fails open on an unknown REQUIRED level") has two halves. Its **verify** half cites `routes/verification.ts:554-557`, which KS-1628 removes, so that half no longer applies; its **create** half (`POST /api/documents`) is unaffected.
* `VerificationRouteDeps.meetsVerificationLevel` is now unused by the routes and kept only so existing test doubles still type-check (comment in place; removable together with whichever option is chosen).

## Dedupe

`description: contains` over all issues: `verifierVerificationLevel` 1 (KS-1190), `verifier_verification_level` 1 (KS-1190), `meetsVerificationLevel` 3 (KS-1628, KS-1190, KS-1176), `verifier level` 0. None records the setting as inert. Control: a nonsense literal returns 0.

Filed by Seat R 49th from KS-1628 PR 2. Not built.

title: Chain-first verify blobs hard-code `anchored: true` and drop anchoring's status/acknowledged, so a 'submitting' or failed anchor reads isAnchored: true (v1 + v2)
description:
## BLUF

**The chain-first verify branches build their blockchain blob with** `anchored: true` **hard-coded and no** `status`**, which makes the honest-anchor guard** `settled` **BY CONSTRUCTION.** An anchoring reply that is still in flight or has failed — `status: 'submitting'`, `acknowledged: false`, the KS-726 class — is therefore presented as `isAnchored: true`, in both the v1 and the v2 verify routes.

The code says so itself. `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:130-132`:

> *"KS-1628: a failed anchor is not an anchor, whatever else the blob says. The chain-first blobs carry* `anchored: true` *and no status, so they are unaffected; a stored blob that pairs* `anchored: true` *with a failed status was on-chain before this line."*

That comment reads as a reassurance. It is in fact the statement of the defect: *unaffected by the failed-status guard* is exactly the problem, because the guard is the thing that would have caught this.

Gate O1's Minor 2 on the twelve-PR batch, 2026-10-19T01:00:25Z. Pre-existing; not in those merges.

## The mechanism, measured

`isAnchoredHonestly` (`verification.ts:120`) decides the claim:

```ts
if (FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES.has(String(c.status))) return false;   // :133
const settled = c.anchored === true || c.status === 'confirmed';  // :141
```

* A **real stored** anchor row has no `anchored` boolean at all — the comment at `:136-139` says so: *"anchoring's vocabulary is pending | submitted | confirmed | failed … and there is NO* `anchored` *boolean on a real row."* For those rows only `status === 'confirmed'` earns the claim, and `'submitted'` deliberately does not, because *"the tx is in flight and may still fail — the KS-535 class."*
* A **chain-first** blob is built by hand with `anchored: true` and **no** `status` **key**. So `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES.has(String(undefined))` is false — the failed guard cannot fire — and `settled` is true on the first disjunct, whatever anchoring actually reported.

**The four construction sites:**

| route | site |
| -- | -- |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:717` |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:1237` |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:1259` |
| **v2** | `services/originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts:233`, inside `chainOnlyMatch` |

The `status` argument the call sites pass does not rescue it: `verification.ts:758`, `:1297` and `verificationV2.ts:271` pass the **literal** `'anchored'`, and in any case the second argument is only consulted when there is no chain blob at all (`:149`).

**What bounds the severity.** `settled` is necessary but not sufficient: the claim also needs `typeof c.txHash === 'string'`, `REAL_TXHASH_RE` (64 hex) and `heightOk`. So the hash must already look like a real one, and it comes from the chain index. The defect is that **in-flight and failed anchors the index knows about still read as anchored** — not that an arbitrary blob does.

## Why High

On a document-authenticity platform, `isAnchored: true` is the product's central claim to a verifier. Presenting a `'submitting'` or failed anchor as anchored is the same family as KS-535 (a failed on-chain anchor reporting `status: anchored`) and KS-1634 (a simulated anchor returned unlabelled), and KS-1634 is High. The failure direction is always *over*-claiming, never under-claiming.

**Honest limit on this rating: I did not run a census.** I have not measured how many rows can reach these branches with a non-confirmed status today. The nearest evidence is KS-1634's census — 0 qualifying rows on both boxes at 2026-10-18, with kintsugi's 0 noted as contingent on one document row — and that census was for a different precondition. **A census is the first step on this ticket, and the rating should be revisited against it.**

## Recommendation

1. Carry anchoring's own fields into the chain-first blob instead of asserting the conclusion: pass `status` and `acknowledged` through, and let `isAnchoredHonestly` apply the same rules it applies to a stored row. Dropping `anchored: true` entirely is the cleaner shape, since no real row carries it — but `ks563` pins the current chain-first shape, so that is a deliberate change with a test to re-cut, not a one-liner.
2. A cell per site: a chain-first match whose anchoring status is `'submitting'` (and one that is `'failed'`) must read `isAnchored: false`. A mutant restoring the hard-coded `anchored: true` must red each of them.
3. Fold the **v2** site in with KS-1634's v2 work — it is the same four lines of construction, and splitting them across two tickets invites one to be done and the other forgotten.

## Dedupe

Over all **1,627** Secuura-PK issues including archived: `chainOnlyMatch` **→ 0 hits.** `anchored: true` → 4, each a different subject (KS-1634 the simulated-label defect, KS-1628 the route retirement, KS-834 a decision on verify auth, KS-535 the document-status variant, Done). `acknowledged` → 6, none about this presenter. `isAnchored` → 9; the nearest, KS-1637, is gate N1's residue about the removal pin reading only the router — a different mechanism, read and confirmed distinct. Positive controls on the same corpus: `verification` 360, `anchor` 313. Zero control: a nonsense token reads 0.

**Related:** KS-1634 (the same presenter, the `simulated` signal, and the v2 site it shares), KS-726 (the `status: 'submitting'` / `acknowledged: false` reply class this mis-presents; Done), KS-535 (the document-status variant; Done), KS-563 (which pins the current chain-first shape, so its cells are in scope for any change here).

---

*Filed by Seat R 51st on Wednesday's instruction of 2026-10-19T01:00:25Z, citing gate O1's verdict section "Minor 2". The Linear actor field is shared across the fleet, so authorship is this line, not the actor. Everything above the "Why High" section I verified in the source at develop* `37834600a543cb0276f427d969ac034d9df74fbd`*; the severity and the census limit are my own call, stated as such. Not fixed in these merges.*

title: KS-1385 (b) follow-up: a non-object INCOMING secuura still raises, and dbPersistAnchor's own row handling is pinned only by source
description:
**Refs KS-1385.** These are the two Info items gate U1 (Opus, tier 1) raised on #1607 round 2 (head `243d324d4dd7`), filed on Wednesday's GO of 2026-10-19T04:49:21Z. **Low:** neither is reachable through any route today. The code is `services/anchoring/src/index.ts` (`dbPersistAnchor`, the `anchor_store` upsert) and `services/anchoring/src/anchorOverwriteGuard.ts` (`classifyPersistOutcome`).

## INF-1: an INCOMING `secuura` that is not an object still raises

* Round 2 guarded every read of the **stored** payload with `jsonb_typeof`. The **incoming** side is still read without a guard:

* **Not reachable today:** both payload builders (`buildFlatAnchorMetadataPayload` for single anchors, and the batch builder) always produce an object `secuura`.
* **Suggested shape:** guard the incoming reads the same way, or assert the builder's output shape at the call site; add cells that feed a non-object incoming `secuura` through the real statement.

## INF-2: `dbPersistAnchor`'s own handling of the returned row is pinned only by source text

* The cells run the product's real statement, and `classifyPersistOutcome` on the real returned row. `dbPersistAnchor` **itself is not driven by any committed cell:** `index.ts` listens at import.
* W4 pins three lines, the `classifyPersistOutcome(overwrite, row, anchor.documentId)` call and the two `outcome === …` branches, but not how `row` is derived. U1 showed that a mutant corrupting the row at the call site survives the committed suite; only the gate's booted cell caught it.

title: A fresh clone has no pre-push gate: core.hooksPath is unset, so the 16-leg preflight silently does not run
description:
**BLUF: a working copy cloned from GitHub has NO pre-push gate.** `core.hooksPath` **is unset in a fresh clone,** `.git/hooks/pre-push` **does not exist there, so the 16-leg preflight does not run — silently. The push just succeeds. A worktree off the shared checkout inherits the gate; a clone does not.**

## Measured 2026-10-19, read-only `git config --get core.hooksPath`

| working copy | `core.hooksPath` | gate runs? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| the shared checkout `2_Project_Files` | `.githooks` | yes |
| a worktree off it (`worktrees/s-r46-ks1462`) | `.githooks` (inherited) | yes |
| a fresh `git clone` from GitHub | **UNSET** | **NO** |
| `deploy-clones/seatC25-7e2f8157cec2` (a live seat's clone at the time) | **UNSET** | **NO** |

`.githooks/pre-push` is present and executable in the clone — it is simply never invoked, because nothing points git at it.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note

**The failure is silent and it looks like success.** A push from an unwired clone prints no warning and no leg output; it prints the ordinary "new branch" line. There is nothing in the output that says the gate was skipped, so the only way to notice is to know the leg headers should be there and see that they are not.

**It happened, on this ticket's own session.** Seat E 3rd's first push of the KS-1195 branch ran with no gate. It was rejected by the remote for an unrelated reason — the branch name collided with a stale 17-September branch — so nothing landed and no ungated commit exists. Had the name been free, an ungated push would have succeeded and been reported as pushed. That is luck, not a control.

**It is already documented**, at `Blockchain/Dev/CONTRIBUTING.md:389`:
`git config core.hooksPath .githooks && chmod +x .githooks/pre-push`
So this is a missable step, not an undocumented hole. The problem is that missing it is undetectable from the push's own output.

## Fix shapes (not chosen here)

1. **Make the absence loud rather than the wiring mandatory.** A tracked `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/*` check, or a preflight leg, that refuses when `core.hooksPath` does not resolve to `.githooks` — this cannot help the very push it would gate, so it only helps on the *second* push onward.
2. **A** `postinstall` **/ bootstrap step** that sets `core.hooksPath` when it is unset. `npm ci` is `ignore-scripts` in this repo, so a postinstall would not fire; it would have to hang off an existing bootstrap script the seats already run.
3. **Have the launcher wire it for every working copy it knows about**, including `deploy-clones/*`, rather than relying on the clone inheriting anything.
4. **A server-side ruleset** that refuses a push without the evidence the hook produces. The strongest, and the most work; also note "Require status checks" must never be enabled while Actions are retired, so this would need to be something other than a check.

Shape 1 or 3 looks like the cheapest honest improvement; the decision is not mine.

## Reproduce

```
git clone --single-branch --branch develop git@github.com:Secuura/Distributed_Secuura.git /tmp/probe
git -C /tmp/probe config --get core.hooksPath   # prints nothing, exit 1
ls /tmp/probe/.git/hooks/pre-push               # No such file or directory
```

Discovered 2026-10-19 by Seat E 3rd during the KS-1195 build (PR #1613), after the push log showed zero leg output.

title: registerInPlatformRegistry's failure is swallowed twice (.catch(() => {}) over a warn-only try/catch), so a refused platform_document_registry write leaves a document permanently invisible to cross-tenant verify with a 201 and no error
description:
## BLUF

**A failed** `platform_document_registry` **write is invisible.** `routes/documents.ts:772-777` calls `registerInPlatformRegistry(...)` fire-and-forget with `.catch(() => {})`, on top of a `try/catch` in `routes/verification.ts:515-537` whose only action is `logger.warn`. So when the registry write is refused, the caller still gets **201**, the document is correct in its own tenant, and nothing but a warn line records that the cross-tenant pointer was never written. **The document is then invisible to** `crossTenantLookup` **forever** — it presents as "verify works for us and not for anyone else", with no error anywhere a caller or a health check would see.

**Measured, read-only, on develop** `722e07f19cee683ea037930e601e380a9491f7b5`**. Facts only — no fix shape chosen, and no code touched:** `routes/documents.ts` **belongs to another lane this round.**

## How it was measured

Found while settling the KS-1557 integration harness (that work is on KS-1557; this is the product reading separated out of it).

Running `ks1557-verify-trusts-certification-evidence.integration.test.ts` with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` as `secuura_app` against a scratch PostgreSQL 15 built from `docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql`:

* the service logged, **26 times**, `warn: Failed to register document in platform registry {"error":"insert or update on table \"platform_document_registry\" violates foreign key constraint \"platform_document_registry_tenant_id_fkey\""}`;
* `platform_document_registry` held **0 rows** afterwards;
* **every document create still answered 201**, and the only trace was that warn line.

A there-and-back control isolates the write as the whole cause of the downstream behaviour: with the foreign key dropped the registry rows land and the cross-tenant read path works (17/17); with it restored the rows vanish and the cross-tenant read answers "not found" again (26 warnings). Role controls: as `secuura_app` the registry INSERT succeeds when the FK is satisfiable, and `CREATE TABLE` is refused `permission denied for schema public`, so the refusal is the constraint and not a missing grant.

## The two lines

* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:772-777` — `const { registerInPlatformRegistry } = require('./verification'); registerInPlatformRegistry({...}).catch(() => {});` The comment above it says "fire-and-forget". The `.catch(() => {})` discards whatever the inner handler re-raises.
* `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:515-537` — the function's own `catch` does `logger.warn('Failed to register document in platform registry', { error: err?.message })` and returns normally. Nothing retries, nothing records the gap, nothing reconciles later.

## What this is NOT

* **Not a read-side defect.** Given a registry row, `crossTenantLookup` behaves correctly — that is what the control above shows.
* **Not necessarily live today.** The production path satisfies the foreign key: `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:216` inserts the tenant into the platform database's `tenants` table through `platformPool` (`:47`, `:53`). As far as this reading goes the exposure is a **provisioning gap** — any tenant that reaches document registration without a platform `tenants` row loses cross-tenant verify silently — not a defect firing on every request. **I have no box access and have not counted registry rows or warn lines in any deployed environment.**
* **The foreign key is only ONE trigger.** Per **KS-1528**, `platform_document_registry.tenant_id` has three disagreeing declarations: the init schema's `UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id)`, the gateway's in-code CREATE at `startup-migrations.ts:1123-1138` (`TEXT`, **no foreign key**), and the main-database copy at `:473-501` (`TEXT`). So whether the write is refused at all depends on which declaration created the table in that environment. **The silent swallow is the finding; the FK is one way to reach it.** Any failure — a constraint, a connection drop, a permission — lands the same way.

## Related, and why none of them is this

Searched Linear for `registerInPlatformRegistry`, `platform_document_registry`, `platform registry`, `cross-tenant verify registry` and `crossTenantLookup` before filing. Three near neighbours, all on the same function, none covering the swallow:

* **KS-1528** — the `tenant_id` *type declaration* disagreement. States "nothing is broken today because both spellings now work"; says nothing about a refused write being invisible. Direct context for this ticket (above).
* **KS-598** — the registry *upsert* (`ON CONFLICT (content_hash, tenant_id) DO UPDATE`) silently collapsing registrations per (hash, tenant) if the flag is enabled. A different defect in the same function: that one is about a write that **succeeds** and overwrites.
* **KS-1590** — the registry *lookup* comparing a `sha256:`-prefixed hash against unnormalised stored values. The read half, not the write half.

## Suggested shapes — a choice for whoever picks it up, not a decision made here

1. Surface the failure to the caller's own observability without failing the create: count it, or raise it to `logger.error`, so the gap is visible rather than a warn line in a stream nobody greps.
2. Reconcile later: a job that finds documents with no registry row for their (hash, tenant) and writes them.
3. Make the create fail when the registry write fails. **Strongest and probably wrong** — it would couple document registration to the platform database's availability, and the registry is a read optimisation, not the record.

Shapes 1 and 2 are compatible. The choice is a product call about how loudly a degraded cross-tenant index should announce itself.

title: api-gateway falls back to a 60 s window where security defaults to 3,600: a NULL rate_limit_window would enforce a per-hour ceiling per minute
description:
**BLUF: the api-gateway falls back to a 60-second window where the security service defaults to 3,600. A key whose stored** `rate_limit_window` **reads as NULL or 0 would have its per-hour ceiling enforced per MINUTE — 60× more permissive. Measured UNREACHABLE from every tracked writer today, so Low; the residual is that the column is nullable and nothing refuses a NULL.**

## The two fallbacks, at develop `722e07f19cee`

* `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:249` — `rateLimitWindow: data.rateLimitWindow || 60,` (building `meta` from the validate response)
* `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimitEnforce.ts:67` — `const DEFAULT_MACHINE_RATE_WINDOW = 60; // seconds`, applied at `:184` as `(user.rateLimitWindow || DEFAULT_MACHINE_RATE_WINDOW) * 1000`

Against: `services/security/src/index.ts:667` — `rateLimitWindow: z.number().int().min(60).max(86400).default(3600)`.

## How a NULL would get there

* The column is `rate_limit_window INTEGER DEFAULT 3600` (`migrations/002_verification-tiers.sql:561`; re-added the same way by `018_svc_api_keys_reconcile.sql:75`). **No** `NOT NULL`**.** A DEFAULT applies only when the column is omitted; an explicit NULL is accepted.
* `services/security/src/converters.ts:168` reads it as `Number(r.rate_limit_window)`, and `Number(null)` is `0`. Validate returns that `0`, and both gateway fallbacks treat `0` as "no window".

**The direction matters:** this case is *more permissive*, not stricter. A key with `rate_limit = 3000` and a NULL window would be enforced at 3,000 per **60 s** — 180,000 per hour.

## Measured unreachable today — every tracked writer

| writer | window it writes |
| -- | -- |
| security mint + rotate, the shared `apiKeyInsertStatement` (`security/src/index.ts:418-438`) | the parsed schema value — never absent, default 3600 |
| migration 019, JSONB path and TEXT\[\] path | literal `3600` |
| originate `POST /api/admin/api-keys` (`routes/adminConfig.ts:1031-1048`) | literal `3600` |
| test-only inserts (originate `__tests__`) | omit it, so the column DEFAULT `3600` |

Census method: `git grep -i -E '(insert into|update) +svc_api_keys'` over the whole tree at `722e07f19cee`, excluding Markdown; positive control — it finds the security INSERT I had already read. No `UPDATE` sets `rate_limit_window`.

So the hazard needs a hand-edited row or a future writer that passes NULL. That is why this is Low.

## Not the same thing as the deliberate machine default

`DEFAULT_MACHINE_RATE_LIMIT = 100` with `DEFAULT_MACHINE_RATE_WINDOW = 60` is the intended allowance for a machine caller that has **no allowance at all** (the KS-1205 R-2 warning path). That pairing is not the defect. The defect is the **mixed** case — a real per-hour limit paired with a missing window, so the 60 s default meant for "no allowance" silently re-scales someone else's allowance.

## Fix shapes (not chosen)

1. A migration making `rate_limit_window` `NOT NULL`, **after** a census on each box that 0 rows are NULL (it must not be applied blind to a live table).
2. Map NULL to 3,600 in `converters.ts`, so the security service never reports a 0 window.
3. When `rateLimit` is present but the window is missing, use 3,600 in the gateway, not 60, and keep 60 only for the no-allowance path.

Shape 2 is the smallest, but it masks the row instead of refusing it. Shape 1 is the honest one.

Found 2026-10-19 by Seat E 3rd while tracing the KS-1195 store-and-enforce chain for gate X1 (PR #1613). Related: KS-1195.

title: originate POST /api/anchors: the already-anchored check is not network-bound and sits in a TOCTOU window, so the second unguarded anchor_store upsert can still rewrite a row the caller was never shown to own
description:
**BLUF:** `originate/src/routes/anchors.ts` **holds a SECOND, unguarded** `anchor_store` **upsert, and after KS-1629 the only way to reach its cross-tenant overwrite is a time-of-check-to-time-of-use race on** `POST /api/anchors`**. Measured read-only at develop** `722e07f19cee683ea037930e601e380a9491f7b5`**. Filed on Wednesday's instruction (2026-10-19T05:55:40Z) as ruled residue of KS-1603 rather than folded into its pull request.**

## What

`saveAnchorToDb` (`routes/anchors.ts:96-134`) ends in `ON CONFLICT (document_id, network) DO UPDATE SET transaction_hash, block_number, content_hash, simulated, confirmed_at, updated_at` (`:122-128`). It takes no caller, performs no identity or tenant check, and never calls `mayOverwriteStoredMetadata`. KS-1603 recorded it; this ticket is what is left of it once that ticket's interim check is in.

## Why the exposure is narrower than the upsert looks — the three call sites

* `:219`**, inside the GET.** That is **KS-1629** — a read that writes. Not this ticket.
* `:442`**,** `POST /submit`**.** The `documentId` is a **fresh v4 minted at** `:394`, so it can collide with nothing.
* `:342`**,** `POST /`**.** The handler refuses at `:262` when `anchorExistsInDb(documentId)` is true — 400 `Document is already anchored`. So for **any** already-anchored id the `DO UPDATE` arm is never reached, and the route is a pure INSERT.

## So what is actually left

**A TOCTOU window between the check at** `:262` **and the write at** `:342`**.** Nothing holds a lock or a transaction across them: between the two, the whole forward to anchoring happens (`:283-317`, a network call with no timeout of its own on this path). Two concurrent `POST /api/anchors` for the same id — or one racing another writer of the same row — both pass the check and the second takes the `DO UPDATE` arm, rewriting `transaction_hash`, `block_number`, `content_hash`, `simulated` and `confirmed_at` on a row the caller was never shown to own.

**And the check is wider than the key it guards, which widens the window's reach rather than narrowing it.** `anchorExistsInDb` is **not network-bound** — `SELECT 1 FROM anchor_store WHERE document_id = ${documentId} LIMIT 1`, a Prisma tagged template (`:139`) — while the upsert conflicts on `(document_id, network)`. So a row on one network makes the route answer 400 for a *different* network (a legitimate second-network anchor is refused), and the row the eventual `DO UPDATE` lands on need not be the row the check saw.

## Not claimed

I have not run the race, and I have not measured whether anything in front of originate retries `POST /api/anchors` concurrently. The reading is from source. What **is** measured is the reachability argument above: the three call sites, the 400 at `:262`, the fresh v4 at `:394`, and the missing network bound at `:139`.

## Fix shapes (not chosen here)

1. **Bind the check to the network** and make the write conditional on the row still being absent — `ON CONFLICT … DO NOTHING` plus a row-count check, or `WHERE NOT EXISTS`, so a losing racer refuses instead of overwriting.
2. **A** `SECURITY DEFINER` **lookup function** returning a `documentId`'s owning tenant across tenants, in the shape of migration 051. This is the only way originate gets the **same** ownership answer KS-1603's interim check uses, because a guard inside anchoring cannot reach this file (Seat J 13th's #1568 handover says so) and `anchorOverwriteGuard.ts` is not importable across services. KS-1603 deliberately did **not** add it, to avoid a second `052_` migration beside KS-1402's.
3. Both, eventually subsumed by **KS-1384**'s tenant column on `anchor_store`, after which ownership stops being inferred from `documents` at all.

## Dedupe

Literal `containsIgnoreCase` over title **and** description, not `searchIssues` (which is fuzzy): `saveAnchorToDb` → **1** (KS-1629, read: the GET that writes, a different defect on the same helper), `anchorExistsInDb` → **0**, `already anchored` → **0**, `TOCTOU` → **0**. Positive control: the `saveAnchorToDb` hit proves the query finds matches. Negative control: a freshly generated token written nowhere → **0**.

*Filed by Seat J 14th while building KS-1603. Nothing deployed.*

title: ownership_transferred carries the raw principal where the custody row carries the resolved actor
description:
## BLUF

`document.ownership_transferred` **carries the raw principal, while the custody row carries the resolved actor.** For a connector caller the event says `transferredById: "connector:<id>"`. The `custody_events` row says the `onBehalfOf`-resolved same-org user, or NULL. **Nothing consumes the event today, so there is no runtime effect.** Filed so the divergence is on record before anything subscribes.

Refs [KS-1402](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1402/auth-get-apiuserslookup-refuses-connector-tokens-so-every-platform-s).

## Recommendation

Decide the event's actor contract when the event first gets a consumer, or when `EventTypes` gains `DOCUMENT_OWNERSHIP_TRANSFERRED`, whichever comes first. The likely shape is to publish the same `transferredByUuid` the row stores, and to name the connector in its own field if a consumer needs it. Changing it now would be a contract change for no reader.

## Detail

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, the `publishEvent('document.ownership_transferred' as never, { … transferredById: user.id, … })` in `POST /:id/transfer-custody`.
  * At develop `722e07f19cee` that line is **1899**.
  * On PR #1614's head `ddd54b836394` it is **1906**.
* **Why it diverges now:** #1614 binds `custody_events.transferred_by_id` through `toActorUuid(user.id, transferObo.resolvedUserId)`, the KS-564 treatment `/share` got in migration 043. A connector principal is the literal `connector:<id>`, which is not a UUID. So the row holds the resolved user or NULL, and the event still holds the raw principal.
  * For an interactive caller the two agree: `user.id` is a UUID, and no `onBehalfOf` is allowed.
* **Measured: no consumer.** I searched `services/` and `packages/` for `ownership_transferred`, `OWNERSHIP_TRANSFERRED` and `transferredById`, excluding tests and `.md`, with `git grep`. Nothing outside the publisher matches. Control: the same search finds `document.created` in four other places (api-gateway `routes/admin.ts`, `docs/developer-portal.html`, auth `events.ts`, originate `events.ts`), so it discriminates.
* **The publish is typed** `as never`**:** the comment above it says `EventTypes` has no constant for this event yet.
* **Not a duplicate.** I searched Linear with `searchIssues` (comments included), paged every result and literal-matched title, description and the first 40 comments:
  * `ownership_transferred`: literal in 0 of 90 results over 4 pages;
  * `OWNERSHIP_TRANSFERRED`: 0 of 90 over 4 pages;
  * `transferredById`: 0 of 0.
  * Control `toActorUuid`: literal in 1 of 1 (PS-616), so the literal pass can fire.
* **Out of #1614 by ruling:** Wednesday, 2026-10-19T06:24:08Z.

Found and filed by Seat C 25th (Opus 5.5) during the gate hold on #1614.

title: KS-1603 residue: the interim anchor-ownership check does not apply to a tenantless caller, so absence of a tenant claim still permits a cross-tenant anchor write
description:
## BLUF

**The KS-1603 interim ownership check does not apply to a caller whose token carries no usable tenant claim: that caller can still write an anchor onto another tenant's document, exactly as on develop.** Landed in `anchorOverwriteGuard.ts:544-550` (develop `ad784e702ca205230e39d329abefa8a85fb5946c`), where a tenant claim that is absent, blank or not uuid-shaped returns `allow: true, reason: 'caller-has-no-usable-tenant'` with a warn.

**This was accepted deliberately at plan time, not missed.** Wednesday's ruling on the KS-1603 plan (2026-10-19T05:55:40Z, Recommendation item 3) reads, verbatim: *"Everything else is develop: no document anywhere (S's flat anchors, including retries) allow; own tenant allow; **no tenantId allow + warn**."* PR #1615's own predicate table states it, and the code comment at `:541-543` gives the reason. Gate AA1 raised it as note 1 and characterised it as outside those rulings; that characterisation is mistaken — the acceptance is in the ruling mail. **What is correct is that an accepted interim limitation deserves its own ticket rather than living only in a merged PR body, which is why this exists.**

## Why it was allowed, and why that reasoning has a limit

`tenantId` is genuinely optional on the token: auth signs it conditionally (`services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:263`). A claim that is absent or not uuid-shaped is not something a Postgres-rendered `uuid` can equal, so **comparing** it would refuse rather than compare — and KS-1603 was ruled a pure narrowing, so a new refusal there was out of scope.

The limit of that reasoning: "cannot be compared" and "should therefore be allowed" are different statements. The second is a choice, and it makes the absence of a tenant the thing that widens access.

## Scope

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/anchorOverwriteGuard.ts:535-575` — `mayWriteAnchorRows`, the `isUuidShaped(callerTenantId)` arm at `:544`.
* Reached from `index.ts:1403` (every persist, via `dbPersistAnchor`) and `index.ts:761` (the batch pre-check).
* `POST /api/anchors` and `POST /api/anchors/batch`.

## The question to settle before fixing

What should a tenantless caller get? Candidates, none chosen here: refuse (403, so absence never widens); allow only when no `documents` row holds the id at all (which keeps Platform S's flat anchors working while refusing anything that names a real document); or platform-principal-only. **The Platform S constraint is the thing to check first** — S's flat anchors must keep working, including retries, and whether S's token carries a tenant claim has not been measured here.

## Same class, different component

**KS-1406** is the same shape in the **auth** service — the cross-tenant guard on `GET /api/users/lookup` and `POST /api/users/stub` is skipped for a tenantless token (`userRepo.ts:759`). Different service, different route, same principle: the absence of a tenant should never be what widens a read or a write. Worth settling the two together so the convention is one decision.

## Two further gate AA1 notes, same two files

**1. Cell D1's leak proof is weaker than it reads.** `ks1603-the-flat-anchor-write-refuses-a-foreign-tenants-document.integration.test.ts` D1 asserts that the transaction-scoped `app.tenant_scope_bypass` does not survive the probe's transaction, by reading again on the same pool. It only catches a leak because the pool hands back the most recently released connection; it does not pin one. Harden it to pin a single backend by its pid (`pg_backend_pid()`), as gate AA1 did in its own connection-tracking cells. **Test hardening only — the product behaviour is correct and the gate's own cells pass.**

**2. The batch route probes N+1 times.** The batch pre-check reads every id once up front, and `dbPersistAnchor` then probes per item, so a 100-item batch runs up to 101 short transactions. Deliberate at the time: the pre-check buys "writes nothing on refusal", the per-item gate buys "no later caller can route around it". Each probe is one indexed read on `documents` and the route already does N upserts, so it is the same order — **speed only, no correctness consequence.**

## Provenance

* Landed code read at develop `ad784e702ca205230e39d329abefa8a85fb5946c` (the KS-1603 merge), `anchorOverwriteGuard.ts:535-575`.
* The ruling quoted above: Wednesday's ANSWER to Secuura/Blockchain-J, 2026-10-19T05:55:40Z, Recommendation item 3, read back from the project inbox.
* Gate AA1 notes 1-3, verdict `2026-10-19_gate-AA1-pr1615-ks1603/verdict.md`.
* Duplicate search before filing: `tenantless` 2 hits (KS-1406, KS-745), `no tenant claim` 6, `tenant claim` 6 — KS-1406 read in full and is the auth-service instance, not this one. Must-hit control: the same search for `tenant` returns many.

title: Two routes answer the same cross-tenant recipient miss with different codes: RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND vs RECIPIENT_NOT_AVAILABLE
description:
## BLUF

For the identical situation — a recipient email that already belongs to a user in a **different**
tenant — `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` answers `404 RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` while
`POST /api/certifications/issue` answers `404 RECIPIENT_NOT_AVAILABLE`. Both come from auth's same
deliberate cross-tenant 404 on `/api/users/stub`.

## Recommendation

Pick one code and converge, as a contract change with Platform S in the loop — not unilaterally.
KS-1402 deliberately kept `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` on transfer-custody because changing it would be a
contract change Platform S did not ask for.

## Detail

* transfer-custody: `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, the `mintInvitedStubHolder`
  helper's `stubRes.status === 404` arm.
* certifications/issue: `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:287-300`.
* Both are the same upstream condition (auth `userRepo.createInvitedStub` throwing
  `EMAIL_RESERVED_ELSEWHERE`, surfaced as 404 to avoid cross-tenant existence disclosure).
* The status is the same (404) in both, so this is a code-string inconsistency, not a behavioural
  divergence. Anything branching on `error.code` across the two routes has to special-case them.
* Worth checking against PS-side handling before changing either.

title: No retention rule for never-claimed INVITED stub users — a transfer to an unknown email now creates a durable row
description:
## BLUF

Since KS-1402's invited-stub build, a custody transfer naming an email Platform K has never seen
**creates a durable** `users` **row** (`status = 'invited'`) instead of answering 404 and leaving no
trace. A stub is claimed when that person signs up. Nothing expires or reviews the ones that are
never claimed, and there is no documented retention position for them.

## Recommendation

Decide and document a retention rule for `users` rows that are `status = 'invited'` and never
claimed — a review/erase window, or an explicit "retained indefinitely" position with a reason.
This is a privacy decision, not an engineering one, so it wants an owner rather than a default.

## Detail

* **The privacy delta, stated plainly:** an email address that previously produced a 404 and
  persisted nothing is now stored. It is the only PII the row carries, and it is PII the caller
  already supplied in the request.
* The row carries: `id`, `email` (encrypted at rest, with `email_lookup_hash` as its HMAC sibling),
  `email_verified = false`, `status = 'invited'`, `tenant_id` = the caller's tenant. No password
  hash, no name, no phone (auth `repositories/userRepo.ts:753-793`, `createInvitedStub`).
* Not a new PII **class** — K already held and hashed these emails transiently to resolve them. What
  changed is persistence.
* Pre-dates KS-1402 in one respect: `certifications/issue` has minted stubs the same way since
  KS-74, so any rule should cover both paths rather than only transfer-custody.
* Adjacent, not duplicate: KS-1406 (cross-tenant guard fails open for tenantless tokens on
  `/lookup` and `/stub`); PS-1144 (invitation link carries the email in the URL).

title: POST /api/certifications/issue asks assertNoCycle about the certification uuid, not the derived row's external_id, so the lineage-cycle arm cannot fire for the row it creates - the three documents.ts call sites pass the minted external id
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/certifications/issue` **asks the cycle walker about an identifier the row it creates never carries, so the lineage-cycle arm on that route cannot fire for the row being created.** `certifications.ts:417` passes `id` — the certification's uuid from `:363` — as the walker's `newExternalId`, while the derived document it goes on to write carries `external_id = doc-${Date.now()}-${id.slice(0, 8)}` (`:544`). The walker searches the proposed parent's ancestor chain for the first value and never for the second.

**The other three call sites do it the other way round, and they are the control.** `documents.ts:2055`, `:2788` and `:2986` each mint `const newExternalId = doc-<ms>-<8hex>` **first** and pass **that** — the value that becomes the new row's `external_id`. **One outlier in four.**

**Measured read-only at develop** `80868551e67934cb951d28eec44ce3bdf835944c`**. No code touched. Facts and a suggested shape; the owner decides.**

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a comment

The guard exists to stop a lineage loop being written and anchored — `certifications.ts:409-412` says so: *"Walk the proposed parent's ancestor chain to reject cycles BEFORE we anchor or write — the anchoring call is expensive and an invalid lineage shouldn't be visible on-chain."* On the certify route that sentence is not true of the row the request creates. Whatever a loop through a certification-derived row would cost, this call cannot refuse it.

## The mechanism, line by line

* `repositories/documentRepo.ts:891` — `assertNoCycle(newExternalId, proposedParentExternalId, tenantId, options)` delegates the whole walk to `walkAncestors` and then compares `entry.id === newExternalId` for each ancestor.
* `repositories/documentRepo.ts:744` — `walkAncestors` resolves each step with `WHERE d.external_id = ${cursor} AND d.tenant_id = ${tenantId}::uuid` (`:781-782`), following `p.external_id` through a `LEFT JOIN documents p ON p.id = d.parent_document_id`. So every `entry.id` it yields is an `external_id` (or, for a row with none, that row's pkey — `:789`).
* `routes/certifications.ts:363` — `const id = uuidv4()`. Assigned once; the only other `id =` in the file is inside a SQL string at `:347`.
* `routes/certifications.ts:417` — `await assertNoCycle(id, parentDocumentId, lifecycleTenantId, { db })`.
* `routes/certifications.ts:544` — `const derivedExternalId = \`doc-${[Date.now](<http://Date.now>)()}-${id.slice(0, 8)}\``, and `:546`builds the row with`id: derivedExternalId`, which `saveDocument`binds into`external_id\`.

A `doc-<ms>-<8hex>` string is never a uuid, so the compared value and the written value **cannot** coincide.

## The second half, and the reason this is ONE ticket and not two

Even at the three `documents.ts` sites the compared value is **freshly minted for a row that does not exist yet**, so no ancestor can equal it there either. Taken literally, `assertNoCycle`'s own comparison arm is unreachable from every route; what actually bounds a malformed chain at runtime is `walkAncestors`'s `seen` set (`:756-758`) and `MAX_LINEAGE_DEPTH`. The difference is that `documents.ts` passes the identifier that **will** be the row's `external_id`, so it is correct the moment a caller can supply or reuse one; `certifications.ts` passes an identifier that never becomes one, so it is wrong independently of that. Both readings are about the same call, so they belong on one ticket.

## What corroborates it, with the control stated

* **No route-level cell anywhere asserts the 422 fires.** Searched `services/originate/src/__tests__` for `LINEAGE_CYCLE`: **2 files**. `ks1228-a-refused-request-writes-no-provenance-row.test.ts` reaches the 422 **only by mocking** `assertNoCycle` **to throw** (`mockAssertNoCycle.mockImplementation(async () => cycle())`), which tests the handler and not the walker. `documentRepo.test.ts` exercises `walkAncestors`/`assertNoCycle` at **unit** level, where the caller can pass an id that genuinely IS in the chain — which is why the arm is provably alive there and nowhere else.
* **Control for that search:** the same grep over the same directory for `assertNoCycle` returns `documentRepo.test.ts`, so the search does find what is there.

## Rating

**Low.** Nothing is known to be exploitable: a caller cannot choose the derived row's `external_id` (the server mints it from a timestamp and the fresh certification uuid), so there is no demonstrated way to construct the loop the arm would have caught. The cost is a guard that reads as protection and is not, plus the 422 it documents being unreachable on that route. **A re-rate is reasonable and is not mine to do.**

## Suggested shapes — a choice for whoever picks it up

1. **Mint the derived external id before the walk and pass it**, as `documents.ts` already does — moves `derivedExternalId` above the `assertNoCycle` call and passes it. Smallest change, makes the four call sites consistent, and makes the arm correct in intent at all four.
2. **Decide the arm is redundant and say so** — if `walkAncestors`'s `seen` set plus the depth cap are the real protection, keep the walk for its lineage read and drop the comparison, with the comment rewritten to stop promising a refusal that cannot happen.
3. **Give the arm a route-level cell** that constructs a chain the walk must refuse, so whichever of (1) or (2) is chosen is pinned by a test rather than by a reading.

**A cell either way:** a certify whose proposed parent chain already contains the identifier the new row will carry must answer 422 `LINEAGE_CYCLE`, and the route must have no path that reaches `saveCertification` in that case.

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues`, archived included: `assertNoCycle` → **2 hits**, both Done (**KS-70**, which introduced `parent_document_id` lineage and the walker, and **KS-86**, the watermark endpoint) — neither is about which identifier the walker is given. `lineage cycle detection external_id` → 25 hits, none on this call (the nearest, **KS-299**, is a verify-side walk-input gap, and **KS-280** is forward lineage). Also read **KS-1612** and **KS-1633**, which are about `anchor_store` and the certify route's write ORDER, not its cycle check.

## Related

* **KS-1557** — found while building its write side; that PR adds the parent-access predicate immediately above this call and deliberately does **not** touch it. The access check runs **before** the walk there, so a caller who may not read the parent no longer has its chain walked at all.
* **KS-1633** — the same route's anchor-before-row ordering.

title: anchoring readOwningDocument: a correct tenant bound resting on a false reason — `users` is NOT open for SELECT (users_auth_lookup is role-restricted, not public)
description:
## BLUF

**A correct guard resting on a false reason.** `services/anchoring/src/anchorOverwriteGuard.ts:255-261`
justifies the LEFT JOIN's own `u.tenant_id = $2::uuid` bound by stating that `users` is open for
SELECT by construction. **That is not true.** The guard itself is right and should stay; only its
stated reason is wrong, and the same wrong inference is repeated in a test.

## Recommendation

Correct both comments to the measured facts below, keeping the bound. Then answer the one question
this ticket leaves open (see "Unmeasured"), because that is the only part that could be a real
defect rather than a wrong sentence.

## The two sites

1. `services/anchoring/src/anchorOverwriteGuard.ts:255-261`, inside `readOwningDocument`:

   ```
   // `users` has a SECOND, permissive policy — `users_auth_lookup`, whose qual is literally
   // `true` — and Postgres ORs permissive policies together, so tenant isolation on `users` is
   // open for SELECT by construction. Measured on the repo schema. A join without its own
   // bound would read a custodian row from ANY tenant.
   ```
2. `services/anchoring/src/__tests__/ks1385-anchor-store-keeps-the-latest-events-metadata.integration.test.ts:535`
   — the same inference, in the test's own prose.

## Why it is false — measured on the repo's migrated schema (pg 15), 2026-10-19 at develop `a0da739b6954`

The claim omits the policy's `roles` column, which is what decides it:

| instrument | value |
| -- | -- |
| `users` | `relrowsecurity = t`, `relforcerowsecurity = t` |
| policy `tenant_isolation` | `cmd = ALL`, `roles = {public}`, keyed on `app.current_tenant_id` |
| policy `users_auth_lookup` | `cmd = SELECT`, qual `true`, `roles = {secuura_auth_lookup}` — a dedicated role, NOT `public` |
| `secuura_app` | `rolsuper = f`, `rolbypassrls = f` |
| as `secuura_app`, no GUC | **0 rows** in `users` |
| as `secuura_app`, GUC = tenant A | tenant B's row **0** (invisible); tenant A's row **1** |
| control | `documents`: **0** as `secuura_app`, **17** as the owner — so the instrument discriminates |

**A permissive policy restricted to a role you are not does not OR into your result.** anchoring
connects as `secuura_app` (`docker-compose.yml:1294`; Azure wires the same split — the owner
connection is `MIGRATION_*` only, `services.bicep:51-55`), so `users_auth_lookup` never applies to
it and `tenant_isolation` is live. `users_auth_lookup` is created by
`migrations/039_rls_fail_closed.sql:156-157`.

## Unmeasured, and the reason this is a ticket rather than a comment fix

**Does anything else in anchoring lean on the belief that** `users` **is open for SELECT?** Not checked.
The one site found draws a conservative conclusion, so it is safe; a site that relied on the belief
the *other* way — e.g. assuming a cross-tenant `users` read will succeed, or treating an empty
result as "no such user" rather than "not in this tenant" — would be a real defect. Worth a grep of
anchoring for `users` reads before closing.

## Method note, because the error is reusable

The false claim traces to a schema read that captured each policy's `qual` and **not** its `roles`.
Any conclusion about an RLS policy needs `cmd` **and** `roles` together:
`SELECT policyname, cmd, permissive, roles::text, qual FROM pg_policies WHERE tablename = '…'` —
then a behavioural check as the role the service actually connects as, with a control table that has
no escape policy.

## Provenance

Found while measuring KS-1662 item (a). Not edited: `anchorOverwriteGuard.ts` is another lane's
partition. The equivalent claim in originate was the inverse error — `documents.ts:1907` / `:1999`
call tenant RLS *inert* when it is the enforcement — and that is being corrected under **KS-1662**.

title: POST /api/certifications/{id}/recertify anchors BEFORE it writes its documents row - the same orphan-anchor ordering as KS-1633, on the sibling handler (gate AI1 note N7)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/certifications/{id}/recertify` **has the same ordering as the** `/issue` **route KS-1633 fixes: it anchors BEFORE it writes its** `documents` **row, so any failure of that write leaves an** `anchor_store` **row naming no document.** Same class, same file, different handler — and it is **not** changed by KS-1633, deliberately.

**Filed on gate AI1's note N7 (PR #1623). Read-only at develop** `a0da739b6954d42333640ea190d877f031803c7f`**. No code touched.**

## The ordering

In `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts`, the recertify handler:

| step | what |
| -- | -- |
| 1 | the anchoring POST (`const anchoringBase = …`, then `fetch(…/api/anchors…)`) — anchoring persists its `anchor_store` row **before** it answers 202 (`anchoring/src/index.ts:507` `await dbPersistAnchor(...)` precedes `:543` `res.status(202)`) |
| 2 | the production refusal: `if (anchoringStatus === 'failed' && process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production')` → 503 |
| 3 | `await saveCertification(verificationCert, tenantId, (req as any).db)` |

So the anchor row exists before the `documents` row, and a failure at step 3 leaves an orphan anchor — a row whose anchored identity another registration can later claim (the KS-1612 round-2 Major), created by a legitimate authenticated flow with no cleanup.

## Why it is not in KS-1633's PR

KS-1633's scope is `POST /api/certifications/issue`, which is what its description and its gate measured. Widening the PR to a second handler mid-gate would have changed the surface under review at the cap round. The two handlers do not share the ordering code, so the `/issue` fix does not reach this one.

## What the /issue fix looks like, for whoever picks this up

The shape ruled for `/issue` was: write the `documents` row **first** via an **event-free reservation** that shares the row SQL with `saveCertification`; make that reservation **non-deciding** (a failure is logged and the request continues, so the production 503 is never replaced by the write's own error); and on the production 503 **compensate the row away**, reporting any delete that removes no row. Three things that fix needed and this one will need too:

1. **The reservation must not decide the response.** On `/issue` an unwrapped early write turned the 503 into 400 for a NUL byte, 400 for a connector principal and 500 for a throwing save — measured.
2. **The compensating delete must carry the tenant GUC and the request's pool.** `documents` is FORCE RLS under `tenant_isolation`, whose USING clause reads the transaction-local `app.current_tenant_id`: a DELETE outside that transaction answers `DELETE 0` **and raises nothing**, so a compensation can silently remove nothing and still look like success.
3. **Only one writer may write the** `certification_events` **row**, or an accepted recertify ends with two ISSUE events instead of one.

## Rating
