* **Cross-tenant exposure is inferred, not measured.** Five of the six handlers carry no tenant filter, so a caller in another tenant can probably read them too. The local stack has no way to place a user in a second tenant, so the Schemathesis leg only covers two users in one tenant ([KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) keeps the cross-tenant pairing open).
* I did not trace database row-level security, and did not check whether the governance service itself refuses an unauthenticated caller.
* Whether same-tenant OWNER users are *meant* to read each other's objects is not written down anywhere I could find (no rule in the platform docs or `systemTest/CLAUDE.md`). For transfers and delegations the mutating routes already use the authenticated caller (and the delegation list is scoped to the caller), so I read those as defects. The transfer *list* is the exception: it is unscoped today, which is a second exposure (acceptance criterion 5). For **analytics exports, governance participants and security audit** it may be deliberate; those three need a ruling. Severity is left unset for you.

## Acceptance criteria

1. For each of the six routes, a caller who is not entitled to the object receives 404 (the convention `security/audit/{id}` already documents: a foreign id returns 404 so existence is not leaked), or the route is recorded as deliberately shared with the reason written beside the handler and in the OpenAPI description. Entitlement for transfers and delegations is the party fields the mutating routes already use (`currentOwnerId`/`newOwnerId`/`initiatedBy`; `delegatorId`/`delegateId`).
2. **An automated test that demonstrates the fix**, per route, red before and green after: a service-level test with two users where the second user's GET of the first user's object is refused. (No UI surface, so no Playwright test applies.)
3. A live `full` sweep on a slot no longer reports the six `object_level_authorization` pairs (the Schemathesis leg from [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) is the end-to-end evidence); any remaining pair is either fixed or baselined with a reason and an owner, never masked.
4. A decision recorded on whether same-tenant visibility is intended for analytics exports, governance participants and security audit entries, and, if a tenant filter is added, a cross-tenant test (a second tenant needs a way to be provisioned for it).
5. `GET /api/transfers` returns only the caller's transfers (or the ones they are a party to), not every transfer; the scope is the same rule as the by-id read, and is decided together with it.
6. The systemTest module `tests/test_get_by_id_object_authorization.py` (six tests, below) XPASSes strictly for each fixed route; the `xfail` marker on each is removed in the same change, so a fixed route is then asserted for real. A route ruled deliberately shared is moved to `test_by_design_permissive.py` instead.
7. `schemathesis-baseline.json` entries for the six `object_level_authorization::<operation>` pairs (if added meanwhile) are removed when this lands.

Classification tags: platform-k has no `test_taxonomy.ts` (that file is platform-s), so none are given. Same class, different routes: [KS-1699](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1699/security-three-certification-write-routes-have-no-per-record-access) (certification write routes without a per-record check), [KS-1686](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1686/prism-get-apicredentialsid-returns-any-stored-prism-credential-by-id) (prism credentials by id without an owner check). Found under [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under); part of Review A ([KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor)).

## Test details (everything needed to reproduce)

**Where.** Branch `feature/ks-1674-schemathesis-object_level_authorization-4310-never-runs`, commit `8a203488b` on `develop` `32964477f` plus later uncommitted test/doc changes (a PR will follow under [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under)). The platform under test is `develop` unchanged: that branch changes only `systemTest/`. Mac, Docker Desktop (8 CPUs / 31.3 GiB), Python 3.14.8, Node 24.22.0, Schemathesis 4.32.1, hypothesis 6.170.2.

**Stack.** platform-k slot 2 (`SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=2`, gateway `http://localhost:6982`), built from that worktree: 33 of 33 containers healthy, 0 restarts, `/health/deep` ready, 48 migrations applied and 0 failed, admin seeded.

**Actors.** Generated by `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts` (seed `local`): `owner` and `ownerPeer`, both role OWNER, in the same tenant (`ownerPeer` was added to `fixtures/actors.ts` for this). Provisioned with the bootstrap admin authenticated, so the roles are as requested. Passwords are not recorded here.

**A. The sweep that found it** (`systemTest/schemathesis`):

`systemTest/run-in-slot.sh 2 python3 scripts/setup.py` then `systemTest/run-in-slot.sh 2 python3 scripts/run.py full --seed 1674` (with `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` set; 26.0 min). After the main sweep the profile runs a second sweep with only the `object_level_authorization` check (`scripts/runner/ola_leg.py`): the shipped `schemathesis.toml` plus one appended `[auth.wfc]` table (two peers, bearer tokens minted at run time), phases `fuzzing,stateful`, `--max-examples 25`, and four operations excluded (`POST /api/auth/logout`, `/api/auth/refresh`, `/api/auth/login`, `/api/oauth/authorize`: they would revoke or lock a peer). Run directory `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/full-ks-1674-2026-10-20T10-52-16Z-slot2/object-level-authorization/` (NDJSON, HAR, VCR, JSON verdict, WFC, console, native HTML).

* 259 peer replays; requests by identity: owner 3,766, ownerPeer 1,276; 5.7 min, exit 1.
* 6 ST402 (failure type `ObjectLevelAuthorizationViolation`, WFC code 906), equal in NDJSON and JSON verdict.
* What the check does: a GET by `owner` of an object `owner`'s own earlier request produced is replayed as `ownerPeer`; it fails when the peer gets a 200 with an equivalent body, an anonymous replay is refused, and the peer's own list of the collection does not contain it.
* Replay any case: `st replay <case id>` (ids in the table above), or e.g. `curl -X GET -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ownerPeer token>' http://localhost:6982/api/delegations/<id>`.
* Creating requests in that run: `POST /api/delegations {"delegateId": "<uuid>", "delegationType": ["full"]}` (201); `POST /api/analytics/exports {"format": "csv", "period": "all", "type": ""}` (202); `POST /api/governance/participants/register {"stakedAmount": 0, "walletAddress": "0"}` (201); `POST /api/security/audit {"action": "read", "resourceType": "0", "userId": "<uuid>"}` (201). The two transfers came from the stateful phase.
* Sample bodies the peer received: an analytics export `{"status": "failed", "type": "", "format": "csv", "error": "Unknown export type: "}`; a governance participant (`walletAddress`, `stakedAmount`, `tier`, `votePower`, `isDRep`, ...); a delegation (`delegatorId`, `delegateId`, `delegationType`); an audit entry (`tenantId`, `userId`, `organizationId`, `action`); a transfer (`documentId`, `currentOwnerId`, `newOwnerId`, `transferType`, status history).

**B. A deterministic reproduction, no sweep needed** (new systemTest module):

`systemTest/run-in-slot.sh 2 ./venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/test_get_by_id_object_authorization.py -v --no-cov -rxXfE` (from `systemTest/schemathesis`; add `--runxfail` to see the failures).

* `owner` creates each object (a fixture asserts the create status and that `owner` can read it back, 200, so a refusal for the peer cannot be a broken create): transfer `{documentId: doc-<ms>-<hex>, transferType: simple, currentOwnerId/newOwnerId: two throwaway uuids, documentHash: 64 hex, documentTitle, documentType}` (201); delegation, export, participant (unique wallet address) and audit entry as above.
* `ownerPeer` then GETs it and the test asserts a refusal (403 or 404).
* Measured on slot 2, 2026-10-20, with the `xfail` markers disabled: **6 FAILED**, each `assert 200 in (403, 404)`, for `/transfers/{id}`, `/transfers/{id}/history`, `/delegations/{id}`, `/analytics/exports/{id}`, `/governance/participants/{id}`, `/security/audit/{id}`. The transfers were between two throwaway party ids, so neither peer is a party to the transfer they read.
* With the markers on: 6 xfailed (`strict=True`, `raises=AssertionError`, reason cites this ticket). Transfers, history and delegations are marked as confirmed defects; analytics, governance and audit as "ruling pending". A missing generated actor fails the module; it never skips.

**C. Same run, not part of this ticket** (recorded so nothing is lost; not classified, because that needs a control run on develop): five main-sweep pairs not in the triaged baseline (`positive_data_acceptance` on `GET /api/admin/audit/export` x10, `POST /api/security/keys` x3, `POST /api/timestamps/verify` x2, `PUT /api/security/keys/admin-scopes/{userId}` x7; `response_schema_conformance` on `GET /api/admin/audit/export` x1), and two live integration failures (`test_cross_tenant_isolation`, `test_api_key_cross_tenant_isolation`).

**Not covered.** Cross-tenant reads (the local stack cannot place a user in a second tenant); database row-level security; whether the governance service rejects an unauthenticated caller.

title: Security: two cross-tenant isolation regressions fail on develop — a super-admin's X-Tenant-Override does not scope a document read or the api-key list (BUG-ISOLATION-001 / KS-4 and KS-513 are Done)
description:
**BLUF:** Two systemTest regression guards for tenant isolation fail on `develop` today, measured twice on 2026-10-20 against the same stack. The tickets they guard, [KS-4](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-4/critical-cross-tenant-document-leak-via-x-tenant-override-bug) (BUG-ISOLATION-001) and [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions), are both Done, so the regressions currently have no owner. This ticket gives them one. Kamil, I'd be grateful if you could look at the mechanism. My best reading is below, clearly labelled as a hypothesis.

## What fails (measured)

**1.** `tests/test_tenant_isolation.py::test_cross_tenant_isolation` **(BUG-ISOLATION-001 /** [KS-4](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-4/critical-cross-tenant-document-leak-via-x-tenant-override-bug)**)**
An ISSUER_ADMIN creates a document. A SYSTEM_ADMIN reads it in its own tenant context (200, the control). The same SYSTEM_ADMIN then reads it with `X-Tenant-Override: 00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000deadbeef`, a tenant that owns nothing. **Expected:** not 200 (the tenant predicate hides it). **Got:** 200 with the document body.

> `AssertionError: BUG-ISOLATION-001 regression: document doc-1792496776162-f65739ee was readable from a foreign tenant context (00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000deadbeef). The tenant predicate is not being applied.`

**2.** `tests/test_tenant_isolation_writes.py::test_api_key_cross_tenant_isolation` **(**[KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions)**)**
A SYSTEM_ADMIN creates an API key under the Oxford override, then lists keys under the BUPA override. **Expected:** the Oxford key is not listed. **Got:** it is listed.

> `AssertionError: KS-513 cross-tenant api-key disclosure: key key_3d152a73-… created under Oxford is visible when listed under the BUPA tenant override.`

## Evidence that it is develop, not the change under test

* **Control run:** both tests run from `develop`'s own harness (a detached worktree at `develop` `32964477f`), on platform-k slot 2 built at that platform code. Both FAILED as above.
* **Branch run:** the same two tests from the [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) branch (systemTest-only changes) on the same stack, back to back. Both FAILED identically. They also failed in that branch's full run (`full-ks-1674-2026-10-20T10-52-16Z-slot2`): live integration 426 passed / 2 failed.
* **Not the** [KS-1054](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1054/fresh-databases-are-fail-open-until-the-second-boot-039-rls-fail) **fresh-database window:** the migration runner shows `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` and its [KS-1054](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1054/fresh-databases-are-fail-open-until-the-second-boot-039-rls-fail) fix `038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` already applied by the database's first boot. I could not read `pg_policy` directly (it needs the database password, which I do not handle).

## Where I'd look first (hypothesis, NOT verified)

One mechanism fits both failures: **the gateway-verified** `X-Tenant-Override` **does not reach originate as the request's tenant**, so both calls fall back to the default tenant.

* The api-key list filters `WHERE tenant_id = ${req.tenantId || 'a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'}` (`services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:893-900`). If the override is not applied, a key created "under Oxford" and a list "under BUPA" both land in the default tenant, which is exactly what the test sees.
* The document read: `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1924-1930` states the platform-admin RLS bypass is unreachable from that route, so with the override applied the foreign tenant GUC should hide the document. A 200 means the GUC was the document's own tenant (or none was applied).
* Possibly the same class as [KS-1084](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1084/read-only-unverified-the-gateways-own-authorization-only-calls-to) (gateway calls to originate send no `x-tenant-id`, so single-tenant originate may scope to the default tenant; In Progress) or [KS-619](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-619/gateway-tenant-resolution-falls-through-to-the-callers-x-tenant-id) (gateway tenant resolution falls through to the caller's `x-tenant-id`; Backlog). I have not confirmed either; please treat this as a pointer, not a diagnosis.

## How to reproduce

From `systemTest/schemathesis` on a slot with the actors provisioned:

`systemTest/run-in-slot.sh <N> ./venv/bin/python3 -m pytest "tests/test_tenant_isolation.py::test_cross_tenant_isolation" "tests/test_tenant_isolation_writes.py::test_api_key_cross_tenant_isolation" -v --no-cov`

Stack used: platform-k slot 2, 33/33 containers healthy, 48 migrations applied and 0 failed; Python 3.14.8, Schemathesis 4.32.1. The tests use the seeded SYSTEM_ADMIN (super-admin) and ISSUER_ADMIN personas, and the Oxford and BUPA seed tenants.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **The two existing integration tests above pass** on a freshly built slot and on a second boot of the same database. They are the automated tests that demonstrate the fix (no UI surface, so no Playwright test applies).
2. The root cause is written down in the fix's PR: why the override did not scope these two requests, and whether other routes that read `req.tenantId` are affected.
3. If [KS-1084](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1084/read-only-unverified-the-gateways-own-authorization-only-calls-to) or [KS-619](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-619/gateway-tenant-resolution-falls-through-to-the-callers-x-tenant-id) turns out to be the cause, this ticket is linked to it as a duplicate or blocked-by, rather than closed silently.
4. The test docstrings that cite [KS-4](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-4/critical-cross-tenant-document-leak-via-x-tenant-override-bug) and [KS-513](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-513/systemtest-cross-tenant-cross-owner-document-isolation-regressions) are updated to cite this ticket while it is open, so a failing run names a live owner (systemTest; Peter will do that part once this ticket exists).

Classification tags: platform-k has no `test_taxonomy.ts`, so none are given. Found while classifying the full-run failures for [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) (step 11b).

title: Spec: three more operations reject a "valid" empty body (KS-1364 class) — POST /api/security/keys, PUT /api/security/keys/admin-scopes/{userId}, POST /api/timestamps/verify; and POST /api/security/keys declares no body schema at all
description:
**BLUF:** Three operations not on [KS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1364/spec-85-of-145-request-bodies-are-not-marked-required-true-so)'s list show the same spec drift: the published spec does not mark their request body `required: true`, so Schemathesis sends a schema-"valid" request with **no body**, and the service correctly answers 400. In addition, `POST /api/security/keys` publishes **no body properties at all**. These are spec fixes, not service fixes. [KS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1364/spec-85-of-145-request-bodies-are-not-marked-required-true-so) owns the class but is In Progress, so this is a small linked ticket rather than an edit to it. Thank you, Kamil.

## Measured

Run `full-ks-1674-2026-10-20T10-52-16Z-slot2` (platform-k slot 2, Schemathesis 4.32.1, seed 1674), check `positive_data_acceptance` ("schema-valid request rejected"), plus a control run from `develop`'s own harness (`develop` `32964477f`, same slot, seed 1674, freshly reset database):

| Operation | Branch run | Develop control | Request sent | Response |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `PUT /api/security/keys/admin-scopes/{userId}` | 7 | 5 | no body (all 7) | 400 `Validation failed`, `invalid_type` / `received: undefined` |
| `POST /api/security/keys` | 3 | 3 | no body (2 of 3) | 400 `Validation failed`, `invalid_type` / `received: undefined` |
| `POST /api/timestamps/verify` | 2 | 0 | no body (both) | 400 `Validation failed`, `hash` `Required` |

The differing counts are sampling: whether a run generates an empty body for an operation varies. `positive_data_acceptance` on `POST /api/timestamps/verify` is in neither the baseline nor [KS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1364/spec-85-of-145-request-bodies-are-not-marked-required-true-so)'s table; the two `/api/security/keys` operations are not in [KS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1364/spec-85-of-145-request-bodies-are-not-marked-required-true-so)'s table either. None of these pairs is in `config/schemathesis-baseline.json`.

**The third** `POST /api/security/keys` **case** sent a body with `name: "\n"`. The service trims it and refuses an empty name (`too_small`, `min 1`, path `name`), which is correct ([KS-202](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-202/enforce-input-trimming-on-all-user-facing-string-fields-across) trim rule). It reads as a failure only because the published schema for this operation declares no properties and no `required` list: checked in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, `paths./api/security/keys.post.requestBody` has no `required` flag and an empty schema.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The spec marks `requestBody.required: true` for all three operations (at the generator, `*.openapi.ts` then `npm run generate-openapi`, as [KS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1364/spec-85-of-145-request-bodies-are-not-marked-required-true-so) proposes).
2. `POST /api/security/keys` publishes its real body schema: the fields the service's Zod schema accepts, `name` with `minLength: 1` after trimming, and the `required` list.
3. **Automated test:** a full Schemathesis sweep on a slot reports no `positive_data_acceptance` failure for these three operations, and the offline spec checks pass (`npm run check:openapi` / the preflight). No UI surface, so no Playwright test applies.
4. If [KS-1364](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1364/spec-85-of-145-request-bodies-are-not-marked-required-true-so) lands a blanket fix first, this ticket is closed as covered, with the measured re-run as evidence.

Classification tags: platform-k has no `test_taxonomy.ts`, so none are given. Found while classifying the full-run failures for [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) (step 11b).

title: Akto harness: reuse one scan token or scan as more than one user — deferred from KS-724, build only if credentialInvalidated fires on a non-excluded template
description:
## BLUF

This ticket holds items 2 and 3 of [KS-724](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-724/a-scan-that-logs-in-more-than-ten-times-as-one-user-revokes-its-own), split out on 2026-10-22 so [KS-724](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-724/a-scan-that-logs-in-more-than-ten-times-as-one-user-revokes-its-own) could close on item 1. Neither item is to be built unless the trigger below fires. It sits under [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage) because any work it leads to is a systemTest harness change.

## Background (from [KS-724](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-724/a-scan-that-logs-in-more-than-ten-times-as-one-user-revokes-its-own))

`GET /api/sessions` keeps a rolling window of a user's 10 most recent sessions, and an evicted session is invalidated. A scan that logs in more than ten times as one user therefore revokes the token it is scanning with, and every later request returns `401 "Session has been invalidated"`.

[KS-724](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-724/a-scan-that-logs-in-more-than-ten-times-as-one-user-revokes-its-own) proposed three remedies:

1. **Assert the scan credential is still alive.** Done: `assertCredentialAlive`, PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1336](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1286-akto-2356-honest-coverage-paced-tiers-stall-stop-and-slot-safe-cba284970402) ([KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and), `f3fb25e3e`), wired into all three Akto tiers. The `AUTH_BYPASS_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_ROLE` exclusion was ruled "Accept as built" by Kam on 2026-10-18 and quoted in code via PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1565](https://linear.app/secuura/review/refs-ks-724-quote-kams-accept-as-built-ruling-beside-the-locked-561001a9bedd).
2. **Don't re-login per request.** Reuse one token, so a scan can't evict itself. *(this ticket)*
3. **Or scan as more than one user,** so no single account's window fills. *(this ticket)*

## Why these are deferred

* The gate has never caught this defect in a harness run. Its only non-zero reading was the locked-account template's 66 results, which are by design. Slot 2 `test:pr` on 2026-09-28 recorded `credentialInvalidated: 0`.
* The [KS-1440](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1440/akto-image-23610-2371-release-v2371-2026-10-06-both-local-tags) platform log showed about 9 successful logins since the stack started and no revoke inside the failure window. The \~30 logins that evicted the token came from the [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) probe run, not the harness.
* Item 3 would add actors, tenancy variables and more logins to a suite we are trying to make deterministic ([KS-696](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-696/akto-pr-scan-is-non-deterministic-three-runs-on-near-identical-code), [KS-709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-709/akto-reports-a-pass-for-a-test-that-executed-nothing-clean-0-not)).

## Trigger

Build item 2 or 3 **only if** an Akto run reports `credentialInvalidated > 0` on a template other than `AUTH_BYPASS_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_ROLE`. When it fires, attach the run artifact here and move this ticket to Todo.

## Open question to read first if it fires

**Not verified:** whether Akto already reuses one token or re-logs in per iteration (`configureBearerAuth` only writes the token; the harness has no read path for it). If Akto already reuses one token, item 2 is already true and the cause lies elsewhere.

## Source

[KS-724](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-724/a-scan-that-logs-in-more-than-ten-times-as-one-user-revokes-its-own) (description re-scope paragraph and the 2026-10-22 comment).

title: Harden the e2e readiness check: zero-byte browser file, webkit for the mobile project, API-only runs (KS-734 follow-up)
description:
**Ask:** fix three edges in the e2e readiness check (`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/check-e2e-ready.mjs` and `global-setup.ts`).

1. **A truncated browser passes.** The browser check is `existsSync(chromium.executablePath())`; with a zero-byte, non-executable file at that path the script printed OK and rc 0.
2. **Chromium only.** The `mobile` project uses `devices['iPhone 13']`, whose `defaultBrowserType` is webkit (measured), and `e2e:install` installs only chromium. A mobile run on a fresh checkout passes this check and then fails.
3. **An API-only run is refused.** `global-setup.ts` now calls the same check for every project, so `--project=api`, which needs no browser, is refused when chromium is absent (read from code by the gate, not run). Also, the dependency check is `require.resolve` of three declared names: presence, not version.

None is a defect in the 'refuse' direction PR #920 was asked for; they are false-green and over-refusal edges.

Source: QA gate DA3, round 1 (verdict `2026-10-23_gate-DA3-five-prs/verdict.md`). The gate's measurements, not re-measured by the seat that filed this.

title: test-account password is derivable from the redacted message, and the redaction misses JSON, URL and HTML-escaped echoes
description:
**Ask:** make the redaction in the pre-suite step actually protect the generated test-account password, or say in a comment that it is cosmetic.

**What the gate found (notes N1 and N2 of the #989 verdict):** #989 (merged, KS-973 items 5 and 6) replaces the generated password with `[REDACTED]` in the DEGRADED banner (`redactSecrets(...)` at `systemTest/fixtures/provision.ts` line 342 on develop `a9ce2cff1594`). The gate, verbatim:

* **N1:** *"The redaction can be undone by derivation.* `actors.ts:98`*:* `buildPassword = \`*Ks256-${key}-${seed}-Pw!\`*`. The redacted message names `*"${spec.key}"*`and`[*spec.email*](<http://spec.email>)`=`*ks256-<key>-<seed>@secuura-test.invalid*`, and the new test asserts both are present. `*provision-actors.ts:246*`prints the seed outright. Anyone reading the DEGRADED banner can therefore reconstruct the password. Impact is low: these are test accounts on undeliverable addresses, provisioning against a remote host is refused without`*ALLOW_REMOTE_PROVISION\`, and the manifest holds the passwords anyway. This is outside item 6's literal scope ("cleartext in the banner"). It is worth a ticket, either a non-derivable password (seed plus a random component) or an honest comment saying the redaction is cosmetic."*
* **N2:** *"Matching is exact-substring. An echo that JSON-escapes, URL-encodes or HTML-escapes the password would not match. The fixed parts of the password (*`Ks256-`*,* `-Pw!`*) need no escaping, but* `--seed` *is caller-supplied, so a seed containing* `"` *or* `\` *would escape in a JSON echo. This is an edge case."*

**Fix shapes the gate named (proposals):** a password that is not a pure function of the printed key and seed (the seed plus a random component, kept in the manifest which already holds the passwords), and/or redact the escaped forms of the password too (JSON, URL, HTML), with a cell per form. If neither is wanted, an honest comment at `redactSecrets` that it is cosmetic.

Related and unchanged: the manifest `generated/actors.json` stores passwords in cleartext (gitignored), which the gate noted as a pre-existing exposure by design.

Source: QA gate DA5, tier 1, round 1 (verdict `2026-10-23_gate-DA5-pr989-995-tier1/verdict.md`, sha256/16 of the body `be2f26d014ae8997`). Quoted from the verdict; **not re-measured by the seat that filed this.**

title: systemTest/schemathesis: plain `mypy tests/` aborts on develop with "Source file found twice under different module names" (stub_sweep/stubs/admin_list.py)
description:
## BLUF

`mypy tests/`, the mypy leg of `systemTest/schemathesis/validate-lint.sh`, exits 2 on `origin/develop` `1ae6f17d19a8` without checking any file: *"Source file found twice under different module names"*. Run with `--explicit-package-bases` it completes and reports **317 errors in 100 files**.

## Seen

Found during [KS-1719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1719) (PR #1687), 2026-10-26. Python 3.14.9 linux/arm64 (official `python:3.14` image), venv built from `constraints.txt` (schemathesis 4.32.1) plus the `dev` extra. Run from `systemTest/schemathesis` on a `git archive origin/develop systemTest/schemathesis` export in an empty directory, so no working-tree state is in it.

* `mypy tests/` → `tests/functional/stub_sweep/stubs/admin_list.py: error: Source file found twice under different module names: "functional.stub_sweep.stubs.admin_list" and "tests.functional.stub_sweep.stubs.admin_list"`, then `Found 1 error in 1 file (errors prevented further checking)`.
* `mypy tests/precondition_probes.py` on the KS-1719 branch → the same class: `"precondition_probes" and "tests.precondition_probes"`.
* `mypy --explicit-package-bases tests/` → `Found 317 errors in 100 files (checked 403 source files)`. mypy's own note names that flag.

## Where

`systemTest/schemathesis/validate-lint.sh` runs `mypy tests/ --no-error-summary 2>/dev/null` and counts a non-zero exit as FAIL. `[tool.mypy]` in `pyproject.toml` holds only `python_version = "3.14"` (read with `tomllib`): no `files`, `mypy_path`, `explicit_package_bases` or `exclude`.

## Searched

Secuura-PK, all states, title and description: `found twice under different module names`, `explicit-package-bases`, `stub_sweep/stubs/admin_list`: 0 hits each. Control: `_free_active_proposal_slot` returned KS-1719, so the search can fire.

## Not established

* Whether Peter's or Stuart's environment aborts the same way. Measured on one machine only.

* What invokes `validate-lint.sh` besides running it directly. Not checked.

title: systemTest/schemathesis: test_symlinked_venv_is_refused_not_looped fails on Linux, because sys.executable keeps the symlink path and the KS-738 loop it asserts never occurs
description:
## BLUF

`tests/unit/runner/test_prevenv_bootstrap.py::TestReexecBehavesAsAProcess::test_symlinked_venv_is_refused_not_looped` fails on Linux at `origin/develop` `1ae6f17d19a8`. It expects exit 1 and the *"refusing to loop (KS-738)"* line; the script exits 0.

## Seen

Found during [KS-1719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1719) (PR #1687), 2026-10-26. Python 3.14.9 linux/arm64 (official `python:3.14` image), `tests/unit` with `-n 4 --no-cov`:

* `origin/develop`: **1 failed, 4343 passed, 2 skipped**. This is the one failure.
* After PR #1687: 1 failed, 4359 passed, 2 skipped. The same single failure.
* Assertion: `AssertionError: expected the loop guard's exit 1, got 0` (`assert result.returncode == 1`).
* `scripts/venv_reexec.py:30-37` states the case the guard covers: with `<root>/venv` a symlink, *"CPython sets* `sys.executable` *to the RESOLVED target"*, so the venv-membership test never becomes true and the old prelude re-exec'd forever.
* Measured on Linux: a symlink `/tmp/x/python3` → `/usr/local/bin/python3.14`, run as `/tmp/x/python3 -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)"`, prints `/tmp/x/python3`, not the resolved target. No resolved-target path means no loop for the guard to refuse.

## Searched

Secuura-PK, all states, title and description: `test_symlinked_venv_is_refused_not_looped`: 0 hits. Control: `_free_active_proposal_slot` returned KS-1719, so the search can fire.

## Not established

* That the test passes on macOS. Not run there: the host Python was 3.14.7 when this was measured, below the suite's pin, so pytest exits before collecting.
* The experiment symlinked the interpreter *file*. The test stages a symlinked venv *directory* (`_stage_tree(tmp_path, venv="symlink")`). The same CPython behaviour is inferred for the directory case, not measured.
* Which hosts run `tests/unit` on Linux today. Not checked.

title: packages/shared wallet-signature.test.ts: the only positive cell fails on develop - verifyMessageSignature returns false for a valid CIP-8 signature
description:

```
AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/__tests__/wallet-signature.test.ts:49:63

```

* Seen on four runs today (2026-10-26) on the Studio. It is not tied to the day's machine load.

**Where it is used outside tests:** `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:3254`. The detached `/sign-wallet` route (KS-278) runs `const signatureValid = verifyMessageSignature(walletAddress, …)`. **Not measured:** whether that route refuses genuine wallet signatures at runtime. No live route was exercised.

**History, stated and not interpreted:**

* The test file was added in `7c045a78a` (2026-06-16, KS-278).
* The verifier's file was last changed in `ef687539c` (2026-07-20, *"#4 lucid-cardano → @lucid-evolution (#566)"*).
* When the cell started failing is not measured.

**Searched first:** `wallet-signature.test.ts`, the full path `packages/shared/src/__tests__/wallet-signature.test.ts`, `accepts a valid wallet signature over the message`, `verifyMessageSignature`, `makeWalletSignature`. That is 0 exact hits in titles, descriptions or comments, and no BACKLOG.md entry. title: Azure template: no deploy path supplies EMITTER_SIGNING_SECRET (services.bicep:139 defaults to '', so both apps boot fail-closed); the vouch's twin gap is KS-1083
description:
**What is missing:** on the Container Apps (Azure template) path, no tracked deploy entry point supplies `EMITTER_SIGNING_SECRET`. Found by the tier-1 gate on PR #1690 (KS-1717), round 1, Minor 1.

**The facts, at PR #1690's head** `dfc89078979b`**:**

* `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/services.bicep:139` is `param emitterSigningSecret string = ''`. The two apps wire `EMITTER_SIGNING_SECRET` ONLY when that param is non-empty (originate and anchoring, both conditional).
* A grep of every tracked file names the param or the variable in only four places: `services.bicep`, the two env templates, and `docker-compose.yml:618` and `:1327`. Excluded from that grep: service source, `packages/`, tests and docs. That leaves no deploy script (`deployment/azure/*.sh`, including `deploy.sh`, `deploy-all.sh` and `setup-keyvault.sh`), no workflow under `.github/workflows/` (including `deploy-demo.yml`) and no parameters file.
* So a Container Apps deploy from this template boots both services with the variable UNSET. By design that is **fail-closed**: anchoring honours no `x-emitter-internal` marker and logs `[emitter-guard] FAIL-CLOSED …` at boot. Each connector-initiated create, share, transfer-custody, revoke or lifecycle call then writes one extra `anchor` provenance row.
* **Not measured live:** the Container Apps estate was deleted on 2026-07-31, so this is the template only.

**The same gap for the sibling secret, already recorded:** `services.bicep:131` is `param gatewayVouchSecret string = ''`, and the same grep finds no deploy entry point that passes it. KS-1083 already records that *"no tracked deploy, bootstrap or CI path supplies"* `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET`. That half is KS-1083's; it is named here only so the two are fixed together if that is the cheaper route.

**Where the secret IS supplied:** the compose path that kintsugi and demo run. `docker-compose.yml` passes `EMITTER_SIGNING_SECRET` from the box's `.env` to originate (`:618`) and anchoring (`:1327`), and `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` to api-gateway and originate (`:452`, `:610`). The KS-1717 deploy round sets it there. **This ticket is the Azure template only.**

**Searched first:** `emitterSigningSecret` (0 hits) and `EMITTER_SIGNING_SECRET` (only KS-1726, which names it as a sibling and not this gap). `deploy-demo.yml` and `setup-keyvault.sh` turned up only generic mentions, plus KS-1083 for the vouch. Control: the same search finds KS-1083 for `gatewayVouchSecret`.

**Not done here, by ruling:** the deploy scripts are not changed in PR #1690.

title: governance: a failed database read answers as empty - GET /proposals returns 200 [] and the active-proposal cap fails OPEN (dbGetAllProposals swallows into [])
description:
## BLUF

**In** `services/governance`**, a FAILED database read answers as if the data were empty.** `dbGetAllProposals` catches every error and returns `[]` (`governanceService.ts:254-256`), and nothing above it checks. So:

* `GET /api/governance/proposals` and `GET /api/governance/proposals/active` answer **200 with an empty list** when the database fails. A caller cannot tell "no proposals" from "the read failed".
* **The active-proposal cap fails OPEN.** `createProposal` enforces `maxActiveProposals` by reading active and queued proposals through the same helper (`:495-497`). A failed read returns `[]`, the `>=` check is false, and the cap is not applied.

This is KS-1345's class (webhooks), which does not cover governance. **Not fixed in PR #1696**, which leaves `governanceService.ts` untouched.

## Where (develop `c2505d5c6fe0`; read from source, not run against a database)

`services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts`:

* `:224-258` `dbGetAllProposals`, with `} catch (err: any) { logger.error('DB get all proposals failed', …); return []; }` at `:254-256`. The error is logged server-side; the caller gets `[]`.
* Its callers:
  * `:605` `getProposals`, used by the route `GET /proposals` (`routes/governance.ts:150`) and `GET /proposals/active` (`:168`). Both answer `200 { success: true, data: [], count: 0 }`, and neither route has an error path.
  * `:495` `createProposal` — the cap check at `:496`: `if (activeProposals.length >= governanceConfig.maxActiveProposals) throw new ConflictError(…)`.
  * `:977` `getGovernanceStats`.
  * `:1013` `processExpiredProposals` — a failed read expires nothing.

## The same shape elsewhere in the file (facts; consequences not traced unless stated)

Every `catch` in `governanceService.ts` that returns a value instead of rethrowing:

| line | helper | returns on failure |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `:218` | `dbGetProposal` | `undefined` (read by callers as "no such proposal") |
| `:254` | `dbGetAllProposals` | `[]` |
| `:264` | `dbGetParticipant` | `undefined` |
| `:274` | `dbGetParticipantByAddress` | `undefined` |
| `:312` | `dbGetAllParticipants` | `[]` |
| `:341` | `dbGetActiveDelegations` | `[]` |
| `:447` | `getTotalVotePower` | `0`, used at `:571` (`submitProposal`) and `:979` |
| `:1025` | `processExpiredProposals` | `0` |

The three save helpers (`:166`, `:186`, `:204`) and `verifyDbReady` (`:365`) rethrow. **What a** `0` **total vote power does to quorum is not traced.**

## Why it matters

* KS-1345 records that this exact shape once hid a real defect for its whole life: a query that always failed and always read as empty.
* Here the same failure can also lift an abuse limit (the cap), not just blank a list.
* Combined with a partial failure, a failed SELECT can disable the cap while the INSERT succeeds. In a full outage the INSERT fails too, at `dbSaveProposal`, which rethrows.

## Fix shape (not chosen here)

KS-1345's shape: let the read reject to the route, so it answers a constant 500 with the error logged server-side. Ruling-sensitive choices for whoever fixes it:

* whether a NOT-FOUND (`undefined`) must stay distinguishable from a FAILED read;
* whether the cap should refuse, rather than allow, when it cannot count.

## Related, NOT duplicates

* **KS-1345** — `GET /api/webhooks` swallows a failed list query into `200 []`. Same class, different service.
* **KS-1722** / PR #1696 — the proposals-list filter. Found while building it, and not touched by it.

## Searched first

Exact substring over the title and description of all **711** Secuura-PK issues, all states:

* `dbGetAllProposals` → KS-1722 only (the filter, not the catch).
* `governanceService.ts` → KS-1722 only.
* `DB get all proposals failed` → 0.
* `swallows a failed` → KS-1657 (originate anchors), KS-1345 (webhooks), KS-888 (`dbSaveApiKey`) — other services.
* `into 200 with an empty` and `return [];` → KS-1345 only.

KS-1345's description names only `routes/webhooks.ts:196` and `:412`. Control: `GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828` finds KS-1723.

## Found by

Seat K while building KS-1722 (PR #1696), filed facts-only on the coordinator's ruling. Not measured against a running database.

title: services/vc-issuer test files cannot use a top-level await: the enrolled type-check refuses it with TS1378 under module: commonjs, foreclosing the module-scope fix shape
description:
## BLUF

**A test file in** `services/vc-issuer` **cannot use a top-level** `await`**.** The service compiles
`module: commonjs` / `target: es2021`, and its enrolled test-file type-check
(`tsconfig.test.json`, read by `scripts/typecheck-tests/check.cjs`) therefore reports **TS1378**
for one. That forecloses a fix shape KS 1729 explicitly sanctions — doing an expensive import
once at module scope, so the cost falls at collection where there is no hook timeout.

Filed on the coordinator's ruling, facts only. **No fix is proposed here**: the trade-off is
named below and belongs to whoever owns the service's compile target.

## Measured

At develop `8661f5d418b23ffb0c63a2504d707eb12189b5ad`, adding one `await freshModules();` at
module scope in each of three test files, then running
`node scripts/typecheck-tests/check.cjs services/vc-issuer` from `Blockchain/Dev`:

**rc 1**, one error per file, verbatim:

```
src/__tests__/ks1020-presentation-lookup-exact-or-404.test.ts(91,1): TS1378: Top-level 'await' expressions are only allowed when the 'module' option is set to 'es2022', 'esnext', 'system', 'node16', 'node18', 'node20', 'nodenext', or 'preserve', and the 'target' option is set to 'es2017' or higher.
src/__tests__/ks1116-presentation-and-credential-reads-bound-to-the-creator.test.ts(192,1): TS1378: Top-level 'await' expressions are only allowed when the 'module' option is set to 'es2022', 'esnext', 'system', 'node16', 'node18', 'node20', 'nodenext', or 'preserve', and the 'target' option is set to 'es2017' or higher.
src/__tests__/ks1683-credential-list-and-by-hash-bound-to-the-creator.test.ts(134,1): TS1378: Top-level 'await' expressions are only allowed when the 'module' option is set to 'es2022', 'esnext', 'system', 'node16', 'node18', 'node20', 'nodenext', or 'preserve', and the 'target' option is set to 'es2017' or higher.
```

Without that line the same command is **rc 0** ("tsc examined 33 files, 19 of them under
`__tests__`; 0 errors: 0 in the baseline, 0 new; 0 stale baseline entries").

**Note the asymmetry:** vitest runs such a file fine — only the type-check refuses it. So the
pattern is available at runtime and unavailable under the gate.

## The config lines

`services/vc-issuer/tsconfig.json`:

* `"module": "commonjs"`
* `"target": "es2021"`

`services/vc-issuer/tsconfig.test.json` (what the ratchet reads) adds nothing relevant — it is:

```json
{
  "extends": "./tsconfig.json",
  "compilerOptions": { "noEmit": true },
  "include": ["src/**/*"],
  "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist"]
}
```

So the refusal comes from the **service's own** compile settings, inherited by the test config.
It is not specific to the ratchet, and it applies to every service enrolled the same way.

## The trade-off, named not resolved

* Raising `module`/`target` **only in** `tsconfig.test.json` would unblock the pattern without
  touching the service build, since that config is `noEmit` — but it makes the test program's
  module semantics differ from the shipped code's, which is the kind of divergence a type-check
  exists to prevent.
* Raising them in `tsconfig.json` keeps test and source aligned but **changes the service's**
  **emit**, which is a real change to shipped output.
* Leaving it means the module-scope shape stays unavailable and callers reach for a per-hook
  timeout instead — which is what KS 1729 did, deliberately, with the reason written in-file.

## Related, NOT a duplicate

**KS 1329** — `packages/shared` does not type-check `src/__tests__`. It is the only other open
issue naming `TS1378`, and it was read before filing rather than matched on the token:

* It concerns `packages/shared`, not `services/vc-issuer`.
* Its subject is test files being **excluded** from the type-check, hiding 10 errors.
* Its TS1378 appear as **probe artefacts** — it raises `module`/`target` in an out-of-repo probe
  precisely because that package's tests **already use** top-level `await`, and says leaving
  them at `commonjs` produces "9x TS1343 and 5x TS1378 that are artefacts of the probe".

That makes KS 1329 evidence the same constraint bites elsewhere, with the opposite symptom:
there the tests already use the pattern and are simply never type-checked; here they are
type-checked and the pattern is refused.

## Searched first

Exact substring over the title and description of all **705** open Secuura-PK issues:

* `TS1378` -> **1** (KS 1329, above).
* `top-level await` -> 0. `top-level 'await'` -> 0.
* `module: commonjs` -> 0. `"module": "commonjs"` -> 0.
* `tsconfig.test.json` -> 4 (KS 1554, KS 1494, KS 1090, KS 1000) — all about enrolment, none
  about this refusal.

Controls showing the instrument finds known tickets: `Hook timed out in 10000ms` -> 4,
`exceed vitest's 5 s default` -> 4, `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT` -> 3.

## Found by

Seat S 2nd while building KS 1729 (pull request 1714), 2026-10-26. The module-scope shape was
built first, measured as above, and reverted in full — the three files were verified
byte-identical to develop afterwards. Measured on Node v26.8.1.

title: Node 26's semver-major Readable.read() change truncates every synchronous cbor.encode() to its first byte on host test runs - images pin node:24 and are unaffected
description:
**Node 26.0.0 removed the behaviour** `cbor`**'s synchronous encoder depends on, so on a Node 26 host every** `cbor.encode()` **of a value longer than one byte returns only its first byte. Host-side test runs are affected; the deployed images are not. The failure mode is fail-closed.**

## The mechanism

Node commit `fadb214d95` / PR 60441, *"stream: readable read one buffer at a time"*, is listed **semver-major in the v26.0.0 changelog** (2026-05-05): `Readable.prototype.read()` with no size argument no longer concatenates the internal buffer, it returns one queued chunk. Deliberate, to avoid the cost of merging buffers — **so this is not a bug and no Node patch will restore the old behaviour.** *(Commit, PR and changelog entry identified via web search, not read at source.)*

`cbor`'s synchronous `encode()` / `encodeOne()` / `encodeCanonical()` are all `_encodeAll` (`encoder.js:595-602`):

```js
_encodeAll(objs) { const bs = new NoFilter({…}); this.pipe(bs); … this.end(); return bs.read() }
```

`NoFilter.read(size)` (`nofilter@3.1.0`, `lib/index.js:285`) delegates straight to `super.read(size)`. Its own documented contract is "no size argument → return all the data in the internal buffer", which is exactly what Node 26 withdrew.

## Measured on this host (Node v26.8.1, `cbor@9.0.2`)

| value encoded | returned | correct |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `['Signature1', …]` | `84` (1 B) | \~90 B |
| `'Signature1'` | `6a` (1 B) | `6a5369676e617475726531` |
| `Buffer.alloc(4,0xab)` | `44` (1 B) | `44abababab` |
| `Map{1:-8}` | `a1` (1 B) | `a10127` |
| `Map{1:1,3:-8,-1:6,-2:<32B>}` | `a4` (1 B) | \~45 B |

Not container-specific — **every** value whose encoding exceeds one byte is truncated. `7` and `Map{}` come back correct only because they are one byte already, which is what makes this quiet. Decoding a truncated value throws `Insufficient data`.

Scoped to the synchronous path: `cbor.encodeAsync` **is correct** (`83010203`) and **the decoder is healthy** (`decodeFirstSync('83010203')` → `[1,2,3]`).

## It is the runtime, proven with zero dependencies and a second runtime

Pure `stream.PassThrough`, 4 bytes written as 3 chunks, no packages involved:

|  | Node v26.8.1 | Node v24.22.1 |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 3 chunks, `read()` | `83` | `83010203` |
| 3 chunks + `end()`, `read()` | `83` | `83010203` |
| one 4-byte chunk, `read()` *(control)* | `83010203` | `83010203` |
| `read(4)` explicit size | `83010203` | `83010203` |

The control discriminates, so the zero is a real zero. Successive `read()` calls on Node 26 return `83`,`01`,`0203` in order — the bytes are all present, merely no longer concatenated. `read(readableLength)` is the documented approximation and was verified on Node 26.

Node 24 runs were in throwaway `docker run --rm node:24-alpine` containers from an image already present on the host; nothing was installed, downloaded or built. This laptop has **only** Homebrew `node@26` (v26.8.1) — no Node 24, no nvm/fnm/volta/asdf.

## Items

### (a) Remedy options — no choice made, this needs a ruling

1. **Pin the dev/test runtime to Node 24**, which is what every image already ships: tighten `engines.node` (today the root is `>=18.0.0`, which *permits* Node 26) and add a runtime file (`.nvmrc` / `.node-version`) so host runs match the images. There is currently **no** `.nvmrc` in the repo and `packages/shared` declares **no** `engines` **at all**.
2. **An upstream fix in** `cbor` **and/or** `nofilter` — have `_encodeAll` read the whole buffer (`read(readableLength)`, or drain in a loop and concatenate). Not filed upstream by this investigation; `cbor`/`nofilter` issue trackers were **not** searched.
3. ⚠ **Not an option: bumping** `cbor`**.** `cbor@10.0.12` **is broken identically — measured**, not assumed, against an on-disk copy under `@meshsdk/provider`: all four cases truncate the same way. **The open dependabot PR 635 (**`cbor` **9.0.2 → 10.0.12) does NOT fix this.**

### (b) KS-1727 is the first known symptom

`packages/shared/src/__tests__/wallet-signature.test.ts:47-49`, the file's only positive cell. `verifyMessageSignature` exits at `wallet.ts:372` (`CIP-8: failed to extract Ed25519 public key from COSEKey`) because the COSEKey the test hands it is the 1-byte `a4`. **Both** `wallet.ts` **and the test are correct**; the four negative cells pass only because all four assert `false`, which a verifier that always returns false satisfies. On Node 24, same cbor bytes from the same disk, the positive cell `RETURNS TRUE` **(**`wallet.ts:418`**)** and the negative exits at `:391` (payload mismatch), so the KS 278 payload binding is intact.

### (c) Related — flagged, not investigated

* **KS 1734** — `services/security`, 11 of 33 test files fail on the first run after `npm ci`; records Node v26.
* **KS 1729** — vc-issuer unit suite cold-run skips; records Node v26.
* **KS 1625** — the standing contradiction that admits a Node 26 host at all: declared Node floor `engines.node >=18.0.0` versus what the images actually ship.

None of these was examined for this cause. They are named because they share the runtime, not because a link was measured.

## Scope — deployed services are NOT affected

* **All 32 Dockerfiles pin** `node:24-alpine` (75 `FROM` lines, zero exceptions), `originate` included — the service hosting `/sign-wallet`. Node 24 encodes correctly, so no deployed route carries this. **No deployed route was called.**
* The only synchronous `cbor.encode` in tracked production source is `wallet.ts:397`; the other five occurrences are inside the test file. Two `decodeFirstSync` sites, both on the healthy decoder.
* Where it would bite on a Node 26 host, it **fails closed**: a real wallet supplies a properly-encoded COSEKey, so the failure lands at `:397` and surfaces as `Ed25519 signature verification failed` — valid signatures rejected, never invalid ones accepted. **Not a forgery surface.**

## Searched first

By symbol, file path and error string, titles + descriptions, `includeArchived: true`: `cbor.encode`, `nofilter`, `Readable.read`, `_encodeAll`, `encodeAsync`, `readableHighWaterMark` — **0 hits each**. `verifyMessageSignature` → 2 hits, KS-1727 and KS 1229 (Done). Control: the same instrument returns 25 hits for `node:24-alpine` and 3 for `Node v26`, so it can fire.

## UNMEASURED

* Whether the transitive `cbor` consumers (`services/anchoring`, `services/nft-certificate`, `frontend/issuer` lockfiles, `@meshsdk/provider`) call the synchronous encode internally — not traced.
* Whether `cbor` or `nofilter` upstream has a fix or an open issue for Node ≥26.
* Which other packages on this laptop depend on the same withdrawn `read()` contract — the repo-wide blast radius of Node 26 beyond CBOR.
* When host runs first moved to Node 26, and when KS-1727's cell began failing (develop was not bisected).

Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-26_seatV-2nd/` — 8 probes, 19 output files, secret-scanned.

title: No supported way to put a user in a second tenant on a local stack — needed for cross-tenant systemTest peers (split from KS-1674)
description:
**BLUF:** systemTest needs two ordinary (non-super-admin) users in two **different** tenants on a local slot, so the Schemathesis `object_level_authorization` check (BOLA/IDOR, WFC 906) can test cross-tenant isolation. On develop there is no supported route that does this. This ticket asks for that capability; how it is built is your call. The systemTest side is a separate ticket, blocked by this one.

## Why it is needed

[KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) (PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1673](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1674-schemathesis-object-level-authorization-runs-in-its-own-aec22065af81), merged as `5671d5115`) runs `object_level_authorization` with two OWNER peers in the **same** tenant (`systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis_tests.yaml:650-668`). The ticket asked for peers across two tenants. Without them, cross-tenant exposure on findings such as [KS-1703](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1703/security-seven-get-by-id-routes-serve-any-authenticated-callers-object) is inferred, not measured.

## Why the existing routes do not work (read on develop `5f6899918`; nothing run)

1. **Self-registration lands in the default tenant.** `POST /api/auth/register` takes the tenant from `x-tenant-id` / `x-tenant-slug` (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:217-218`), but the gateway strips client-sent trust headers (`services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:309-330`). A tenantless token is then given `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:503`).
2. **Tenant from email domain at login is off, and would not persist.** `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:549-586` runs only when `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` (defaults to `false` in `docker-compose.yml`). Its own comment says the `UPDATE users SET tenant_id` is a no-op under fail-closed RLS ([KS-458](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-458/rls-fail-closed-flip-guc-on-checkout-flip-the-consolidated-tenant)).
3. `X-Tenant-Override` **applies only to super-admin roles** (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:515-521`). A super-admin can read every object, so it cannot act as a peer. (The override is also partly broken: [KS-1704](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1704/security-two-cross-tenant-isolation-regressions-fail-on-develop-a).)
4. **Invited stub then register keeps the stub's tenant** (`auth.ts:237-242`, [KS-74](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-74/pending-invite-ux-post-apicertificationsissue-accepts-holderemail-and)), but `POST /api/users/stub` takes the tenant from the caller's own verified token (`services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:398`). A caller can only mint stubs in a tenant they are already in.
5. **Not verified:** a connector token carries its own tenant (`services/auth/src/middleware/authenticate.ts:116`) and is accepted on `/api/users/stub`. If a connector can be issued for a second tenant, that may already be a route. Worth checking before building anything new.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A documented, supported sequence of API calls, runnable on a local slot without editing the database by hand, that (a) creates or selects a second tenant and (b) leaves a named, non-super-admin user (OWNER or another self-service role) whose verified token carries that tenant's id.
2. The user can log in and is scoped to that tenant on later requests (the gateway forwards its `x-tenant-id`, not the default).
3. The sequence is described here, or in the relevant service docs, so systemTest can call it from `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts`.

Raised from [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) at Peter's request (2026-10-26). The systemTest follow-up is assigned to Peter and blocked by this ticket.

title: systemTest (Schemathesis): run the object_level_authorization leg with peers in two different tenants (split from KS-1674)
description:
> ⛔ **Blocked by** [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack) (2026-10-27). Parked until [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack) delivers a supported way to put a user in a second tenant on a local stack. No work starts here before then.

**BLUF:** [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) made Schemathesis's `object_level_authorization` check (BOLA/IDOR, WFC 906, ST402) run in its own `[auth.wfc]` leg, but with two OWNER peers in the **same** tenant. This ticket is the remaining part of [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under)'s scope: peers in two **different** tenants, so cross-tenant exposure is measured rather than inferred. It is blocked by [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack), which asks for a supported way to put a user in a second tenant.

## Today (develop, after PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1673](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1674-schemathesis-object-level-authorization-runs-in-its-own-aec22065af81), `5671d5115`)

* Peers: `["owner", "ownerPeer"]`, both OWNER in the default tenant (`systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis_tests.yaml:650-668`; actors in `systemTest/fixtures/actors.ts`, provisioned by `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts`).
* Why: no local route places a user in a second tenant. The reasons are in [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack).

## Scope (once [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack) lands)

* Provision a peer in the second tenant through the route [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack) delivers (API only; no direct database writes).
* Point the leg's peers at the cross-tenant pair. Whether to keep the same-tenant pair as well (two leg runs, or three peers) is decided in the plan.
* Update the comment above the leg config, which today records the cross-tenant pairing as remaining scope on [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under).

## Acceptance criteria

Every new pair from the first live run is triaged: an existing ticket ([KS-1703](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1703/security-seven-get-by-id-routes-serve-any-authenticated-callers-object), [KS-1704](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1704/security-two-cross-tenant-isolation-regressions-fail-on-develop-a)) or a new KS ticket, never masked or baselined without an owner.

title: m365 OAuth callback: a provider error_description of ~170+ astral characters makes the nginx edge answer 502 ("upstream sent too big header") instead of the redirect - on develop
description:
**BLUF:** On **develop**, the public `GET /api/m365/callback` with a long provider `error_description` made of 4-byte characters (emoji) gets **502 BAD_GATEWAY from the nginx edge**. m365 and api-gateway both answer the expected 302. [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route)'s merged 200-code-point cap keeps the redirect `Location` bounded, at about 2,460 characters, but not small enough for the edge: together with the gateway's other response headers it passes the edge's response-header buffer. Nothing crashes. The admin sees a gateway error instead of the OAuth outcome. Kamil, I'd be grateful for your view on the fix below.

## Where and when (develop)

The product code under test was **develop, unchanged**. The two builds below differ from develop only by a systemTest-only commit ([KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route)'s new test file and docs), so no product code differed.

| Build | Product = develop at | Build started (UTC) | Stack |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `4111d0cf6` | `8661f5d41` | 2026-10-26 10:45:05 | platform-k slot 1, Peter's Mac |
| `65ced3173` | `5f689991861b3b9be295797a437ef18b6f55a492` | 2026-10-26 11:17:45 | platform-k slot 1, Peter's Mac |

Image revision labels on api-gateway, originate, m365-integration and nginx-gateway matched each build. Every container was healthy, with RestartCount 0 before and after.

**Seen 5 of 5 runs** on 2026-10-26: targeted runs at 10:59 (build `4111d0cf6`) and 11:37, the full pre-merge sweep at 11:38-11:56, and the two re-check rounds at 12:18 and 12:20 (all on `65ced3173`).

**Not measured on a develop-only harness:** the develop control sweep that day (slot 2, develop `5f6899918`, built 2026-10-26 12:20:09 UTC) has no test for this route, because the test is new on the [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) branch. The product code was identical in every run, so the result applies to develop.

## What was measured

Request (unauthenticated, as Microsoft's redirect is): `GET /api/m365/callback?error=access_denied&error_description=` + 400 × U+1F600, URL-encoded.

| Layer | Answer | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| m365-integration | 302 | its log: `OAuth callback error`, then `Request completed … statusCode 302` |
| api-gateway | 302 | its log: `path /api/callback, statusCode 302` |
| nginx edge (`secuura-nginx-gateway`) | **502** | `upstream sent too big header while reading response header from upstream, client: 192.168.65.1, server: localhost, request: "GET /api/m365/callback?error=access_denied&error_description=%F0%9F%98%80…` |
| caller | **502** | `{"success":false,"error":{"code":"BAD_GATEWAY","message":"The upstream service is not reachable right now."}}` |

**Control:** 150 × U+1F600 passes: 302, `Location` 1,860 characters, about 3,676 bytes of response headers in total. ASCII descriptions of 5,000 characters and a 199-character string with an emoji at the boundary also pass (302, bounded).

**Not a missing service** (the usual meaning of a 502 here, per DEV-PROCESS.md): all 33 services were up and healthy, and nginx names the cause.

## Cause: verified and assumed

* **Verified:** the edge rejects the upstream's response headers as too large. The 200-code-point cap makes the reflected `message` up to 200 × 12 = 2,400 encoded characters for astral text.
* **Assumed, not verified:** the edge uses nginx's default `proxy_buffer_size`, which is one memory page, usually 4 KB. `nginx -T` in the container shows no `proxy_buffer_size` or `proxy_buffers` directive.
* **Inferred, not measured:** the demo VM puts the same nginx gateway behind Caddy, so it is likely to behave the same.

## Suggested fix

The fix [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) already recommends removes this: put only a short **code** on the redirect URL (for example the provider's `error` code), and keep the provider's `error_description` in the server log only, as `services/auth` does. Then the `Location` stays small whatever the provider sends. Raising the edge's `proxy_buffer_size` would also stop the 502, but it would leave the reflection in place.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Automated test:** `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_m365_callback_redirect.py::TestM365CallbackReflectedText::test_ks1641_oversized_description_keeps_the_redirect_bounded_and_the_service_up[400-astral-code-points]` (added on the [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) branch) passes on a slot built from the fix: a 302 with a `Location` of at most 2,500 characters, and the service answers the next callback. A service-level unit cell with the same 400-emoji input asserting a 302 is also wanted. No UI surface, so no Playwright test applies.
2. **Docs:** if the codes-only fix lands, no doc change beyond [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route)'s. If the edge buffer is changed instead, document the value and the reason beside the nginx config.
3. **systemTests:** no further change; the cell above already exists. Update `systemTest/schemathesis/docs/known-issues-and-baseline.md` → [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) when it turns green.

Classification tags: platform-k has no `test_taxonomy.ts`, so none are given.

**Related:** [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) (the reflection and redirect target; the merged cap this follows from), [KS-1670](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1670/m365-integration-three-more-reflection-sites-from-gate-am1-an) (other reflection sites in the same file).

*Raised on Peter's instruction, 2026-10-26, from the* [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) *test pass. Duplicate searches, KS and PS, including archived, all with no match: "upstream sent too big header", "proxy_buffer_size", "nginx 502 Location header", "m365 callback 502". Closest:* [KS-529](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529/gateway-intermittent-502-bad-gateway-to-healthy-upstreams-under-sweep) *(Done) and* [KS-1369](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1369/api-gateway-crashes-under-load-onproxyreq-calls-setheader-after-the) *(In Progress), both gateway 502s under load, a different cause.*

title: POST /api/documents with a 10,000-character title answers 500 instead of a 4xx - on develop
description:
**BLUF:** On **develop**, `POST /api/documents` with `{"title": "x" × 10000}` answers **500** (an 89-byte body) instead of a clean 4xx. The other nine fuzzed titles in the same test pass: empty, NUL, XSS, whitespace, emoji, CJK, Hebrew, SQL-like and path-like. Nothing is logged by originate or api-gateway, so the cause is not visible from the logs. The likely cause is below, marked as unverified. Kamil, I'd be grateful if you could take a look.

## Where and when (develop)

| Run | Build / product | Build started (UTC) | Stack | Result |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **develop control** pre-merge sweep, 12:23-12:40, seed 2391897950 | **develop** `5f689991861b3b9be295797a437ef18b6f55a492` (clean develop worktree) | 2026-10-26 12:20:09 | platform-k slot 2, Peter's Mac | **500** |
| pre-merge sweep, 11:38-11:56, same seed | `65ced3173` = develop `5f6899918` + a systemTest-only commit | 2026-10-26 11:17:45 | platform-k slot 1 | 500 |
| targeted re-check, 12:17:45 | same | same | slot 1 | 500 |
| targeted re-check, 12:19:52 | same | same | slot 1 | 500 |

**Seen 4 of 4 runs, including on clean develop.** Every container was healthy with RestartCount 0. Image revision labels matched each build.

## What was measured

* **Test:** `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_fuzz_comprehensive.py::test_string_parameter_fuzzing[xxxx…]`, failing with `AssertionError: KS-1042: title 'xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx' → 500 | assert 500 < 500`. The test's contract is "never a 5xx, and a refusal carries an error body". A 201 is acceptable for legitimate titles. Caller: ISSUER_ADMIN, which holds documents:write.
* **Edge:** nginx `"POST /api/documents HTTP/1.1" 500 89` at 11:40:41, 12:17:45 and 12:19:52.
* **api-gateway:** `method POST, path /api/documents, statusCode 500, duration 4-5ms`, with no error line before it.
* **originate:** no error line for these requests in its log.

## Cause: verified and assumed

* **Verified from source (develop):** the published `DocumentCreateRequest.title` (`services/originate/src/originate.openapi.ts`) is `z.string()` with **no** `maxLength`. `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:97` declares a `title VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL` column.
* **Assumed, not verified:** the 10,000-character title reaches the insert and Postgres refuses it (`22001`, value too long), which surfaces as a 500. I have not confirmed that `:97` is the table this route writes, or that the refusal is what produces the 500. Nothing is logged, which is itself worth fixing, in the same way as [KS-1510](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1510/get-apiplatformdocument-lookup-answers-a-constant-500-and-logs-nothing).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Automated test:** the existing `test_string_parameter_fuzzing[xxxx…]` cell passes on a slot built from the fix: a 4xx with the error envelope, or a 201 if long titles are accepted by design. Plus a service-level unit cell in originate that sends a title one character over the limit and asserts a 400 with a field-named message. No UI surface, so no Playwright test applies.
2. **Docs:** the spec declares the real bound: `maxLength` on `DocumentCreateRequest.title` at the generator, then `npm run generate-openapi`, with api-gateway rebuilt or restarted so it serves the new spec. No other doc change.
3. **systemTests:** no change needed; the cell already exists and turns green with the fix. If Schemathesis then reports a `negative_data_rejection` pair for the new bound, it is triaged separately.

Duplicate searches, KS and PS, including archived, with no match: "document title length 500", "title maxLength", "value too long for type character varying".* [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema)*'s three 500s are on other routes.*

title: m365 OAuth callback product fix (split from KS-1641): repoint the five redirects to a declared admin route, and put only a short code on the redirect URL
description:
**BLUF:** This is the **product-code half** of [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route), split out on Peter's instruction (2026-10-26) so [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) can close on its systemTest work. Two changes are needed in m365-integration and the admin app. [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route)'s systemTest cells already exist and are **red on develop**. They are this ticket's acceptance test and turn green when the fix lands. Kamil, I'd be grateful if you could take this one.

## The two findings (re-read at develop `5f689991861b3b9be295797a437ef18b6f55a492`, 2026-10-26)

**Finding 1: no redirect lands on a route the admin app declares.** All five admin-facing redirects in `Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` target `/admin/integrations`: `:626` provider error, `:630` missing code or state, `:644` invalid state, `:677` **success**, `:684` token exchange failed.

* The admin app is mounted at `/admin/` with `<BrowserRouter basename="/admin">`, so that URL is matched as `/integrations`. `frontend/admin/src/App.tsx` declares no such route.
* The browser therefore falls to `path="*"` and lands on `/`, and the OAuth outcome is lost.
* "Integrations" is a tab inside `/settings` (`frontend/admin/src/pages/Settings.tsx`). Settings opens on `useState('general')` and reads no tab from the URL.

**Finding 2: provider and internal text is reflected into the redirect URL.**

* `:626` puts the provider's `error_description` on the URL. [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1622](https://linear.app/secuura/review/refs-ks-1641-1-of-3-sites-bound-the-provider-error-text-the-m365-oauth-02f753c1f67e) caps it at 200 code points but still reflects it.
* `:684` puts MSAL's `err.message` on the URL, uncapped.

[KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) recommends following `services/auth`: log the detail, put only a short code on the URL. The cap also leaves a bounded but large `Location` that the nginx edge refuses with **502** for long astral input ([KS-1742](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1742/m365-oauth-callback-a-provider-error-description-of-170-astral)).

## What to change ([KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route)'s recommendation)

1. **Finding 2 first, or with finding 1**, because repointing the redirects is what makes the reflected text render:
   * On the provider-error redirect, use a short **code** (the provider's `error`, restricted to `[a-z_]`), not `error_description`.
   * Make `:684` send `token_exchange_failed`.
   * Keep the detail in the (capped) log and in `connection.errorMessage`.
   * Encode `connectionId` on `:677` ([KS-1670](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1670/m365-integration-three-more-reflection-sites-from-gate-am1-an) site 1).
2. **Finding 1:** repoint all five redirects to `/admin/settings` with a tab query the page reads (for example `?tab=integrations&m365=…&message=…`), and teach `Settings.tsx` to open the tab from the URL. If anything renders the outcome, it should render known codes from a fixed table, never URL text.

Note: the connect flow starts in `M365SetupWizard` (inside `IntegrationHub`, under `/platform/clients/:id?tab=integrations`) and opens the Microsoft sign-in in a popup, so the redirect lands in that popup. [KS-1678](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1678/m365-admin-setup-wizard-sends-a-secuura-tenant-id-as-organizationid) records that the connection's `organizationId` is the caller's org, not the client id, so a redirect back to `/platform/clients/:id` cannot be built reliably. Hence `/admin/settings`, as [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) recommends.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Automated tests:**
   * [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route)'s `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_m365_callback_redirect.py`: the three `test_ks1641_redirect_targets_a_declared_admin_route` cells, the three `test_ks1641_error_description_never_reaches_the_redirect` cells, and `test_ks1641_oversized_description_keeps_the_redirect_bounded_and_the_service_up[400-astral-code-points]` ([KS-1742](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1742/m365-oauth-callback-a-provider-error-description-of-170-astral)) all **pass** on a slot built from the fix. The other three stay green.
   * m365 unit cells for each of the five redirects (target path and code-only `message`), including a non-ASCII and a 400-emoji description, and `:684` never carrying `err.message`.
   * A browser test that `/admin/settings?tab=integrations` opens the Integrations tab (the `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e` suite; platform-k's systemTest Playwright is API-only).
2. **Docs:** the `/admin/integrations` wording in `services/m365-integration/src/m365-integration.openapi.ts` (then `npm run generate-openapi`, and restart or rebuild api-gateway), `USER_TESTING/M365-Integration-Test-Guide.md:65`, the comment in `deployment/azure/services.bicep`, and the comment in `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/test_workflows_http.py`.
3. **systemTests:** no test change needed if the redirects target `/admin/settings`. If a new admin route is declared instead, update `ADMIN_DECLARED_ROUTES` in the test from this ticket's PR. On green, update the [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) section of `systemTest/schemathesis/docs/known-issues-and-baseline.md`.

Classification tags: platform-k has no `test_taxonomy.ts`, so none are given.

## Measured state today

Developed under [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route)'s systemTest pass on Peter's Mac, 2026-10-26, at develop `5f6899918`:

* slot 1, built 11:17:45 UTC;
* develop control on slot 2, built 12:20:09 UTC.

The six finding cells were red in all 5 runs. The full results are on [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route).

**Related:** [KS-1641](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1641/m365-oauth-redirects-all-target-adminintegrations-which-is-not-a-route) (origin; systemTest coverage), [KS-1742](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1742/m365-oauth-callback-a-provider-error-description-of-170-astral) (edge 502, cleared by finding 2), [KS-1670](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1670/m365-integration-three-more-reflection-sites-from-gate-am1-an) (other reflection sites; site 1 above), [KS-1678](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1678/m365-admin-setup-wizard-sends-a-secuura-tenant-id-as-organizationid) (organisation id in the wizard), [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1622](https://linear.app/secuura/review/refs-ks-1641-1-of-3-sites-bound-the-provider-error-text-the-m365-oauth-02f753c1f67e) (the merged cap).
