title: api-gateway: specRouteMap.ts:47 arms the edge auth gate only for bearerAuth, so GET /api/connector/info (connectorApiKey only) is absent from authedMethods
description:
## BLUF

`specRouteMap.ts:47` **arms the gateway's edge auth gate only for** `bearerAuth`**, so an operation secured by any other scheme is not armed there.** As of 27 Oct this is no longer hypothetical: `GET /api/connector/info` **is the first published operation secured by** `connectorApiKey` **alone**, and it is therefore absent from `authedMethods`. Facts only — whether this is a defect is for the board. Raised by the tier-1 gate on #1732 as the U2 item.

Refs KS-1531, KS-944.

## The code, read at develop `c3eb63c9d23b08132482f3211dbf8755312a7ca0`

`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/specRouteMap.ts:47`, verbatim:

```
      if (Array.isArray(security) && security.some((s) => s && typeof s === 'object' && 'bearerAuth' in s)) {
```

`'bearerAuth'` is the only scheme name in the file that affects behaviour — three occurrences in all: `:27` (the field comment on `authedMethods`), `:45` (the comment above the test) and `:47` (the test itself). `authedMethods.add(upper)` at `:48` is reached only through it.

The consumer is `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts`: `resolveSpecRoute` at `:1064`, and the auth branch at `:1084` `if (authedMethods.has(upperMethod)) {`. `buildSpecMethodMap` is called at `:612` and again at `:654` (the spec-reload path).

## What the published spec now declares — measured

In `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, `securitySchemes` is at `:83` and declares exactly **two** schemes: `bearerAuth` (`:84`) and `connectorApiKey` (`:89`).

Per-operation usage across the whole file: **311** `- bearerAuth` lines, **2** `- connectorApiKey` lines. The two `connectorApiKey` uses resolve as:

| operation | security block | schemes | armed at the edge gate? |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /api/connector/info` (path `:15961`, method `:15962`) | `:15971-15972` | `connectorApiKey` **only** | **no** |
| `POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector` (path `:36426`, method `:36427`) | `:36440-36442` | `bearerAuth` **and** `connectorApiKey` | yes — on the `bearerAuth` entry |

So of the two operations using the scheme, **one is secured by it alone**, and that one is not armed. The source of that declaration is `services/api-gateway/src/api-gateway.openapi.ts:908` — `security: [{ connectorApiKey: [] }]`.

## Why this is not currently an exposure, and why that is not reassuring

The tier-1 gate on #1732 mutated the yaml declaration to `bearerAuth` and recorded the 28-cell behaviour matrix as **byte-identical** — the GET is answered before the edge gate is reached, so arming it changes nothing for this route today. **That ordering is the gate's measurement and I did not reproduce it:** the verdict cites `index.ts:837` for the health router and `:1054` for the edge gate, neither of which matches this tree (see above), and the symbol `createHealthRouter` does not occur in `index.ts`. Treat the ordering as the gate's claim, not as established here.

What stands without that claim is the structural fact: the edge gate's notion of "this operation requires authentication" is **narrower than the spec's**, and it is narrow in a way no reader of the spec would expect. An operation that is authenticated by declaration is unauthenticated by the gate.

## Prior art, read and not a duplicate

**KS-944** (Done, archived) — *"The gateway's auth gate reads the spec's* `security: []` *— nothing pins the four public wallet ops"* — is the same mechanism and the same line. It was closed by a cell (`services/auth/src/__tests__/ks944-the-gateway-s-auth-gate-reads.test.ts`) pinning the wallet operations' declarations, paired with a reverse `bearerAuth` assertion. **It reasoned about exactly two cases,** `[]` **and** `bearerAuth`, because at the time those were the only two in the spec. A third case now exists and KS-944's cell does not speak to it.

**KS-1469** (In Progress) — a trailing slash skipping the spec method and auth gate — is a different mechanism (path matching, not scheme matching) on the same gate.

## Not established

* Whether any operation *should* be armed by `connectorApiKey` at the edge. That is the contract question this ticket hands to the board; no behaviour is proposed.
* The router ordering that makes today's instance harmless (above).
* Whether a future operation secured by `connectorApiKey` alone would be answered before the edge gate the way this one is. Nothing was measured about any other route.
* No suite was run and no request was issued. This is a source and spec read.

## Searched (board, KS team, title + description + comments, archived and Done included)

* `specRouteMap` — **6 hits**: KS-1531, KS-1469, KS-1358, KS-944 (archived), KS-120 (archived), KS-118 (archived).
* `authedMethods` — **3 hits**: KS-1531, KS-946, KS-944 (archived).
* `bearerAuth` — scanned; the hits are the same gateway-gate family above.

title: CLASS: a module-level beforeAll that imports a router pays the cold Vite transform inside the hook budget - five locations, two fix shapes, no owner for the pattern
description:
## BLUF

**A test file whose module-level** `beforeAll` **imports a router pays the cold Vite transform inside the hook's budget, so the whole file's cells are skipped when the machine is loaded.** Five locations have hit this independently. Each has been fixed in its own place, by two different shapes, and **no ticket owns the pattern** — so the next service to grow such a file is on the default budget again. This ticket records the class and asks for one decision: a fleet-wide convention, or an explicit statement that per-location budgets are the convention.

Facts only; nothing is built and no fix is chosen. Raised as the class behind the tier-2 gate on #1727.

Refs KS-1734, KS-1602, KS-1155, KS-1328, KS-1729.

## The five instances, by key

| ticket | location | state | shape of the fix |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **KS-1734** | `services/security` — 10 files lapsed the 10 s hook, 1 test lapsed 5 s | merged `5c40e82cb539` | service-wide `hookTimeout`/`testTimeout` 60 s in `vitest.config.ts` |
| **KS-1602** | `services/security`, `ks742-keys-tenancy-route-contract.test.ts` alone | In Progress | explicit per-hook budget in the one file |
| **KS-1155** | `packages/shared` tree-walking guards over the 5 s default | In Progress | not read here |
| **KS-1328** | `services/kyc`, `db.retry.test.ts` | In Review | not read here |
| **KS-1729** | `vc-issuer` — first run after `npm ci` skips 110 cells, three files cold-import routers | Done | not read here |

The two shapes are in tension: KS-1602 budgets one file, KS-1734 budgets a whole service. Both are live in `services/security` at once — KS-1734's comment records that KS-1602's explicit per-hook budget "still overrides the default underneath, so that file's behaviour is unchanged."

## What #1727's gate measured, and the figure to carry

From the tier-2 gate on #1727 (`2026-10-27_gate-t3r4-batch/verdict.md`) and the evidence recorded on KS-1734, **quoted, not re-run by me**:

* The knob governs the failure class: `hookTimeout` forced to 25 ms → **18 files red**; `testTimeout` 25 ms → **11 files red**.
* The full ladder, each rung on a cold `.vite` cache: 1 ms → 23 of 33 files; 25 ms → 20; 100 ms → 19; 400 ms → 8; 1000 ms → 0; 10000 ms (the replaced default) → 0.
* **The governed population is WIDER than the ten files KS-1734 named.** 19 of 33 files already exceed a 100 ms hook. KS-1734's own comment carries this as a correction to its first wording — the PR had claimed the knob "governs exactly the files the ticket names", and the accurate figure is 18 at the `hookTimeout` rung, not 10.
* The hooks finish under 1 s at load1 3.3–6.6, against the 10 000 ms they blew at load1 11.21: **a >10x inflation under contention.**
* **Contention, not coldness, is the driver.** Four cold first-runs after `npm ci` at load1 3.31–4.44 each passed 33/33 — so KS-1734's red did not reproduce, and the budget change has **no red→green pair** behind it.

## The decision this ticket asks for

Not which budget — that is settled per location. The open question is the **convention**: a file that imports a router at module level inside `beforeAll` will exceed a short hook budget on a loaded box, and the budget masks the cost rather than removing it. Either

1. state a fleet-wide rule (for example: every service's `vitest.config.ts` carries a budget that clears the observed contention inflation, as `services/security` and its `vitest.integration.config.ts` now do), or
2. state that per-location budgets are the convention and that a new file is expected to set its own,

so that the sixth location is a known case rather than a new ticket.

## Not established

* No suite was run for this ticket and no measurement here is mine. Every figure above is quoted from the #1727 gate verdict or from KS-1734's comment.
* **Whether the cold Vite transform is the mechanism** in KS-1155, KS-1328 and KS-1729. Those three are cited from KS-1734's own "Same class, other places" list; their bodies were **not** read here, so the shared mechanism is KS-1734's attribution, not a finding of this ticket.
* Whether any location other than `services/security` currently lacks a budget. Not surveyed.
* Whether the >10x inflation figure generalises beyond `services/security` at this load.

## Searched (board, KS team, title + description + comments, archived and Done included)

* `module-level beforeAll` — **0 hits**. `cold transform` — **0 hits**. `Vite transform` — **0 hits**. So no class ticket exists under any of those names.
* `hookTimeout` — **4 hits**: KS-1734, KS-1729, KS-1602, KS-1155 — the four instances, no class ticket.
* `first run after` — **4 hits**: KS-1739 (a Node 26 cbor defect, unrelated), KS-1734, KS-1729, KS-1053.
* `vitest.config.ts` — **12 hits**; the timeout family among them is the five instances above, the rest unrelated (KS-1582, KS-1319, KS-993, KS-846, KS-830, KS-177, KS-149).
* **Positive controls, same instrument and session:** `KS-1531` → 5 hits, `run_shell_suites` → 35 hits. **Zero control:** `zzqqxx-no-such-symbol-9931` → 0 hits.
* **Decision recorded:** KS-1734 was read in full. This is **not** its residue — KS-1734 is scoped to `services/security` and its fix covers that whole service. What is unowned is the pattern across services, which is why this is filed rather than commented there.

*Filed by Seat G 22nd, 2026-10-27, on Wednesday's brief.*

title: Retire the Schemathesis unexpected-methods suppression released by Kam's KS-1358 ruling: three places still state the superseded KS-406 posture, plus a stale pin path
description:
## BLUF

**Kam ruled on 2026-10-27 that 405 +** `Allow` **before authentication stands and KS-406 is superseded. The Schemathesis harness still suppresses the probes that ruling released, and three places still carry KS-406's rationale as current.** KS-1358's own closing comment says this retirement "is follow-up work that nobody has picked up yet" — this ticket is that work, so it has an owner. Facts only; nothing changed.

Refs KS-1358, KS-406.

⚠ **This is not a question.** The brief that ordered this filing framed it as *"ask whether the suppression is still needed"*. It is not needed — that was decided. The three file:line facts below are what is left to act on.

## The ruling

From KS-1358's comment of 2026-10-26T21:15:26Z (comment id `82451a21-f7f0-4af3-b45c-21a5061392f8`), quoting the decision card `secuura-ks1358-405-before-auth-posture-1027`, verbatim:

> `Decision secuura-ks1358-405-before-auth-posture-1027: a — Keep 405 + Allow before auth: KS-406 superseded (recommended)`

and, from the same comment:

> **Not done here, and not in the KS-1531 change:** the harness still suppresses those probes (`unexpected-methods = []`, recorded as `DRIFT-METHOD-405`). Retiring the suppression and asserting 405 is follow-up work that nobody has picked up yet; no harness file was touched.

KS-1358 recorded the scale of what the suppression costs: across one full sweep's undeclared-method probes, **405 ×1,760**, 204 ×307 (OPTIONS), 404 ×29, 401 ×2 — and its option 1 states retiring the suppression "turns \~1,760 requests per sweep into real coverage."

## The three places, read at develop `c3eb63c9d23b08132482f3211dbf8755312a7ca0`

**1. The suppression itself.** `systemTest/schemathesis/schemathesis.toml:126` — `unexpected-methods = []`, under `[phases.coverage]` at `:125`. The rationale above it, `:118-123`, states the superseded posture as current:

> `authenticated route by design (228 findings = 100% of the 2026-07-07 sweep's` / `failures), so we stop generating those probes rather than asserting a 405 the` / `platform deliberately does not send.`

"a 405 the platform deliberately does not send" is now false: the platform does send it.

**2. A test asserts the suppression holds.** `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/functional/config/test_coverage_unexpected_methods.py` — the assert is at `:36` (`assert coverage.unexpected_methods == set()`), and its failure message at `:37-39` repeats the superseded rationale:

> `"schemathesis.toml must set [phases.coverage] unexpected-methods = [] — "` / `"auth-first 401 on undeclared methods is the intended posture (KS-406); "` / `"restoring the probes re-fails` `unsupported_method` `on every authenticated route."`

So retiring the suppression makes this test fail by design; it has to be retired or inverted in the same change. *(The brief cited* `:37` *for the assertion;* `:37` *is the first line of the message string,* `:36` *is the assert.)*

**3. The register prose.** `systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis_tests.yaml:977-982` records the check as inert for the same superseded reason:

> `KS-406 (2026-07-08): effectively INERT on this platform — schemathesis.toml sets` / `[phases.coverage] unexpected-methods = [] because auth-first 401 on undeclared methods is` / `the intended posture (auth runs before routing), so no unexpected-method probes are` / `generated for this check to judge.`

"auth runs before routing" is the claim the ruling reverses.

**4. A stale path, found while reading the above.** `schemathesis.toml:121` says the suppression is *"Pinned by tests/unit/test_coverage_unexpected_methods.py"*. The file is at `tests/functional/config/test_coverage_unexpected_methods.py`. The pointer names a path that does not exist.

## Not established

* **Whether 405 is what the probes would now meet on every undeclared method.** KS-1358's measurement was one sweep on slot 3 at develop `d9ce1403d` on 2026-09-28 — 405 ×1,760 but also 204 ×307, 404 ×29 and **401 ×2**. The 401 ×2 is unexplained in that record. Restoring the probes without accounting for the non-405 tail would trade a suppression for a baseline.
* **No sweep was run for this ticket.** Every figure above is KS-1358's.
* Whether `expected-statuses` or the `unsupported_method` check configuration needs a matching change. Not examined.
* Whether `DRIFT-METHOD-405` in `systemTest/schemathesis/docs/known-issues-and-baseline.md` is the only other record of the suppression. Only the four places above were read.

## Searched (board, KS team, title + description + comments, archived and Done included)

* `unexpected-methods` — **6 hits**: KS-1502 (Canceled, a version bump), **KS-1358** (Done — the ruling), KS-1270, KS-1268, KS-416, **KS-406** (all Done/archived).
* `DRIFT-METHOD-405` — **1 hit**, KS-1358 only.
* `retire the suppression` — **0 hits**. `unexpected_method` — **1 hit**, KS-1268 (archived, a pin bump).
* `test_coverage_unexpected_methods` — **1 hit**, KS-1268 (archived). `schemathesis.toml` — 50 hits, scanned; the posture family is the six above.
* **Positive controls, same instrument and session:** `KS-1531` → 5 hits, `run_shell_suites` → 35 hits. **Zero control:** `zzqqxx-no-such-symbol-9931` → 0 hits.
* **Decision recorded.** KS-1358 was read in full, state and comments. It is **Done** and its question is answered, so the ruling needs no further comment there; what it names as unowned is filed here instead. **KS-406** is Done and archived and was already commented as superseded per KS-1358's record.

title: kintsugi anchor_store: two rows are simulated=true AND status='confirmed' (block_number NULL) - a shape KS-587's Done-when and proposed guard both pass over
description:
## BLUF

**Kintsugi's** `anchor_store` **holds two rows that are simultaneously** `simulated = true` **and** `status = 'confirmed'`**.** An honestly-flagged placeholder that also claims a confirmed anchor is a contradictory pair, and it is **not** the shape KS-587 closed — KS-587's "Done when" is *satisfied* by these rows, and its proposed guard would not see them. Demo's 83 placeholder rows are the counter-case: all `failed`, all carrying an error_message.

Facts only. No row, box or code was touched, and no fix is proposed.

Refs KS-587, KS-520, KS-522.

## The measurement — Seat D 35th's, relayed, NOT re-measured here

⚠ **Provenance, stated plainly: every figure in this section is Seat D 35th's read-only measurement** of 2026-10-26T23:13Z (its STATUS A), relayed to this ticket by Wednesday. **I did not connect to either box and did not re-run any query.** Nothing here is mine.

**The two kintsugi rows:**

| field | both rows |
| -- | -- |
| created | 2026-08-20 |
| `transaction_hash` | `mock_tx_a6435a40…` and `mock_tx_2081b052…` (length **72**) |
| `simulated` | **true** |
| `status` | `confirmed` |
| `confirmations` | 1 |
| `block_number` | NULL |
| `error_message` | NULL |
| `network` | preview |

**Classifier control, same read:** over kintsugi's non-simulated rows, **31** real 64-hex hashes and **0** mock — so the classifier distinguishes the two populations rather than matching everything.

**The counter-case on demo:** **83** simulated rows, **all** `failed`, each with an error_message (the KS-587 corpus shape), and **0** simulated-and-confirmed.

## Why KS-587 does not cover this

KS-587 (Deployed to UAT, archived) — *"84 demo anchors carry mock_tx\_ hashes but are flagged simulated=false + confirmed"* — is the **inverse flag on a different box**. Read in full, three of its own lines decide the question:

* Its **"Done when"**: *"no row in* `anchor_store` *carries a mock/sim hash while claiming* `simulated = false`*, and the runbook covers reconciliation."* These rows carry `simulated = true`, so they **satisfy** it.
* Its **recommendation 1**: *"Reconcile the 84 rows — at minimum set* `simulated = true` *so the KS-520/522 honesty path engages and they stop claiming on-chain proof."* Setting `simulated = true` is exactly the state these rows are already in — and they still say `confirmed`, with `confirmations = 1`.
* Its **recommendation 3**: *"a* `mock_tx_`*/*`tx_sim_` *prefix with* `simulated = false` *is a contradiction that could be asserted in a test or a boot-time check."* That guard is keyed on `simulated = false`; it would read these two rows as correct.

So the residue KS-587 left is narrower than its own remedy assumed: the remedy addresses the **flag**, not the **status**, and `status = 'confirmed'` with `block_number` NULL was never in its scope.

KS-520 and KS-522 (both Done, archived) are the code-path pair — the fail-open fabrication, and the absence of an honest-labelling signal downstream. Neither is about rows already stored on a box.

## A documentation fact this bears on

The project's `CLAUDE.md` states that **zero** rows are `simulated = true` and `confirmed`. Per the relay, that figure was measured **on demo only**, where it holds (0 of 83). It is not true of kintsugi. *No repository file was edited by this ticket — recorded here so whoever picks this up knows the doc's scope.*

## Not established

* **How the two rows were written.** Unknown.
* **Whether any document reads them as anchored**, or is presented as verified on their basis. Not checked.
* **Whether the code path that produced them still exists.** Not checked.
* Whether `confirmations = 1` with `block_number` NULL is reachable through any current writer.
* Whether other boxes or environments hold rows in this presentation. Only kintsugi and demo were read, and by someone else.
* Anything about the correct remedy. Deleting, re-flagging or failing these rows is a product call, and the rows are **not** to be touched on the strength of this ticket.

## Searched (board, KS team, title + description + comments, archived and Done included)

* `mock_tx_` — **23 hits**. The nearest were read: **KS-587** (the inverse flag, demo, archived — decision above), KS-589 (archived; a Schemathesis anchor-honesty consistency test for `mock_tx_`), KS-1626 (In Progress; five placeholder checks still reading `mock_batch_`), KS-1485, KS-1634, KS-683.
* `simulated` — **50 hits**, scanned; the anchor-honesty family is the set above plus KS-1661, KS-1676, KS-1629, KS-1640, KS-1650.
* `anchor_store` — **50 hits**, scanned; none names a simulated-and-confirmed row.
* `KS-587` — **28 hits** (tickets citing it). `simulated+confirmed` — **0 hits**. `simulated = true` — **6 hits**: KS-1634, KS-683, KS-670, KS-589, KS-587, KS-519 — none is this presentation.
* `KS-520` / `KS-522` — both read in full; both Done and archived, both about the code path, neither about stored rows.
* **Positive controls, same instrument and session:** `KS-1531` → 5 hits, `run_shell_suites` → 35 hits. **Zero control:** `zzqqxx-no-such-symbol-9931` → 0 hits.

title: preflight.sh:722-724 derives the hook's controls from ${NAME:- only, so a control read as ${NAME}, ${NAME:?} or bare $NAME is not stripped — and broadening the pattern also catches the hook's own ZERO constant (KS-1643 nit 3)
description:
## BLUF

`preflight.sh:722-724` **derives the pre-push hook's control variables from one read shape,** `${NAME:-`**. A control read as** `${NAME}`**,** `${NAME:?}` **or bare** `$NAME` **is silently not stripped, so an in-hook suite would inherit it.** Zero such controls exist today, so nothing is missed now — this is the successor ticket the source comment and KS-1643 both say is needed, not a live defect.

**It cannot be closed by widening the pattern.** A pattern broad enough to catch the other read shapes also catches names the hook ASSIGNS itself, and stripping one of those would break the hook. Closing it needs a way to tell "read from the caller" from "assigned internally" — which is why KS-1643 recorded nit 3 and deliberately did not close it.

Nothing here is a fix. No shape is chosen and none is proposed.

Refs KS-1643 (the parent that recorded this as nit 3) and KS-1638 (the parent that asked for the stripping).

Every file:line below was read by me at develop `c3eb63c9d23b08132482f3211dbf8755312a7ca0`; every count is my own measurement in the same session, not carried from the brief that ordered this filing.

## 1 — what the derivation does today

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:722-724`, verbatim:

> `hook_controls=$(grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#' "$hook_src" 2>/dev/null \` / `| grep -oE '\$\{[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*:-' \` / `| tr -d '${:-' | sort -u)`

`hook_src` is `../../.githooks/pre-push` (`:708`). Running that exact pipeline over the hook at this tip yields **one** name: `ALLOW_FORCE`, from the single live-code match at `.githooks/pre-push:77` (`${ALLOW_FORCE:-0}`). The hook is 400 lines, sha256 `74e8d270607c138b…`.

## 2 — the blind spot, and its size today

The source records it at `preflight.sh:715-721`. The operative sentences, verbatim:

> `KS-1643 nit 3, RECORDED AND NOT CLOSED:` `:-` `is the only read shape this derives. A` / `control read as` `${NAME}`, `${NAME:?}` `or bare` `$NAME` `is silently NOT stripped.`

and

> `Closing it needs a way to` / `tell "read from the caller" from "assigned internally", which is its own ticket.`

**Measured size of the gap today: zero.** Over the hook's live code (comments excluded, as `:722` does), braced ALL-CAPS reads of *any* form — `${NAME`, `${NAME:-`, `${NAME:?`, `${NAME}` — number **exactly one**, and it is the `${ALLOW_FORCE:` the derivation already finds. So no control is being missed at this tip.

Two near-misses that the ALL-CAPS pattern correctly does **not** match, recorded so a future reader does not mistake them for instances:

* `.githooks/pre-push:53` is `_remote="${1:-origin}"` — a `:-` read, but of a positional, not an `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*` name.
* The hook's locals are underscore-prefixed lower-case (`$_jr_lsha`, `$_tip`, …). A `\$[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*` pattern matches only their leading `$_`, 62 times, and yields no name. `preflight.sh:706-707` already notes this.

## 3 — why widening the pattern is not the fix: the `ZERO` counter-example

The hook assigns `ZERO=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000` at `.githooks/pre-push:52` and reads it **bare**, at **four** lines:

| line | use |
| -- | -- |
| `:60` | `[ "$local_sha" = "$ZERO" ] && continue` — deleting a branch rewrites nothing |
| `:61` | `[ "$remote_sha" = "$ZERO" ] && continue` — brand-new branch at origin |
| `:113` | `[ "$_jr_lsha" = "$ZERO" ] && { _jr_skip=delete; return 0; }` — deleting a ref |
| `:122` | `[ "$_jr_rsha" != "$ZERO" ] && git cat-file -e …` — guards the remote-sha read |

Broadening the derivation to bare `$NAME` over live code yields exactly two names, measured: `ALLOW_FORCE` **and** `ZERO`. `ALLOW_FORCE` is a control read from the caller and must be stripped; `ZERO` is a constant the hook assigns itself and must not be. The pattern cannot tell them apart, which is precisely the discriminator the source comment says is needed.

**Mechanism of the breakage, reasoned from the source and NOT executed:** with `ZERO` stripped from the suites' environment, `"$ZERO"` expands empty inside the hook's own run. A real delete push presents `local_sha` as the all-zeros string, which does not equal the empty string, so the `:60` and `:113` guards would stop firing and a branch deletion would be judged a rewrite. Whether that is what the hook would actually do is not established here — see Not established.

A third group exists and is **not** in the blind spot, recorded so the discriminator is specified against the real set: `FORMAT_GATE_TREE` (`:363`, `:365`) and `FORMAT_GATE_BASE_MAY_BE_STALE` (`:365`) are ALL-CAPS names the hook assigns as a command prefix and never reads with `$`. A read-shape broadening does not catch them; a *name*-based one would.

## Not established

* Whether any control will ever be read in a shape other than `${NAME:-`. None exists today, so the gap is latent and its size is zero — this ticket records a known blind spot, not an observed miss.
* What discriminator separates "read from the caller" from "assigned internally". The source comment states only that one is needed. **No shape is proposed here.**
* That the `:-` derivation has no *other* blind spot. Only the read-shape axis was measured.
* That stripping `ZERO` would break the hook in the way §3 describes. That is reasoned from the four read sites, not reproduced — no mutant was run and no push was made.
* The `68/0` mutant figure and every suite ratio on KS-1643 are the author's and the gate's, quoted there, not re-run by me.

## Searched (board, KS team, title + description + comments, archived and Done included, paginated)

Each line is a query I ran this session; counts are mine.

* `${NAME:?}` — 1 hit, KS-1643. `NAME:?` — 1 hit, KS-1643. `caller-read` — 1 hit, KS-1643.
* `hook_controls` — 1 hit, KS-1746. `hook controls` — 4 hits: KS-772, KS-1634, KS-1638, KS-1643. `read from the caller` — 2 hits: KS-772, KS-1643.
* `nit 3` — 4 hits: KS-544 (archived), KS-1385, KS-1643, KS-1746.
* `bare $NAME` — 0 hits. `assigns itself` — 0 hits.
* **Read whole before filing, and none is coverage** (a matcher for the blind-spot concepts — `${NAME}` / `${NAME:?}` / `bare $` / `read shape` / `assigned internally` / `read from the caller` / `caller-read` — scored **0** on all four, against **2** on KS-1643 as a firing control):
  * **KS-1634** (In Progress) — one occurrence of `hook controls`, inside a quoted log line. Its subject is a simulated anchor presented as anchored. A mention, not coverage.
  * **KS-772** (Todo) — one occurrence, also a quoted log line in a digest comment. A mention, not coverage.
  * **KS-1638** (In Review) — the parent that asked for the stripping. Its fix shape at its own §2 reads *"also strips* `ALLOW_FORCE` *— and arguably every variable the hook itself reads"*. That is the broader **aim**; the implementation narrowed it to the `:-` shape, and this ticket is that narrowing's residue. KS-1638 names no alternative read shape and proposes no discriminator. Not coverage.
  * **KS-1483** (Backlog) — zero occurrences of either term; its subject is the checked-out-branch guard. Not coverage.
* **Positive controls, same instrument and session:** `KS-1531` → 13 hits, `run_shell_suites` → 42 hits. **Zero control:** a fresh nonsense token → 0 hits. The token KS-1746 to KS-1751 used as their zero control is now **dead** — it returns 7 hits, because those six tickets and KS-1643 quote it; measured, not assumed.

*Filed by Seat G 23rd, 2026-10-27, on Wednesday's brief, as the successor KS-1643's comment of 2026-10-26T23:23Z says does not exist.*

title: ks1564-admin-api-keys-page-sends-no-default-org.test.ts: the AST guard does not see a member call, a bracket call or a bare undefined/null id (gate t4s4 LOW on #1734)
description:
## BLUF

**Gate t4s4 residue on PR #1734 (KS-1589 item A), LOW, GO WITH NOTES.** The rewritten AST guard kills all five mutants the round-2 gate recorded as surviving, and the gate confirmed that. It also found **three call shapes that stay GREEN** and that the guard's header does not list. None is live in the page today.

Facts only. **No fix is proposed** — the source ticket proposes none for these, and two of the three are deliberate exclusions whose boundary is a judgement, not a defect.

Refs KS-1589, KS-1564, KS-1319, KS-1329.

Guard: `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks1564-admin-api-keys-page-sends-no-default-org.test.ts`, 521 lines, **13 cells**, merged as `bc958363c549` (#1734). All line numbers read at develop `885d69b06f5fce7c8f58effea68623ecb25407b1`.

## 1 — The three blind spots, as the gate recorded them

From `2026-10-27_gate-t4s4-batch/verdict.md`, the #1734 row, verbatim:

> LOW: the AST guard has three reachable blind spots it does not claim to close (namespace/member call `api.fetchApiKeys('x' || 'y')`, bracket call, a bare `undefined`/`null` passed as the id).

and from that section's vacuity probes, **GREEN, not caught**:

> `api.fetchApiKeys('x' || 'y')` through a namespace import (the checker excludes property-access names by design, "someone else's .fetchApiKeys"); `(api as any)['fetchApiKeys']('x')` (a string, not an identifier); `fetchApiKeys(undefined)` (the `PLAIN_IDENTIFIER` regex accepts `undefined`/`null`); an alias in a `.js` file (walker takes only .ts/.tsx; none exist in the tree today).

The gate adds: *"The file header says it refuses 'expressions at the call sites, not provenance'; it does not list these. The current page imports by name, so none is live today."*

## 2 — Where each one lives in the guard, read at the tip

| shape | the code that lets it through | line |
| -- | -- | -- |
| member / namespace call `api.fetchApiKeys(…)` | `fetchApiKeysArgs` requires the callee to be an identifier: `if (ts.isCallExpression(n) && ts.isIdentifier(n.expression) && n.expression.text === 'fetchApiKeys')` | `:193` |
| the same, via the value-use checker | `fetchApiKeysValueUses` excludes property access explicitly: `if (ts.isPropertyAccessExpression(p) && p.name === n) continue;` | `:224` |
| bracket call `(api as any)['fetchApiKeys']('x')` | the element-access name is a string literal, not an `Identifier`, so neither walker sees it | `:193`, `:218` |
| a bare `undefined` / `null` id | `const PLAIN_IDENTIFIER = /^[A-Za-z_$][\w$.]*$/;` — the literals `undefined` and `null` match it | `:365`, asserted at `:397` and `:404` |
| an alias in a `.js` file | `const kind = fileName.endsWith('.tsx') ? ts.ScriptKind.TSX : ts.ScriptKind.TS;` and the walk takes only `.ts`/`.tsx` | `:134` |

The guard's own statement of scope is at `:69`: *"call sites, not the provenance of a variable."* The property-access exclusion at `:224` is documented in the comment above it (`:216-223`) as deliberate — "someone else's `.fetchApiKeys` property is not this function" — and that comment also names the shape the exclusion must **not** swallow, a renaming destructure.

**One further property of the regex, mine rather than the gate's and NOT tested with a mutant:** `PLAIN_IDENTIFIER`'s tail class is `[\w$.]*`, which admits a dot, so a dotted expression passed as the id would also match. Recorded as a read of the regex text, not as a demonstrated escape.

## 3 — What the guard reads, and what type-checks it

`ADMIN_SRC` at `:99` is `process.env.KS1564_ADMIN_SRC ?? join(DEV_ROOT, 'frontend', 'admin', 'src')`, so the guard reads the admin frontend's source from a test in `packages/shared`. `KS1564_ADMIN_SRC` (`:94`, `:99`) exists so a mutant harness can point it at a copy; the gate used exactly that, with the copy's tree sha256 asserted changed per mutant.

**Nothing in the repository type-checks this file.** `packages/shared/tsconfig.json:21` excludes `src/__tests__`, and the push preflight's leg 16 ratchet carries baselines for five services only — api-gateway, auth, m365-integration, security, vc-issuer — with no `packages/shared` baseline. That is KS-1329's subject, named here because a guard that parses the TypeScript AST is exactly the kind of file a type error can rot unseen.

## Not established

* **I ran nothing.** Every green/red above is the gate's; no mutant was constructed or re-run here, and the dotted-expression note in section 2 is a read of the regex, not a mutant.
* Whether any of the three is worth closing. The property-access exclusion is deliberate and has a stated reason; closing it needs a rule for telling "the imported function, accessed as a member" from "someone else's property of the same name". **Not decided.**
* Whether a `.js` file could ever appear under `frontend/admin/src`. The gate says none exists in the tree today; I did not re-count.
* KS-1589's items **B** (the quadratic trailing trim in `ApiKeys.tsx`) and **C** (three Playwright cells that have never run) are untouched by this and by #1734 — that ticket stays open for them.

## Searched

Board, KS team, `includeArchived: true`, title + description + comments, paginated to `hasNextPage` false — never capped.

* `api.fetchApiKeys` → **0 hits**. `PLAIN_IDENTIFIER` → **0 hits**.
* `ks1564-admin-api-keys-page` → **1 hit**, KS-1589. `KS1564_ADMIN_SRC` → **1 hit**, KS-1589. `fetchApiKeys` → **4 hits**: KS-1594, KS-1589, KS-1564, KS-1514.
* **KS-1589 was read whole**, description and comment. Its item A is what #1734 merged; its comment records the five mutants now red and says the ticket stays open for B and C. **It does not carry these three shapes** — they are the gate's finding on the merged result, which is after that ticket's text.
* `blind spot` → 69 hits, too broad to decide on alone; used only to check the narrow terms were not missing a nearer ticket.
* **Decision, stated:** filed rather than commented on KS-1589, because this board files one gate-residue ticket per merged PR (KS-1637 on #1589, KS-1643 on #1606, KS-1746 on #1733 are the precedent) and because KS-1589 stays open for B and C, which are different work in different files.
* **Positive controls, same instrument and session:** `KS-1531` → **18 hits**; `fetchApiKeys` → **4 hits**. **Zero control:** a token coined for this session and written to no ticket → **0 hits**.

*Filed by Seat G 24th, 2026-10-27, on Wednesday's brief.*

title: systemTest/schemathesis: a sweep leaves governance proposals from the OLA leg's `owner` actor on the cap, which the KS-1719 slot-freeing helper never cancels — on a long-lived slot they alone fill the cap and the §11 test skips with `freed 0`
description:
## BLUF

The [KS-1719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1719/systemtest-preconditions-test-execute-from-draft-is-refused-skips-when) helper (`_free_active_proposal_slot`, PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1687](https://linear.app/secuura/review/fixschemathesis-free-the-governance-caps-queued-proposals-too-oldest-fc6447b24b1f)) cancels only proposals the super-admin persona proposed. Its docstring assumed the sweep proposes only as `super_admin`. Measured under [KS-1762](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1762/ks-1719-residue-the-governance-cap-slot-freeing-helper-is-proven-live): a sweep also proposes as an `owner`-role user, which the helper never touches. Each sweep leaves a few of that user's proposals counting toward the 20-proposal cap. On a slot that hosts sweeps for long enough, those alone fill the cap, the helper frees 0, and `test_execute_from_draft_is_refused` skips with `freed 0 proposal(s)`, which fails the pre-merge gate (a skip is INCOMPLETE, [KS-478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful)). This is the mechanism [KS-1719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1719/systemtest-preconditions-test-execute-from-draft-is-refused-skips-when) described, now with a named proposer.

## Measured ([KS-1762](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1762/ks-1719-residue-the-governance-cap-slot-freeing-helper-is-proven-live), 27 Oct 2026)

One `pre-merge` sweep on a fresh platform-k slot 2 at develop `dcf1ca244` (run `pre-merge-2026-10-27T11-21-02Z-slot2`, seed 1286291329, Schemathesis 4.32.1). `svc_proposals` afterwards, grouped by `proposer_id`:

| Proposer | Role | Created | Proposals | Still counted by the cap (`active`) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000020` | system_admin (the seeded super-admin) | seed | 60 | 2 |
| `468839f4-cfb0-4fe2-a322-623e7699e348` | owner | 11:21:04, the run's start | 5 | 1 |
| `19d84f36-0474-4369-bf59-fd535c5ef2a9` | issuer_admin | seed | 4 (the §11 probes' drafts) | 0, all cancelled |

The `owner` user's creation time matches `provision-actors` for the OLA leg (`ks256-owner-local`, role OWNER, [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under)). The identity is inferred from role and timing: `users.email` is encrypted, so it was not confirmed by email.

So about one proposal per sweep is left on the cap by a proposer the helper cannot cancel. The helper's behaviour on that cap was proven live under [KS-1762](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1762/ks-1719-residue-the-governance-cap-slot-freeing-helper-is-proven-live): the create skips with `(freed 0 proposal(s) before this; only proposals proposed by the super-admin are cancelled)`.

## Fix options (systemTest only, pick in the plan)

1. The OLA leg cancels every proposal its peers created, as the §11 fixture does for its own drafts (`test_state_machine_preconditions.py` `draft_proposal` teardown).
2. The helper also frees as the `owner` actor, from the actor manifest, with the same oldest-first and own-proposals-only rules.

Option 1 is cleaner: the residue is cleared by the leg that made it, and the helper's scope stays narrow.

## Acceptance

1. **Automated test:** red on the current code, green after. Offline: a unit test driving the chosen code path over a model of the routes (as `tests/unit/support/test_precondition_probes_proposal_cap.py` does). Live: after one `pre-merge` sweep on a fresh slot, `select count(*) from svc_proposals where status in ('active','queued') and proposer_id <> <super-admin id>` is 0, or the [KS-1762](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1762/ks-1719-residue-the-governance-cap-slot-freeing-helper-is-proven-live) opt-in suite (`tests/governance_cap_live`) still passes 3/3 on that slot after the sweep.
2. **Docs:** the `_free_active_proposal_slot` docstring's MEASURED paragraph (added by [KS-1762](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1762/ks-1719-residue-the-governance-cap-slot-freeing-helper-is-proven-live)) updated to say the residue is now cleared; `docs/running-tests.md` and the two `Projects Documents` HTML files if the OLA leg's behaviour is described there.
3. **systemTests:** the change lives under `systemTest/schemathesis/`; no product code.

## Related

* [KS-1762](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1762/ks-1719-residue-the-governance-cap-slot-freeing-helper-is-proven-live) (In Progress): the measurement and the live proof of the helper.
* [KS-1719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1719/systemtest-preconditions-test-execute-from-draft-is-refused-skips-when) (Done): the original skip and the helper fix ([Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1687](https://linear.app/secuura/review/fixschemathesis-free-the-governance-caps-queued-proposals-too-oldest-fc6447b24b1f)).
* [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) (Done): the OLA leg and its `owner` / `ownerPeer` actors.
* [KS-1732](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1732/governance-a-failed-database-read-answers-as-empty-get-proposals) (Backlog, Kamil): the cap fails open on a database read error; not this ticket.

title: preflight.sh:731: the -z "$hook_controls" disjunct is implied by the second disjunct, so deleting it moves no cell and no outcome; delete it or keep it as a documented refusal is undecided
description:
## BLUF

**At** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:731` **the** `-z "$hook_controls"` **disjunct is implied by the second disjunct, so deleting it changes no outcome and no test cell can go red on its deletion (an equivalent mutant).** Whether to delete the dead disjunct, or keep it as a documented refusal, is **not decided**. Until now the question was recorded only inside KS-1756's comment (2026-10-27T06:19:35Z: "Whether to delete the dead disjunct is a `preflight.sh` question and is not made here"), and KS-1756 is a ticket about to be closed, so this ticket is the question's home.

Facts only. **No fix is proposed.**

Refs KS-1756, KS-1746, KS-1638.

All line numbers were read at develop `061c3a4f62d563e723b8cee5fe792b4c27dc3014`. The finding is Seat Z 1st's (STATUS 2026-10-27T05:54Z, and KS-1756's comment), relayed through Wednesday; the truth table in section 2 is re-measured here.

## 1 — The line

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:731`, verbatim:

`if [ -z "$hook_controls" ] || ! printf '%s\n' "$hook_controls" | grep -qx 'ALLOW_FORCE'; then`

The comment above it (`:725-730`) says an empty derivation "would mean the hook moved or the pattern stopped matching", and that `ALLOW_FORCE` is named "because it is the one control known to exist today". The refusal text starts at `:732`: `FAIL - could not derive the pre-push hook's own control variables from $hook_src.`

## 2 — The truth table, measured here

`/bin/bash` 3.2.57 with `set -o pipefail`. I ran the full condition and the second disjunct alone over seven derived sets: empty; `ALLOW_FORCE`; `NAME`; `FOO BAR`; `ALLOW_FORCE` then `NAME` on two lines; `NAME` then `ALLOW_FORCE` on two lines; `ALLOW_FORCE_X`.

Result: **7 of 7 identical** (refuse, pass, refuse, refuse, pass, pass, refuse). For the empty set, `printf '%s\n' ""` writes one empty line, `grep -qx 'ALLOW_FORCE'` exits 1, and `!` makes that true, so the second disjunct refuses on its own.

Control on the same harness: with the second disjunct replaced by `false`, the empty set **does** differ (refuse with the `-z` disjunct, pass without it), so the harness can tell the two forms apart.

## 3 — What the suites measured (relayed, not re-run here)

From KS-1756's comment, which is Seat Z 1st's: the mutant that deletes the disjunct reads `preflight_deps.test.sh` 82/0 with zero cells moving, so no cell can fail on it. The mutants the cells do kill are `M_accept` (an empty set is accepted: 75/0 and surviving at base, 76/6 after) and `M_2nd` (only `-z` remains: 71/4 before, 79/3 after).

## Not established

* **Whether to delete the dead disjunct or keep it.** Not decided, and not chosen here.
* **I ran no suite.** The 82/0, 76/6 and 79/3 figures are KS-1756's, not reproduced.
* Whether any other `if` in `preflight.sh` has the same implied-disjunct shape. Not searched.

## Searched

Board, KS team, title + description + comment bodies, `includeArchived: true`, paged to the end. `preflight.sh:731` → **1 hit**, KS-1756. `hook_controls` → **3 hits**: KS-1756, KS-1755 (the derivation reads `${NAME:-` only, a different defect), KS-1746. `equivalent mutant` → **1 hit**, KS-1687 (m365, unrelated). `disjunct` → **4 hits**: KS-1756, KS-1640, KS-1078 (archived), KS-1017; none of the other three contains `preflight.sh:731`, and I read their titles only. **Positive control** `KS-1531` → 24 hits. **Zero control:** a token coined for this read and written nowhere → 0 hits.

*Filed by Seat G 25th, 2026-10-27 UTC, on Wednesday's brief.*

description:

Gate A on PR 1765 also left three mutation survivors open (a predicate held in a name or** `new RegExp('')`**, and a swapped predicate), and the figure "39 calls / 9 under test" written into the test file and two docs is the base measurement; the head has 42 / 12.** All in `services/auth`. Nothing is failing; each is a place where a regression would stay green.

Facts only. **No fix is proposed.** KS-1765 closed the same shape for `AUTH_GREEN_SUMMARY` alone; its own comment records the other call sites as "unchanged" and they have no other home on the board.

Refs KS-1765, KS-1529, KS-1519, KS-1000.

## 1 — Sixteen call sites use a digit-led string predicate

`// SEED DEMO USERS — runs once at startup via the repository`

`setTimeout(() => { userRepo.seedDemoUsers(hashPassword).catch((err) => logger.error('Failed to seed demo users', { error: err }), ); }, 2000);`

The `setTimeout` is at `:62` and the `seedDemoUsers` call at `:63`. It sits at module scope, so it is armed by the first import of the module. The lines have no environment or test check, and nothing is chained on `setTimeout(...)` after the `2000` (no `unref`).

title: api-gateway middleware/scopes.ts:57: requireScope answers 403 with a flat body ({ error: 'Insufficient scope', required, granted, hint }), not the published { success: false, error: { code, message } } envelope; the sibling requireScopeOrRole uses the envelope, and three systemTest files read the flat text
description:
## BLUF

**The api-gateway's** `requireScope` **answers a scope refusal with a flat body,** `{ error: 'Insufficient scope', required, granted, hint }`**, where the published error envelope is** `{ success: false, error: { code, message } }`**. The sibling** `requireScopeOrRole` **in the same file answers with the envelope (code** `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`**), and so does the 401 in** `requireScope` **itself.** Three `systemTest` files read the flat shape by its text. Reported by Seat Z 2nd (STATUS C 15:57Z and READY 17:28Z, 2026-10-27; HANDOVER line 44) while working KS-1767.

Facts only. **No fix is proposed** and none is implied: the flat body is relied on by test code (item 4).

Refs KS-1767, KS-843.

All line numbers were read at develop `c18552d94de23b4da365ce02e02be5d06793bbcb`, under `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src` unless another path is given. Read from source only; no request was made to a gateway.

## 1 — Three refusals in one file, two shapes

`middleware/scopes.ts`:

* `:29` (in `requireScope`), the 401: `res.status(401).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'UNAUTHORIZED', message: 'Authentication required' } });` — the envelope.
* `:57`-`:62` (in `requireScope`), the **403**: `res.status(403).json({` then `error: 'Insufficient scope',` (`:58`), `required: requiredScopes,` (`:59`), `granted: userScopes,` (`:60`) and a `hint:` template string (`:61`) — **flat**; `error` is a string, there is no `success` and no `code`.
* `:148` (in `requireScopeOrRole`), the 401: the same envelope as `:29`.
* `:184`-`:192` (in `requireScopeOrRole`), the 403: `res.status(403).json({ success: false, error: { code: 'INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE', message: ..., required: requiredScope, granted: scopes } })` — the envelope, with `required` and `granted` inside `error`.

## 2 — What the published contract says

`Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/openapi/responses.ts`: the registered `ErrorResponse` schema is at `:44`, with `success: z.literal(false)` at `:48` and `error` an object holding `code`, `message` and an optional `details`. The docblock at `:40`-`:41` says: "Every service emits this on any non-2xx response". `commonErrorResponses[403]` (`:156`) uses that schema. Whether each of the six operations in item 3 publishes its 403 through `commonErrorResponses[403]` was not read.

## 3 — Which routes mount the flat gate

`requireScope(` is mounted at six places in `routes/proxy.ts`: `:445` (`'webhooks:manage'`), `:464` (`'users:read'`), `:638` (`'documents:read', 'documents:write'`), `:645` (`'certifications:read', 'certifications:write'`) and `:876` and `:882` (each `'anchors:write'`). `requireScopeOrRole(` is mounted at `:807` and `:860`.

`requireScope` lets a principal whose `authMethod` is `jwt` or `email` through before any scope test (`:35`-`:36`), so the flat 403 reaches OAuth-app and API-key callers, which carry explicit scopes (`:41`-`:42`).

## 4 — What reads the flat shape today

The text `Insufficient scope` occurs in **4 files** in the whole tree at this tip (7 lines): `middleware/scopes.ts:58` and three under `systemTest`:

* `systemTest/playwright/tests/path-spelling/scope-gate-path-spelling.spec.ts:49`: `const GATE_FINGERPRINT = { error: 'Insufficient scope', required: ['anchors:write'] };`, with the comment at `:48` "The gate's own 403 body, from `middleware/scopes.ts` `requireScope` — its fingerprint".
* `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/support/connector_identity.py:20`-`:23`: the comment reads "Gateway `requireScope` ... answers `{"error": "Insufficient scope", "required": [...], "granted": [...]}` — a bare string, not the usual `{error: {code, message}}` envelope." and `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE = "Insufficient scope"`; also `:91` in the `is_scope_refusal` docstring.
* `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/unit/support/test_connector_identity.py:30`-`:31` (`_SCOPE_403 = {"error": "Insufficient scope", ...}`, commented "a bare-string `error`") and `:50`.

So the harness already treats the flat body as a known, unpublished shape.

## 5 — On the board

KS-1767 mentions it in one sentence in its PR comment of 2026-10-27T17:27Z: "The scope guard's flat 403 body (`middleware/scopes.ts:58`), seen while reading, is outside this ticket." No ticket records it.

## Not established

* **I ran nothing and sent no request.** The body is read from `res.status(403).json(...)`, not observed from a live gateway.
* **Whether each of the six mounts in item 3 is reachable for every method on its path.** It is not for `POST /api/documents`: that request is answered earlier by the gateway's own handler, `routes/verification.ts:662`, whose router is mounted at `index.ts:901` before `createProxyRoutes` at `index.ts:1107`, and no `next(` or `_next(` call occurs in `routes/verification.ts` from `:662` to `:918`; so the `:638` mount is not reached for that request. `GET /api/workflow-instances/:id` is likewise handled at `routes/verification.ts:449`. The other mounts and methods were not traced. (Added after filing, 2026-10-27 UTC, found while tracing the routes that mcp-server's `register.ts` and `info.ts` call.)
* Whether the six operations publish their 403 with the shared `ErrorResponse` or declare another shape (not read).
* Whether the flat body is deliberate. The code comment above `requireScope` does not say.
* What the three `systemTest` consumers would do if the shape changed; they match on the text, so a change would reach them.
* What, if anything, to do. Not decided.

## Searched

Board, KS team, title + description + comment bodies, `includeArchived: true`, paged to the end. `Insufficient scope` → **0 hits**. `GATE_FINGERPRINT` → **0**. `bare-string` → **0**. `flat body` → **0**. `flat 403` → **1 hit**, KS-1767 (the sentence quoted in item 5). `connector_identity` → 2 hits (KS-568, KS-492), not read. `middleware/scopes` → 12 hits, `scopes.ts` → 22, `requireScope` → 24; I read the threads of KS-1767, KS-1472, KS-1433, KS-1156, KS-843, KS-695, KS-822, KS-835, KS-1603, KS-1385, KS-1150, KS-1032, KS-869, KS-858 and KS-839 for `Insufficient`, `flat body`, `hint`, `granted:` and `scopes.ts`: none describes the 403 body shape (KS-843 mentions a `403 INSUFFICI...` from the envelope gate, `requireScopeOrRole`). `bare string` → 7 hits, read: none is about this gate (KS-1462 is a different bare string, in originate's `migrate-tenant-data`). **Positive control** `KS-1531` → 40 hits. **Zero control:** a token coined for this seat and written nowhere → 0 hits.

title: Question: what should the `error` field of mcp-server's secuura_check_workflow, secuura_register_document and secuura_register_documents carry? Three sites relay the gateway's data.error unchanged; the published contract makes it an object and api-client.ts declares a string
description:
## BLUF

**Question: what should the** `error` **field of three MCP tools carry?** `secuura_check_workflow`, `secuura_register_document` and `secuura_register_documents` put the gateway's `data.error` into their own `error` field **unchanged**, so the tool's `error` is whatever type the wire holds on that route. The published contract makes that value an object `{ code, message }`; the client declares it a string; and the one other tool in the package that reads the field (`secuura_get_connector_info`) accepts a string or a `{ message }` and bounds the text. This is a behaviour question about what the tools expose, not a defect report. Seat Z 2nd raised it as "out of scope for KS-1767".

Facts only. **No fix is proposed** and no answer is suggested.

Refs KS-1767, KS-1372.

All line numbers were read at develop `c18552d94de23b4da365ce02e02be5d06793bbcb`, under `Blockchain/Dev/services/mcp-server/src` unless another path is given. Source reads only; nothing was run.

## 1 — The three relays

* `tools/info.ts:83`, in `secuura_check_workflow` (`:67`-`:68`), calling `getWorkflowInstance`: `` error: result.data?.error || `HTTP ${result.status}`, ``
* `tools/register.ts:28`, in `secuura_register_document` (`:7`-`:8`): `error: result.data?.error || 'Failed to register document',`, beside `httpStatus: result.status` (`:27`).
* `tools/register.ts:117`, in `secuura_register_documents` (`:73`-`:74`), inside the per-document loop: `` error: result.data?.error || `HTTP ${result.status}`, ``

Each puts the value into `JSON.stringify({ success: false, ... })` as the tool's text content. None tests the value's type or bounds its length.

## 2 — The one place that does

`tools/info.ts:130`-`:131`, in `secuura_get_connector_info`: `const gatewayError = (connectorResult?.data as unknown as { error?: unknown } | undefined)?.error;` then `const refusalText = typeof gatewayError === 'string' ? gatewayError : typeof (gatewayError as { message?: unknown } | undefined)?.message === 'string' ? ...`, and `:132`-`:134` bound the relayed text to 200 characters (KS-1620).

## 3 — The declared type and the contract

`api-client.ts` declares `error?: string;` at `:57` (`registerDocument`, `POST /api/documents`), `:105` (`getWorkflowInstance`, `GET /api/workflow-instances/:id`) and `:125` (`getConnectorInfo`). KS-1767 owns that mismatch; its PR 1769 comment describes a `string | { code?: string; message?: string }` alias and says the three relays above "relay the value unchanged, compile under either type and are not changed". The published `ErrorResponse` is `{ success: false, error: { code, message, details? } }` (`Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/openapi/responses.ts:44`, `:48`).

## 4 — What the wire holds on the two routes, by source read

* Both `POST /api/documents` and `GET /api/workflow-instances/:id` are answered by the gateway's own handlers in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` (`:662` and `:449`). That router is mounted at `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:901`, before `createProxyRoutes` at `:1107`, inside an unconditional block (`:893`-`:906`), and no `next(` or `_next(` call occurs in `verification.ts` from `:662` to `:918`. KS-1767's PR comment counts, from source: **13 object-literal** `error` **values and 0 strings in the POST handler, 1 object in the workflow read, and 115 object-literal values with 0 string literals at the top level of a response in originate's documents router** (those counts are its author's; not recounted here).
* The one flat-string body KS-1767's comment names on a shared layer is the brute-force limiter's `429 { error: 'Too many failed attempts', ... }` at `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/security.ts:166`-`:167`, mounted at `index.ts:450`. The middleware returns early unless the request path includes `/auth/login` (`:152`-`:153`), and none of the three tools' paths does. KS-1372 (Todo) records that nothing calls its `recordFailure`.
* Seat Z 2nd's correction of its own report (STATUS C, 15:57Z, 2026-10-27): "no running gateway sends a string today". This item agrees for the two routes these three sites call (`POST /api/documents`, `GET /api/workflow-instances/:id`), as far as the source goes.

So the question is about the contract the tools expose to an MCP client, not about a string observed arriving.

## Not established

* **I ran nothing and observed no response.** The wire value on these routes is a source read; the reverse proxy in front of the gateway was not read.
* The counts in item 4 (13 / 0 / 1 / 115) are KS-1767's author's, not recounted.
* Whether any MCP client reads the tools' `error` expecting a string or an object. Not searched.
* Whether a gateway-level refusal other than the login 429 can reach these three paths (for example from middleware mounted ahead of the verification router). Not traced.
* What the field should carry. **Not decided**; that is the question.

## Searched

Board, KS team, title + description + comment bodies, `includeArchived: true`, paged to the end. `data.error` → **3 hits**: KS-1767, KS-1620, KS-177 (archived, Done; a jest/vitest mock, unrelated). `info.ts:83` → **1**, KS-1767. `register.ts` → **1**, KS-1767. `tools/register` → **1**, KS-1767. `tools/info` → **4**: KS-1767, KS-1620, KS-1541, KS-1232. KS-1767 and KS-1372 were read whole; KS-1767 records the three sites as "not changed" and the behaviour question as one "the ticket does not ask"; KS-1620 and KS-1541 were read for the lines quoted. **Positive control** `KS-1531` → 40 hits. **Zero control:** a token coined for this seat and written nowhere → 0 hits.

description:
## BLUF

**The api-gateway unit run on Node v26.8.1 prints a** `DEP0060` **deprecation (the** `util._extend` **API) from each of 24 processes and a** `MaxListenersExceededWarning` **(11 close listeners on a Server) once; both appear identically in the base run and in five later runs, so they predate PRs 1764, 1766 and 1767. Neither source is identified.** Nothing is failing: the base run reads 124 files, 1212 tests, all passed. Seat Y 2nd noticed both while measuring KS-1771 and KS-1766 and left them unfiled.

Facts only. **No fix is proposed.**

Refs KS-1766, KS-1771.

The run outputs are Seat Y 2nd's, under `5_Project_History/2026-10-27_seatY-2nd/` in the Blockchain project folder; the counts below were measured by this seat with `grep -c` on those saved files. Nothing was run.

## 1 — The two warnings, verbatim

From `evidence/measure/base_full.out`, line 4:

`` (node:45790) [DEP0060] DeprecationWarning: The `util._extend` API is deprecated. Please use Object.assign() instead. ``

followed on the next line by Node's own hint to run with `node --trace-deprecation ...` to show where the warning was created. From the same file, line 48:

title: originate: three L6 cells titled 'simulated true with a real hash' take the hash from a chainReply default and assert nothing about it (ks1634-v2-chain-only-match-carries-simulated.test.ts:117, ks1634-a-simulated-anchor-verified-by-hash-verify-route.test.ts:107, ks1634-a-simulated-anchor-verified-by-hash.test.ts:102)
description:
## BLUF

**Three originate test cells are titled "simulated true with a real hash" and exist to prove that** `chain.simulated` **is carried into the reply, but each takes its hash from a** `chainReply` **helper default (**`txHash: REAL_TX`**) and none of its assertions reads that hash. The presenter marks a reply simulated from a placeholder-shaped hash alone, so with a placeholder-shaped default these cells could pass without the fix.** Seat Y 1st measured this for one of the three; the other two are the same shape and were not measured. The item is carried over from KS-1634, where it is the only thing still open.

Facts only. **No fix is proposed.**

Refs KS-1634, KS-1628.

All line numbers were read at develop `c18552d94de23b4da365ce02e02be5d06793bbcb`, under `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src` (`__tests__/` for the test files). develop has since moved one commit (#1770, 27 `package-lock.json` files); none of the paths below changed. This seat ran nothing.

## 1 — The three cells

* `__tests__/ks1634-v2-chain-only-match-carries-simulated.test.ts:117`: `it('RED KS-1634 L6 v2: simulated true with a real hash reads NOT on-chain', async () => {`. `:118` builds the reply as `callV2(chainReply({ simulated: true }))`. The helper `function chainReply` is at `:79` and its `txHash: REAL_TX` at `:84`; `REAL_TX` is declared at `:44`. The assertions at `:119`-`:125` are about the reply: `body.count`, `m.blockchain.simulated`, `m.blockchain.anchored`, `m.blockchain.txHash` null, `m.simulated`, `m.checks.isAnchored`.
* `__tests__/ks1634-a-simulated-anchor-verified-by-hash-verify-route.test.ts:107`: `it('RED KS-1628 L6 verify: simulated true with a real hash is not on-chain', async () => {`. `:108` is `callSite(chainReply({ simulated: true }))`; `chainReply` is at `:75` with `txHash: REAL_TX` at `:80`. Assertions `:109`-`:112`: `body.blockchain.simulated` true, `body.blockchain.anchored` false, `body.blockchain.txHash` null, `body.checks.isAnchored` false.
* `__tests__/ks1634-a-simulated-anchor-verified-by-hash.test.ts:102`: `it('RED KS-1628 L6 verify-file: simulated true with a real hash is not on-chain', async () => {`. `:103` is `callSite(chainReply({ simulated: true }))`; `chainReply` is at `:74` with `txHash: REAL_TX` at `:79`. Assertions `:104`-`:107`: the same four.

In none of the three does an assertion read the hash the cell sent. In the two verify files, the neighbouring cell ("the shape anchoring really sends (simulated true, txHash null)", `:115` and `:110`) overrides `txHash` with `null` and a `mock_tx_` reference, so it does not depend on the default.

## 2 — Why the hash matters here

`routes/verification.ts:52`: `const FABRICATED_TXHASH_RE = /^(tx_sim_|mock_tx_|mock_batch_tx_|tx_)/;`. `presentBlockchainHonestly` (`:54`) computes `const simulated = Boolean(b.simulated) || (tx !== undefined && FABRICATED_TXHASH_RE.test(tx));` at `:60`. So a blob whose hash matches that pattern is marked simulated whether or not `simulated` was copied into it. KS-1634's description records the same thing as a control row: "a placeholder hash, `simulated` absent: marked simulated YES". A cell meant to show that `simulated` is carried must therefore send a real hash, and it says "real hash" in its title; the only thing holding the hash real is the helper default.

## 3 — What is already pinned, and what was measured

* PR #1748 (`eedc4948b66d`) added `REAL_TX_SHAPE` (`ks1634-v2-chain-only-match-carries-simulated.test.ts:49`) and `expect(reply.txHash).toMatch(REAL_TX_SHAPE)` at `:159` and `:173`, in the two N3 cells of that file only. KS-1634's comment of 2026-10-19T16:10Z calls the gap for those two cells "one assertion in each of the two tests, checking that the hash is real".
* `REAL_TX_SHAPE` occurs in neither verify file (a search of each returned no line).
* Seat Y 1st, quoted in KS-1634's comment of 2026-10-27T07:11Z (not re-run here): with the `chainReply` default planted as a mock-prefixed hash in a copy, the v2 file reads 6 of 10 passing and both N3 cells stay green; its fixed version reads 4 of 10 with both N3 cells failing; and "the original RED cell 'simulated true with a real hash' depends on the same default and stays green under a mock-prefixed default in both files". Whether "both files" means the v2 file before and after, or two files, is not stated; the two verify files were not measured.

## Not established

* **I ran nothing.** Whether the two verify-file cells (`:107` and `:102`) stay green under a placeholder-shaped default is not measured; section 2 is a source read.
* Whether the v2 cell's assertions at `:119`-`:125` fail under such a default beyond what Seat Y 1st measured.
* What to do. Not decided.

## Searched

Board, KS team, title + description + comment bodies, `includeArchived: true`, paged to the end. `ks1634-v2-chain-only` → **1 hit**, KS-1634. `ks1634-a-simulated-anchor` → **1**, KS-1634. `mock-prefixed default` → **1**, KS-1634. `placeholder-shaped` → **1**, KS-1634. `helper default` → **1**, KS-1634. `simulated true with a real hash` → **1**, KS-1634. `REAL_TX_SHAPE` → **1**, KS-1634. `FABRICATED_TXHASH_RE` → **4**: KS-1634, KS-1626, KS-589, KS-587; the last three read for `real hash`, `REAL_TX`, `chainReply`, `L6` and `vacuous`: none holds this item (KS-1626 is the regex's missing `mock_batch_tx_` prefix, fixed at this tip). **Positive control** `KS-1531` → 48 hits. **Zero control:** a token coined for this seat and written nowhere → 0 hits.

title: Claude Code sessions have no secret-file guard on platform-k: add the PS-1361 hook with PS-1387's local-only exemption, covering every systemTest env and secrets file (and .env.stripe is not git-ignored)
description:
## BLUF

platform-s blocks a Claude Code session from printing a secret file ([PS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1361/block-claude-code-sessions-from-printing-secret-files-hook-rule)), and is about to let through files that hold only local values ([PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot), [Secuura/platform-s#1199](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1387-secret-file-guard-lets-local-only-values-through-55c48feacc56), In Review). **platform-k has neither.** At `develop` `bd6697e07` the repo's tracked `.claude/` holds only `skills/secuura-test-discipline/SKILL.md`: no `settings.json` and no hook. Nothing stops a session from running `cat`, `grep` or `diff` on `Blockchain/Dev/.env` (PII keys, JWT keys, datastore passwords), `.env.local` (OAuth and IdP credentials) or any systemTest secrets file. The only protection is a rule the session has to remember. [PS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1361/block-claude-code-sessions-from-printing-secret-files-hook-rule) exists because that failed on platform-s on 26 Oct 2026 (`terraform fmt -check -diff .` printed every dev-ps secret).

Separately, `.env.stripe`-style files, which are planned, are **not git-ignored** on platform-k today (measured below).

## Verified (28 Oct 2026, K `develop` `bd6697e07`)

**K has no guard:** `git ls-files .claude` returns only the skill file.

**systemTest env and secrets files: tracked templates, and the real file each produces (all git-ignored, checked with** `git check-ignore` **on the file path):**

| Real file (git-ignored) | Template (tracked) | Holds |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `systemTest/playwright/.env` | `systemTest/playwright/.env.example` | Playwright credentials and targets |
| `systemTest/akto/.env` | `systemTest/akto/.env.example` | Akto harness env |
| `systemTest/akto/docker.env` | `systemTest/akto/docker.env.example` | Akto container env |
| `systemTest/akto/config/secrets.yml` | `systemTest/akto/config/secrets.example.yml` | Akto role credentials |
| `systemTest/performance/config/secrets.yml` | `systemTest/performance/config/secrets.example.yml` | k6 credentials |
| `systemTest/schemathesis/.env-slot<N>` | written by `scripts/run.py setup` | per-slot API token |
| `.env-*` slot credential files ([KS-674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-674/playwright-documentsspects-3-cases-fail-whenever-their-slot-runs), root `.gitignore:14-16`) | written by tooling | slot-scoped credentials |

`systemTest/performance/config/environments.yml` is tracked. Whether it may name a secret value is not established.

**platform-k product code: env and credential files the services, frontends and deployments read.** Each was checked with `git check-ignore` on the real file path, 28 Oct 2026, `bd6697e07`.

| Real file | Template (tracked) | Ignored? | Holds |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env` | `Blockchain/Dev/env.example` (canonical, [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap)); also `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` | yes | PII encryption and lookup keys, JWT keypair, datastore passwords, `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local` | `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example` (also `env.local.example`) | yes | OAuth / IdP client secrets |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/<svc>/.env` for analytics, anchoring, api-gateway, auth, billing, governance, guardian, kyc, m365-integration, nft-certificate, originate, prism, queue, referral, security, staking, timestamping, transfer, vc-issuer, wallet-connector (20 services) | `services/<svc>/.env.example` | yes, all 20 | per-service secrets (billing: Stripe keys; m365: Microsoft app secret; kyc: provider keys) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/billing/` real file for its second template | `services/billing/env.example` | **not established**: the real file name for this no-dot template is unknown | Stripe keys |
| `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/.env.staging` | `deployment/azure/env.staging.example` | yes | Azure staging deployment values |
| `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/cardano/.env` | `deployment/cardano/env.example` | yes | Cardano node / wallet configuration |
| `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/{admin,issuer,verifier}/.env.development` | none tracked | yes | frontend local overrides |
| `Blockchain/Dev/test-wallet.env`, `Blockchain/Dev/*.wallet.env` | none | yes (`.gitignore:133-135`) | wallet seed phrases |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docker/nginx-gateway/ssl/*.pem`, `*.key` | none | yes (`.gitignore:70-72`) | TLS private keys |
| `.keys/`, `credentials.json`, `*-credentials.json` | none | yes (`.gitignore:93`, `:138-139`) | key material, service-account credentials |
| `USER_TESTING/Testing Harness/handoff/` | none | yes (`.gitignore:185-186`) | super-admin login handoff |
| `observability/.env`, `observability/config/alerting.env` | `observability/.env.example`, `observability/config/alerting.env.example` | yes | alerting webhooks and tokens |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/billing/.env.stripe` (planned style) | none | **NOT ignored** | would hold Stripe keys |

Every row except the last belongs in the hook's refuse list, and none qualifies for the local-only exemption: these are product secrets, not systemTest targets. The "Holds" column is from the template names and the service's purpose, not from opening any real file.

`.env.stripe` **is not git-ignored:**

```
K  systemTest/.env.stripe          NOT-ignored
K  Blockchain/Dev/.env.stripe      NOT-ignored
```

K's root `.gitignore` names `.env`, `.env-*`, `.env.local` and a fixed list of `.env.<stage>` names, not `.env.*`. A Stripe file created today could be committed.

## Proposed scope (for the owner to decide)

1. **A PreToolUse hook for Bash, Read and Grep**, `onFailure: block`, modelled on platform-s's `.claude/hooks/block_secret_reads.py`:
   * it refuses any reader (cat, grep, sed, diff, jq, base64, …) pointed at the files above, plus Terraform state, plans and tfvars, and an unformatted `docker inspect` or `docker exec … env` on K containers;
   * it allows a command that only names a file (`ls`, `stat`, `test -f`, `git check-ignore`);
   * it allows a single-field `docker inspect --format`, which the K build proof uses for `org.opencontainers.image.revision`.
2. [PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot)**'s local-only exemption, if Kamil agrees.** A systemTest env file whose every URL / base-URL key points at `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` is readable. Anything remote, missing or unreadable stays secret. `Blockchain/Dev/.env` **and** `.env.local` **stay guarded whatever their URLs**, because they hold real PII-encryption, JWT and OAuth material.
3. **A** `.gitignore` **rule for** `.env.*` **env files** (`.env.stripe` and successors) that keeps every `*.example` template tracked.
4. **A contract test pinning what the hook refuses and allows**, as platform-s's `SecretReadHookContractTests` does. Fixture files go in a temp folder, never the real ones.

**Why it matters for running the suites.** Building K, building S and running every systemTest suite need these files created and merged from their templates. With a guard on K, the exemption in item 2 decides which K files a session can merge blind. That needs settling before the guard lands, or the env-setup step breaks the same way.

## Runs on a developer's Mac, as platform-s#1199 does

platform-s#1199 ([PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot)) is written for a developer's own Mac running local stack slots. The platform-k guard should take the same shape:

* **Where it runs.** A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook on the Mac, registered in `.claude/settings.json` as `python3 "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/<name>.py"`, `onFailure: block`. `python3` ships with macOS (Xcode Command Line Tools), so no install is needed. `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is the session's project folder, normally the root checkout, not a ticket worktree. A guard change therefore takes effect once the root checkout is on a `develop` that contains it.
* **What "this machine" means.** As in #1199: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `[::1]`. A systemTest env file is exempt only while every URL / base-URL key in it points there. That covers the local slots `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` 1–4, gateway `6882 + 100·(N−1)`. A file pointed at Kintsugi, demo-pk, Container Apps or any remote host stays secret, and so does a missing or unreadable file.
* **Still guarded on the Mac, as in #1199:**
  * a bare `env` / `printenv`, because the developer's shell holds real tokens;
  * the product files in the table above, which are real keys even on a laptop;
  * Terraform state, plans and tfvars.
* **K slot containers (**`secuura-s<N>-*`**, and slot 1's** `secuura-*`**).** Unlike platform-s's slot containers, they are **not** exempt. Their environment comes from `Blockchain/Dev/.env` and `.env.local` (PII and JWT keys, OAuth secrets). An unformatted `docker inspect`, or `docker exec … env` / `printenv`, is refused. A single-field `docker inspect --format '{{ index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.revision" }}'` and `--format '{{.RestartCount}}'` stay allowed, because the build proof needs them.
* **macOS tools.** The rules match on command text, so they must hold for BSD `sed`, `grep`, `stat` and `xargs` as well as GNU forms.
* **A search pattern that names a secret file is not a read** (the #1199 false-positive fix). For example, `grep -E 'tfvars|tfstate' .gitignore` is allowed. A secret file as a file operand, or as the value of `-f`, is still refused. This session's own grep of K's `.gitignore` was refused by platform-s's guard for exactly this reason.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **An automated test, offline on macOS.** A contract test, run by the K preflight and the pre-push hook with no stack up, drives the hook through `python3` on the Mac. It covers:
   * a refused and an allowed case for every file in the tables above;
   * a localhost, a remote-URL and a missing-file case for each exempt systemTest file;
   * the K-container `docker inspect` / `exec` rules;
   * a search-pattern-only grep (allowed);
   * a `.env.stripe` file that is git-ignored while its `.example` is not.

   Fixture files go in a temp folder, never the real ones.
2. **Docs:** `CLAUDE.md` → security section, and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md`, name the guard, the exemption and the file list. `Projects Documents/Stack-Slots-How-To.md` is changed only if the env-setup steps change.
3. **systemTests:** no spec, page object or fixture change. The guard's test is a contract test. Each systemTest `.env.example` should say in a comment whether its real file is exempt.

## Related

* [PS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1361/block-claude-code-sessions-from-printing-secret-files-hook-rule) (the platform-s guard).
* [PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot) / platform-s#1199 (the local-only exemption, In Review).
