title: e2e gdpr-compliance.prelaunch.spec.ts cells 15.2.2 and 15.2.3 POST a DSR body the route refuses with 400 (subjectEmail and reason, not userId and email)
description:
## BLUF

Cells `15.2.2 Request data access` and `15.2.3 Request data erasure` in `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/gdpr-compliance.prelaunch.spec.ts` POST a DSR body that the create route refuses, so each should read 400 where it asserts 200, 201 or 202. **Neither cell was run.** The shape was measured on the cell next door (15.2.5, KS-1113), which sends the same two fields, and on the route directly.

## What the code says

* The cells (develop `bd6697e079fc`): 15.2.2 sends `subjectEmail` and `reason` (lines 332-333) and asserts `[200, 201, 202].includes(res.status)` (line 339); 15.2.3 does the same (lines 357-358, assertion at 364).
* The route: `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts:321`, `POST /dsr`, takes `{ type, userId, email, notes }` and answers 400 `type, userId, and email are required` (line 325) when any of the first three is missing. `userId` is the uuid of a real user (the table's `user_id` is a foreign key; a non-uuid answers 404).

## Measured

Throwaway stack at develop `bd6697e079fc`: api-gateway, auth and originate run natively against one `postgres:15-alpine` and one `redis:7-alpine`; host Node v26.8.1, which is not an LTS line.

* `POST /api/gdpr/dsr` as the seeded admin with the cell's fields (`type`, `subjectEmail`, `reason`): **400** `{"success":false,"error":{"code":"BAD_REQUEST","message":"type, userId, and email are required"}}`.
* The same route with the route's fields (`type`, `userId` = the admin's id from `GET /api/auth/me`, `email`, `notes`): **201** `{ success, request: { id, ... } }`.
* The 15.2.5 cell, which sends the same two wrong fields, failed at its create step in 30 ms ("Could not create DSR to test processing").
* **Not run:** cells 15.2.2 and 15.2.3 themselves.

## Fix shape

Test-only, in the spec: send the route's own fields (`userId` from `GET /api/auth/me`, `data.id`; `email`; `notes`), which makes 201 the answer the cells already accept. This is the change KS-1113 makes in 15.2.5. One test pass proves both cells, so they share this ticket.

## Dedupe, before filing

Literal census on 2026-10-28 over issue titles and descriptions, archived included, with a present control and a nonsense control: `15.2.2` 0 hits, `15.2.3` 0 hits, `gdpr-compliance.prelaunch` 1 hit (KS-1113 only), `subjectEmail` 2 hits (KS-537 and KS-466, both about the lifecycle-events payload, not the DSR route), nonsense token 0.

Related: KS-1113 (cell 15.2.5, same file).

title: Blockchain/Testing slot guard: the 'another slot's gateway' refusal is bypassed by LOCALHOST, HTTP://, 0.0.0.0 and 127.0.1.1, and the Azure RUNBOOK's pre-deploy audit step now refuses until it names a slot
description:
**BLUF: the refusal KS-1382 adds for a local TARGET_BASE that is another slot's gateway only recognises lowercase localhost, 127.0.0.1, \[::1\] and host.docker.internal behind a lowercase scheme, so eight other spellings are accepted and the run aims at slot 1's stack while slot 3 is named (Low). Separately, the Azure RUNBOOK's pre-deploy audit step now refuses until it names a slot. Found by the tier-1 gate on PR #1786 (Wednesday's ANSWER of 2026-10-28 10:26Z) and re-measured by Seat Z 3rd.**

## 1. The "another slot's gateway" refusal is bypassed by spellings that reach the same host

**Measured** with the committed [run-internal-audit.sh](<http://run-internal-audit.sh>) from PR #1786 (head 5d23044d272d), `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3 SECUURA_TARGET_RESOLVE_ONLY=1 TARGET_BASE=<spelling>:<slot 1's gateway port>`, port read from stack_env.sh:

| TARGET_BASE host spelling | result |
| -- | -- |
| [http://localhost](<http://localhost>) (control) | refused, rc 2 |
| [http://127.0.0.1](<http://127.0.0.1>) (control) | refused, rc 2 |
| [HTTP://localhost](<HTTP://localhost>) | **accepted**, rc 0, TARGET_BASE unchanged |
| [http://LOCALHOST](<http://LOCALHOST>) | **accepted** |
| [http://0.0.0.0](<http://0.0.0.0>) | **accepted** |
| [http://127.0.1.1](<http://127.0.1.1>) | **accepted** |
| [http://127.1](<http://127.1>) | **accepted** |
| http://\[::ffff:127.0.0.1\] | **accepted** |
| [http://localhost](<http://localhost>). (trailing dot) | **accepted** |
| [http://127.0.0.2](<http://127.0.0.2>) | **accepted** |
| [https://audit.example.invalid](<https://audit.example.invalid>) (remote, left alone by design) | accepted |

An accepted spelling means a run that named slot 3 sends its scan to slot 1's gateway, which is the KS 1373 shape this refusal exists to stop.

**Where:** the variable \_ks1382_re in the KS-1382 resolution block, byte-identical in the five entry points (ci/orchestrate.sh, ci/tools/run-schemathesis.sh, jobs/05-dast-zap.sh, jobs/06-tenant-isolation.sh, [run-internal-audit.sh](<http://run-internal-audit.sh>)). The same lowercase-only set is in is_local_url at systemTest/slot-target.sh lines 94 to 96, which this change reads but does not edit.

**Fix shapes (not decided here):** fold scheme and host to lowercase before matching; treat all of 127.0.0.0/8, 0.0.0.0, a trailing-dot localhost and IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback as local; or parse the URL instead of matching a regex. The five blocks must stay byte-identical (a suite cell pins that), and each new spelling wants a cell in blockchain_testing_target_base_follows_the_slot.test.sh.

**Not measured:** only the guard's decision. Whether each spelling really connects to the local host on a given machine was not tested (127.0.0.2, for one, is not configured on macOS by default). No scan was run.

## 2. The Azure RUNBOOK's pre-deploy audit step now refuses

Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/RUNBOOK.md line 56, step 0.4 "Internal-audit harness clean", runs `cd ../../Testing && ./run-internal-audit.sh` with no TARGET_BASE and no slot. Since KS-1382 that run refuses (rc 2, "No stack slot named"), so the checklist step cannot be completed as written. It was disclosed in the PR body and the READY mail; the runbook was outside KS-1382's file grant and is not updated. The fix is to say which target that step audits (a named slot, or TARGET_BASE for a remote one) and write the command.

Related: KS 1382 (the change that introduced both).

title: tenant-provisioning: the key service still writes a tenant's key row after the caller gives up, and neither the create rollback nor tenant delete removes it
description:
**BLUF:** The tokenisation service's `POST /api/generate-key` does not notice that its caller has gone: it still inserts the tenant's wrapped key row (`tenant_keys`) and an audit row afterwards. When tenant creation gives up (its fetch bound, a client disconnect) or rolls back, nothing removes that row. The create rollback deletes only `tenant_config`, `tenant_contacts` and `tenants`; tenant delete deletes `vault_entries`, `tenant_contacts`, `tenant_config` and `platform_document_registry`; tokenisation has no delete route. The result is an ACTIVE wrapped key for a tenant whose `vault_key_hash` is NULL, or for a tenant that no longer exists. Low: nothing reachable reads it today (see the vault-key trace on KS-1240).

## Exercised

A probe against the real tokenisation entry module (`pg` replaced by a recorder and the JWT middleware stubbed; no database, no Docker): the key INSERT slowed by 400 ms and the client aborting at 150 ms. Result, verbatim:

```
{ "clientOutcome": "client aborted: AbortError",
  "tenantKeysInsertsAtTheMomentTheClientGaveUp": 0,
  "tenantKeysInsertsOneAndAHalfSecondsLater": 1,
  "auditInsertsOneAndAHalfSecondsLater": 1 }
```

So the handler does not observe a client disconnect; the key row and the audit row land after the caller has left. File in the Platform K project folder: `5_Project_History/2026-10-28_seatY-4th/evidence/trace/generate_key_abort_probe.json` (the probe source is beside it as a `.txt`).

## Read (develop `2b7ef12fa564`)

* `services/tokenisation/src/index.ts`: the `generate-key` route is at `:220` and the key INSERT at `:238`; no `req.on('close')` handling and no delete route (routes: health, tokenise, detokenise, generate-key, rotate-key, detect-pii, hash-key).
* `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts`: the rollback at `:322` to `:324` and the tenant delete list at `:520` name no `tenant_keys`. `tenant_keys` is written by tokenisation into the main database, tenant provisioning's `platformQuery` writes the platform database.
* `migrations/029_tokenisation_tenant_keys.sql`: `UNIQUE (tenant_id, version, status)`. A second `generate-key` for a tenant that already has an active version 1 would insert `(tenant_id, 1, 'active')` again and so answer 500 (read; not executed, it needs a real Postgres).

## Why it matters

* Tenant creation now gives up on a key service that is slower than 3 s (KS-1240 part 4). A key service that is slow but not hung still completes its insert, and the tenant ends up with a key row and a NULL `vault_key_hash`.
* The decision that keeps tenant creation answering 201 with a `keyPending` flag (KS-1240) leaves such tenants in place; a later attempt to generate their key by hand would meet the unique constraint above.
* A create that is rolled back after the key was written leaves a key (and its audit row) for a tenant that no longer exists.

## Options (not chosen here)

1. A platform-admin route on tokenisation that deletes a tenant's key rows, called by the create rollback and the tenant delete.
2. Make `generate-key` idempotent per tenant (answer with the existing active key's id and hash), so a retry or a late completion can be reconciled.
3. Have tenant creation read the hash back from the key service after a timeout instead of leaving it NULL.

## Not covered

A real Postgres (the unique-constraint rejection is read), live data (how many such rows exist on the demo or kintsugi boxes is unmeasured), and any other caller of `generate-key` (the search found tenant provisioning only).

## Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, `issues()` filter over title and description, archived included)

Literals: `requestKeyGeneration` (1 hit, KS-336, Done; the firing control), `zzqx-no-such-literal-9931` (0; the null control), `tenant_keys` (KS-311, KS-288, both Done and about earlier errors in these routes), `generate-key` (KS-476, KS-311, KS-310, KS-288, KS-175, all Done or Deployed To Prod), `rotate-key` (6 hits: KS-667, KS-476, KS-311, KS-310, KS-288, KS-175, all closed or deployed work on these routes), `wrapped key` (0), `vault key` (0), `key row` (6 hits, none about the key service), `keyPending` (0). None records this behaviour.

Related to KS-1240 (not a blocker).

title: The tenant-creation contract, TOKENISATION.md and the admin UI still describe a key file returned once at creation; the key service has not returned one since 2026-04-28
description:
**BLUF:** The published tenant-creation contract, `docs/TOKENISATION.md`, `docs/METERING-USAGE-API.md` and the admin UI all describe a vault key file that tenant creation returns once. The key service has not returned a key since 2026-04-28 (commit `1f1cba638`, "Audit Tier-0 ... B-5", which changed `generate-key` to persist the key wrapped server-side and answer only `{ keyId, keyHash }`), so since that commit the real service has not let `POST /api/tenants` carry a key file on success, and the admin UI's key-file dialog can never open. One logical path, three kinds of site; the checklist below names each. Low: it misleads readers and consumers, it does not break a request.

## Exercised (real entry modules, `pg` and JWT stubbed, no Docker)

* The real `generate-key` answers with the fields `algorithm, createdAt, keyHash, keyId, success, tenantId, tenantSlug, version`: no `keyFile`, no `key`.
* Tenant creation against that answer: `201` with body keys `meteringApiKey, success, tenant` (no `keyFile` key at all); with the key service refusing (403 `success: false`) the same `201` carries `keyFile: null`. So success and failure differ only as "key absent" versus "key null", and the admin UI treats both as "no key dialog".
* Files in the Platform K project folder: `5_Project_History/2026-10-28_seatY-4th/evidence/trace/generate_key_probe.json` and `tenant_create_real_shape.json`.

## Checklist (develop `2b7ef12fa564`, line numbers from there)

- [ ] **Published contract.** The `keyFile` property of the 201 of `POST /api/platform/tenants`: description "The tenant's vault key material (PII/encryption), returned once at creation; null if key generation failed (mint manually later)." Source `services/tenant-provisioning/src/tenant-provisioning.openapi.ts:385`, published in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` (regenerate it with `npm run generate-openapi`).
- [ ] **Docs.** `docs/TOKENISATION.md`: the key file format and the example response near `:312` to `:321`, the Key Security note at `:182`, the write-path example at `:201` (`"key": "<from vault_key_hash lookup>"`; no code does that lookup and a SHA-256 hash cannot give the key back), Key Lifecycle step 4 at `:382` to `:385` ("The key file is returned to the super-admin"), and the troubleshooting step at `:486`. `docs/METERING-USAGE-API.md:120` ("alongside the vault `keyFile`").
- [ ] **Code and UI.** `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:125` to `:139`: `requestKeyGeneration` is typed as returning `keyFile`, and the handler copies `keyResult.keyFile` (undefined on the real answer). `frontend/admin/src/pages/platform/ClientList.tsx:70` (`if (result.keyFile) setKeyFileJson(...)`) with the dialog at `:323` to `:332`, and the type at `frontend/admin/src/services/api.ts:1045`.

## A decision sits under this (not mine)

Either a way to deliver the tenant's key is restored or `keyFile` is retired from the contract, the docs and the UI. The design comment in `services/tokenisation/src/index.ts:126` promises "a separate admin-only, audited endpoint can return the wrapped envelope"; no such route exists (routes: health, tokenise, detokenise, generate-key, rotate-key, detect-pii, hash-key). Related: the gateway keeps a per-session tenant key that an administrator uploads (`POST /api/platform/tenant-key`), but no route returns a key to upload, and the gateway's tokenise and detokenise helpers have no caller in the tree (none at the commit that introduced them either).

## Not covered

The admin UI was read, not rendered; consumers outside this repository (the Extranet, other repositories, runbooks) are unmeasured; live data on the boxes is unmeasured.

## Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, `issues()` filter over title and description, archived included)

Literals: `requestKeyGeneration` (1 hit, KS-336, Done; the firing control), `zzqx-no-such-literal-9931` (0; the null control), `keyFile` (1 hit, KS-336, Done, the original design), `key file` (3 hits, none about tenant creation), `B-5` (KS-630, KS-612; neither concerns this), `TOKENISATION.md` (KS-525, KS-300; neither concerns this), `ClientList` (0), `vault key` (0), `keyPending` (0). None records that the key file is no longer returned.

Related to KS-1240 (not a blocker).

title: ks1263 KS-1310 describe: the disposable-database guard reads new URL(dsn), so a ?host= or ?port= in the DSN query string passes it (same hole as KS-1340, on a guard that protects DDL)
description:
**BLUF:** the disposable-database guard in the third describe of `ks1263-multi-write-rolls-back.integration.test.ts` (the KS 1310 describe, which creates a trigger on `documents`) judges `new URL(DEFAULT_DB)`, the host and port the DSN's authority names. A `?host=` or `?port=` in the query string passes it while the pg client dials the remote host, or port 5432. It is the same hole as KS-1340, in a guard that protects schema DDL. Not fixed in pull request 1790, pull request 1792 or the KS-1600 pull request; Wednesday asked for this ticket (ANSWER 2026-10-28 12:23:51Z).

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1263-multi-write-rolls-back.integration.test.ts`, the `beforeAll` of the describe "KS-1310 ROUTE-LEVEL ...". At develop `d531abd5f34b` the block is lines 589 to 598: `new URL(DEFAULT_DB)`, hostname in `['127.0.0.1', 'localhost']`, port in 55410 to 55419, else it throws "KS-1310 installs a trigger (schema DDL) and therefore refuses any database that is not this seat's disposable one".

## Measured

The exact predicate of line 591 run beside the pg client on four DSNs (pg 8.20.0, pg-connection-string 2.12.0; constructing a Client opens no socket, so nothing was dialled):

```
DSN                                      guard accepts   pg dials
postgres://u:p@127.0.0.1:55412/db        true            127.0.0.1:55412
...@127.0.0.1:55412/db?host=203.0.113.7  true            203.0.113.7:55412
...@127.0.0.1:55412/db?port=5432         true            127.0.0.1:5432
postgres://u:p@203.0.113.7:55412/db      false           203.0.113.7:55412
```

A DSN that names no port is already refused here (`Number('')` is 0, outside the range), which is not true of the ks597 guard KS-1340 fixes. Probe script: `5_Project_History/2026-10-28_seatT-5th/tools/sibling_guard_probe_t5.js` in the project record.

## Why it matters, and its limit

The guard's own comment says a cell that writes DDL must be unable to reach a shared or real database. This describe runs `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` and `CREATE TRIGGER ... ON documents` against whatever `TEST_DATABASE_URL` names. The hole is reachable only if that variable carries such a query string (an operator mistake or an unusual DSN); it is not reachable by default, and nothing was run against a shared database to test it.

## Fix shape (the KS-1340 one; not chosen here)

Judge the host and port the pg client will dial, by asking the client (`new Client({ connectionString }).host` and `.port`), as pull request 1790 does for the ks597 guard, and keep the 55410 to 55419 range test on that answer. KS-1340 also refuses a DSN that names `hostaddr` (pg ignores it, libpq honours it).

## Board search before filing

Issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, run at 12:2xZ and again immediately before filing: `55410` gave 0 hits, `refuses any database that is not this` gave 0, `KS-1310 installs a trigger` gave 0. Positive control `disposable`: 19 hits at filing time (19 at the first run). Zero control: a fresh token never written to the board returned 0; the token is not recorded here so that it stays a control. No existing ticket covers this guard.

## Related

KS-1340 (the ks597 guard, pull request 1790). KS-1310 (added this guard; Done). KS-1499 (pull request 1792 edits the same file for other reasons and leaves this guard as it is).

title: smoke-test.sh is not remote-clean: 12 localhost:60xx checks, RUNBOOK 2.2's remote full run, and URL credentials echoed in "Smoke target:"
description:
**BLUF:** `scripts/smoke-test.sh` is still not remote-clean after PR 1793 made its `GATEWAY` honour `SMOKE_BASE_URL` (KS-1250). One remote full run would show all three problems below at once, which is why they are one ticket. Low. Related to KS-1250. Filed on the tier-2 gate's note (gate 8, 2026-10-28), after a search of the board (quoted at the end).

**Nobody runs this script against kintsugi, demo or any live box to reproduce or check any of this.** A full run anchors a real document, and that run is held for Kam (the KS-1250 hold). Everything below was read from the script or measured with a stub `curl` on a private PATH against a `.invalid` host.

1. **12 hard-coded** `http://localhost:60xx` **service-port checks remain in the full run** (sections 7 onward): lines 259, 263, 267, 275, 283, 292, 305, 307, 317, 319, 327 and 329 of `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh` at PR 1793's head `29989b01ab05`. PR 1793 moves only `GATEWAY`, so with `SMOKE_BASE_URL` set to a remote gateway those 12 checks still hit localhost, and the run mixes two environments while reading as a result for one.
2. **RUNBOOK section 2.2 still tells an operator to do a remote full run.** `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/RUNBOOK.md` lines 139 to 143: `SMOKE_BASE_URL=https://<prod-gateway-fqdn> ../../scripts/smoke-test.sh`, under the heading "Bash smoke against production gateway", with no `--quick`.
3. **The** `Smoke target:` **line echoes credentials embedded in the URL verbatim.** Measured with a stub `curl` and `--quick`: `SMOKE_BASE_URL='https://alice:s3cr3t-token@smoke-target.invalid:9999'` (a fake credential) prints, as line 1 of the output, `Smoke target: https://alice:s3cr3t-token@smoke-target.invalid:9999`. A base URL carrying a token or basic-auth would be written to the terminal and to any CI log. The stub recorded 9 requests, all to `smoke-target.invalid`.

Also on this ticket: **no test cell uses an** `https://` **base** (the new suite uses `http://smoke-target.invalid:9999`), so the gate's mutant M11 survives.

Fix shapes, not chosen here: route the 12 service-port checks through a base the way `GATEWAY` is, or skip them with a printed line when the base is not localhost; make section 2.2 say `--quick` or say what a remote full run does not cover; print the target as scheme, host and port only.

**Searched before filing** (Linear `issues` filter over title, description and comments, archived included, team KS, 2026-10-28 13:4xZ): `remote-clean` 1 hit, KS-1250 itself; `smoke-test.sh` 11 hits, read: none is this follow-up (KS 1245 is the Done degraded-health fix, KS 1139 the arithmetic-under-errexit fix, KS 1101 a health-aggregation ticket); `SMOKE_BASE_URL` 2 hits, KS-1250 and a review comment on KS 1101 that repeats the same O-2 finding; `Smoke target` 1 hit, KS-1250; the zero control `zzqq-no-such-token-r6b` 0 hits.

title: ks597 integration guard (KS-1340): 127.0.0.1:6433, the shared stack's pgbouncer, is accepted, and the hostaddr refusal is case- and percent-encoding-literal
description:
**BLUF:** the guard that pull request 1790 gives the ks597 integration file (KS-1340) refuses the shared stack's Postgres ports 5432 and 6432 but not **6433**, the port docker-compose publishes for the shared stack's pgbouncer, which fronts the same shared database. `postgres://u:p@127.0.0.1:6433/db` is accepted, and so is `...:55412/db?port=6433`. Separately, its `hostaddr` refusal matches the lower-case key literally, so `?HOSTADDR=` and `?host%61ddr=` pass it. One guard and one logical path, so one ticket. Neither is a change to pull request 1790, which merges as gated (gate 8, 2026-10-29: #1790 GO). Filed on Wednesday's ANSWER of 2026-10-28 13:38:21Z; gate 8 findings 1790-1 and 1790-2.

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks597-issuer-organization-id.integration.test.ts`: the `SHARED_STACK_PORTS` list (the port `5432` plus the `POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT` default read from docker-compose.yml) and the `hostaddr` test in `disposableDsnTarget()`, at the head of pull request 1790 (`3a9b1c121f6d`). The port list is pre-existing (KS-1306); the pull request did not change it.

## 1. Port 6433

docker-compose.yml publishes the shared stack's Postgres on `127.0.0.1:${POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT:-6432}` (line 156) and its pgbouncer on `127.0.0.1:${PGBOUNCER_PORT:-6433}` (line 262, container port 6432), the pooler every service connects through. The guard's list is `["5432","6432"]` (printed by the probe below). KS-296 records the labels (6432 = direct Postgres, 6433 = pgbouncer) and the compose stack-safety script's list in KS-1558's description already includes 6433.

Measured by running the pull request's own guard function, extracted from the file at its head and transpiled, beside the pg client (pg 8.20.0; no database and no socket: 0 connect calls, with a control reading 1):

```
DSN                                    guard                       pg dials
control: clean loopback, free port     ACCEPTED 127.0.0.1:55412    127.0.0.1:55412
control: shared postgres port 5432     REFUSED                     127.0.0.1:5432
control: shared published port 6432    REFUSED                     127.0.0.1:6432
pgbouncer published port 6433          ACCEPTED 127.0.0.1:6433     127.0.0.1:6433
6433 named only in the query string    ACCEPTED 127.0.0.1:6433     127.0.0.1:6433
```

Nothing was run against a pooler. Gate 8 found the same independently. Not measured: a stack started on another slot publishes pgbouncer and Postgres on other ports (KS-390's table lists 6533, 6633 and so on), and the list reads only the default; whether it should cover slot ports is a decision for whoever fixes this.

## 2. The hostaddr refusal is literal

The test is `/[?&]hostaddr(=|&|$)/`: lower case, not percent-decoded. Measured with the same probe: `?HOSTADDR=203.0.113.7` and `?host%61ddr=203.0.113.7` are accepted, and the pg client dials the authority (`127.0.0.1:55412`) for both. There is **no measured bypass**: pg ignores `hostaddr` in every spelling, and no consumer of the DSN in this file is libpq. The rule's stated reason is that libpq honours `hostaddr`; the gate states that libpq also decodes percent-escapes in a key, so the rule only partly meets that reason. I did not run libpq here.

## Fix shape (not chosen here)

Read the pgbouncer default from the compose file the way the Postgres one is read (`PGBOUNCER_PORT:-(\d+)\}:6432`), so the list cannot drift; and either decode and lower-case the query's keys before the `hostaddr` test, or refuse any query key outside a short allow-list.

## Also noted by the gate, not measured

Finding 1790-3: the same DSN is handed to the product as `DATABASE_URL` (Prisma), whose parser may read a duplicate or overriding query key differently from the pg client. Checking that needs a connection attempt.

## Board search before filing

title: change-password publishes no 422: a weak new password is documented under 400 while the route answers 422
description:
**BLUF:** the published contract for `POST /api/users/me/change-password` lists **no 422** and documents a too-weak new password under **400** ("Wrong current password or new password too weak"), while the route answers **422** for a weak password. This is a pre-existing contract gap, found by the tier-1 gate on the KS-1467 services/auth change (finding 1799-7); KS-1467 was ruled to change no OpenAPI, so it did not touch it. Low. Related to KS-1467.

**What I read, at develop** `802eb2b8ecaf`**:**

1. `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, operation `/api/users/me/change-password`, response codes: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 415, 429, 500, 502, 503. There is no 422. The 400 description reads "Wrong current password or new password too weak".
2. The source of that text is `services/auth/src/auth.openapi.ts` line 1012: `400: { ...commonErrorResponses[400], description: 'Wrong current password or new password too weak' }`, and that operation's `responses` has no 422 entry.
3. The two sibling routes do publish it: reset-password has `422: ... 'New password too weak'` (a comment at `auth.openapi.ts` line 813 cites KS 255), and register has a 422 described "Weak password, or client-supplied `role` field (not permitted)".
4. The route throws `new ValidationError('New password is too weak', ...)` (`services/auth/src/routes/users.ts`, around line 993 at the pin), and `ValidationError` answers 422. The route-level cell for change-password in the KS-1467 PR drives the real route and reads status 422 for weak candidates.

**Not claimed:** I ran no schema-conformance tool against the yaml for this; the gate measured it on the wire (finding 1799-7). A wrong *current* password is a 400 and stays one.

**Fix shapes, not chosen here:** add `422: { ...commonErrorResponses[422], description: 'New password too weak' }` to the change-password operation and take "or new password too weak" out of the 400 text, then regenerate the yaml (`generate-openapi`, `check:openapi`). That changes the published contract, so it wants its own ruling; the KS-1467 ruling was no OpenAPI change. Since KS-1467 round 2 the 422 `details` is the published ZodIssue-compatible array, so documenting the 422 matches what the route sends.

**Searched before filing** (Linear `issues` filter over title, description and comments, archived included, team KS, 2026-10-28 15:5xZ): `new password too weak` 0 hits; `publishes no 422` 0; `no 422` with `change-password` 0; `change-password` with `422` 7 hits (KS-1467, KS-1005, KS-732, KS-501, KS-486, KS-485, KS-480), read: none records this gap; `too weak` with `yaml` 2 hits (KS 255, KS 141), neither covers change-password; the zero control `zzqq-no-such-token-r6c` 0 hits; the positive control (title `AppError resets`) found KS-1467.

title: Security (nit): decideMint's toUpperCase admits a dotless-i, a long-s and an array role as a key admin; plus the role-comparison sweep
description:
**BLUF:** `decideMint` (`services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:96-97`, the `POST /api/keys` admission test) still compares `String(caller?.role ?? '').toUpperCase()` against the key-admin set, so a role spelled with U+0131 (dotless i) or U+017F (long s), or an array role, can be read as an admin role. KS-1591 fixed the same shape in `isPlatformRole` and `requireKeyAdmin` and deliberately left this site; this ticket tracks it, and the sweep of other role comparisons that KS-1591's description asks for, so that KS-1591 can close. Reachability is not established.

## Where

`services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts` at develop `5dccdcb29ec20393e80cbdb1e359a49caa633165` (the build on both boxes), read with `git show`:

* line 96: `const role = String(caller?.role ?? '');`
* line 97: `if (KEY_ADMIN_ROLES.has(role.toUpperCase())) {`

## What is measured and what is not

* Measured by the tier-2 gate on 2026-10-28 (the batch covering PRs 1775, 1776 and 1780, GO WITH NOTES): `decideMint` admits a role spelled with U+0131 or U+017F, and an array role, at PR 1776's head `8b92887a6fac`. The gate's note was filed on KS-1591 as a comment (`42e97e12`).
* Read by me, not run: lines 96 and 97 are unchanged at the deployed build. I ran no test of `decideMint` with those roles.
* Not established: whether any issuer, user-management path or seed can store or sign a token with such a role. That needs a token the auth service signs. KS-1591 said the same. Until someone measures it this is a nit; if any path can, it is a privilege escalation (admission to mint API keys) and should be re-rated at once.

## Recommendation

Not built. Apply the KS-1591 remedy here: fold ASCII letters only (`replace(/[a-z]/g, ...)`, as `isPlatformRole` now does) and refuse a role that is not a string, in the one shared definition so every caller inherits it. Cells: a dotless-i spelling, a long-s spelling and an array role each refused by `decideMint`; a control that every ASCII spelling admitted today is still admitted.

## Sweep candidates (not findings)

Method: `git grep -n -I "toUpperCase()"` at `5dccdcb29ec2` over `Blockchain/Dev/services` and `Blockchain/Dev/packages`, tests, `dist` and `node_modules` excluded, keeping lines that also contain "role" (case-insensitive). 14 lines. Controls: the `decideMint` line is in the result (1 line from `provisioningPolicy.ts`); a nonsense token over the same paths matches 0 files. Of the 14: 2 are comments, 2 are the sites KS-1591 fixed (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:144`, `security/src/index.ts:1104`), 1 is `decideMint`, and 9 are other candidates:

* `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:85` and `:102` (`ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES`, `SCOPED_ADMIN_ROLES`; the same file KS-1591 changed at `:144`)
* `packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts:288`
* `services/auth/src/routes/issuerCerts.ts:71`
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:285` and `:377`
* `services/auth/src/services/password.ts:234` (whether it is a role comparison is unread)
* `services/originate/src/middleware/rbac.ts:56` and `:58`

I read none of these beyond the matching line. The census misses a comparison split across lines or through another variable name. KS-1601 tracks the SQL counterpart (`upper(role) = $3` in the admin-scope route).

## Board search (before filing)

Issues filter with `includeArchived: true`, title or description (comments excluded), read 2026-10-29: tickets whose title contains `decideMint`: 0. Tickets naming `decideMint` together with "dotless", "0131" or "017F": 0. Controls: `isPlatformRole` finds 7 tickets (KS-1701, KS-1601, KS-1591, KS-1536, KS-1535, KS-976, KS-743); a random nonsense token finds 0. The only place the gap is recorded is the gate's note on KS-1591 (a comment, which this search excludes). title: A kept (refused-anchor) certification reads anchored: true on GET /api/documents/{id}, and POST /anchor 400s "already anchored"
description:
**BLUF:** A certification whose anchor was refused is now kept and marked unanchored (KS-1709, Kam's 2026-10-23 ruling b: "keep it, but mark it unanchored"). Its blob carries `blockchain.status` `failed`. The documents surface still reads that blob as anchored: `GET /api/documents/{id}` answers `blockchain.anchored: true`, and `POST /api/documents/{id}/anchor` answers 400 "Document is already anchored", so the documents retry route cannot re-anchor it. The comparison dates from KS-1124 F4 (2026-09-28); the ruling turns it into a contradiction on a second read surface.

**What was measured** (QA gate 15, finding 1806-1, on the KS-1709 pull request head; documentRepo mocked, the real `documentsRouter`):

* A certification is a row in `documents`, so `GET /api/documents/{certUuid}` serves it. With the blob the KS-1709 cells assert (`status: 'failed'`, `anchoringStatus: 'failed'`, `anchorId: null`), GET answers `blockchain.anchored: true` and `POST /api/documents/{id}/anchor` answers 400 "Document is already anchored".
* Controls in the same probe: a blob with `status: 'anchor_failed'` gives `anchored: false` and POST 202; a null blob gives `anchored: false` and POST 202.
* `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` returns early on `anchorId: null`, so nothing heals it.

**Where** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`):

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1200`: `anchored: !!document.blockchain && document.blockchain.status !== 'anchor_failed'`.
* `documents.ts:1458`: `if (document.blockchain && document.blockchain.status !== 'anchor_failed')` then 400 "Document is already anchored".
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:99-100`: `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES` is `['failed', 'anchor_failed']`, so the verify surfaces already read `failed` as failed.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:1204`: `POST /api/certifications/{id}/verify` builds `checks.blockchainAnchored` as `!!certification.blockchain`, which is true for a kept failed certification (Seat U 6th recorded this in its KS-1709 wrap; I read the line and did not run it).

**The gate's fix-shape (not ruled):** use one set, for example `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES`, at both `documents.ts` sites. The regression test the gate proposed: the kept-certification blob gives GET `anchored: false` and POST `/anchor` 202.

**Evidence:**

* `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-29_gate15-1805-1806/verdict.md`, finding 1806-1
* the probe it names, in the same folder: `evidence/probe/_quarantine_2026-10-29/gate15-probe-docs.test.ts` and `evidence/probe/probe_docs.out`

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 9 hits, a random token 0 hits): `documents.ts:1200` 0 hits; `documents.ts:1458` 2 hits, read (KS-1709's description lists that line among three other sites with the same missing `else` for a non-ok anchoring response, which is a different defect; KS-772 comments describe the retry route's 400 for the stuck kintsugi document, and there is no ticket for this defect there); `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES` 1 hit (KS-1640, chain-first verify blobs: a different surface); "Document is already anchored" 2 hits (KS-1650, the check is not network-bound; KS-282, archived, document versions); "status !== 'anchor_failed'" 3 hits (KS-1628, the deprecated verify route and placeholder hashes; KS-1158; KS-1004, archived); "keep it, but mark" and "kept certification": KS-1709 only. None of these describes this defect.

**Not measured:** I read the lines above at develop `6d41673e0f79` and did not re-run the gate's probe.

**Related:** KS-1709 (the ruling and the change), KS-1124 (where the `failed` blob began), KS-1640.

title: KS-1709 follow-ups: non-JSON 2xx reads 'failed'; recertify unpublished with no fetch timeout; no re-anchor for a kept certification
description:
**BLUF:** Four loose ends from KS-1709, none introduced by it. QA gate 15 (1806-2, 1806-3) and Seat U 6th listed them in comments on KS-1709, and none has a ticket of its own: (1) an accepted 2xx from the anchoring service whose body is not JSON is reported as `failed`; (2) `POST /api/certifications/{id}/recertify` is not in the published spec; (3) its anchoring `fetch` has no timeout; (4) Platform K has no re-anchor for a kept certification.

**1. A non-JSON 2xx reads** `failed` (gate 15, 1806-2, measured at runtime). `upstream.json()` throws inside the `try` before `anchoringStatus = 'submitted'` is set (`certifications.ts:619-621` on the issue route; the same shape at `:1393-1395` on recertify, read only). On the issue route a 202 with an empty body gives 201 with `anchoringStatus: "failed"`, and a 200 with the text `ok` gives the same. In production the 202-empty case gives 503 with the provisional row deleted although anchoring had accepted the request (an orphan anchor; the gate records the production part as pre-existing). A 202 or 299 with a JSON id, and a 202 without `data.id`, give no key and `submitted`; a 409 gives `failed`. The published description says "a 4xx, a 5xx, an unreachable service or a timeout" and omits this case. The gate's likelihood note: low, since anchoring always answers JSON. The gate's fix-shape (not ruled): set `submitted` on `upstream.ok` before parsing (anchorId null when unreadable), or add "or an unreadable acceptance" to the description.

**2. Recertify is not published** (gate 15, 1806-3, read). `originate.openapi.ts:27` lists `/:id/recertify` among the endpoints not yet registered, and `secuura-api.yaml` has 0 matches for `recertify` (counted at develop `6d41673e0f79`). So the top-level `anchoringStatus` that KS-1709 added to the recertify 201 ships unpublished; `CertificationIssueResponse` covers the issue route only.

**3. Recertify's anchoring fetch has no timeout** (gate 15, 1806-3, read). The issue route's fetch carries `AbortSignal.timeout(10000)` (`certifications.ts:616`). The recertify fetch (`certifications.ts:1375-1395`) carries none, and the builder's own test header says so. The effective bound is the runtime's default fetch timeout, which nobody measured.

**4. No re-anchor for a kept certification** (Seat U 6th's KS-1709 wrap). A kept certification has `anchorId: null`. U 6th records that Platform K has no re-anchor for it; I did not search for one.

**Evidence:**

* `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-29_gate15-1805-1806/verdict.md`, findings 1806-2 and 1806-3
* the gate's probe output in the same folder: `evidence/probe/probe1806.out` (P1 to P10)
* Seat U 6th's wrap: `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatU-6th/HANDOVER.md`

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 9 hits, a random token 0 hits): "unreadable acceptance" 0 hits; "AbortSignal" 10 hits, read for relevance (KS-1666 names the issue route's 10 second window; KS-1664 has no timeout text; the rest are other services); "recertify" 13 hits, read for relevance (KS-1664 and KS-1633 are the orphan-anchor ordering, a different defect). The four items appear only as comments on KS-1709 (07:02Z) and KS-1175.

**Not measured:** the recertify default fetch timeout; items 2 and 3 are source readings at develop `6d41673e0f79`, not runs.

**Related:** KS-1709.

title: For one anchor id the anchor row reads failed while its document reads confirmed; a document read and a verify can settle it either way
description:

The document's stored blob reads `confirmed` against the upload transaction `b1cc72f9…` (block 4801203), written at 08:56:52Z after two `POST /api/verification/verify` calls. The code has two readers that can settle the same pair in opposite directions: a document read can write `anchor_failed`, a verify wrote `confirmed`. Only the verify-first order was observed.

title: didJwkRefusal's early return for a pattern-refused value is pinned by no cell: removing it leaves 183 of 183 cells green
description:
**BLUF:** In `didJwkRefusal` (anchoring `anchorSchema.ts`, the KS-1175 private-key guard) the early return for a value the shape checks already refuse is pinned by no cell. I removed its pattern clause on develop `6d41673e0f79` and all 183 cells of the two DID test files stayed green. Without the clause a malformed `did:jwk` reports two issues instead of one. It is still a 400, so the effect is on the error body only.

**Source** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`): `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts:166` is `if (!value.startsWith(DID_JWK_PREFIX) || value.length > DID_MAX_LENGTH || !DID_PATTERN.test(value)) return null;`. The comment above it (`:157`) says a value the shape checks already refuse is left to those checks, "refused once, for its own reason". The cap clause on the same line is pinned: gate 16's mutant X11 is killed by the "over the cap, refused once, as too_big" cells. The pattern clause is not.

**Measured by me, on develop** `6d41673e0f79` (`services/anchoring`, vitest, Node v26.8.1):

* Control, nothing planted: `ks1175-identity-anchoring.test.ts` and `anchorSchema.test.ts`, 2 files, **183 passed (183)**.
* Mutant X12, the line with `|| !DID_PATTERN.test(value)` removed (an exact-once replace, restored afterwards; file blob equal to the staged blob after the restore): the same 2 files, **183 passed (183)**. The mutant survives every cell.
* What the mutant changes, probed through `identitySchema`: `did:jwk:<public P-256 payload>==` and `did:jwk:ab cd` report `["invalid_string","custom"]`. With the code as it is, both report exactly `["invalid_string"]`. (Positive control in the same probe: a public P-256 `did:jwk` is accepted and a private one is refused.)
* Zod runs `superRefine` even after `.regex` or `.max` failed (gate 16 measured it on `z.string().max(5).regex(/^a+$/).superRefine(...)`: `"b"` gives `invalid_string ; custom`), which is why the clause matters.

**Regression test the gate proposed (not ruled):** for both fields, `issuesFor(field, 'did:jwk:' + <public payload> + '==')` and `issuesFor(field, 'did:jwk:ab cd')` each equal exactly `['invalid_string']`.

**Evidence:**

* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatR-61st/evidence/anchoring/` : `g_control_two_files.log`, `g_mutant_x12_two_files.log`, `g_mutant_x12_probe.log`, `probe_didjwk_develop_6d41673e.log`; the probe is `tools/probe_didjwk_r61.ts`

title: The published did:jwk pattern admits values the runtime refuses (5,000 of 5,000 sampled); POST /api/anchors has no Schemathesis override
description:
**BLUF:** The published `did:jwk` pattern admits values the runtime refuses. In a seeded sample of 5,000 values that satisfy the published pattern, `identitySchema` refused 5,000 of 5,000 `did:jwk` values, against 0 of 5,000 for `did:key` and 0 of 5,000 for `did:web`. `systemTest/schemathesis/schemathesis.toml` has no `[[operations]]` entry for `POST /api/anchors`, so a Schemathesis positive-data sweep that generates a `did:jwk` for `actorDid` or `orgDid` is expected to meet a 400. Not measured against a stack: no sweep was run.

**Facts** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`):

* `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml:1295` and `:1320` publish `pattern: ^did:(key|web|jwk):[A-Za-z0-9._:%-]+$` for both identity DID fields. `POST /api/anchors` is published at `:14619`. The yaml holds 0 `did:jwk` examples and 1 `did:key` example.
* Since KS-1175's private-key guard, the runtime refuses a `did:jwk` unless the payload is unpadded base64url of a JSON object with none of `d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi`, `k` (`anchorSchema.ts:165-178`). A random string over the pattern's alphabet almost never decodes to a JSON object. The JSON-decodability half cannot be written as a JSON-Schema pattern at all, so some gap is irreducible.
* `systemTest/schemathesis/schemathesis.toml`: `[checks.positive_data_acceptance]` at `:128`; the file's per-operation entries scope some paths (for example `include-name = "POST /api/auth/login"`), and the only line that names an anchors operation is `include-name = "POST /api/anchors/thread-mint"` at `:424`; the mentions of flat `/api/anchors` at `:509-515` are in a comment. The global positive-data-acceptance list excludes 400.
* The description text on both fields states the rule and the 400; gate 16 records that it is generated from the imported member list and that `generate-openapi --check` goes rc 1 when a member is dropped.

**Measured:**

* By me, on develop `6d41673e0f79`: `tools/probe_didjwk_r61.ts` draws 5,000 values per method, seeded, length 1 to 40, uniform over the 67-character alphabet, keeps those that pass `DID_PATTERN`, and counts refusals by `identitySchema`: did:key 0 of 5000, did:web 0 of 5000, did:jwk 5000 of 5000. Positive controls in the same run: a public P-256 `did:jwk`, a `did:key` and a `did:web` are accepted; a private `did:jwk` is refused.
* By QA gate 16 on the KS-1175 guard's pull request head: the same sampling gave the same three figures.

**Fix-shape (gate 16 and Wednesday's addendum prefer (a); not ruled):**

* (a) In the KS-571 style, a `map_case` hook (like `systemTest/schemathesis/config/connector_only_field.py`) that swaps a generated `did:jwk` for a valid public one in POSITIVE bodies of `POST /api/anchors`. Not a widened `expected-statuses`, which the file's own KS-544 rule calls masking.
* (b) Optional: a per-method pattern, `^did:(key|web):[A-Za-z0-9._:%-]+$|^did:jwk:[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`. That aligns the alphabet half with the runtime's strict check but changes the error code for a stray `.`, `:` or `%` from `custom` to `invalid_string`, so cells move.

**Evidence:**

* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatR-61st/evidence/anchoring/probe_didjwk_develop_6d41673e.log`

title: The ruled-retry cell (ks726:414) paraphrases the node's reply: with the real text it fails, and deleting the clause breaks no cell
description:
**BLUF:** The cell that pins the ruled retry after a node rejection, `ks726-write-ahead-tx-hash.test.ts:414`, feeds the guard a paraphrase of the node's reply (`"All inputs are spent"`). The node's real text, stored in `ks705-submission-idempotency.test.ts:48-50`, carries a second phrase, "already been included", and the `ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY` clause in `anchorSubmission.ts` turns the retry off for any text that contains it. No test pairs the real text with a write-ahead and an absent re-poll. I deleted the clause on develop `6d41673e0f79` and the whole anchoring suite's failing set stayed identical to the control; and when I gave the `:414` cell the real text, it failed. So the clause that makes the ruled retry unreachable for the real reply is unpinned, and the cell that should have caught it tests a text the node does not send.

**Source** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/`):

* `anchorSubmission.ts:112` `const ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY = /already been included/i;`, also listed among the patterns `isAlreadySubmittedError` matches (`:115-124`).
* `anchorSubmission.ts:637-641`: `refusedAndAbsent = found === 'absent' && known === writtenAheadTxHash && !ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY.test(message ?? '')`, then `if (!refusedAndAbsent) return;`. The comment at `:635-636` says "already been included" names this transaction as in the ledger and never reaches this branch's retry.
* `__tests__/ks726-write-ahead-tx-hash.test.ts:414` the cell "a 400 "All inputs are spent" after onSigned, the re-poll finds the hash ABSENT with DEFINITIVE evidence → scheduleRetry, no submitting rest"; its fixture at `:417` is `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent"`. The control at `:452` uses `'this transaction has already been included'` (`:453`), a text that matches no reply recorded in the repo.
* `__tests__/ks705-submission-idempotency.test.ts:47-50`: "The node reply measured on demo, as Blockfrost surfaces it": `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent. Transaction has probably already been included in a successfully applied block."`
* Phrase census at the pin: "already been included" appears in `ks705` (4 times), `ks726` (2), `anchorSubmission.ts` (3) and `Blockchain/Dev/env.example` (1); the long form "probably already been included" appears in `ks705` only, and `ks705` has no write-ahead, no `status_code` and no absent re-poll (per Seat W 7th's reading; I did not re-read every cell of that file). The KS-1171 files that use `onSigned` or the poll constants contain neither phrase.

**Measured by me** (develop `6d41673e0f79`, `services/anchoring`, vitest, Node v26.8.1; logs in `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatR-61st/evidence/anchoring/`, files `j_*`):

* Control, whole suite, nothing planted: 33 files, 456 cells, **1 failed** (`threadTokenMint … parameterises mint + spend with a deterministic per-seed policyId`, which is red on develop already).
* Control mutant M0, `&& false` appended to the conjunction: **4 failed**; the three extra reds are `ks726…:414`, `ks1171-b1-absent-boundary-is-inclusive` and `ks1171b-absent-needs-both-conditions`. So the suite does notice changes to this line.
* Mutant X, the `!ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY.test(message ?? '')` line deleted (an exact-once replace, restored afterwards with the file's blob read back equal to the staged blob): **1 failed**, and the failing set is byte-identical to the control's (`j_failset_control.txt`, `j_failset_x.txt`). X survives.
* Probe, three untracked copies of `ks726`, each run on that one cell and then deleted: (1) unchanged, short text: **passes**; (2) the line-417 fixture replaced with the `ks705` text, clause present: **fails**, `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` (`scheduleRetry` never called); (3) the same real text with mutant X planted: **passes**. So for the node's real reply the clause is exactly what stops the retry.
* Reproduce: copy `ks726-write-ahead-tx-hash.test.ts`, replace line 417 with the string from `ks705:48-50`, run the cell with `vitest run <copy> -t "the re-poll finds the hash ABSENT with DEFINITIVE evidence"`.

**What this does and does not say:** it says the real reply makes the `:414` cell fail on today's code and that no cell would notice the clause going. It does not say which side is right: whether the clause should stay is a product question, and Seat W 7th's KS-1384 revision (section 3.2) proposes dropping it. Whether the node's refusal text at the two incidents of 28 and 29 October was this long form was not measured (the logs are cut; Seat W 7th lists it as unmeasured).

**Evidence:**

* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatR-61st/evidence/anchoring/` : `j_control_whole_anchoring_suite.log`, `j_m0_conjunction_false.log`, `j_x_clause_deleted.log`, `j_probe_short.log`, `j_probe_long.log`, `j_probe_long_x.log`, `j_failset_*.txt`
* `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatW-7th/KS-1384-per-event-anchor-DESIGN-rev2.md`, section 3.2 (the code path) and 3.5 (the six cells; sub-agent B's reading, "not run" there, which this ticket now runs); section 16 item 4.

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 17 hits, a random token 0 hits): `ALREADY_INCLUDED_REPLY` 0 hits; `ks726-write-ahead-tx-hash.test.ts:414` 0 hits; `refusedAndAbsent` 1 hit, read: KS-1171 calls `refusedAndAbsent` the reader of the "absent" verdict and says nothing about the text clause; "already been included" 4 hits and "probably already been included" 4 hits, read: KS-726, KS-705 and KS-535 (all archived) record the reply, and KS-607 (Backlog) tabulates UAT anchors by the node's text `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent"`, which is a different defect (GET /api/anchors and verify disagree on status). No ticket describes the paraphrased cell or the unpinned clause.

**Related:** KS-1384 (the revision that proposes dropping the clause), KS-1171 (the absence rule the retry depends on), KS-726 (the write-ahead; archived, so Linear refuses a relation to it: named here only).

title: anchoring POST /api/anchors/thread-mint spends the platform wallet outside withWalletLock for any authenticated caller (fee drain)
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/anchors/thread-mint` has no role check, and a non-dry-run call signs and submits a mint transaction from the platform wallet without taking `withWalletLock`, which the anchoring paths use. By the source, any caller with a valid token that reaches the anchoring service can spend the platform wallet's funds, and its spend can race the anchoring queue for the same UTxOs (the failure class KS-535 recorded; the race is inferred, not reproduced). High, security.

## What I read (develop 6d41673e0f79)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts:470`: `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate())`, so the route is authenticated, nothing more.
* `index.ts:1008-1089`: the handler validates the body, then (when `BLOCKFROST_API_KEY` and `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` are set) imports `mintAndLock` (`:1052`) and calls it. It reads no caller, role or tenant, and runs no database query.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/cardano/threadTokenMint.ts`: `mintAndLock` picks a seed UTxO from the platform wallet (`:262-266`), builds, signs and calls `signed.submit()` (`:339`). `dryRun: true` returns before the submit (`:322`).
* `withWalletLock` appears 0 times in `threadTokenMint.ts` and in the handler. Control: 5 times in `anchorSubmission.ts`, and the batch path calls it at `index.ts:1991`.

## What I did not run or read

* No request to any box or process. Whether the gateway routes this path to outside callers: not read. How much each call costs (I did not read `threadTokenMint.ts:262-340` beyond the lines above): not measured. Whether the race with anchoring happens in practice: not reproduced.

title: anchoring: the in-lock confirmed write omits the transaction hash, so a same-payload upsert can leave a confirmed row with a NULL hash
description:
**BLUF:** Inferred from the code, not reproduced. The in-lock `confirmed` write carries no `transactionHash`, the front-door upsert overwrites the stored hash on conflict, and guard 2 treats a row without a 64-hex hash as "no known submission". A same-payload upsert that lands during the roughly 27-minute in-lock confirmation poll could therefore leave the row `confirmed` with a NULL hash, and the queued call would build and submit a second transaction. Money-class; ruled High by Wednesday.

## What I read (develop 6d41673e0f79)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/anchorSubmission.ts:490-499`: the `confirmed` update sets status, confirmations, block number, slot, block hash, `confirmedAt` and `expectMetadataPayload`, and no `transactionHash`; the earlier `submitted` update (`:482`) does set it.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1454-1456`: the front-door insert is `ON CONFLICT (document_id, network) DO UPDATE SET status = EXCLUDED.status, transaction_hash = EXCLUDED.transaction_hash, ...`.
* `anchorSubmission.ts:430-432` (guard 2 re-reads the row inside the lock and returns "already" only if `knownChainSubmission` yields a hash) and `:244-251` (`knownChainSubmission` needs status submitting, submitted or confirmed AND a 64-hex `transactionHash`).
* The poll length comes from Seat R 61st's arithmetic on KS-1816 (27.2 to 28.2 minutes); I did not recompute it.

## What I did not run or read

* No reproduction, no database, no box. I did not read the compare-and-set in `anchorStatusUpdate.ts` or whether `expectMetadataPayload` would restore the hash on the `confirmed` write.

title: POST /api/documents/:id/sign: any tenant user can sign any document, can turn a revoked document into signed, and no signature is verified
description:
**BLUF:** originate `POST /api/documents/:id/sign` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1271-1346` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication, the request body, the caller's tenant and the signing nonce, and nothing about the caller or the document's state. It then appends a signature and writes `status: 'signed'` (:1326-1329) through `updateDocument` with no options, so a revoked or deleted document is written back to `signed`. The signature itself is not verified: `isValidSignature` (:1313) accepts any string that starts `mock_signature_` or is longer than 50 characters, in every environment. Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No role or scope gate, no owner or signer check and no terminal-status check between :1271 and :1346. `getDocument` (:1294) scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* The nonce (:1299-1311) ties the call to a `POST /:id/sign/request` for the same document id, and that route is open to any authenticated user in the tenant (filed separately).
* `updateDocument(id, tenantId, { signatures, status: 'signed' })` passes no `preserveTerminalStatuses`, so documentRepo's KS-521 guard (it keeps `revoked` and `deleted` only when asked) is off for this write.
* `isValidSignature = signature.startsWith('mock_signature_') || signature.length > 50` (:1313): no cryptographic check and no environment guard. KS-627 is the wallet-connector analogue (`POST /api/wallets/verify`), not this route.
* Callers: the issuer UI's Sign button posts here (`frontend/issuer/src/components/DocumentDetail.tsx:252`); the api-gateway mounts it with `authenticateToken(true)` and `blockPendingApproval` only (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1026`). Platform S does not list this verb among the ones it sends (KS-1688, comment of 2026-10-19).

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** the anchor route's predicate (a write role or scope, then admin, owner or creating connector) does not apply unchanged here. A signer is not necessarily the owner or a write-role holder, so who may sign is this route's own policy question. A terminal-status refusal would apply, but on its own it does not close the route.

**Priority 2:** the route mutates a document (its signatures and its status).

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; whether any environment relies on the `mock_signature_` prefix today is not measured.

title: POST /api/documents/:id/sign/request returns any tenant document's content hash and a signing nonce to any authenticated caller
description:
**BLUF:** originate `POST /api/documents/:id/sign/request` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1223-1265` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication and the caller's tenant only. For any document in the tenant it returns the document's `contentHash` and a signing nonce, and stores a signing request, even to a caller that `GET /api/documents/:id` refuses with its ownership 404 (:1142-1160). Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No role, scope, owner, recipient or creating-connector check between :1223 and :1265. `getDocument` (:1236) scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* The response carries `hash` (the document's `contentHash`), `nonce`, `message` and `expiresAt` (:1253-1259), and `saveSigningRequest` (:1245) stores the nonce that `POST /:id/sign` accepts (filed separately).
* So a same-tenant user who is not the owner, an admin or the recipient learns a document's content hash that `GET /:id` cloaks from them, and can mint the nonce the sign route needs.
* Callers: the api-gateway mounts it with `authenticateToken(true)` and `blockPendingApproval` only (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1027`).

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** it writes nothing to the document, so the anchor route's write predicate is the wrong shape. The natural fix is `GET /:id`'s read check, plus whatever the sign route's own signer policy decides.

**Priority 3:** a read gap. It mutates no document; it stores an in-memory signing request.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written.

title: POST /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events: any tenant user can record a lifecycle event on any document and trigger its anchor emission
description:
**BLUF:** originate `POST /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:2757-2877` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication, the action vocabulary, the payload's shape and the caller's tenant, and nothing about the caller's role or relation to the document. Any authenticated user in the tenant can record a lifecycle event on any document. The route then calls `emitLifecycleAnchor` (:2843), which posts to the anchoring service with the caller's bearer. Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No `isAllowedByRoleOrScope`, no owner check and no creating-connector check between :2757 and :2877. `getDocument` scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* It writes an event row (`createLifecycleEvent`, :2809), records connector provenance for a connector caller, and calls `emitLifecycleAnchor` (:2843), then stores the anchor id on the event.
* `emitLifecycleAnchor`'s comment (:1349-1362) says anchoring is idempotent per (document, network): re-anchoring an already-anchored document returns its existing anchor id. For a document with no anchor row, whether the call submits a new transaction (and spends a fee) is UNMEASURED; I did not read anchoring's `POST /api/anchors` wallet path.
* The vocabulary includes `delete` and `restore` (`services/originate/src/lifecycleActions.ts:38-46`).

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** the anchor route's checks do not apply unchanged. A terminal-status refusal would break `restore` on a deleted document. Platform S sends this route under the owning organisation's connector key (KS-1688, comment of 2026-10-19), and which humans should be allowed is not settled, so it needs its own predicate.

**Priority 2:** the route mutates the document's record (an event row) and may cause an anchoring submission.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; the fee question above is unmeasured.

title: GET /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events lists any tenant document's events without the ownership 404 that GET /:id applies
description:
**BLUF:** originate `GET /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:2885-2907` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication and the caller's tenant only, then returns every lifecycle event of the document (`listLifecycleEvents`, :2900). The ownership 404 that `GET /api/documents/:id` applies (:1142-1160) is missing, so a same-tenant caller who cannot read the document can read its events. Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No owner, admin, recipient or creating-connector check between :2885 and :2907. `getDocument` scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* The response is `{ documentId, count, events }`: the events as stored, with their actions and payloads.

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** it is a read, and the anchor route's write predicate is the wrong shape for it. The natural fix is `GET /:id`'s read check (owner, admin, recipient or creating connector, else the same 404).

**Priority 3:** a read gap; it mutates nothing.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; what the stored payloads contain for real documents is not measured.

title: POST /api/documents/:id/anchor answers status 'anchored' in its 202 body even when a mid-flight revoke kept the row revoked
description:
**BLUF:** after pull request 1814 (KS-1814), `POST /api/documents/:id/anchor` writes `status: 'anchored'` with `preserveTerminalStatuses: true`, so a revoke that lands while the anchoring call is in flight keeps `revoked` in the row. The handler still always answers `202` with `status: 'anchored'`; it never reads what `updateDocument` returned. The row is right; the response body misreports it. Found by QA gate 19 on pull request 1814 (finding 1814-2), measured over a mocked repository only.

**What was read and measured**

* The write: `updateDocument(id, tenantId, { blockchain, status: 'anchored' }, undefined, { preserveTerminalStatuses: true })` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1584-1587` at the pull request 1814 head `277e5ba6b7ae`; `:1534-1537` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`, where the write has no options at all). documentRepo's KS-521 CASE keeps `revoked` / `deleted` when that option is set.
* The answer: `res.status(202).json({ id, status: 'anchored', transactionHash, blockchain })` (`:1611-1613` at the head; `:1560-1562` at develop). It does not read `updateDocument`'s return value, which is `Promise<DocumentRecord | null>` (`services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts`).
* Gate 19's cell B6: a mocked `updateDocument` that returns a revoked record. The body still says `anchored`.

**Fix shape (the gate's):** answer from the returned record, or say plainly that the row's status was not updated. Whether the real repository's returned record carries the kept `revoked` status was not measured, so read that before choosing.

**Priority 3:** the response is wrong but the stored data is right, so it is not a data-integrity defect. A caller that trusts the 202 body over a read-back would believe a revoked document is anchored.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written. The race window (a revoke during the anchoring call) was not driven against a database.

title: nft-certificate mintNFT fetches the certification with no Authorization header: production mints fail, other envs mint on fabricated data
description:
**BLUF:** Inferred from the code, not reproduced. `mintNFT` fetches the certification from originate with a bare `fetch` and no Authorization header, against a router that authenticates every request. In production that request should never succeed, so a mint ends in "Certification not found". Outside production the same failure falls through to a fabricated "Secuura Demo Issuer" certification, and the mint goes ahead on that.

## What I read (develop d7ddfa1f6433)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/services/minting.service.ts:146-168` (production): `` fetch(`${ORIGINATE_SERVICE_URL}/api/certifications/${certificationId}`) `` at `:148`, no headers. A non-ok answer logs and returns null (`:154`); an exception logs and returns null (`:167`). `mintNFT` then throws "Certification not found" (`:237-239`), after it has already saved the PENDING record (`:234`).
* `minting.service.ts:171-184` (not production): the same fetch at `:173`. A non-ok answer or an exception falls through to `:186-205`, which logs "Using mock certification data ... DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION" and builds a certification with issuer "Secuura Demo Issuer" (`did:prism:demo123`), recipient "Demo Recipient" and a `documentHash` derived from the certification id, caches it (`:204`) and returns it.
* `minting.service.ts:140-143`: a cached certification is returned before any fetch, so once the fabricated entry is cached that id keeps the fabricated data without calling originate again.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:62-66`: `certificationsRouter.use(authenticate());`, with a comment that every route there requires an authenticated Bearer JWT.

## What I did not run or read

* No run, no box. Whether any box runs nft-certificate with `NODE_ENV=production`, what `ORIGINATE_SERVICE_URL` points at there, and whether a mint has ever been attempted: UNMEASURED.
* The catch block of `mintNFT`: what happens to the PENDING record saved at `:234` when the certification lookup throws.
* What `mintNFT` stores for a mint that went ahead on the fabricated data.
* Whether the mint route could supply the certification some other way: `nft.routes.ts:75-80` sets `documentData: undefined` with the comment "Would be fetched from certification", and I read nothing further.

Seat A 17th's design note (/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-10-30_seatA-17th/KS-1819-KS-1820-design-note.md, section 7 item 1, and rows 19 and 20 of its section 1 table) and Wednesday's addendum, item E2.
