title: nft-certificate: the row-owner trim is asymmetric between the two read paths, and getWalletNFTCertificates still gets the raw ?walletAddress (gate 23, F2 and F3)
description:
**BLUF:** Two follow-ups from the gate on pull request 1819 (KS-1836), neither a regression. F2 (Low): `selectReadableCertificates` compares `cert.userId.trim()` with the owner, while `getUserNFTCertificates(ownerId)` matches `cert.userId === userId` exactly, so a row stamped `'user-A '` is returned to user-A on the `?walletAddress` path but not on the bare list. The trim never lets a different owner through; mutant Mc (drop the trim) survives every cell; no write path stamps a padded owner today. F3 (Info): `getWalletNFTCertificates` still receives the raw `?walletAddress` string (parameterised equality, no injection); removing that is a design choice, not a defect.

**Source.** QA gate 23 on pull request 1819 (KS-1836; tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-29), findings F2 and F3 only. F1 of the same gate (the foreign-selector log arm) is being worked separately under KS-1836 and is not part of this filing. Related: KS-1836. Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate23-1819/verdict.md`.

**The verdict text, quoted (F2 and F3, lines 32 to 52 of the verdict, unedited):**

**F2 (Low, consistency). The row-owner trim is asymmetric between the two read paths.**

* **What happens:**
  * `selectReadableCertificates` compares `cert.userId.trim()` with the owner.
  * `getUserNFTCertificates(ownerId)` matches `cert.userId === userId` exactly, both in memory and in SQL.
  * So a row stamped `'user-A '` is returned to user-A on the `?walletAddress` path but not on the bare list. Attack cell A-M2 logged `padded-row/null-row -> ["n2"]`.
* **What does not happen:** the trim never lets a different owner through. It only matters for rows whose trimmed owner equals the caller.
* **Mutant:** Mc (drop the trim) survives every cell. No fixture has a padded owner.
* **Reachability:** no write path stamps a padded owner today; every row is `'user-id'`.

**F3 (Info). The wallet reader still receives attacker-controlled strings.**

* **What I saw:** `getWalletNFTCertificates` is called with the raw `?walletAddress` string, for example `" "`, `"%"` and `" addr_..."` (A-Q log lines).
* **No injection:** the query is parameterised equality (`wallet_address = $1`), not LIKE.
* **Side effects:**
  * The foreign wallet's rows are read and cached into `memNftCertificates`, which `loadFromDb` already fills at boot anyway.
  * In-process timing difference, a median of 15 calls:
    * foreign wallet with 0 rows: 1.59 ms;
    * foreign wallet with 2000 rows: 1.91 ms.
  * That is a weak size oracle at best. I measured it over loopback in-process, not over a network.
* **What would remove both:** querying by `ownerId` and narrowing by wallet in memory. That is a design choice, not a defect.
* The userId selector never reaches a service method. Every A-Q cell shows the user reader called only with `["user-A"]`.

**Where this lands.** Its own ticket and not a comment on KS-1836, because KS-1836 closes when a deploy round carries pull request 1819's merge, and these follow-ups outlive it. KS-1836 read whole: it holds neither F2 nor F3.

**Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `getUserNFTCertificates` 1 hit (KS-1836). `selectReadableCertificates` 1 hit (KS-1836); `getWalletNFTCertificates` 1 hit (KS-1836); `row-owner` 0; `userId.trim` 0; `padded` 20 hits, of which the first 15 titles were read and none is about the NFT read paths.

**Not measured by this filing:** nothing was run here; the timing figures in F3 are the gate's in-process loopback measurements.

title: Scope vocabulary and enforcement drift: five scopes gate nothing or name missing routes, gateway requireScope ignores <resource>:*, mints never call validateScopes, * is mintable by every key-admin role (SCOPES.md vs code)
description:
**BLUF:** Six differences between what `SCOPES.md` (and the KS-540 inventory) say about scopes and what the code enforces. Five scopes in the vocabulary gate nothing or name routes that do not exist; the gateway's `requireScope` does not honour `<resource>:*` although the shared helper does; the key mints never call `validateScopes`; `*` can be minted by every key-admin role although the docs say super-admin only; and gates and mints use scope strings that are not in the 32-member `SCOPES` array. `anchors:read` and `documents:revoke` (minted but unenforced) are already tracked in KS-1433 and are not repeated here. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; the gateway and mint behaviour was not exercised against a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1). PR-1 rewrites `SCOPES.md` to describe what is built and marks each open question `UNDECIDED (KS-1807, 2026-10-30)`; this ticket is where the code side is decided.

## Items

1. **Declared, enforced nowhere.** `certifications:share`: `POST /api/certifications/{id}/share` exists in `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts` with no scope or role check (and is not in the published spec). `certifications:revoke`: the route checks the caller is the certification's issuer, no scope (not in the spec). `analytics:read`: the `/api/analytics` gateway mount is authentication only. `analytics:export`: `POST /api/analytics/exports` exists (in the spec) with no scope check. `users:write`: no reference in any source file outside `packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts`.
2. **Names routes that do not exist.** `certifications:sign` (no `/{id}/sign` route in originate, not in the spec), `kyc:submit` (no `/api/kyc/submit`), `kyc:read` (no `/api/kyc/status`). The vocabulary entries are pinned by `packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks843-subjects-erase-scope.test.ts`, so removing them is a decision and a test edit.
3. **Gateway wildcard.** `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/scopes.ts` `requireScope` tests `userScopes.includes(s)` (exact) plus a lone `*`; the imported shared `hasScope` is shadowed by a local `const hasScope` in the same function. A key holding only `documents:*` is refused 403 on `GET /api/documents` and every other `/api/documents` method except create (the gateway's create handler in `routes/verification.ts` does accept `documents:*`). The KS-843 comment in the same file already calls the exact match "silent". No gateway test covers a `<resource>:*` key (control: the shared tests have 8 such cells).
4. **No validation at mint.** `services/security/src/index.ts` mint schema is `scopes: z.array(z.string()).default(['read'])`; originate `POST /api/admin/api-keys` (`services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`) stores the list as given; the shared `validateScopes` has no caller outside its own tests. The default `read` is not a vocabulary scope.
5. `*` **is not reserved.** `decideMint` in `services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts` allows every `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` member (`SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN`, `ORG_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN`, `ADMIN`) with any scope list, `*` included; only a provisioning key is refused wildcards. `SCOPES.md` says `*` is "reserved for super-admin keys".
6. **Out-of-vocabulary strings in use.** `webhooks:manage` (gates `/api/webhooks`), `users:create` (accepted by auth's `POST /api/users/stub`), `register` (legacy literal in the gateway's create handler), `metering:read` (minted onto the metering key by `services/tenant-provisioning/src/meteringKey.ts`; no gate reads it), `read`/`write` (mint defaults and the fixed set the admin portal sends), and the OAuth list (`verify:read`, `admin:read`, `admin:write` in `services/auth/src/services/oauth.ts`). The KS-540 inventory raised items 3, 4 and 6 as F-3, F-4 and F-5 on 2026-07-31; none is done.

Related and not repeated: KS-1433 (anchors:read, documents:revoke), KS-1777 (the flat 403 body of `requireScope`), KS-1653 (`certifications:write` admits `POST /api/users/stub`), KS-839 (OAuth `*`), KS-1535 and KS-1536 (which roles may mint keys).

Searched the board before filing: `certifications:share`, `certifications:revoke`, `analytics:read`, `users:write`, `kyc:submit`, `certifications:sign`, `metering:read` and `hasScope` each 0 hits; `wildcard` 4 hits (KS-839, KS-1584, KS-1156, KS-1210, none about the gateway helper); `validateScopes` 2 hits (KS-839, KS-1156). Controls in the same session: `subjects:erase` returned KS-843 and `documents:revoke` returned KS-1433.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 (docs lead, code aligns), either make each declared scope gate its route, or take the entry out of the vocabulary and out of the docs; make `requireScope` call `hasScope`; call `validateScopes` at both mints; restrict `*` to the roles the docs name. Which of these is intended is open, and PR-1 says so in the docs.

title: Docs claim rules the code does not apply: share checks no document access, ownerless documents skip the read check, a revoked key works 60 s at the gateway, the admin dashboard reads X-Tenant-Override, metering is certification-only
description:
**BLUF:** Five statements in the platform-k security docs describe a rule the code does not apply: document share checks no per-document access, a document with no recorded owner skips the read check, a revoked API key is still accepted by the gateway for up to 60 seconds, `GET /api/admin/dashboard` reads `X-Tenant-Override` from the raw header for an `ORG_ADMIN`, and the claim that agent document operations are metered holds only for certification operations. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; none of these was exercised against a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1). The docs and the code disagree on each; PR-1 describes what is built, names this ticket beside the passage, and does not write either behaviour as the intended one.

## Items

1. **Share has no per-document access check.** `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`): after the role-or-scope gate (`DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES` or `documents:share`) the handler runs `getDocument(id, tenantId)` and answers 404 only when the document is absent from the tenant; it never compares the caller with the owner, a recipient or an admin. `AGENT-DOCUMENT-OPERATION-RULES.md` R4 says "ownership checks still apply on read/share/revoke". Same class as KS-1688 (version) and KS-1814 (anchor; fixed), and as KS-1833/KS-1834 (lifecycle events).
2. **Ownerless documents skip the read check.** `GET /api/documents/{id}`: the refusal is guarded by `userId && document.owner?.id && document.owner.id !== userId && !isAdmin && !isRecipient`. `documentRepo` maps the owner as `row.owner_user_id || row.issuer_user_id || ''`, so a row with neither column set has `owner.id === ''` and the guard is false for every caller in the tenant. The inventory (§2.3) says reading needs owner, admin, recipient or creating connector. Not measured: how many rows have no owner.
3. **A revoked key keeps working at the gateway.** `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts` caches a valid `sk_` key in `apiKeyCache` for 60 s (a rejection for 30 s); nothing outside tests deletes or clears the cache (zero hits for `apiKeyCache.delete` and `apiKeyCache.clear`; control: `apiKeyCache.set` has two). The security service's revoke is immediate. The rules doc R6 says keys are "revocable immediately", contract §5 says "takes effect on next validate", and the rotation grace default `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS=0` was ruled "instant revoke" (2026-08-07, KS-577).
4. `X-Tenant-Override` **is read raw by one admin route.** The inventory (§2.4) says the override is "honoured only for the super-admin list". The gateway applies that list when it sets the tenant GUC, but it also allow-lists the header through to the services (`TRUST_HEADER_ALLOW_LIST` in `services/api-gateway/src/utils/trustHeaders.ts`), and `GET /api/admin/dashboard` in `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts` reads `req.headers['x-tenant-override']` itself and, if it is a UUID, counts documents, users and verifications for that tenant under `runWithPlatformScope`; with no header it returns platform-wide totals. That router admits `ORG_ADMIN` (`requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN')`) and so does the gateway's `/api/admin/` proxy (`enforceAdminProxy`). By this reading an `ORG_ADMIN` can read counts for another tenant. Counts only; not exercised live.
5. **Metering covers certifications only.** The rules doc R7 says agent document operations are metered (KS-320). `charge_events` rows are inserted only by `services/originate/src/services/chargeEvents.ts`, which only `routes/certifications.ts` calls for writes; `documents.ts` and anchoring do not import it. Create, version, share, revoke, transfer-custody and anchor write none. Which operations should be metered is a product call, not a code reading.

Related and not repeated: KS-1433 (connectors cannot revoke; unenforced scopes), KS-1688, KS-1833, KS-1834, KS-1814.

Searched the board before filing: `x-tenant-override` 8 hits (none about the dashboard; KS-1704 is about a super-admin's override), `apiKeyCache` 0, `charge_events` 1 (KS-1401, RLS on the table, not coverage), `lifecycle-events` hits KS-1833 and KS-1834 (excluded above). Controls in the same session: `subjects:erase` returned KS-843.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns. Items 1 and 2 are access checks in originate; item 3 is a cache invalidation or a stated TTL; item 4 is to read the override from the verified request context, not the header; item 5 needs a ruling on what is metered first.

title: api-gateway: a 401 or 403 from in front of the security service is cached as a 30 s key rejection; should an infrastructure 401/403 count as "could not answer"? (gate 31, F2)
description:
**BLUF:** A design question, not a defect found today. The gateway's `checkApiKey` treats any non-OK status from the key-validate call outside 5xx, 408 and 429 as a key rejection and negative-caches it for about 30 s (answering 401 `Invalid API key`). By the gate's reading, the real `/api/keys/validate` never answers 401 or 403 (`security/src/index.ts:775-779` skips JWT auth for that path; the handler near line 1800 answers 400, 503 or 200 with `valid: false`), so a 401 or 403 at the gateway would come from something **in front of** the security service (ingress or a WAF) and would make every key, valid ones included, answer 401 `Invalid API key` for 30 s. Pull request 1827 (KS-1788 item 3) now pins today's behaviour for a 403, which turns it into a tested contract. Should an infrastructure 401/403 count as "could not answer" (503, not cached) instead?

**Source.** QA gate 31 on pull request 1827 (KS-1788 item 3; tier 1, GO WITH NOTES, 2026-10-30), finding F2 (Note, a design question for Kam, not that pull request's defect). Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate31-1827/verdict.md`. Related: KS-1788, where the 403 cell was asked for; KS-1174, which is about forwarding a distinct code per key failure and not about this classification; KS-1240, the original timeout work. Filed on Wednesday's word.

**The verdict text, quoted (F2, lines 56 to 59 of the verdict, unedited):**

* **F2 (Note, design question for Kam, not this PR's defect).** The cell freezes "any non-OK status outside {5xx, 408, 429} is a key rejection, negative-cached 30 s".
  * The real `/api/keys/validate` never answers 401 or 403. `security/src/index.ts:775-779` skips JWT auth for that path, and the handler at l.1800 answers 400 (schema), 503 (KS-1370) or 200 `valid:false`.
  * So a 401 or 403 at the gateway would come from something **in front of** the security service (ingress or WAF). Today that would answer every key, valid ones included, `401 Invalid API key` for 30 s.
  * Pinning today's behaviour is what the ticket asked for, so this is fine to merge. But this PR now makes it a pinned contract, so whether an infrastructure 401/403 should count as "could not answer" deserves a ruling.

**Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `checkApiKey` 1 hit (KS-1788). `couldNotAnswer` 0, `infrastructure 401` 0, `negative cache` 2 (KS-1788, KS-1207: neither asks this), `keys/validate` 23 (read: KS-1174, KS-1788, KS-1240 for ingress, WAF, status or "could not answer" text: none asks whether an infrastructure 401/403 is a rejection), `WAF` 8 (none about the key-validate call).

**Not measured by this filing:** the security service's routes (the statements about them are the gate's reading, not re-read here); what any ingress or WAF in front of the service answers in practice; whether one exists on any box.

title: Spec and docs describe contracts the code does not follow: analytics export sends no Location or Retry-After and returns a data URI; kyc/submit and kyc/status are listed but absent; KYC approval never raises a verification level
description:
**BLUF:** In three areas the published spec and the docs describe a contract the code does not follow: the analytics export, the KYC steps, and the link between KYC and a user's verification level. The analytics export 202 declares `Location` and `Retry-After` headers and a poll-until-`done` flow; the code sends neither header, returns the file inline as a `data:` URI, and calls the field `downloadUrl`, not `url`. The spec's `info.x-workflows` lists `POST /api/kyc/submit` and `GET /api/kyc/status`, which do not exist. And no code path raises a user's verification level when a KYC verification is approved, although `WORKFLOWS.md` says it does. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2). The contract is generated from `services/*/src/*.openapi.ts`, so correcting it is a product-source change and is held (findings only this round); this ticket is where it is decided which side moves.

## Analytics export (`services/analytics`)

* **Headers:** the spec's `POST /api/analytics/exports` 202 says "poll the URL in the `Location` header until state=`done`" and declares `Location` and `Retry-After` response headers. `services/analytics/src/routes/analytics.ts` sets no header (zero hits for `setHeader`, `res.set`, `location` or `retry-after`; control: `setHeader('Location'` has hits in originate's `documents.ts`).
* **Status values and fields:** `exportService.ts` sets `pending`, `processing`, `completed` and `failed`; the spec's `AnalyticsExport` schema has `completed` in its status enum but also declares `url`, `sizeBytes` and `completedAt`, which the code does not send. The code sends `downloadUrl` and `expiresAt`. `WORKFLOWS.md` says `ready` and `url` (a presigned URL with a finite TTL).
* **The download:** `downloadUrl` is `data:<mime>;base64,<payload>` (`createDownloadUrl` in `exportService.ts`), so the file travels inside the status response; there is no separate download request. `pdf` and `xlsx` exports contain JSON text, and `pdf` is labelled `application/octet-stream` (a placeholder, per its own comment).
* **Request and 202 body:** the spec's request declares `from` and `to`; the code reads `period` (required) with `startDate` and `endDate`, and also accepts `xlsx`. The 202 body is `{ success, data: { id, status, type, format, createdAt } }`, not the bare object.

## KYC (`services/kyc`)

* **Steps:** the spec's `info.x-workflows` lists `POST /api/kyc/submit` and `GET /api/kyc/status`. `services/kyc/src/index.ts` registers `initiate`, `/:id`, `/user/:userId`, `/:id/document`, `/:id/selfie`, `/:id/complete`, `/:id/review`, `/:id/result` and `DELETE /user/:userId/data`. `GET /api/kyc/status` is read as `/:id` with id `status` and answers 404; `POST /api/kyc/submit` matches no service route (by reading the gateway's method map it would answer 405, because the path matches the spec's `/api/kyc/{id}`, which allows only GET; not executed). `initiate` answers 201 (not 202) with `verificationId`; statuses are lowercase `pending`, `in_progress`, `under_review`, `approved`, `rejected`.
* **The level never moves:** `WORKFLOWS.md` says `GET /api/users/me` shows the new `verificationLevel` after KYC and that a raised level unlocks higher-tier document types. A search of service source (tests excluded) finds `users.verification_level` written only by the gateway admin route, the social-login path in auth and originate's admin route; the kyc service has no access to the users table (0 hits for `FROM users`, `UPDATE users`, `INTO users` in `services/kyc/src`; control: `verification_level` has 5 hits in `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`). So an approved KYC verification does not change a token's level by this reading. The seeded `PROPERTY_DEED` document type also needs no level (`creatorVerificationLevel: 'none'`), though the gate itself exists.

## Not repeated here

The create-document response shape (flat, not `DocumentDetail`), the `/anchor` 202 body, the verify `source` values and the error messages are recorded in the PR-2 pull request body as doc corrections, because there the code is plainly the intended behaviour; if you want them in the contract-corrections batch, say so.

Searched the board before filing: `kyc/submit`, `analytics exports`, `Retry-After` returned no ticket about these contract differences (KS-1327 is about KYC write races, KS-1372 about the login lockout). Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. For the export, either send the headers and a real download, or change the spec and docs to the inline `data:` form; for KYC, remove the two steps from `x-workflows` and decide whether approval should raise the level.

title: Reset-password has no rate limit of its own (the limiter is mounted on /api/auth/password-reset, which has no route) and billing GET /customers/by-email can never match (/customers/:id is registered first)
description:
**BLUF:** Two routing slips in code that the docs describe as working: `POST /api/auth/reset-password`, the route that consumes a reset token, has no rate limit of its own because the reset limiter is mounted on `/api/auth/password-reset`, a path no route serves; and billing `GET /customers/by-email` can never match because `GET /customers/:id` is registered first and takes `by-email` as an id. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2). `WORKFLOWS.md`'s rate-limit sheet lists `password_reset` as 15 minutes, 5 attempts, on `POST /api/auth/password-reset`; the published spec declares `GET /api/billing/customers/by-email`.

## 1. The reset limiter guards a path with no handler

* **Limiter mounts** in `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` (`app.use(...)`, in this order): `/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/register`, `/api/auth/forgot-password` (1 hour, 5 in production, `PASSWORD_RESET_RATE_LIMIT`), `/api/auth/refresh`, `/api/auth/password-reset` (15 minutes, 5 in production, 50 otherwise), `/api/auth/verify-email`.
* **Auth routes** in `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` for the same flow: `POST /forgot-password` and `POST /reset-password`. There is no `/password-reset` route (control: the `/login` route is found by the same search).
* So `/api/auth/forgot-password` is limited, and `/api/auth/reset-password`, which takes the token and a new password, is limited only by the global limiter (300 per 60 s per IP in production). The 15-minute limiter on the dead path never sees a request. Not assessed: how guessable a reset token is; not probed.
* The login brute-force guard has a related defect already on the board: KS-1372 (nothing calls `recordFailure`).

## 2. Billing by-email is unreachable

`services/billing/src/routes/billing.ts` registers `router.get('/customers/:id', ...)` before `router.get('/customers/by-email', ...)`, so Express matches `by-email` as an `:id` and the by-email handler is never reached. The published spec declares `GET /api/billing/customers/by-email`.

## Not a finding (recorded in the PR for KS-1807 PR-2 as a doc correction)

`GET /billing/pricing` needs a login although a code comment calls it public: `services/billing/src/index.ts` says the public marketing endpoints are "intentionally behind JWT" (`app.use('/billing', jwtAuthenticate())`), so the doc is what is wrong.

Searched the board before filing: `password-reset`, `reset-password` and `by-email` returned no ticket about these two slips. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. Mount the limiter on `/api/auth/reset-password` (and drop or fix the dead mount), and register `/customers/by-email` before `/customers/:id`.

title: The gateway answers four admin and verify routes from stand-ins registered before the proxy: fixed audit-log arrays, an always-empty verification queue, and certification verify that always says verified:false
description:
**BLUF:** The api-gateway answers four routes itself, from stand-ins registered before the proxy to the real service, with no environment guard around them: `GET /api/admin/audit-logs` and `GET /api/security/audit` return fixed arrays of fabricated rows (actor `admin` at `test.local`), `GET /api/admin/verification-queue` returns an array nothing ever writes to (so it is always empty) and its action route answers `success: true` for any id without changing anything, and `POST /api/certifications/{id}/verify` always answers `verified: false` with a hard-coded issuer `test-issuer`. The real database-backed handlers in originate are never reached for the first three. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2, document lifecycle, status codes, error envelope). The docs and the published spec describe these as real operations; the code comment on the queue says "in-memory, development only" but nothing enforces that.

## Evidence

* **Registration order:** `app.use(createAdminRoutes(...))` and `app.use(createVerificationRoutes(...))` in `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` come before `app.use(createProxyRoutes(...))`, so a route defined in `routes/admin.ts` or `routes/verification.ts` answers before the `/api/admin/` proxy to originate is reached. The only environment check in `routes/admin.ts` is the demo-seed flag; none wraps these handlers.
* **Audit logs:** `router.get('/api/admin/audit-logs', requireAdmin, ...)` in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts` filters a literal 4-row array (`evt-1` to `evt-4`, actor `admin` at `test.local`) by `action` and `resourceType` and returns `{ success, logs, events, total }`. `router.get('/api/security/audit', ...)` does the same with a literal 3-row array. Originate has the real handler (`adminConfigRouter.get('/audit-logs')` in `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`); it is shadowed.
* **Verification queue:** `const mockVerificationQueue = []` ("in-memory, development only") backs `GET /api/admin/verification-queue` (always `items: []`, `total: 0`) and `POST /api/admin/verification-queue/{id}/action`, which validates the action word, updates the array entry only if one exists, and answers `{ success: true, id, action, ... }` for any id. Originate's database-backed `GET`/`POST` for the same paths (`adminConfig.ts`) are shadowed.
* **Certification verify:** `router.post('/api/certifications/:id/verify', ...)` in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` ("MOCK ... ENDPOINTS (for E2E tests)", "for test compatibility") checks that the certification exists, then answers `verified: false`, `status: 'issued'`, `issuer: { id: 'test-issuer', verified: true }`, `blockchain.anchored: false`, `confidence: 'pending-onchain'` whatever the certification is. Its comment says it is a stopgap "until the originate→anchoring rewire lands". Originate's own verify handler is never reached.
* **What the docs and spec say:** `QUICK-REFERENCE.md` lists all four as working endpoints (certification verify, the verification queue and its action, audit logs and the `security/audit` alias). The published spec declares only `GET /api/security/audit`; certification verify, `admin/audit-logs` and the two queue routes are live routes with no spec entry (0 hits for each path in `secuura-api.yaml`; control: `/api/billing/customers/by-email` hits).

## How to confirm

As a platform admin, call `GET /api/admin/audit-logs` on a stack with real audit rows and compare with the database; call the verification-queue action with a random id and read `success: true`; call certification verify on a real certification. Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. Either remove the gateway stand-ins so the proxy reaches originate, or gate them to test environments behind an explicit flag and document that they are test doubles.

Searched the board before filing: `verification-queue` and `audit-logs` are not covered by an existing ticket about the gateway stand-ins; KS-736 is about mount authentication, not these handlers. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: GET /api/analytics/exports lists every caller's exports with their files inline, and any signed-in user can request users and revenue exports: no role, tenant or user is used (KS-1703 covers only the by-id read)
description:
**BLUF:** `GET /api/analytics/exports` returns every analytics export the service holds, whoever asked for it, and a completed export carries its file inline (`downloadUrl` is a `data:` URI), so one list call returns other callers' files; and any signed-in caller can request the `users` and `revenue` report types, because the analytics service checks no role. KS-1703 already covers the by-id read (`GET /api/analytics/exports/{id}`, found by Schemathesis) and records that for exports "it may be deliberate" and needs a ruling; this ticket adds the list route, the missing role check on creation, and a rule the docs state that the code does not meet. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2, `WORKFLOWS.md` section 3). Related: KS-1703.

## What is not in KS-1703

* **The list route:** `router.get('/exports')` in `services/analytics/src/routes/analytics.ts` calls `exportService.listExports(limit)` (default 20), which returns the values of the service's process-wide map (`memExports` in `services/analytics/src/services/exportService.ts`) with no caller or tenant filter. KS-1703's table names the by-id read only. The list makes ids discoverable, so the by-id read does not even need a guessed id.
* **Creation has no role check and stores no caller:** `router.post('/exports')` parses the body and calls `exportService.createExport(request)`; the request carries no identity and `createExport` stores none. Accepted report types: `certifications`, `verifications`, `users`, `governance`, `revenue`, each built from `analyticsService.get<Type>Metrics(query)` where `query` holds only `period`, `startDate` and `endDate`. The gateway mount `/api/analytics` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts`) is `authenticateToken(true)` and the service mounts only `jwtAuthenticate` (`services/analytics/src/index.ts`): no role, no scope.
* **Persistence:** the newest 500 export rows are reloaded into the map at boot, so the exposure survives a restart.
* **Tenancy:** the word `tenant` appears in the analytics service's non-test source only in `db.ts`; the routes and `exportService.ts` never read a tenant or user from the request (control: the same search finds `req.params` in the routes file).

## A rule the docs state that this contradicts

`docs/security/ROLES-AND-AUTHORIZATION-INVENTORY.md` section 2.1 (as rewritten in KS-1807 PR-1) says services without a role gate "rely on gateway-level auth plus ownership and tenant checks"; for the analytics exports neither exists. PR-1 lists five routes as exceptions; this is a sixth, and PR-1's text will need one more name once this is ruled.

## How to confirm

As two users in different tenants: user A creates a `revenue` export and waits for `completed`; user B calls `GET /api/analytics/exports`. Expected by the platform's tenancy rule: B sees nothing of A's. By this reading: B receives A's export including the file. Not run. Not assessed: whether the metrics functions return platform-wide totals or are narrowed by a database tenant setting that this reading did not find.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves, and KS-1703 holds the open question whether exports are meant to be shared. If they are not: store the creating principal and tenant with each export, filter the list and the by-id read the same way and answer 404 to anyone else (as KS-1116 did for credentials), and decide which roles may request `users` and `revenue`.

Searched the board before filing: `analytics exports`, `listExports`, `exportService` and `analytics/exports` returned KS-1703 (by-id read, referenced above), KS-1853 and KS-1846 (this pass's tickets, about the export contract and the scope table) and KS-188 (stateful testing); none covers the list route or the missing role check. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: register-connector is idempotent only for sequential calls: two concurrent first registrations of one externalRef create two Organisations and two live keys
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector` is only idempotent for sequential calls. Two concurrent first-time registrations of the same `externalRef` can both create an Organisation row and both mint a live `sk_` key: the lookup is a plain `SELECT ... LIMIT 1` with no lock and no transaction, there is no unique index on the reference, and the one constraint that would have stopped the second insert (unique `slug`) is turned into a successful second insert by a collision retry. The S-K ownership contract says registration is "idempotent on the Org GUID so retries and replays are safe". Read from code, not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying `docs/S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md` for KS-1807 (PR-3). Related: KS-1549 (two concurrent rotates), which is the same class on the rotate path and is a different defect.

## What the code does

All in `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts`, the register-connector handler:

* **Lookup (:729):** `SELECT id, tenant_id::text AS tenant_id, slug, name FROM organizations WHERE metadata->>'externalRef' = $1 LIMIT 1`, run under platform scope. No `FOR UPDATE`, no advisory lock, no transaction around the lookup, the insert and the mint (searched `platform.ts` for `advisory`, `FOR UPDATE`, `BEGIN` and `transaction(`: 0 hits; control: `runWithPlatformScope` has 6).
* **Insert (:827-832):** `INSERT INTO organizations (name, slug, ...) ... metadata = {"externalRef": ...}`. The reference lives in a JSON key of `metadata`, not in a column. The only uniqueness on `organizations` is on `slug` and `did` (`docker/init/01-schema.sql`, `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql`); no index covers `metadata->>'externalRef'` (searched every `.sql` under `migrations` and `docker` for `externalRef`: the only hit is a comment in `041_action_provenance.sql`).
* **Collision handling (:835-839):** the slug comes from the name, or from `org-<externalRef>` when there is none. Two concurrent calls for the same reference therefore compute the same slug. The second insert fails with `23505`, and the code answers that with "one deterministic retry with an entropy suffix" (`slugBase` plus 4 random hex characters), which succeeds. Its own comment calls the fallback slug "collision-free"; the retry is what lets the duplicate through.
* **Mint (:848-873):** both calls then reach the key mint with the same `connectorId: 'platform-s:<externalRef>'`, their own `organizationId` and `rotate: false`. The file's own KS-577 comment says that without `rotate` "the mint is purely additive", so neither call retires the other's key.

## Effect

Two Organisation rows for one S Organisation GUID and two live keys for it, each key carrying a different `organizationId`. Later registrations of the same reference read `LIMIT 1` with no `ORDER BY`, so which row they return is not defined.

## How to confirm

Two parallel `register-connector` calls for a fresh `externalRef` with a provisioning key, then `SELECT count(*) FROM organizations WHERE metadata->>'externalRef' = '<ref>'`. Expected by the contract: 1. By this reading: 2, and two keys returned. Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

A unique expression index on `(metadata->>'externalRef')` (or a real column) plus handling `23505` on that index by re-reading, or an advisory lock keyed on the reference around lookup, insert and mint. The slug retry should not be the path that absorbs a same-reference collision.

Searched the board before filing: `register-connector`, `idempoten`, `two organisations` and `concurrent`; KS-1549 (concurrent rotates) is the nearest and is a different path; nothing covers concurrent first registrations. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: PII tokenisation is on no request path: the gateway helpers have no callers, skipTokenisation is read by nothing, and only key generation uses the service
description:
**BLUF:** PII tokenisation is on no request path. The tokenisation service exists and tenant provisioning asks it for a key, but nothing calls its `tokenise` or `detokenise` endpoints, the gateway helpers that would (`tokeniseFields`, `detokeniseValues`, `extractPiiFields`) have no callers, and the default tenant's `skipTokenisation` flag is read nowhere. `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md` says PII "is tokenised at entry and stored in encrypted form" and that new tenants "get full tokenisation from day one". Read from code, not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md` for KS-1807 (PR-3). Related: KS-1336, KS-1860 and KS-1861, which sit next to it in the same document.

## What the code does

All paths under `Blockchain/Dev/`.

* **Helpers with no callers:** `services/api-gateway/src/services/tokenisation.ts` defines `tokeniseFields` (`:101`), `detokeniseValues` (`:136`) and `extractPiiFields` (`:178`). Searching `services`, `packages` and `frontend` (non-test, excluding `node_modules`) for each name outside that file finds 0 hits. The gateway's `index.ts` imports only `setTenantKey`, `getTenantKey` and `removeTenantKey` from it. Control: `setTenantKey(` is called once outside the file (the tenant-key load route in `routes/platform.ts`).
* **The service's own API has one real caller:** searching for `api/tokenise`, `api/detokenise` and `TOKENISATION_URL` outside `services/tokenisation/` finds only `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts` (which requests a key) and the unused gateway helper file. No request path tokenises or detokenises a field.
* `skipTokenisation` **is read by nothing:** it appears in `docker/init-platform/02-seed-default-tenant.sql` and in no non-test source under `services` or `packages` (0 hits). The default tenant's data stays plaintext because nothing tokenises any tenant's data, not because of the flag.
* **What PII encryption does exist:** auth encrypts user PII columns itself, per user (`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`, `encryptPiiCol(value, column, userId)`); that is a separate mechanism from the tenant tokenisation key and vault.
* **Not audited either:** tokenise and detokenise write no audit row (`services/tokenisation/src/index.ts`); only generate-key and rotate-key call `emitAudit`, and that writes to the main database's `audit_logs`, not the platform audit table the document names.

## Effect

The per-tenant key lifecycle is real (generate, load, rotate), but the thing the key is for does not run. A reader of the architecture document, or a customer told that their PII is tokenised and decryptable only with their key, is told something the code does not do. Whether any contract or marketing text makes that promise was not checked.

## How to confirm

Create a tenant, load its key, create a user and a document containing an email address, then read the stored rows: expected by the document, tokens (`tok_...`) and `vault_entries` rows; by this reading, the original values and no vault rows beyond those from direct `POST /api/tokenise` calls. Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Decide whether request-path tokenisation is still intended. If it is, wire the gateway helpers (or the service) onto the request path and record the default-tenant behaviour in code; if it is not, the documents and the key-lifecycle endpoints should say that the service is key management only. Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves.

Searched the board before filing: `tokeniseFields`, `KS1336`, `vault_entries`, `suspend`; nothing covers tokenisation being unwired. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: Workflow configurations are one shared table with no tenant column: an ORG_ADMIN of any tenant can list, change and delete all of them
description:
**BLUF:** The workflow-configuration routes in originate (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE /api/admin/workflows`) read and write one table, `workflow_configs`, that has no tenant column, with no tenant filter, behind a router gate of `SYSTEM_ADMIN` or `ORG_ADMIN`. `ORG_ADMIN` is a tenant-scoped role, so an `ORG_ADMIN` of any tenant can list, change and delete every workflow configuration, including ones another tenant uses. `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md` drew "workflows" as a tenant-scoped table (`workflows + tenant_id`). Read from code, not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md` for KS-1807 (PR-3). Whether these configurations are meant to be platform-wide was not found written down.

## What the code does

Under `Blockchain/Dev/`:

* **The table has no tenant column and nothing adds one:** `workflow_configs` is created in `migrations/002_verification-tiers.sql` and `docker/init/05-admin-tables.sql`. No `ALTER TABLE` in the TypeScript services adds `tenant_id` to it (searched non-test TypeScript; control: `startup-migrations.ts` has 19 `ALTER TABLE` statements), and no SQL line ties the table to `tenant_id` (the two migrations that add a tenant column generically, 026 and 030, name other tables).
* **The router gate:** `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`, `adminConfigRouter.use(authenticate(), requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN'))`. The gateway's `/api/admin/` proxy admits `ORG_ADMIN` as well (`PROXY_ADMIN_ROLES`).
* **No tenant filter on any workflow route:** the list is `SELECT * FROM workflow_configs ORDER BY name ASC`; create inserts `(name, description, type, is_active, steps, document_types, sla_hours)`; update and delete address a row by `id` alone (`DELETE FROM workflow_configs WHERE id = ${req.params.id}::uuid`).
* **Why it looks this way:** the gateway's `clone-to-tenant` route copies platform workflow templates with `tenantPool.query("INSERT INTO workflow_configs ...")` (`routes/platform.ts`), which assumes each tenant has its own database. On the shared-database path every tenant's pool is the same database, so that route and the admin routes above all write the one table.

## Effect

A tenant administrator can read and alter the configuration of workflows that every tenant shares, or delete one. Because there is no tenant column, row-level security has nothing to key on. Whether the rows are in practice shared platform templates, and whether anything reads `workflow_configs` at request time for another tenant, was not checked.

## How to confirm

As an `ORG_ADMIN` of tenant A, `GET /api/admin/workflows` and note the ids; as an `ORG_ADMIN` of tenant B, `PUT` or `DELETE /api/admin/workflows/{id}` on one of them. Expected by the tenancy rule: refused or invisible. By this reading: allowed. Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Decide whether workflow configurations are platform-wide (then restrict the routes to platform roles and say so in the docs) or per tenant (then add a tenant column, backfill it, and key the routes and a policy on it). Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves.

Searched the board before filing: `workflow_configs`, `admin/workflows`, `workflow config`; nothing covers this. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: Reconciler R7 not built: non-final anchor rows with a placeholder hash are never settled on a real-chain box (census needed first)
description:
## BLUF

**Rule R7 of the KS-1384 recovery table (design rev 2 §9) is not built, and the KS-1384 train will not build it.** A non-final `anchor_store` row (`pending`, `submitting` or `submitted`) whose hash is a placeholder (`mock_tx_`, `tx_sim_`, `mock_batch_tx_`) is never settled by anything on a real-chain box today: the reconciler skips any hash that is not 64 hex (`services/anchoring/src/reconciler.ts:123` at F0c's head `dfc0dd61d75e`), and no other code writes it. Rev 2 §9 says such a row, when no process is driving it, should be written `failed` with KS-587's wording, with no chain call.

Facts only. No row, box or code was touched.

## Why it is a ticket and not part of KS-1384 F-b

Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-30 (ANSWER 07:03:15Z to Seat W 13th) that F-b PINS today's behaviour for R7 and does not add the write:

* it would be a new terminal write class on a real-chain box, outside F-b's listed scope (rev 4 §4.3 and §14);
* it would touch kintsugi-shaped rows (KS-1751) with no census of the rows it would change;
* a `failed` row is what Platform S parks and re-reads, so the write has an external effect.

F-b's cell (j) row R7 pins exactly that: the reconciler never chain-checks and never writes a fabricated non-final row.

## What building it needs first

1. **A read-only census on each box**: the count of non-final rows with a placeholder hash, by status, `simulated` flag and age. KS-1751 measured kintsugi's FINAL simulated rows (two `simulated = true` and `confirmed`); the non-final population is not measured anywhere I could find.
2. A ruling on the wording and on whether a `simulated = false` placeholder row (the KS-587 incident shape) is treated the same.
3. The same "not driven" rule F-b introduces (the in-memory driving set), so a row a live mock-mode process is still writing is never touched.

## Searched before filing (board search over title, description and comments, archived included; controls: a literal in archived KS-336 found, a nonsense token 0)

* `KS-587`: 30 issues; `fabricated`: 44. Read the closest:
  * **KS-1751** is the kintsugi rows that are simulated AND confirmed: FINAL rows, a different shape.
  * **KS-683** is the consumer-side standoff over `failed` rows: no K-side settling write.
  * **KS-587**, **KS-520** and **KS-522** are the honest-labelling work on read paths and the demo corpus.
* `never chain-checked`, `fabricated hash on a real-chain`, `non-final fabricated`, `KS-587 owns`: 0 each.

Refs KS-1384, KS-1751, KS-587.

title: nginx sends /analytics/ straight to the analytics service, so a revoked-session token still works there and the gateway's rate limits and audit are skipped
description:
**Read from code at develop** `e43a289c1c7b`**, not run against a stack.** Found while checking `ARCHITECTURE.md` for KS-1807 PR-4 and re-read by me.

**What the code does.** All three nginx configs route `/analytics/` straight to the analytics service, not through the api-gateway: `location /analytics/ { set $svc_analytics "analytics:4010"; rewrite ^/analytics/(.*)$ /$1 break; proxy_pass http://$svc_analytics; }` in `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx.conf`, `nginx-production.conf` and `nginx-demo.conf`. The analytics service guards `/api/*` with the shared `authenticate()` (`services/analytics/src/index.ts`, `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate())`), and that middleware (`packages/shared/src/middleware/index.ts`) only verifies the RS256 signature and expiry of the bearer token. It does not consult a session store.

**What the gateway does that this path skips.** The session-revocation check (`SESSION_INVALIDATED`, `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts`), the gateway's rate limiters and its audit middleware. So a token whose session was ended (logout, eviction, admin revoke, erased user) keeps working on `/analytics/...` until the token itself expires (1 hour by the code default, 1 day as the local compose file sets it), and calls on that path are not counted by the gateway limiters or recorded by its audit middleware.

**Searched.** No analytics route has a role gate (searched `services/analytics/src/routes` for `requireRole`, `requireAdmin` and `role`: no hit; positive control: the same directory's route files exist and mount handlers), which is KS-1856's finding for exports. This ticket is the separate point that the route to the service avoids the gateway at all.

**Not established.** Whether the deployed demo and kintsugi edges use these configs or put another proxy in front (the VM runs Caddy in front of the compose nginx per the project notes); whether anything in the portals actually calls `/analytics/`: I found no literal `/analytics/` in `frontend/*/src`, so it may be reachable but unused. Whether the gateway's own CSRF check matters for a bearer-token caller (it is skipped for any bearer token anyway).

**Related.** KS-1856 (analytics exports readable by every caller), KS-1855 (gateway stand-ins), KS-1846 (scope drift), KS-1758 (the gateway's own revocation check fails open when the session store is down; this ticket is the case where the check is not on the path at all), KS-1280 (a revoked session's bearer forwarded past the gateway check).

**Docs.** `ARCHITECTURE.md` will state the real entry point and the bypass in KS-1807 PR-4; the behaviour itself is not fixed by the docs series.

title: GET /api/metering/usage counts free_in_context events as chargeable: totals.count and usdTotal use amount > 0, and the price is applied at read time
description:
**Read from code at develop** `e43a289c1c7b`**, not run against a stack.** Found while checking `METERING-USAGE-API.md` for KS-1807 PR-4 and re-read by me.

**What the code does.** `getUsageSummary` in `services/originate/src/services/chargeEvents.ts` computes `chargeable_count` as `SUM(CASE WHEN amount > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)` and multiplies that by the event type's USD price, read live from the pricing config at request time. It does not look at `fee_status`. `createChargeEvent` stores the event type's price as `amount` even when the caller passes `feeStatus: 'free_in_context'`. The verification-certificate path (`services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts`, around line 1451, "free_in_context for recruitment") records exactly such an event.

**Effect.** Events recorded as `free_in_context` are counted in `totals.count` and in `usdTotal` as if they were chargeable. This is the figure Platform S reads to reconcile K usage against subscriptions (the page says "there is no per-event client billing", so the effect is on reconciliation rather than on a charge). Separately, because the price is applied at read time, the same window read on two days gets two different `usdTotal` values if the price changed in between.

**Not established.** Whether any real tenant has `free_in_context` rows (not measured); whether Platform S subtracts them on its side (not in this tree); the intended definition of "chargeable" (the docs say free usage is not billed, but no ruling was found for this event type).

**Docs.** `METERING-USAGE-API.md` now states what the code does, as a known deviation, in KS-1807 PR-4.

title: GET /api/metering/usage: impossible dates answer 500 not 400, a repeated from/to is ignored, and the route has no spec path
description:
**Read from code at develop** `e43a289c1c7b`**, not run against a stack.** Found while checking `METERING-USAGE-API.md` for KS-1807 PR-4 and re-read by me.

**Three small defects on** `GET /api/metering/usage` (`services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts`, `services/originate/src/services/chargeEvents.ts`):

1. **Impossible dates answer 500, not 400.** The guard is the regular expression `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}([T ][0-9:.+Zz-]*)?$`, which checks shape only. `2026-02-30`, `2026-13-01` and `2026-06-01T99` pass it, the query casts the value `::timestamptz`, the cast fails and the handler's catch answers 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`. The route's own comment says the guard exists so junk is never handed to the cast. The system test only exercises `notadate`.
2. **A repeated** `from` **or** `to` **is silently ignored.** The handler reads `typeof req.query.from === 'string' ? ... : undefined`, so `?from=a&from=b` (an array) is dropped and the call answers 200 with that bound open, which is a wider read than the caller asked for.
3. **The route has no path entry in the published spec.** `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` mentions `/api/metering/usage` once, in the description of another operation, and has no path for it, so the spec-driven suites never exercise it.

**Not established.** Whether the gateway rejects a repeated parameter before it reaches originate (I read originate's handler and the gateway's proxy mount only).

**Docs.** `METERING-USAGE-API.md` states the first two as known deviations in KS-1807 PR-4.

title: Tokenisation rotate-key is not atomic: vault rows are re-encrypted and committed one by one before the new key is stored, so a failure strands them under a key that was never saved
description:
**Read from code at develop** `e43a289c1c7b`**, not run against a stack.** Found while checking `TOKENISATION.md` for KS-1807 PR-4 and re-read by me.

**What the code does.** `POST /api/rotate-key` (`services/tokenisation/src/index.ts`) does four steps with no enclosing transaction: (1) it unwraps the active key and mints a new one in memory; (2) `rotateKey(tenantId, oldKey, newKey)` re-encrypts the tenant's vault rows, and each row's `UPDATE` commits on its own (per-query transactions); (3) it sets the old `tenant_keys` row to `status = 'rotated'`; (4) it `INSERT`s the new key's row as `active`. The new key exists only in memory until step 4.

**Consequences.**

* If step 3 or step 4 fails (a database error, a crash, a restart between them), every re-encrypted vault row is under a key that was never stored. The old key's row may already be `rotated`, so the tenant is left with no active key and the rows cannot be decrypted by anything.
* A row that fails to decrypt in step 2 is only counted (`vaultRowsFailed`) and stays under the old key, while the new key becomes the active one. The response is still `success: true`.
* The platform database's `tenant_config.vault_key_hash` (written at tenant creation) is never updated by a rotation, so it goes stale; nothing reads it today.

**Why the impact is latent today.** No request path writes vault rows: the gateway tokenisation helpers have no callers (KS-1862), so the vault is empty unless something outside this tree writes to it. The defect matters once tokenisation is wired.

**Not established.** Whether any environment has vault rows; whether a retry of `rotate-key` after a step 3 or 4 failure recovers (the old key row would be `rotated`, so the retry finds no active key and answers 404 per the handler).

**Related.** KS-1862 (tokenisation on no request path), KS-288 (vault and tenant keys in the main database), KS-1790 (no key file is returned).

**Docs.** `TOKENISATION.md` states the real order and the failure behaviour as a known deviation in KS-1807 PR-4.

title: Tokenisation spec and handler disagree: detokenise answers values where the spec declares fields, and rotate-key with no active key answers 404 where the spec says 400
description:
**Read from code at develop** `e43a289c1c7b`**, not run against a stack.** Found while checking `TOKENISATION.md` for KS-1807 PR-4.

Two places where the tokenisation service's own OpenAPI declaration (`services/tokenisation/src/tokenisation.openapi.ts`, which feeds the published spec) differs from what the handler (`services/tokenisation/src/index.ts`) answers:

1. `POST /api/detokenise`**.** The `DetokeniseResponse` schema declares `{ success, fields: [{ token, value, error? }] }`. The handler answers `res.json({ success: true, values: results })`. A client generated from the spec reads `fields` and finds nothing.
2. `POST /api/rotate-key` **with no active key.** The spec declares 400 ("Validation error or no active key for tenant"). The handler answers 404 `NOT_FOUND` ("No active key for tenant"); a malformed body is a 400 from the validator, and any other throw is a 500.

Per the KS-1807 rule the contract (`*.openapi.ts` and the generated YAML) is not edited by the docs series; this ticket records the differences. Which side is right is not decided (a client may already depend on either).

Not established: whether anything calls these two endpoints today (nothing on a request path does, KS-1862); whether other tokenisation endpoints differ from their declarations (I compared these two).

title: originate anchor GET labels a real pending anchor simulated: the tx_<id> fallback for a row with no hash reads as a placeholder
description:
## BLUF

**originate's** `GET /api/anchors/:documentId` **labels a real anchor simulated while it is pending.** A row with no transaction hash yet answers `transactionId: null`, `simulated: true`, `simulatedTxRef: tx_anchor_...`, `verified: false`. `verified: false` is the honest part. `simulated: true` is wrong: this is a real anchor that has not landed, not a placeholder.

Facts only. No row, box or code was touched.

## Where (read at KS-1384 F-a's head `f27499dd9027`)

* `services/originate/src/routes/anchors.ts:72`, `anchorFromDbRow`: `transactionId: row.transaction_hash || tx_<id>`. The comment there already notes the fallback "is itself a placeholder the prefix check catches".
* The read handler then runs `isSimulatedAnchor` over that fallback, and `tx_` is one of the placeholder prefixes (`services/anchorHonesty.ts:35`).

## Why it shows up now

KS-1384 F-a (PR 1838) removed `saveAnchorToDb`, which used to write anchoring's id into `transaction_hash` over the row. That hid this path: base answered `transactionId` = the anchor id and `verified: true` in the pending window. Gate 41 measured both answers with a route cell on base and head. It notes other paths already show the same shape on base. The change is listed in PR 1838's body for Kam's Platform S comms step.

## What is open

A row with no hash is pending, not fabricated, so `simulated` should not be derived from the synthetic `tx_<id>`. What this route should answer instead (for example a pending status with no transaction id) is a contract choice, because Platform S reads it. Nothing is proposed here.

## Does another part of KS-1384 cover it?

**No, by reading.** R2's resolver settles the document blob for the readers in design rev 2 §5.1; this route reads `anchor_store` directly, is not among them, and `routes/anchors.ts` is not in R2's write set. R1 does not touch it. F-b settles rows that rest with no hash, which shortens how long a row can show this answer but does not change the answer.

## Searched before filing (title, description and comments, archived included; controls: a literal in archived KS-336 found, a nonsense token 0)

* `tx_anchor` 0; `hashless` 1 (KS-485, unrelated line); `anchorFromDbRow` 1; `simulatedTxRef` 13; `pending anchor` 4.
* Read the nearest: **KS-1657** is this same read answering 404 on a database failure; **KS-1629** is this read minting a row; **KS-522**, **KS-587** and **KS-589** are labelling of fabricated hashes. None covers a real row with no hash.

Refs KS-1384, KS-587.

title: Reconciler batch can be spent on rows it skips, so a real stuck anchor behind non-hex rows is never scanned (box census needed)
description:
## BLUF

**The reconciler's batch can be spent entirely on rows it then skips, so a real stuck anchor behind them is never scanned.** Gate 41 measured it on real Postgres: 25 older non-final rows with non-hex hashes left a real stuck row at scanned 0 across 4 passes. Pre-existing, not worsened by KS-1384 F-a. **Rev 4 §6's "every in-flight row ends" rests on this, so it needs a box census before anyone claims it.**

Facts only. No row, box or code was touched. The figures above are gate 41's (2026-10-30, tier 1 on PR 1838), relayed by Wednesday and not re-measured here. The code path below I read myself.

## Where (`services/anchoring/src/reconciler.ts`, read at F0c's head `dfc0dd61d75e`)

* The SELECT takes non-final rows with `transaction_hash IS NOT NULL` and `simulated = FALSE`, `ORDER BY updated_at ASC`, `LIMIT $2` (batch, default 25, `ANCHOR_RECONCILE_BATCH`).
* The loop then does `if (!REAL_TX_64HEX.test(tx)) continue;`.
* So a row with a non-hex hash takes a batch place, is skipped, and is never moved. Oldest first means it keeps that place on every pass.

## Where such rows come from

Gate 41's reading: base's `saveAnchorToDb` wrote anchoring's id into `transaction_hash`, and on a network mismatch that row is one anchoring never overwrites. KS-1384 F-a removes that write, so it stops NEW ones and cleans no old ones.

## What is needed first

**A read-only census on each box, for a deploy seat:** the count of non-final rows with `simulated = FALSE` and a hash that is not 64 hex, by status and age. If the count is below the batch size on every box, this is latent; at or above it, real rows are stranded today.

## One related shape, for whoever picks this up

KS-1384 F-b's sweep (R6, not merged) selects the same way: oldest first with a LIMIT. Rows it leaves in place (driven, inside the wait marker's bound, or with no stored payload) also take batch places. The first two end by themselves; a no-payload row would not.

## Searched before filing (title, description and comments, archived included; controls: a literal in archived KS-336 found, a nonsense token 0)

* `non-hex` 1 (KS-1628, a different read); `REAL_TX_64HEX` 1 (KS-726); `every in-flight row ends` 0; `starv` 24 and `unscanned` 11, read by title: pools, scanners and queues, none about this reconciler.

Refs KS-1384, KS-1870.

title: shared authenticate() never checks a token's type, so a refresh token is accepted as an access token at a service
description:
**BLUF:** The shared `authenticate()` middleware never checks a token's `type`, so a refresh token is accepted as an access token at a service. QA gate 42 (on KS-1845) measured it: a real RS256 token with `type: 'refresh'` and role SYSTEM_ADMIN got 200 direct-to-service. The auth service's own `verifyAccessToken` refuses that token. This is pre-existing. The gateway was not tested.

## What was read at develop a41909b50b44

* `packages/shared/src/middleware/index.ts:67` `verifyRs256` returns the verified payload, and `:120-121` sets `req.user = decoded`. Neither reads `type`.
* `services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:226` signs refresh tokens with the same claims as an access token, including `userId`, `role`, `tenantId` and `scopes`, plus `type: 'refresh'`. So nothing else in the token tells them apart.
* `services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:339` is the check this class needs: `if (payload.type !== 'access') throw new InvalidTokenError()`. `packages/shared/src/security/token-rotation.ts:295` has the same check.
* `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:556` refuses `type === 'connector'` only. The refresh case there is the denylist KS-1470 records (below).

## Already recorded, and how this differs

KS-1470's description carries a "Related observation" that the gateway's Bearer path accepts `type: 'refresh'` tokens as principals, and says to split it out if the owner prefers. That is the gateway half, unmeasured and with no ticket of its own. This ticket is the class: the shared middleware, measured by the gate, plus that gateway half. KS-1470 is linked and not changed.

## Asked for

An `access`-only allowlist on `type` in the shared middleware and on the gateway's Bearer path, with red-first cells. Check first which legitimate tokens carry no `type` or another value (connector and test tokens, older tokens still within their expiry), so that an allowlist refuses none of them.

## Measured and not measured

* The gate's probe: real RS256, `type: 'refresh'`, SYSTEM_ADMIN, direct to a service: 200.
* Not tested: the gateway, a running stack, or a refresh token minted by the real login flow. A caller needs a refresh token to use this, so its reach is what such a token can do past its rotation and session checks; that is not assessed here.

## Board search before filing

Team KS issues, archived included, titles, descriptions and comments:

* `type: 'refresh'` 1 hit, KS-1470 (above). `type:'refresh'`, `type !== 'access'`, `refresh token as access`, `refresh token as an access`, `refresh-as-access`, `token confusion`, `typ claim`, `access-only`: 0 hits each.
* `type confusion` 2 hits, KS-663 and KS-525. `verifyRs256` 1 hit, KS-584. `refresh JWT` 1 hit, KS-1157. `token type` 4 hits, KS-1406, KS-1402, KS-1205 and KS-486. `tokenType` 1 hit, KS-256. KS-486, KS-1406 and KS-329 were read for a token-type line: only KS-329 matched, on token size. The others were judged by title.
* `refresh token` 31 hits, read by title: none is this class.
* Controls: `run-code-guards` gave hits (positive); a zero token generated at run time gave 0 (not recorded here).

description:
**Read from code at develop** `cb2320368ae4`**, not run against a stack.** Found while checking `CONNECTORS.md` for KS-1807 PR-5 and re-read by me.

Three places where a configuration name is declared but the code reads a different one (or none):

The `KYC_PROVIDER=mock` refusal is correct and works. Same class as the nft-certificate guard in KS-1838.
2. `SHAREPOINT_SITE_URL`**.** The compose file, `env.example`, `services/m365-integration/.env.example` and `deployment/azure/env.dev.json` set it; no source file in `services/m365-integration/src` (or anywhere under `services`/`packages`) reads it. `SETUP.md` lists it as required. The value in `deployment/azure/env.dev.json` is a SharePoint address on the old Secuura tenant that was decommissioned on 2026-06-25.
3. **Apple smoke test requirements.** `tests/connectors/connectors.registry.json` says the Apple connector requires `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, `APPLE_KEY_ID` and `APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY`; the auth service's social provider factory enables Apple from `SOCIAL_APPLE_CLIENT_ID` and `SOCIAL_APPLE_CLIENT_SECRET` and nothing reads the registry's names. (The smoke tests are placeholders, so this affects only what they would skip on.)

**Searched.** Positive control for item 1 and 2: the same searches find `ENTRA_TENANT_ID` in the kyc client and `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` in the m365 service.

**Not established.** What the deployed demo and kintsugi have set; whether anything outside this repository (a deploy script, a Key Vault secret) provides the unused names for a reason I cannot see.

**Docs.** `CONNECTORS.md` and the m365 `SETUP.md` state these as known deviations in KS-1807 PR-5.

title: tenant-provisioning checks no role on its own routes: any signed-in caller who reaches the service can suspend, archive, edit or delete any tenant
description:
## BLUF

`services/tenant-provisioning` **verifies the bearer token on every** `/api/*` **route (**`index.ts:182`**) but checks no role on any of them.** Any caller with a valid JWT who reaches the service directly, rather than through the gateway, can list, read, create, suspend, archive, edit or delete any tenant. The only role gate is the gateway's `requireSuperAdmin` on its proxy routes. **Read from code, not exercised.** Exposure on the deployed boxes is UNMEASURED. This is the same class as KS 1881 and KS 1845: an admin route in a service with no role check of its own.

## Detail (develop `cb2320368ae4`)

* `index.ts:182` is `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate())`. The token is verified, and no role is read afterwards: a search of `services/tenant-provisioning/src` (tests excluded) for `.role`, `isPlatformRole`, `SUPER_ADMIN`, `SYSTEM_ADMIN` and `requireRole` finds only a comment at `index.ts:141`.
* **The routes it leaves open:**
  * `POST /api/tenants` (`index.ts:219`)
  * `GET /api/tenants` (`index.ts:369`)
  * `GET /api/tenants/:id` (`index.ts:398`)
  * `PATCH /api/tenants/:id/status` (`index.ts:432`)
  * `PATCH /api/tenants/:id` (`index.ts:471`)
  * `DELETE /api/tenants/:id` (`index.ts:523`)
  * `GET /api/audit-log` (`index.ts:584`)
* **Create is not fully open.** `POST /api/tenants` writes the tenant row, then forwards the caller's token to tokenisation's `generate-key`, which needs a platform role (`index.ts:139-150`, KS 175). A non-platform caller therefore gets a tenant without a confirmed key, which is the `keyPending` answer from KS 1240.
* **The gateway's gate:** `api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:65-74`, `requireSuperAdmin`, an exact-match list of `'super_admin','SUPER_ADMIN','platform_admin','SYSTEM_ADMIN'`, on the proxies (for example the status and delete proxies at `platform.ts:395-431`). The proxies forward the caller's `Authorization` header (`platform.ts:289-295`). That list differs from the shared `isPlatformRole`: it admits `platform_admin` and does not fold case. KS 1536 tracks the role-vocabulary drift.
* **Reachability by repo config:** the service listens on 4022. `docker-compose.yml:2081-2083` keeps the host port unpublished (pen-test F-04; it was `"6022:4022"`), so the service is reachable from inside the compose network. The deployed hosts are not measured.
* **Related:** KS 1860 and KS 1861 (the status and delete handlers' behaviour) are being fixed separately. This ticket is only about who may call these routes.

## Recommendation

* Gate every `/api` route in tenant-provisioning with the shared `isPlatformRole` straight after `jwtAuthenticate()`, the KS 1845 / KS 1881 shape, with red-first cells per route.
* Decide first whether the gateway's `SUPER_ROLES` list and the shared helper must agree (KS 1536). As things stand, a `platform_admin` or lowercase `super_admin` token that the gateway admits would be refused by the service.

Found by Seat S 9th while writing the KS 1860 / KS 1861 option sets, 2026-10-31. Searched before filing (title or description, team KS): `requireSuperAdmin` 1 (KS 1773, a different route); `SUPER_ROLES` 3 (KS 1536, KS 1535, KS 1472, none naming this service); the 25 tickets whose description names `tenant-provisioning`, filtered for a missing role check: none own it.

title: KS-1384 F0 follow-ups from gate 48: batch write-ahead leaves rows naming an unsent tx, thread-mint has no TTL, the wallet view never shrinks
description:
## BLUF

**Three follow-ups from QA gate 48 on the KS-1384 F0 stack, none blocking: a batch write-ahead that can leave rows naming an unsent transaction, a thread-mint with no TTL that can hold its coins for the life of the process, and a wallet view and family registry that never shrink.** No money is lost in any of them. Gate 48 measured the first two with probes; the third is by reading.

Facts only. Nothing here is built. The figures are gate 48's (2026-10-31, tier 1 on PRs 1853, 1854, 1857 and 1858), relayed by Wednesday and not re-measured here.

## 1. Batch write-ahead, readback honesty (gate 48 N1 / P4; KS-1384 F0a)

* `writeAheadEveryRow` (`services/anchoring/src/anchorSubmission.ts`) writes every row's `submitting` plus the transaction's hash BEFORE it decides whether all N matched. With counts \[1, 0, 1\] it throws, so nothing is submitted, but rows 1 and 3 already hold the unsent hash.
* The batch catch in `index.ts` then writes `failed` to all N rows, unguarded and leaving the hash in place. The rows end `failed` while naming a transaction that was never sent.
* The batch path also takes `NoSpendableUtxo` as a terminal batch failure; only the single path implements the design's §3.5 wait.

## 2. A thread-mint has no TTL (gate 48 N2 / P5; KS-1384 F0c)

* `parseSignedBody` maps a missing TTL to +∞. A mint that is lost, or accepted but never confirmed by the outside-lock poll, stays live and claims its input and collateral until the process restarts; `settleExpiredSpenders` can never settle it. The control, the same spender with a finite TTL, is settled dead by an answered tip.
* This is liveness (coins stranded until restart), not money.

## 3. The wallet view and the family registry never shrink (gate 48 N3; KS-1384 F0a/F0b)

* `WalletView.prune` has no production caller (grep). Dead entries, and confirmed entries older than 24 h, stay for the life of the process, so `claimed()` walks a list that only grows.
* `FamilyRegistry` removes a family only on close.

## Searched before filing (title, description and comments, archived included; controls: a literal in archived KS-336 found, a nonsense token 0)

`writeAheadEveryRow`, `WalletView.prune`, `settleExpiredSpenders`, `FamilyRegistry`, `thread-mint has no TTL`: 0 each. `batch write-ahead`: 2. Read: **KS-726** is the write-ahead itself (Done); **KS-774** is the batch ROW (`anchor_batches`) having no reconciliation path, a different table and a different defect.

Refs KS-1384, KS-774.

title: glob 7.2.3 inside jest and ts-node-dev throws on any non-brace pattern under the forced minimatch 11 (dev tooling, not reached today)
description:
**BLUF:** KS-1891 forces minimatch 11.0.3 everywhere (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249). The glob 7.2.3 that jest and ts-node-dev still carry now throws a TypeError on any glob pattern except a pure brace pattern. Nothing in the repo reaches it today; a future jest config would fail with a confusing error. Dev tooling only, no shipped runtime path.

* **Where:** glob 7.2.3 sits in 5 locks: the root `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` and services governance, originate, referral and vc-issuer. Its parents are jest-config, jest-runtime, jest's reporters package, test-exclude, and ts-node-dev's rimraf 2.7.1.
* **Symptom:** `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'charAt')` at `glob/sync.js:148`.
* **Control (QA gate 51):** the same glob 7.2.3 with minimatch 3.1.5 passes all 5 probe cases. With minimatch 11.0.3, 3 of 5 throw. What changed is the internal shape glob 7 reads from minimatch, not a removed function, so a grep for removed APIs does not see it.
* **Why nothing reaches it today:**
  * jest-runtime's call is inside a try/catch (a "did you mean" hint).
  * jest's reporters package globs only `coverageThreshold` keys, and no jest config sets one.
  * jest-config globs only `projects`, which is unset.
  * ts-node-dev's rimraf globs only paths with magic characters, and its cache path has none.
* **What would trigger it:** a `coverageThreshold` keyed by a glob such as `src/**`; a glob entry in `projects`; or `--coverageProvider=babel`.
* **Same class, also dev-only:**
  * referral and vc-issuer carry test-exclude 6 and babel-plugin-istanbul, which now resolve to minimatch 11. They run vitest, but `jest --coverage` there would break the way governance and originate did before KS-1891 set `coverageProvider: 'v8'`. referral's image copies the builder's node_modules, so that code ships but is never loaded.
  * `tests/connectors/jest.config.cjs` runs no coverage today; a `--coverage` run on it would hit the same break.
* **Why not fixed in KS-1891:** that PR was scoped to the ruling to force the new majors, so it could lift the develop-wide push freeze quickly. The gate rated this Minor, with no current reach.
* **Direction (open):** minimatch 3 cannot come back, because it is inside the advisory's range. Options include a jest major whose internals no longer pull glob 7, replacing ts-node-dev, or a guard that refuses a glob-keyed `coverageThreshold` or `projects` entry until then. Measure before choosing.
* **Found by:** QA gate 51 on pull request 1859 (2026-10-31), finding F2.
* **Related, named rather than linked (archived):** KS-353, npm deprecation warnings at rebuild (glob 7 is among the deprecated packages). Linked: KS-1891.

title: demo-service: the ks1182 error-handler R1 cell (real express on 127.0.0.1) fails intermittently on develop
description:
## BLUF

One cell in `Blockchain/Dev/services/demo-service/src/__tests__/ks1182-error-handler-status-and-headers.test.ts` fails intermittently in full demo-service suite runs, on develop itself: R1, "mounted in a real express app on 127.0.0.1, a status-200 error still answers 500". A failing cell takes 6.6 to 9.5 s and its report carries no assertion text, only vitest's `STACK_TRACE_ERROR`; a passing cell takes 84 to 987 ms. Cause not found. ## Measured (2026-10-31, Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 27.0.1, Node v26.8.1 (not an LTS line), vitest 4.1.12, shared with other seats)
