Whether vc-issuer runs with `VC_SIGNING_KEY` set (the production compose passes it through; when it is set, the `zDEV_` key is that value, not the default) and with `NODE_ENV=production`; and the routes' revocation resolvers, which fail closed on an unknown credential id, so a forgery would also need an id with a stored, unrevoked record. The gate did not check whether this is already ticketed; the board was searched for the default key, `zDEV_` and the `secuura-dev` literal (no ticket found; related reading only: KS-1352, KS-624, KS-625). It does not bear on any merge.

Wednesday's disposition (her 2026-11-04 00:19 note): a ticket candidate for a Secuura seat, to be told to Kam once as an FYI on the morning card with the measurement limit above.

title: health-dashboard checkService: no test pins the DOMException name probe (gate 177 mutant H5 survives and is not equivalent)
description:
**BLUF:** In `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/health-dashboard.ts`, `checkService` (line 44) tells a timeout from other failures with `error instanceof DOMException && error.name === 'AbortError'` (line 83 at develop `ea5134d6b98c`, before KS-1868 pull request 1993 guards the reads). Gate 177's mutant H5 (drop the DOMException-name probe in `checkService`) survives that pull request's tests and all 17 value classes, and it is NOT equivalent: no test pins the probe line. Test gap, not a defect in the pull request, and not a hold for it.

## Measured (gate 177, read from its verdict)

Source: `WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-03_gate177-ks1868-pr1993/verdict.md`, finding G177-F5 (LOW, test gap).

* For a `DOMException('...','AbortError')` whose `name` getter throws (the gate calls it VX, outside the 17 classes), the pull request's head lists the service `down` with the constant error. The H5-mutated head and base both lose the service from the dashboard (the oracle fails: `expected undefined to be 'down'`). So head handles VX correctly, but nothing would notice if the probe were removed.
* Evidence: `scripts/mut_h5.sh` and `results/mut_h5.txt` in the gate's folder (head rc 0, H5 rc 1, base rc 1).

## Follow-up cell

One test cell in the api-gateway `checkService` test: a rejected probe whose value is a `DOMException` with a throwing `name` getter; assert the service is listed `down`. Depends on pull request 1993 being merged (the guarded reads are only in its tree until then).

## Not measured

A real timeout (`AbortController`) path; the gate drove only a stand-in fetch.

title: restore-local-secrets.sh: a .env line that closes stderr hides the PATH refusal (G180-F1); compose config has no time limit; census pin misses 4 of 8 keys
description:
**BLUF:** Four follow-ups on `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/restore-local-secrets.sh` (KS-915, PR 1989, merged 2026-11-04 as squash `26d8314e4f77`). QA gates 174 and 180 named them, and KS-915 comment 820f9aff lists them "for tickets, not in this round". They are one fix to the script and its suite, proven by one suite run, so they are one ticket (Kam, 2026-09-07: the unit of a ticket is the test pass). Item 1 is the one Kam ruled to ticket (live board 2026-11-04 12:51 AEDT, card `secuura-pr1989-round3-go-hold-demo-accounts-1104` = a: "Merge it, and ticket G180-F1"). All are LOW or INFO; none was ruled blocking.

The code was read at develop `5c1ca287ed74` with `git show`. The script blob is the same at the merge squash: `7eef8a0e47e6` at both.

1. **G180-F1 (LOW): a** `.env` **line that closes stderr hides the readonly-PATH refusal.**
   * The bash reader (`restore-local-secrets.sh:306-307`) sources the file under `readonly PATH; set -r; set -a`. It counts refusals by piping the reader's stderr into `grep -c ': PATH: '`.
   * A line that runs `exec 2<&-` before the PATH assignment closes stderr. The refusal is then never counted, while bash still skips the rest of that line.
   * Gate 180 measured a crafted two-line `.env`. At head: rc 0, ADMIN written, mode 600. At round 2: rc 3.
   * Independent readers: dotenv and both compose entries read the local host; a plain `set -a` read a remote POSTGRES_HOST. No command executed (the gate's r3 cell: the PATH lock holds).
   * Measured on macOS bash 3.2.57 only, NOT on bash 4/5 or Linux.
   * Source: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-04_gate180-ks915-pr1989-r3/verdict.md`, section G180-F1.
   * Fix direction (the gate's, direction only): a sentinel the reader must print after the source, whose absence counts as a refusal; or a stderr-liveness check after the source.
2. **G174-F4 (LOW):** `docker compose config` **has no time limit.**
   * The three compose reads (`:326`, `:329`, `:479`) run with no timeout.
   * Gate 174 made `docker compose config` hang. In 3 of 3 runs the script hung until the gate's 45 s alarm (rc 142). The `.env` stayed byte-identical and nothing was written, so it fails closed.
   * In 3 of 3 runs the compose child was still running after the script ended.
   * Source: gate 174 `verdict.md` lines 35-36 (`/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-04_gate174-ks915-pr1989-r2/verdict.md`).
3. **G174-F3 (LOW, test strength): the census pin catches 4 of 8 planted address keys.**
   * `CENSUS_JS` (`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/restore_local_secrets.test.sh:623`) is name-based.
   * The gate planted one key per run through a compose override. The pin caught DB_READ_HOST, PGBOUNCER_UPSTREAM_HOST, READ_REPLICA_URL and SQLALCHEMY_HOST. It missed REPLICA_HOST, TYPEORM_HOST, AUDIT_STORE_ADDR and PRISMA_URL.
   * Source: gate 174 `verdict.md` lines 31-33.
4. **G174-F5 (INFO): the repo-root note is asymmetric.**
   * When ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD is kept (`:537`) and the repo-root entry passes a different value, no note prints. For a kept ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS the note does print (`:482-490`).
   * Gate 174 called this truthful under the note's own rule, "an asymmetry, not a defect". To decide: make the two cases symmetric or leave them.
   * Source: gate 174 `verdict.md` lines 38-39.

**Not measured for this ticket:** none of the four was re-run; every result above is the gate's. Whether item 1 reproduces on bash 4/5 or on Linux is also not measured.

**Related, not filed here:**

* The wider class of a hostile `.env` forging the bash reader (G173-F2), and the looping `.env`. Both are named in KS-915 comment 820f9aff.
* The pgbouncer `entrypoint.sh` userlist echo from the same comment, filed as its own ticket (a different file, fix and test).

**Searched** (board: title, description and comments, archived included):

* `G180-F1`: 0 hits. `exec 2<&-`: 0. `CENSUS_JS`: 0.
* `G174-F3`, `G174-F4`, `G174-F5`: 1 hit each, all in KS-915 comment 820f9aff, which names them for tickets.
* `restore-local-secrets`: 2 hits (KS-915; KS-600, closed). No ticket covers these items.

title: e2e fixtures register with breached passwords: since KS-1968 B1 seven register call sites get 422 instead of an account
description:
**BLUF:** Since KS-1968 B1 (PR 1988, squash `1cbf260548e7`, deployed to kintsugi at `ee1e1b832115`), `POST /api/auth/register` and `POST /api/auth/reset-password` answer 422 to a password that the HaveIBeenPwned range check finds. Seven e2e call sites send such a password to register on the success path, so on a stack with the check on they get 422 instead of an account. Fix: give those fixtures generated, non-breached passwords (or run them with `HIBP_ENABLED=false`, if that is the ruled choice). Medium priority, because a merged and deployed change breaks known test sites. This was measured by reading the code, not by a run.

**Source:** `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-04_seatD-50th/evidence/hibp_corpus_ee1e1b832115.txt`, Seat D 50th's corpus at target `ee1e1b832115`.

* 148 distinct literals, 44 of them breached; 210 breached occurrences, 21 of those within 15 lines of a register or reset mention. Its positive and negative controls fired.
* The file tags 16 rows `[reg/reset]` (the header's 21 counts occurrences; the rows are what it tagged).
* No literal is copied into this ticket.

**The 16 rows, each read at** `ee1e1b832115` **with** `git show`**:**

* **Register on the success path (7): affected.**
  * `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/tests/tier1-api/email-notifications.api.spec.ts:48`. Asserts a status below 500, so a 422 passes silently and no account is made.
  * `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/email-notifications.prelaunch.spec.ts:76`. Registers, then waits for the verification mail.

title: pgbouncer entrypoint.sh writes the four userlist credentials unescaped: a newline in a value adds a userlist entry
description:
**BLUF:** `Blockchain/Dev/docker/pgbouncer/entrypoint.sh:27-30` writes four user/password pairs into `/etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt` with one `echo` per pair and no escaping. A value that contains a newline therefore adds a userlist line of its own: an extra auth entry, not an upstream. Seat E 33rd found this during KS-915 round 3, and it was ruled out of that PR. KS-915 comment 820f9aff names it for a ticket. Low: the values come from the operator's own `.env` or compose environment.

**Read at develop** `5c1ca287ed74` **with** `git show` (the same blob is at `ee1e1b832115`):

  * PGBOUNCER_STATS_USER / PGBOUNCER_STATS_PASSWORD
  * APP_DB_USER / APP_DB_PASSWORD

**Fix direction only:** refuse a newline or a double quote in these eight values at start-up, or double each quote and refuse newlines before writing. Also correct the header comment, or write md5 entries as it says.

**Not measured:**

title: api-gateway image crash-loops under NODE_ENV=production: EACCES mkdir 'logs' (the production File transports write to relative logs/, and /app is not writable by USER nodejs)
description:
## BLUF

* **The api-gateway image does not boot in production mode.** With `NODE_ENV=production` it exits at import with `Error: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir 'logs'` and restarts in a loop.
* **Cause (code at** `ee1e1b832115`**, byte-identical at develop** `d92b849ece73`**):** in production the logger adds two winston File transports at the relative path `logs/`. The image runs as `USER nodejs` in `/app`, a directory that user cannot write to.
* **Measured on a disposable local stack at** `ee1e1b832115`**, not on kintsugi.** `NODE_ENV=production` was set by an override on the base compose; the production compose file itself was not run. A writable tmpfs at `/app/logs` (a stack mount, no code change) let the same image boot and serve.
* **Priority Medium (3).** It is a hard boot failure, but no deployed environment is shown to run this image in production mode. Raise it if one is.

## What ran

Seat W 25th ran this on stack `w25`, 2026-11-04 \~08:34Z, with throwaway data. The api-gateway container was recreated with `NODE_ENV: production` set by a compose override. It crash-looped. Container output, verbatim (lines 1-5 and 11-16 of the saved file):

```
Error: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir 'logs'
    at Object.mkdirSync (node:fs:1410:26)
    at File._createLogDirIfNotExist (/app/node_modules/winston/lib/winston/transports/file.js:791:10)
    at new File (/app/node_modules/winston/lib/winston/transports/file.js:94:28)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/app/dist/utils/logger.js:32:21)
    at Module.require (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1674:12) {
  errno: -13,
  code: 'EACCES',
  syscall: 'mkdir',
  path: 'logs'
}
```

The container was then recreated with a tmpfs at `/app/logs` (mode 1777) added to that override. The production-mode gateway booted and answered 155 requests in the KS-1469/KS-1479 run (307 x31, 404 x122, 429 x2).

## Code (`Blockchain/Dev/`, at `ee1e1b832115`)

* `services/api-gateway/src/utils/logger.ts:30-35`: when `isProduction`, the logger pushes `new winston.transports.File({ filename: 'logs/error.log', ... })` and `new winston.transports.File({ filename: 'logs/combined.log', ... })`. Winston creates the directory at construction time, relative to the cwd.
* `services/api-gateway/Dockerfile` (99 lines, read whole):
  * the runtime stage sets `WORKDIR /app` (line 45);
  * `RUN chmod -R a+rX /app /shared` (line 84) grants read and execute only;
  * the user `nodejs` (uid 1001) is created at lines 87-88, and `USER nodejs` is set at line 89;
  * no line makes a `logs` directory or chowns anything to `nodejs`.
* `docker-compose.production.yml`: the `api-gateway:` block (lines 79-117) sets `NODE_ENV=production` (line 81) and mounts nothing. The whole file has 0 hits for `tmpfs`, `/logs`, `logs:` and `read_only`. The control `NODE_ENV=production` has 22 hits.
* `docker-compose.yml` (the base the production file overlays): the `api-gateway:` block has one volume, the OpenAPI spec mounted read-only. Its comment says Container Apps production deploys do not use this compose file.
* Develop: these four files are byte-identical at `d92b849ece73` and `ee1e1b832115`, read in a kept seat clone.

## Why Medium

* The failure is total for anyone who runs the image in production mode without a writable `/app/logs`.
* No current deployment is shown to do that. Seat U 11th's live check on kintsugi (2026-11-04, at `ee1e1b832115`) read the api-gateway `NODE_ENV=development`; that reading is carried, not re-measured here. The Container Apps estate was deleted on 2026-07-31 (project CLAUDE.md).
* `docker-compose.production.yml` exists to run the stack in production mode. Whoever first uses it will hit this.

## Related

* **KS-1526** (Done) fixed the *format* of these same File transports (a column of `undefined`). Its description listed as unmeasured whether winston's default `mkdir('logs')` throws EACCES for a non-root user, and whether the File transports write anywhere in the deployed containers. This ticket measures the first: it does throw, and the gateway does not boot.
* KS-1348 (Done) is the originate half of the format defect. Whether originate's image has the same boot failure was not measured here.

## Board search before filing (team KS, includeArchived)

* Searched title or description, plus comment bodies, for: `EACCES`, `mkdir('logs')`, `/app/logs`, `tmpfs`, `USER nodejs`, `crash-loop`, `crashloop`, `logger.ts`, `not writable`, `read-only file`, `combined.log`.
* No open ticket covers this.
* The six open `EACCES` hits (KS-1025, 1152, 1402, 1571, 1686, 1776) are false positives: a case-insensitive `EACCES` matches inside `generateAccessToken` and `authenticateAccessOrConnector`.
* The only mentions of the boot failure are Seat W 25th's closing comments on KS-1469 and KS-1479 (both Done), which used the tmpfs as a stack workaround.

## Options (not decided here)

1. Create `/app/logs` owned by `nodejs` in the Dockerfile's runtime stage, before `USER nodejs`.
2. Drop the File transports in containers and keep Console (container logs already capture stdout).
3. Mount a writable volume or tmpfs at `/app/logs` in `docker-compose.production.yml`.

## Not established here

* Anything about kintsugi's configuration, data, env or network beyond the carried `NODE_ENV` reading above.
* Whether originate, or any other service image with production File transports, fails the same way.

## Evidence

`5_Project_History/2026-11-04_seatW-25th/evidence/ks1469/`: `prod_boot1_crash.out` (the crash), `o1469_prod.yml` (the override with the tmpfs), `recreate_prod.out`, `recreate_prod2.out`, `steps.jsonl` (the run after the tmpfs). Code extracts: `5_Project_History/2026-11-04_seatW-26th/evidence/item1/`.

title: Every read of svc_nft_certificates.public_fields runs JSON.parse on an already-parsed JSONB array, so a stored NFT certificate cannot be read back
description:
BLUF: In the nft-certificate service, every read of the `public_fields` column runs `JSON.parse` on a value the Postgres driver has already parsed. The column is JSONB, so the driver returns an array, `JSON.parse` of an array throws, and a stored certificate cannot be read back. The write path stores a JSON array, so this reaches every row the service writes itself. The rows are intact in the database; they are unreadable through the service. Priority High (the brief's suggestion, and my grade): the failure sits on the read path of every stored certificate, and nothing short of a code change works around it.

Source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-04_seatW-27th/HANDOVER.md (lines 28 to 31) and /Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-04_seatW-27th/evidence/search_nft_jsonb.out. Seat W 27th found it on a disposable stack (w27) at ee1e1b832115. I read the code at origin/develop 035685291b9d myself.

What I read (code, not a run):

* `Blockchain/Dev/migrations/002_verification-tiers.sql` line 796, inside `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS svc_nft_certificates` (line 784): `public_fields JSONB DEFAULT '[]'`. No other file under `Blockchain/Dev/migrations` names the column (searched `public_fields`).
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/services/minting.service.ts` line 76 writes `JSON.stringify(cert.publicFields || [])` into that column.
* The same file reads it with `JSON.parse(row.public_fields || '[]')` at line 123 (`loadFromDb`, the startup load, which selects every row of `svc_nft_certificates`) and at lines 505, 592 and 678. The row type declares `public_fields: string`, which is not what a JSONB column returns.
* `loadFromDb` runs the parse inside its loop. The first row that holds an array makes it throw into the function's catch, so no later row is loaded.

What Seat W 27th measured on w27 (disposable stack, ee1e1b832115): the log lines `DB get user certificates failed` and `DB get wallet certificates failed`, each with `Unexpected end of JSON input`. A row whose `public_fields` is NULL reads fine.

Fix shape (not chosen here): accept the value the driver returns for JSONB (an array) at the four read sites, or make the column text and keep the stringify. Either needs a test that round-trips a stored row.

Not measured: a run of this code by me; how many rows `svc_nft_certificates` holds on kintsugi or the demo environment; whether any deployed environment overrides the driver's JSONB parser; what the three DB read paths return to the caller after the catch (W 27th's log lines are the only evidence of the failure itself).
Board search (this seat, 2026-11-05): `public_fields` 0 open and 0 closed literal hits; `minting.service` with `JSON.parse` 0; `Unexpected end of JSON input` 0. Seat W 27th named KS-1843 as the nearest neighbour, a different defect.

title: Platform-settings save: when the Redis write fails after the database write the row and Redis disagree (503 "save again"), and a save during a Redis outage answers 200 while Redis keeps the old value
description:
BLUF: In the api-gateway platform-settings save (PR 2001, KS-1256), the database row and Redis can disagree after a save. If the Redis write fails after the database write, the route answers 503 "Platform settings were stored but the cache could not be refreshed; save again". The row then holds the new value and Redis keeps the old one, and the live answer follows Redis until the next eviction, which flips it to the row. A save during a Redis outage answers 200, writes the row and the in-memory store, and Redis comes back holding the old value. QA gate 189 found neither path looser than develop: a save that adds a restriction and hits this fault leaves the old, looser value live until the retry the 503 asks for, as develop does. Priority Low (the verdict's grade).

Source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-04_gate189-ks1256-pr2001/verdict.md, G189-F3 at line 31 and the TESTED bullets under it (the seat's candidate 2, confirmed by the gate).

Measured by gate 189, not by this seat: real Redis, real Postgres and the real modules, with GET /api/connector/info wired as the gateway wires it. In the gate's runs/real_head.jsonl, step 8 is put 503 with Redis still restricted (old), the row open (new) and create-out 403 while stale; step 8b, after a DEL, is create-out 201 with Redis refilled with the open value; step 10 is a put during an outage answering 200 with the row open. On develop under the same faults the Redis-write fault hangs (status -1, an unhandled rejection, nothing stored), and during an outage the save goes to the in-memory store only.

What this seat read (code, not a run): at origin/develop 035685291b9d, `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts` lines 1207 and 1208 log "Platform settings were stored but Redis could not be refreshed" and answer with the 503 text above.

Fix shape (not chosen here): the gate's HOW notes do not give one. Any fix has to decide which store wins after a partial write, and that is a design call this ticket does not make.

Not measured: a run of this code by me; how often Redis fails after the database write on kintsugi or the demo environment; whether an operator who reads the 503 retries; the gateway's behaviour on a second failed retry.
Board search (this seat, 2026-11-05): "could not be refreshed" 0, "stored but the cache" 0, `G189-F3` 0, `settingsStore` 0 open (1 closed, KS-1540, a different 503), `svc_gateway_settings` with Redis 1 open (KS-1256, the pull request's own ticket, which does not name this).

title: Originals read in verify: MIN(created_at) walks the whole documents table through idx_documents_created for a hash with 300 or more rows (31 ms at 310,030 rows, on an unauthenticated path)
description:
BLUF: In PR 2000's originals read, the subquery that takes MIN(e.created_at) over the hash's three forms runs a different plan depending on how many rows PostgreSQL estimates for the hash. For small groups (24 and 100 rows) it uses a BitmapOr on idx_documents_content_hash: 10 to 13 buffers, about 0.03 ms. From about 300 rows up (300, 576, 1,000, 2,000, 5,000 rows on a 310,030-row table) it uses an index scan backward on idx_documents_created (created_at DESC) with a filter on content_hash, walking created_at from the oldest row until it meets the hash. When the hash's rows are the newest in the table (a recently registered file) that reads every row: Rows Removed by Filter 310,027, 18,899 buffers, about 31 ms, against 136 buffers and about 1 ms for the unchanged row-set read on the same hash. The cost grows linearly with the size of the tenant's documents table, on a verify path that is unauthenticated. Correctness is unaffected. Priority Low (the gate graded it MINOR at the measured scale and said it would be MAJOR if a tenant's table holds millions of rows; that size is not measured).

Source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-04_gate188-ks1561-pr2000/verdict_r2.md, G188-F5 at lines 22 to 40; the plans are in runs_r2/explain.txt, runs_r2/explain2.txt and runs_r2/explain3.txt in that folder (explain3 is a probe that flips between 100 and 300 rows). Measured by gate 188 round 2 on a migrated database (migration 001 creates idx_documents_content_hash and idx_documents_created), PostgreSQL 15, custom plans with literal values and with a prepared statement of three parameters (the pg driver sends unnamed statements, which are custom-planned). A forced generic plan chose the bitmap. With the hash's first row in the middle of the table, the walk was 133,237 rows (3,932 buffers, 13.6 ms). The outer read (created_at = $1) is cheap in every plan. The extra read fires only when the row-set read returns 24 rows. The gate's control: the same file shows the unchanged row-set read using idx_documents_content_hash on the same hash.

What this seat read (code, not a run): at origin/develop 035685291b9d the MIN(e.created_at) subquery is in `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts` at lines 534, 547 and 562 (three statements); line 534 is in ORIGINAL_ROWS_POOL_SQL.

The gate's fix shape (not tested by the gate, not chosen here): read the MIN from the content_hash rows only, by ORDER BY created_at, id LIMIT 1 over a (content_hash, created_at) index, or by a MATERIALIZED CTE over the hash's rows, or by defeating the created_at index with MIN(e.created_at + interval '0').

Not measured: the size of any real tenant's documents table; how often groups of 300 rows or more occur; a run of the plans by this seat.
Board search (this seat, 2026-11-05): idx_documents_created 0 open and 0 closed literal hits; MIN(created_at) 0.

title: run-migrations readiness probe: sed passes an unmatched DATABASE_URL through whole, so a URL with no port or a socket host never becomes ready and the runner exits 2 after 60 s
description:
BLUF: The readiness probe in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh` cuts the host and the port out of DATABASE_URL with two sed commands that assume the shape `USER:PASS@HOST:PORT/DB`. When a URL does not match, sed prints the whole line unchanged, so the host or the port, or both, become the entire URL, and pg_isready is called with a URL as its host or port. It never succeeds, the loop runs its 30 attempts at 2 seconds, and the runner exits 2 after about 60 seconds with "PostgreSQL did not become ready after 30 attempts", although the database may be fine. This is wider than the socket-path case first noted by Seat R 85th: a URL with no port at all fails the same way, and the default on line 73 (the port 5432) can never apply, because sed's pass-through leaves the variable non-empty. Priority Low: the compose deploy path is not shown to use such a URL (not measured), and the failure is loud and the run stops, but it blames the database for a parsing fault.

Source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-04_seatR-85th/HANDOVER.md, "Candidates (none filed)" (line 73: the runner cannot probe a socket-path URL) and "Faults of mine" (its first real-runner run used a socket URL and lost 2 x 60 s, which is 30 attempts x 2 s). I read the code at origin/develop 035685291b9d and ran the two sed commands myself.

What I read: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-migrations.sh` line 71 (PG_HOST by `s|.*@([^:/]+).*|\1|`), line 72 (PG_PORT by `s|.*:([0-9]+)/.*|\1|`), line 73 (`PG_PORT=${PG_PORT:-5432}`), line 76 (the pg_isready call), lines 41 and 42 (MAX_RETRIES=30, RETRY_INTERVAL=2) and line 87 (exit 2).

What I measured (the two sed commands on sample URLs, BSD sed on macOS, no database contact; the credentials in the shapes are placeholders):

* `USER:PASS@host:6432/db` gives host "host", port "6432" (correct).
* `USER:PASS@host/db` (no port) gives host "host" and port equal to the WHOLE URL.
* `USER@/db?host=/var/run/postgresql` (a socket directory) gives host and port both equal to the whole URL.
* `postgresql:///db?host=/tmp/pgsock` (no user, no host) gives host and port both equal to the whole URL.

Related, not the same: KS-1296 (Done) fixed the sibling case where a missing pg_isready was blamed on the database.

Fix shape (not chosen here): parse the URL with a tool that understands it, or test that each sed matched before using its output, and fall back to pg_isready's own connection-string form. A test would run the real runner against each shape on 127.0.0.1 at a free port.

title: Verify by hash shows a later tenant's certification when the original's registry row is missing or past the 8-tenant cap (v2 today, v1 after PR 2004)
description:
**BLUF:** When the tenant holding the ORIGINAL registration of some bytes has no row in `platform_document_registry`, or its row is not among the 8 earliest registry rows for that hash, verify by hash presents a LATER registrant's certification from another tenant. v2 (`POST /api/v2/verification/verify`) does this today. v1 (`/verify` and `verify-file`) does it too once PR 2004 (KS-1986) merges. Found by QA gate 192 on PR 2004 (finding G192-F1, MAJOR, HOLD-FOR-KAM). Filed under the default of Kam's open card `secuura-pr2004-ks1986-gate192-hold-1105` ("files (1) as a ticket"). This ticket records facts only; how to fix it is a design choice for Kam.

**Test pass (one workload, one surface: the cross-tenant "original registration" read over the registry)**

1. **G-ORIGINAL-UNREGISTERED.** B registers the bytes first (t0) in tenant T2 and has NO registry row. Y certifies a copy at t20 in T3 (registered). A certifies a copy at t31 in the caller's tenant.
   * v1 at develop `035685291b9d` (before PR 2004): `cert-a-1`, the caller's own later copy.
   * v1 at PR 2004 (heads `577f668f4786` and `4432db224a58`): `cert-y-1`, document `doc-cert-y-1` (T3's later copy), certifierOrganizationId null, certifiedBy null. Both v1 paths.
   * v2 at develop and at PR 2004: `cert-y-1`, with certifierOrganizationId `dddddddd-0000-4000-8000-00000000000d`.
2. **G-CAP-9-SKEWED.** Ten tenants hold the bytes. B's tenant is registered, but its registry `created_at` is later than the other tenants' rows, so the registry read's `LIMIT 8` (ordered by `created_at`) drops it. T2 to T9 hold certified later copies.
   * v1 before PR 2004: `cert-a-1`. v1 at PR 2004: `cert-y-2`, on both v1 paths.
   * v2 at develop and at PR 2004: the eight certified later copies `cert-y-2` to `cert-y-9`, each with certifierOrganizationId `dddddddd-0000-4000-8000-00000000000d`, and not B.
3. **Controls that pass (same harness).** `G-CAP-9-NATURAL`: the original's registry row is the earliest, so it is read; v1 at PR 2004 presents B with no certification, and v2 presents B. `G-CAP-9-SKEWED-NOCERT`: the same skew with uncertified copies; no certification is presented.

Measured by gate 192 on real PostgreSQL 15 (11 databases: the caller, nine other tenants, the registry), real `verificationRouter` and `verificationV2Router` over HTTP. Re-measured by Seat F 33rd on 2026-11-05 on its own PostgreSQL 15 cluster with the gate's harness copied: the same certifications at develop `035685291b9d`, PR 2004 head `577f668f4786` and PR 2004 round-2 head `4432db224a58`, on `/verify`, `verify-file` and v2.

**Not more permissive by count.** In both cells develop already presents a later copy's certification (the caller's own `cert-a-1`). PR 2004 makes v1 present a DIFFERENT later copy, one in another tenant, as v2 already does. Neither presents the original holder's certification.

**Reachability: read from code at** `577f668f4786`**, NOT measured.**

* Registration is fire-and-forget and its failure is swallowed: `registerInPlatformRegistry` (`services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:733`) only logs a warn in its catch (`:755`), and the create route calls it with a `.catch(() => {})` (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:793-798`). KS-1647 records that double swallow.
* The registry is written only on the create path.
* `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts:500-509` (KS-39 #4) records a past window in which every fresh `/api/documents` create failed to register in the cross-tenant registry.
* How many production hashes have an original with no registry row, or a registry order that puts the original past the eighth row, is NOT measured.

**Where found.** PR 2004 ([https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2004](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2004>)). Gate 192 verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate192-ks1986-pr2004/verdict.md`, lines 14 to 26, with evidence `runs/pg_base2.jsonl`, `runs/pg_head2.jsonl` and `runs/direction_base_head_v2.txt`. Seat F 33rd's re-measure: `5_Project_History/2026-11-05_seatF-33rd/evidence/pg/`.

**Board search before filing (2026-11-05; issues filter on title, description and comments, archived included).** `judgeAcrossTenants` 0, `V1_CROSS_TENANT_ORIGINALS_LIMIT` 0, `V2_CROSS_TENANT_LIMIT` 0, `readCrossTenantOriginals` 0, `G192-F1` 0, `G-ORIGINAL-UNREGISTERED` 0, `G-CAP-9` 0. `registerInPlatformRegistry` 3 open (KS-1647 the swallowed write, KS-1590 the verify-file hash form, KS-598 the registry upsert); `platform_document_registry` 15 open; `verificationV2.ts` 8 open. I read the open hits: none records a later tenant's certification being presented. Controls: `KS-1986` 2 hits (KS-1986, KS-1561), `N-SPLIT` 7, a nonsense token 0.

**Related:** KS-1986 (PR 2004), KS-1647 (a failed registry write is invisible), KS-598 (the registry upsert), KS-590 (verify by hash must not resolve to an arbitrary registration), KS-1561.

title: vc-issuer: a revoke refused with 503 on a database write failure is not retried by anything, and the revoking process keeps a revoked memory copy the database row lacks
description:
**BLUF:** In vc-issuer at develop `07a2d62be6a0`, a revoke whose database UPDATE throws or matches no row is refused with a 503 ("The revocation could not be saved. Retry the revoke."), and nothing in the service retries or queues that write: the revocation exists only if the caller sends it again. Until then the revoking process keeps a revoked memory copy that the database row does not have, and gate 194 measured the credential verifying TRUE both in that process and in a restarted one. The gate graded this residual LOW (G194-F2); on verify it behaves the same at base and head. KS-1959's text names "accept and retry" as an alternative that was not chosen; PR 2005 (merged as `17abf8ee98a5`) built the refuse side.

Source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate194-ks1959/verdict.md, finding G194-F2 (lines 32 to 45), cells RESTART A and matrix C; Seat K 14th's unfiled candidate "durable revocation under write failure ('accept and retry')" in /Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-05_seatK-14th/HANDOVER.md.

## What the code does (read at develop `07a2d62be6a0`; PR 2005 and PR 2004 are both merged)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts`, `revoke()` (lines 534 to 583), writes the revoked copy into `memoryStore` at line 552, before the database UPDATE at lines 559 to 562. The catch at lines 564 to 575 and the `rowCount < 1` check at lines 576 to 579 throw `CredentialStoreWriteError`. The code comment at lines 525 to 529 records that memory is written first on purpose (Wednesday's ruling (a) on KS-1959).
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts` lines 321 to 322 map that error to a 503 with the fixed text defined at line 292.
* Each attempt builds a new `revokedAt` and `revocationReason` and writes them into memory (lines 541 to 552), so every failed attempt overwrites the memory copy's values.
* Retry or queue: a search of the non-test source of `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src` for `retry`, `queue`, `outbox` and `backoff` finds only the database connection probe (`Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/db.ts` lines 57 to 169, KS-377), a comment at `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/index.ts` line 158, and the 503 text. Nothing re-sends a failed revoke write.

## What gate 194 measured (PR 2005 head `a968818a0038`, base and head compared)

* After a revoke answered 503 with the row present, the memory copy is revoked and the database row is not. The next healthy verify in the same process returns verified TRUE with no errors on both routes, because the database row outranks memory (KS-1958). Identical at base, where the same revoke answered 200.
* A restarted process also verifies TRUE (RESTART cell A: process 1 memory true, row false, process 2 verify TRUE on both routes).
* The gate did not drive the readers that fall back to memory on a read failure (`getRecordById`, `getByHash`, `getReadableByHash`) in this state.

## Grade

Low. The caller receives an explicit 503 and can send the revoke again; the gate graded the residual LOW and it is not new at base. The grade is the gate's; the reach is not measured (below).

## Not measured

* A real PostgreSQL: the gate ran an in-memory fake table that can fail its UPDATE.
* Whether a revoke UPDATE fails in any deployed environment (kintsugi, demo, production).
* Behaviour across more than one vc-issuer replica.
* Whether callers of the revoke route send it again after a 503.
* This seat ran no test and no service; the code facts are reads of a depth-1 clone at `07a2d62be6a0`.

## Related

* KS-1959 (In Progress): the swallowed UPDATE, whose Fix class names "accept and retry"; PR 2005 refuses the revoke instead. This ticket records the state after that change and does not reopen it.
* KS-1958: the verify read; PR 2003 (merged as `e899463d2a0b`) changed `getById` on the verify path only.
* Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, archived included): `CredentialStoreWriteError` 0 open, 0 closed; `Retry the revoke` 0 and 0; `durable revocation` 0 and 0; `accept and retry` 1 open (KS-1959), 0 closed; `kept in memory` 1 open (KS-1959), 0 closed. Control: `credentialRepo` 13 open, 11 closed. KS-1900 (a repeat revoke overwrites the first), KS-1569 (the API-key revoke route) and KS-1691 (an auth session) were read whole: each is a different service or defect.

title: vc-issuer revoke: a credential held only in memory answers 503 'Retry the revoke.' on every attempt, and no retry can succeed
description:
**BLUF:** In vc-issuer at develop `07a2d62be6a0`, a credential that exists only in a process's memory (no `vc_credentials_store` row) answers 503 with the text "The revocation could not be saved. Retry the revoke." on every revoke attempt, and no retry can succeed, because the UPDATE matches 0 rows each time. Gate 194 measured it as G194-F3 (LOW, a wording note, not a fail-open): the credential already fails verify in that process and after a restart.

Source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate194-ks1959/verdict.md, finding G194-F3 (lines 47 to 58), cells RESTART Z and matrix Zreal.

## How the state arises (read at develop `07a2d62be6a0`)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts`, `store()`, writes the credential into `memoryStore` at line 69 first. If `isDbAvailable()` is false it logs a warning and returns (lines 73 to 85, KS-1295). If the INSERT throws, the catch at lines 95 to 100 logs "DB write failed for credential — kept in memory" and returns without throwing. In both branches the credential has no database row.
* `revoke()` (same file, lines 534 to 583) finds the memory copy, sets it revoked at line 552 and runs the UPDATE at lines 559 to 562. With no row, `rowCount` is 0 and lines 576 to 579 throw `CredentialStoreWriteError`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts` lines 321 to 322 answer that with a 503 and the fixed text from line 292, "The revocation could not be saved. Retry the revoke."

## What gate 194 measured (PR 2005 head `a968818a0038`)

* First revoke 503, retry 503; the UPDATE matches 0 rows each time; database row "no row"; process 1 memory revoked; in a restarted process the credential is absent.
* Verify is FALSE on both routes in the process (memory is revoked) and FALSE after a restart ("no issuer record"). At base the revoke answered 200 both times with the same verify results.
* PR 2005's body states the cost ("every attempt answers 503"). The verdict reads the text as not fitting this case and grades it LOW, not HOLD-class.

## Grade

Low, the verdict's grade. The caller is told to retry something that cannot succeed; the credential already fails verify.

## Not measured

* A real PostgreSQL: the gate ran an in-memory fake table.
* Whether any memory-only credential exists in a deployed environment (an INSERT failure or an unavailable database at issuance).
* What callers do on repeated 503 answers.
* This seat ran no test and no service; the code facts are reads of a depth-1 clone at `07a2d62be6a0`.

## Related

* KS-1959 (In Progress): the swallowed UPDATE; its text does not mention a memory-only credential.
* KS-1295 (In Progress): the warning at `store()` when the database is unavailable; it names that branch only, not the INSERT catch.
* Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, archived included): `Retry the revoke` 0 open, 0 closed; `CredentialStoreWriteError` 0 and 0; `DB write failed for credential` 0 and 0; `REVOCATION_NOT_SAVED` 0 and 0. Control: `credentialRepo` 13 open, 11 closed.

title: vc-issuer: GET /api/credentials/:id and GET /api/credentials/by-hash/:hash answer from the process's memory copy when the database read throws (KS-1958 changed the verify path only)
description:
**BLUF:** In vc-issuer at develop `07a2d62be6a0`, the readers `getRecordById` and `getReadableByHash` catch a thrown database SELECT and answer from this process's in-memory copy, which `loadFromDb` fills at boot and `store()` and `revoke()` write afterwards. They serve `GET /api/credentials/:id` and `GET /api/credentials/by-hash/:hash`, and `getRecordById` also reads the owner for the revoke route. KS-1958 (PR 2003, merged as `e899463d2a0b`) made `getById` refuse to answer from memory on the verify path only. A third reader, `getByHash`, has the same fall-back and no non-test caller. Pre-existing; neither KS-1958 nor gate 194 drove these readers.

Source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate194-ks1959/verdict.md, finding G194-F2, line 40 ("Readers that fall back to memory on a read failure (getRecordById, getByHash, getReadableByHash; KS-1958 boundary 3, out of scope) would show it as revoked while the DB says it is not ... I did not drive those readers in this state"); /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate192-ks1986-pr2004/ready_2004.txt, FILING CANDIDATES (a), Seat F 31st's; /Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-05_seatK-14th/HANDOVER.md.

## Where (read at develop `07a2d62be6a0`, file `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts`)

* `getRecordById` lines 196 to 227: the catch at lines 212 to 221 logs "DB read failed — falling back to memory"; lines 224 to 226 return the memory copy with the owner from `memoryOwners.get(id) ?? OWNERLESS`.
* `getByHash` lines 236 to 263: the catch at lines 247 to 256 logs "DB hash lookup failed — falling back to memory"; lines 259 to 261 scan `memoryStore`. Its own comment (lines 229 to 235) says no route serves it, and a search of the non-test source of `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src` finds no caller outside this file.
* `getReadableByHash` lines 344 to 380: the catch at lines 369 to 371 logs the same fall-back and reads `err?.message` unguarded (that part is KS-1959's); lines 374 to 378 scan `memoryStore` and apply `mayReadCredential`.
* `getById` lines 148 to 180 now takes `failClosedOnReadError` (interface at lines 130 to 141): on a thrown read it throws `CredentialStoreReadError` instead of falling back. The interface comment (lines 131 to 135) says it is set by the verify path's revocation lookup only; the other readers have no such option.
* Callers, non-test: `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts` line 275 (`GET /:id`), line 309 (the revoke route's owner read, before `revoke()`), line 409 (`GET /by-hash/:hash`).
* `memoryStore` is written at lines 69 (`store`), 552 (`revoke`) and 499 (`loadFromDb`). KS-1958 states `loadFromDb` runs at boot only; this seat did not re-check its callers.

## Cells

The two routed readers (`GET /:id`, `GET /by-hash/:hash`) take the same fixture: a memory copy that differs from the database row, and a SELECT that throws. One pass over that fixture drives both. `getByHash` has no route and needs a repository-level cell. The three catches are separate code paths (lines 212, 247 and 369), so this ticket groups them by the shared fixture and the one file, not by one function.

## Grade

Low, this seat's judgement and not the gate's. A stale answer here reaches the credential's creator (or an administrator of an ownerless row) through an owner-bound read, not a verifier; the verify path was the High finding and is changed.

## Not measured

* The readers' behaviour on a throwing SELECT or with a divergent memory copy: this seat ran no test and no service, and gate 194 did not drive them (verdict line 40).
* A real PostgreSQL, a second replica, and whether any deployed instance can see a database read failure.
* Which direction a divergence takes in practice (memory unrevoked while the row is revoked, or memory revoked while the row is not, G194-F2).

## Related

* KS-1958 (In Progress): the verify path. Its Mechanism names the catches of `getById`, `getRecordById` and `getByHash`, and its fix class is `getById` on the verify path only. It does not name `getReadableByHash` or the GET routes. The string "boundary 3" is in gate 194's verdict and in Seat F 31st's candidate, not in KS-1958's description or its two comments (read whole).
* KS-1684 (Backlog): on the memory path of `getRecordById` the owner entry is missing after a revoke, so the creator is refused; a different consequence of the same fall-back.
* KS-1959 (In Progress): the unguarded `err?.message` at the `getReadableByHash` catch; a different defect.
* Board search before filing (team Secuura-PK, archived included): `getRecordById` 4 open, 1 closed; `getByHash` 2 open, 1 closed; `getReadableByHash` 1 open (KS-1959), 0 closed. Control: `credentialRepo` 13 open, 11 closed. KS-1868 (thrown-value reads) and KS-1899 (the revoke ownership check) appear in the symbol hits; this seat read their titles only.

title: originate verify: scopeTenantFields leaves certification.certifierOrganizationId on the existing cross-tenant answers (v1 /verify, v1 verify-file, v2), against Kam's KS-590 card ruling a
description:
**BLUF:** In originate at develop `07a2d62be6a0`, `scopeTenantFields` nulls `title`, `issuer` and `certification.certifiedBy` on a cross-tenant verify answer but leaves `certification.certifierOrganizationId`. Kam's card `secuura-ks590-verify-disclosure-four-questions-1102` was ruled option a on 2026-11-02 (ruled_ts 12:44:16 +11:00): "Strict: no tenant-owned naming incl. org UUID on all four paths (changes live verify)". PR 2004 (merged as `07a2d62be6a0`) applies that on its NEW path only (D-B3). The EXISTING cross-tenant answers of v1 `/verify`, v1 `verify-file` and v2 still carry the id.

Source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate192-ks1986-pr2004/ready_2004.txt, FILING CANDIDATES (b) (Seat F 32nd's, lines as of head `577f668f4786`); /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate192-ks1986-pr2004/verdict.md, finding G192-F3 (lines 38 to 44) and the D-B3 lines 74 and 76; the card, read with the `show` verb of /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/2_Project_Files/tools/decision_queue.sh on 2026-11-05.

title: originate verify: an original stored with an UPPER-case hex hash is invisible to the originals read, so the caller's own latecomer certification is presented (G193-F4, pre-existing)
description:
**BLUF:** In originate at develop `07a2d62be6a0`, the originals read compares `content_hash` by equality against three forms of the supplied hash (as supplied, bare, `sha256:` plus bare). A foreign original stored with an UPPER-case hex hash matches none of them when the verifying hash is lower-case, so it is not read as the original and the caller's own later certification is presented instead. Gate 193 measured it (G193-F4, NOTE, pre-existing: base = `577f668f4786` = head). Production upper-case counts are not measured.

Source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate193-ks1986-pr2004-r2/verdict.md, finding G193-F4 (lines 63 to 68), cells `G193-L686-HASH-UPPER` and `G193-L686-REGISTRY-PREFIXED-TENANT-UPPER`; /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate192-ks1986-pr2004/verdict.md, G192-F4 last bullet (line 56, read only, not driven).

## Where (read at develop `07a2d62be6a0`)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts`, `ORIGINAL_ROWS_POOL_SQL` lines 528 to 536: `d.content_hash = $1 OR d.content_hash = $2 OR d.content_hash = $3`, in the row filter and in the `MIN(e.created_at)` sub-select. `readCrossTenantOriginals` binds `[hash, hashNorm, 'sha256:' + hashNorm]` (line 605) and enumerates registry tenants with the same three-way equality (lines 608 to 612).
* The verifying hash is lower-case on `verify-file` (`digest('hex')`, lines 905 to 906). On `/verify` the local `normaliseHash` (line 1292) strips only a lower-case `sha256:` prefix and keeps the case as supplied.
* How an upper-case hash is stored: `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts` lines 577 to 582 test a lower-cased, unprefixed COPY of a client `contentHash`; line 679 stores `clientHash` as given and lines 794 to 798 register it as given. A comment at lines 375 to 376 (KS-596) says "mixed case both live in the DB today". This seat read these lines; it did not drive the create route.
* The other same-hash reads in `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts` (for example lines 921, 1393 to 1395 and 1473 to 1475) use the same three-form equality; read, not driven.

## What gate 193 measured (PostgreSQL 15)

* Setup: B is the original in tenant T2 with an upper-case `content_hash`, registered; A is a certified latecomer in the caller's tenant.
* Result: `cert-a-1` (the caller's latecomer) is presented on both v1 paths at base, at `577f668f4786` and at head, so PR 2004 does not change it.

title: api-gateway: after a Redis eviction GET /api/admin/settings and GET /api/verification/policy read only Redis and serve the defaults, so a settings round trip can replace the stored allow-lists
description:
**BLUF:** In api-gateway at develop `07a2d62be6a0`, `GET /api/admin/settings` reads the `platform-settings` key from Redis directly, not through the settings store. After an eviction it serves the four default categories with no `integrations` key, although the stored record still holds the configured settings. `PUT /api/admin/settings` does read the stored record on a miss and merges `{ ...defaults, ...existing, ...body }`, so a body key replaces the stored key whole. A client that saves what the GET showed, with `integrations: []`, replaces the stored allow-lists with an empty list. `GET /api/verification/policy` makes the same direct Redis read. This is Seat E 35th's candidate 1 for PR 2001 (its "item 7").

Source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-04_gate189-ks1256-pr2001/ready_2001.txt, CANDIDATES FOR FILING, item 1.

## Where (read at develop `07a2d62be6a0`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts`)

* Lines 1150 to 1159: `redisService.getNotificationSettings('platform-settings') || {}`, laid over `PLATFORM_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS`.
* Lines 1184 to 1197: the PUT reads through `readPlatformSettings` (stored record on a miss) and merges with `...body` last.
* Lines 1216 to 1228: `GET /api/verification/policy` reads Redis directly and answers the built-in defaults on a miss or a throw.
* The defaults object (`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/settingsStore.ts` lines 38 to 43) holds `general`, `security`, `notifications` and `blockchain`; no `integrations`.

## Measured

Not by gate 189: its findings G189-F1 to F7 do not include this. The READY mail lists it as a candidate. This seat read the code only.

KS-1256 already names the two direct readers: its comment `de80f9b8` (2026-10-06) lists them as "the other readers", and its comment `6d4b1366` (2026-11-04, Seat W 24th, read at `ee1e1b832115`, "read, not measured") restates them by function: `GET /api/admin/settings` "a missing key serves the defaults as if they were stored", and `GET /api/verification/policy` "a missing key, or a throw, answers the defaults", with the line "Left open: ... The other readers are listed above." That text predates PR 2001. What this ticket records is the state at `07a2d62be6a0`: both direct readers are unchanged, and PR 2001 changed `PUT /api/admin/settings` to read the stored record on a miss, which is what makes a round trip of the GET's content replace the stored allow-lists.

## Grade

Low, this seat's judgement. It needs an admin client that round-trips the whole document, and whether one exists is not measured.

## Not measured

* Any run of the GET after an eviction, or of the round trip.
* Whether any admin UI or script sends the whole document back, or sends `integrations`.

* This seat ran no test and no service; the code facts are reads of a depth-1 clone at `07a2d62be6a0`.

title: api-gateway: the deploy-time check for the platform-settings seed row cannot tell a fresh environment from one whose key was evicted before the first Redis hit (G189-F2, candidate 5)
description:
**BLUF:** In api-gateway at develop `07a2d62be6a0`, a configured environment whose Redis `platform-settings` key was evicted before the first Redis hit after a deploy reads the migration's SEED row (no restriction), and the step-3 check in PR 2001's deploy notes ("configured env reads `backfill`, fresh reads `seed`") shows the same rows as a fresh environment at every step, so it cannot tell the two apart. Gate 189 measured the three scenarios on real Redis and real PostgreSQL (G189-F2, LOW; it is Seat E 35th's candidate 5 as well). Not looser than develop, where a missing key already meant no restriction; it weakens the stated mitigation for candidate 5.

Source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-04_gate189-ks1256-pr2001/verdict.md, finding G189-F2 (lines 26 to 29), `runs/real2_head.jsonl` and `runs/real_head.jsonl` step 1 named there; /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-04_gate189-ks1256-pr2001/ready_2001.txt, CANDIDATES FOR FILING, item 5.

## Why one ticket for two items

The same three scenarios (fresh, configured with the key present, configured then evicted at deploy) prove candidate 5 and G189-F2 together, so one test pass covers both.

## Where (read at develop `07a2d62be6a0`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/settingsStore.ts`)

* Lines 24 to 27: the first Redis hit in a process copies the cached value over the row only while the row is still the SEED; "an eviction that lands before that first hit still reads the seed; the deploy step makes one read straight after the deploy".
* Lines 51 to 53: the backfill statement is `UPDATE ... SET settings = $2, origin = 'backfill' ... WHERE key = $1 AND origin = 'seed'`. Lines 91 to 99 and 122 to 124: `backfillSeedRow` runs on any plain-object Redis hit. Lines 131 to 138: a Redis miss with a readable row writes that row back to Redis.
* So on a fresh environment the first miss refills Redis with the seed, and the next hit runs the backfill over the seed row with the seed's own content; the row then reads `backfill`.

## What gate 189 measured (real Redis, real PostgreSQL, `GET /api/connector/info` wired as in the gateway's `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/index.ts`, two reads each)

* Fresh: `seed`, then `backfill`.
* Configured with the key present: `backfill` (restricted), then `backfill`.
* Configured, key evicted at deploy: `seed`, then `backfill`.
* The real sequence in `runs/real_head.jsonl` step 1 also ends at `backfill` after 5 reads on a fresh environment.
* The verdict notes that step 2 of the deploy notes (check the key before deploying) is the part that protects.

## Grade

Low, the verdict's grade.

## Not measured

* Whether any deployed environment (kintsugi, demo, production) had its key evicted at a deploy of PR 2001, or has been deployed with it.
* The wording of the PR's deploy notes beyond the lines the verdict quotes (this seat did not read the PR body).
* This seat ran no test and no service; the code facts are reads of a depth-1 clone at `07a2d62be6a0`.

title: api-gateway: a connector key with no connector id matches an integrations entry with no id, because the allow-list lookups compare ids with === and !== (undefined equals undefined)

title: Redis runs maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru in docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.production.yml, so the platform-settings key can be evicted under memory pressure
description:
**BLUF:** At develop `07a2d62be6a0`, both compose files start Redis with `--maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru`, which lets Redis evict any key, including the `platform-settings` key that holds the connector allow-lists, once memory reaches the limit. This is the condition KS-1256 was filed for. PR 2001 (merged as `6a36d41b9852`) makes a missing key readable from the stored record, so an eviction no longer reads as "no restriction"; the policy itself is unchanged. Seat E 35th listed it as candidate 4 and called it "a config change, not this one".

Source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-04_gate189-ks1256-pr2001/ready_2001.txt, CANDIDATES FOR FILING, item 4.

## Where (read at develop `07a2d62be6a0`)

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` lines 225 to 226: `--maxmemory 256mb` and `--maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.production.yml` lines 50 to 51: `--maxmemory 512mb` and `--maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts` lines 1177 to 1180 state the documented consequence before PR 2001: "the first save after an allkeys-lru eviction stored the defaults plus the body and the evicted allow-lists were gone for good".
* Readers of the key that do not go through the stored-record fallback: `GET /api/admin/settings` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts` line 1152) and `GET /api/verification/policy` (same file, line 1218) read Redis only.

## Measured

Seat W 24th reproduced the original defect on a disposable stack at `ee1e1b832115` by deleting the key with Redis up (KS-1256 comment `6d4b1366`, 2026-11-04). That deleted the key by hand. The same comment names this policy: "`docker-compose.yml:226` and `docker-compose.production.yml:51` set `--maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru`, and the stack reported `allkeys-lru`", and says the key is written with no TTL (the comment's reading of line 698 of `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/redis.ts`), which stops expiry, not eviction. That text predates PR 2001; this ticket records the policy at `07a2d62be6a0` (lines now 225 to 226 and 50 to 51). No eviction by memory pressure was driven by anyone this seat read.

## Grade

Low, this seat's judgement: PR 2001 changed what an eviction does to the connector readers.

## Not measured

* Redis memory use in any environment, and whether any environment has evicted this key by memory pressure.
* Whether the production compose file is what any deployed environment runs.
* This seat ran no test and no service; the facts are reads of a depth-1 clone at `07a2d62be6a0`.

## Related

title: originate seed-demo-users: the Oxford rights-holder block ends in an empty catch, so a failure there leaves no log line, no count and no response field (gate 195: 200 with success true)

title: workflow-approve: the forward to originate sends no x-tenant-id or x-tenant-slug, unlike the direct-create forward beside it
description:
## BLUF

* The workflow-approve forward (the final step of `POST /api/workflow-instances/:id/approve`) sends originate no `x-tenant-id` and no `x-tenant-slug`. The direct-create forward in the same file sends both (KS-39 item 4).
* **Latent today.** Originate refuses this forward with 401 before the tenant matters, because it carries no credential: KS-1087 item 2, held unbuilt by Kam's card `secuura-ks1087-workflow-approve-credential-1102` (option b, ruled 2026-11-02T12:44:48+11:00). The gap becomes live as soon as any credential option for KS-1087 item 2 is built: the document would then be refused with 400 under production multi-tenancy, or written into `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` elsewhere.
* READ from code at develop `5fc5569ed96a`. Nothing driven.

## Recommendation

* Forward the tenant with the approve forward, from a source decided together with KS-1087 item 2:
  * the creator's tenant: record `x-tenant-id` / `x-tenant-slug` on the pending document when the gateway holds it (`services/enforcement.ts:251-258` stores no tenant today);
  * or the approver's tenant, if KS-1087 picks the approver's credential.
* Regression cell: the recorded approve forward carries the tenant headers. A replay into originate, with a credential and the vouch, writes into that tenant and not into `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`.
* Build it with KS-1087 item 2, not before. It changes the same held forward.

## Detail

All paths are under `Blockchain/`, at develop `5fc5569ed96a`.

* `Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:571-579` — the approve forward's headers:
  * `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`;
  * `x-user-id`, from `pendingDoc.createdBy`;
  * the vouch from `vouchHeaderFor('originate')`.

  There is no `x-tenant-id`, no `x-tenant-slug` and no `Authorization`.
* Same file `:935-941` — the direct-create forward copies `x-tenant-id` and `x-tenant-slug` from the request. Its KS-39 item 4 comment gives the reason: without the header, originate writes to the fallback tenant and the new document 404s on the next read.
* `Dev/packages/shared/src/db/tenant-context.ts:60-75` — originate's `extractTenantContext`:
  * answers 400 "Missing tenant context" when `x-tenant-id` is absent and `NODE_ENV=production` (`:68-73`);
  * otherwise uses `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` (`:75`).
* `Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:254-275` — `extractTenantContext` is mounted only when `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`. In single-tenant mode, `getReqTenantId` falls back to the same default.
* `Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts:251-258` — the pending document stores the request body, `id`, `status`, `workflowInstanceId`, `createdBy` and `createdAt`. No tenant.

## Not measured

* Whether any environment has a workflow-gated document type (KS-1087's open reach question).
* `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` and `NODE_ENV` on any box.

## Board searched before filing

Team KS, archived included. Title, description and comments; literal, case-insensitive matches.

* `workflow-instances/:id/approve`: 3 hits (KS-1087, KS-1183, KS-1184). None is about the tenant header.
* Other terms: `x-tenant-slug` 7, `extractTenantContext` 12, `Missing tenant context` 2, `forwardHeaders` 2, the code comment's `KS-39` item-4 tag 4, `approve forward` 11, `pendingDoc` 5, `workflow-approve` 14, `x-tenant-id` 42.
* Nearest tickets, and why neither owns this:
  * **KS-1084** (the gateway's Authorization-only calls to originate send no `x-tenant-id`). Its body lists other call sites and places this forward out of scope. Its 2026-09-11 correction comment records that this forward sends no `x-tenant-id`, and sends the forward's own defect to KS-1087.
  * **KS-1083** (vouch-secret provisioning). It says in passing that this forward "has the same shape". Its fix, the vouch helper, is already on this forward (`verification.ts:579`, KS-955 P2a) and adds no tenant header.
* KS-1087 owns the credential, not the tenant.

Related: KS-1087, KS-1084, KS-1083, KS-1184. Filed by Seat T 11th on Wednesday's ruling (ANSWER 2026-11-05 05:36Z).

title: ks781 LEG F guard walk: indirect-invocation false negative — a guard inside a parser continuation passed by NAME reads guarded: false (under-reports)
description:
**BLUF:** The ks781 LEG F guard walk misses a guard that is invoked indirectly. In `routerParserAnalysis`, a continuation passed to the parser by name is not followed, so a guard that is genuinely mounted there reads `guarded: false`. This under-reports, which is the safe direction. KS-1143 recorded it on 2026-09-25 as a disclosed limit that was "out of scope by ruling"; it has no ticket of its own.

Carried from KS-1143, which recorded it as 'out of scope by ruling' with no ruler named (Wednesday 2026-11-05: no card or mail rules it; filed so it is tracked).

## The limit, in KS-1143's own words (emphasis markup removed)

KS-1143 comment of 2026-09-25 00:01Z:

> The indirect-invocation false negative, disclosed in #1212's own body and not fixed there. The tightened predicate recognises only a direct call through an identifier, so a guard that is genuinely mounted but invoked indirectly now reads as not mounted. This one errs in the opposite direction to GF-1 — it under-reports rather than over-reports.

KS-1143 comment of 2026-09-25 04:20Z:

> Disclosed limit, in the safe direction: a continuation passed by NAME (raw(req, res, afterParse)) is not a function expression, so a guard inside it reads false. That under-reports, and it is the indirect-invocation class kept out of this ticket's scope.

KS-1143 merge comment of 2026-09-25 15:35Z:

> The indirect-invocation false negative — still open, disclosed, out of scope by ruling.

KS-1143's own description covers GF-1, GF-2 and R-1 and does not describe this limit; its comments do.

## Why it is not KS-1316's

KS-1316's description (emphasis markup removed):

> KS-1143 stays In Progress for the indirect-invocation false negative, which is the opposite direction (under-reports: a continuation passed by NAME is not followed, so a genuinely mounted guard reads unguarded). This one over-reports.

## Where

The guard walk in `routerParserAnalysis`, in `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts`. KS-1143's comment of 2026-09-25 00:01Z gives the call-node predicate at line 2336 of that file after PR 1212 (squash `dd8f99cc75b9`); the line has moved since.

## Related

KS-1143 (carried from) and KS-1316 (the opposite direction: a guard defined but never called reads guarded, which over-reports).

## Open

Neither a named ruling that the limit is accepted nor a change that addresses it is recorded.

## Board search before filing

Literal match (title, description and comments of team KS, archived included) on 2026-11-05: `CONT-DEFERRED` 2 (KS-1143, KS-1316); `indirect-invocation` 2 (the same two); `invoked indirectly` 1 (KS-1143); `passed by NAME` 2 (the same two); `afterParse` 1 (KS-1143); `routerParserAnalysis`, `guardSyms`, `guardedWrappers` 1 each (KS-1143); `controlByteGuard` 3 (KS-815, KS-828, KS-1143); `indirect invocation` 0. title: originate certification routes log the database driver's message text, which can carry row values
description:
**BLUF:** In `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts`, six `logger.warn` lines and the issue handler's catch-all write an error's message text into the log. For a database error that text is the driver's own message, and a driver message can echo the offending value. Measured once, by gate AK1 on PR 1623: a 22P02 message of the form `invalid input syntax for type uuid: "<the value>"`. Filed as a class on Wednesday's ruling for KS-1666 (f): changing one of these lines closes nothing, so it is one ticket.

**The lines**, at develop `5fc5569ed96a` (file:line, then what is logged):

* `certifications.ts:379` `users/stub unreachable during certifications/issue`: `error: err?.message`
* `certifications.ts:418` `holderId validation DB error — rejecting`: `error: errMsg`, with the `holderId` beside it
* `certifications.ts:593-597` `KS-1633: the pre-anchor reservation failed…`: `error: reason` (the reservation write's message)
* `certifications.ts:649` `Anchoring service unreachable for certification`: `error: reason`
* `certifications.ts:710` `provenance record failed`: `error: provErr.message`
* `certifications.ts:880` `certification notification failed`: `error: err?.message`
* the catch-all, `certifications.ts:919-928`, `Failed to issue certification` at error level: `error: msg`, `name`, `code` and `stack`

By reading only, not measured line by line: 418, 593 and 710 sit on database calls; 379, 649 and 880 sit on HTTP calls, so their text is a network or service message rather than a driver message. Only the reservation warn (593) was ever seen carrying a driver message with a value in it.

**Response side, same file, noted not measured:** `certifications.ts:935` returns `msg` to the caller as `detail` on a foreign-key 400. The class of err.message in response bodies is KS-1410's (six services); I did not check whether this line is one of its 28.

**Evidence:** gate AK1, note N7 (PR 1623 round 2, 2026-10-19): the reservation warn carried `invalid input syntax for type uuid: "connector:platform-s:<guid>"`; develop's catch-all already logged the same message at error level. PR 1623's body had said "ids only" and was corrected before the merge.

**Decision already made on KS-1666 (f):** keep the text (Wednesday, 2026-11-05, inside commissioned work). This ticket is where the class is decided: keep and say so, redact to ids and SQLSTATE, or a shared logging helper.

**Not known:** whether log storage redacts anything downstream; any service other than originate's certification routes (the search below was on originate's certifications.ts only); whether the `stack` field adds anything beyond the message.

**Related:** KS-1666 (where this came from); KS-1410 (the same text in 500 response bodies, six services, In Progress); KS-1868 (unguarded reads of a thrown value, a different defect).

**Searched before filing** (Linear searchIssues, archived included): "invalid input syntax", "database driver message text", "driver message row values", "reserveErr", "error text can carry row values", "ids only warn line", "certifications.ts warn error message database", "log database error message PII certification routes". No ticket covers log lines that carry driver message text; the nearest are the three above.

title: Security (nit): the admin-scope reader's users-join tenant match is pinned by source text only, no behavioural cell (gate 214 N5, mutant MR5)
description:
## BLUF

PR 2030's reader, `getAdminOrganisationScope` in `Blockchain/Dev/services/security/src/adminScope.ts`, joins `users u ON u.id = s.user_id AND u.tenant_id = s.tenant_id`. The `u.tenant_id = s.tenant_id` match is pinned **only by a source-text cell** (P2 of the unit suite); no cell proves it by behaviour. Mutant MR5 (the join without that match) is equivalent **as deployed**, because compose runs the security service as `secuura_app` with NOBYPASSRLS and FORCE RLS on `users` and on the scope table. It is **not** equivalent on a connection that RLS does not bind. Raised by QA gate 214 (note N5); Wednesday ruled on 2026-11-06 (01:24:12Z) that it is filed as a ticket and not built in the follow-up PR. Facts only; nothing is built.

Gate verdict: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate214-ks1585-ks1377-pr2029-2031/verdict.md`.

## Measured by gate 214 (not by me)

The reader on a user whose `users` row is in tenant T2, with a scope row in tenant T (`runs/evidence/mr5.jsonl` in the gate folder):

| reader | as `secuura_app` | as the RLS-exempt superuser | `secuura_app` inside `runWithPlatformScope` |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| PR 2030's head | 0 rows | 0 rows | 0 rows |
| MR5 | 0 rows | 1 row | 0 rows |

The live control returned 1 row in all four arms. MR5 passes the ks1585, ks1570 and ks1584 files and all 142 integration cells at PR 2030's head. The whole unit suite kills it only through the text cell P2 (1 failed of 495), so the tenant match is pinned by source text and never by behaviour.

## Why it matters (read, not measured)

Wherever RLS does not bind the connection, the tenant match is what keeps another tenant's `users` row from satisfying the join. KS-1665 describes one way a deployed service lands on such a role: a missing `secuura-app-db-password` secret puts every runtime service on the admin/owner role.

## Not measured

* The role the deployed boxes' `DATABASE_URL` actually uses (no box read by the gate or by me).
* Whether the cell belongs in the unit suite (it would need a connection RLS does not bind) or only in the integration suite.

## What closing it would take (a cell, not a design)

An integration cell that runs the reader on a connection RLS does not bind (a superuser pool), with the user's `users` row in T2 and the scope row in T, expecting 0 rows: red on MR5, green on PR 2030's head. It needs a migrated PostgreSQL (the integration suite's private cluster). Not built.
