admin Settings: nine scalar fields under integrations share the key with the connector allow-list array, so they cannot be saved once a connector entry exists
description:
## BLUF

The admin Settings page edits nine named scalar fields under `integrations`, but the platform-settings `integrations` that the gateway reads for connector allow-lists is an ARRAY of connector entries. One key, two shapes. The portal fix on KS 1231 stops the page from corrupting the array: a save that edits one of the nine fields while `integrations` is an array is refused with a visible error naming the field (nothing stored, nothing dropped). That leaves the conflict in place: on an instance that holds any connector entry, those nine fields cannot be saved from the page.

## The nine fields

`frontend/admin/src/pages/Settings.tsx` at develop `2fd6d529573c`: `blockfrostApiKey` (line 424), `blockfrostNetwork` (433), `microsoftTenant` (453), `microsoftClientId` (461), `microsoftClientSecret` (470), `microsoftSSO` (479), `sharePointIntegration` (486), `kycProvider` (503), `kycApiKey` (514). Each is read with `getValue('integrations', '<name>', default)` and written with `handleFieldChange('integrations', '<name>', value)`.

## Evidence

* The gateway merges shallowly: `merged = { ...PLATFORM_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS, ...existing, ...body }` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts`, `PUT /api/admin/settings`), so a body category replaces the stored one whole.
* `PLATFORM_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS` has no `integrations` key (`services/api-gateway/src/services/settingsStore.ts`), so the container exists only once something stores it.
* The readers treat it as an array: `routes/verification.ts` (the create path, `ints` near line 834) and `services/health.ts` (the connector info reader, near line 78). The PUT validation added for KS 1230 checks `integrations[i].config.allowedDocumentTypes` only when `integrations` is an array.
* By name search over `services`, `frontend` and `packages` (tests and docs excluded), seven of the nine names appear in no file other than the Settings page: `blockfrostNetwork`, the four `microsoft*` fields, `sharePointIntegration` and `kycApiKey`. `blockfrostApiKey` matches names in `packages/shared/src/blockchain/event-indexer.ts` and `services/anchoring/src/cardano/threadTokenMint.ts`, and `kycProvider` in `packages/shared/src/vc/identity-credentials.ts`; I did not trace whether those read platform-settings. UNMEASURED.

## Decision needed (not made here)

Where the nine scalars live. Options raised while fixing KS 1231: keep the refusal (the state after that fix); store the scalars under their own category (a data-model change, and the gateway readers would need to know it); or remove the fields the platform does not read. Whether any of these is wanted is a later card.

## Searched first

Linear, titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, 2026-11-06: the nine field names, "shape conflict" and "scalar field" return 0 issues. "Settings.tsx" returns KS 1231, KS 1641 and KS 1744; the last two concern the m365 OAuth redirect target, not this.

title: originate still logs two email addresses after KS-1937: a share recipient's at INFO (certifications.ts:1385) and a demo-seed user's at ERROR (adminConfig.ts:2123)
description:
**BLUF:** Two log calls in `services/originate` still write an email address once the KS-1937 fix lands: `routes/certifications.ts:1385` (INFO, `recipientEmail: recipient.email`, written on every share) and `routes/adminConfig.ts:2123` (ERROR, `email: u.email`, written for each demo-seed user whose insert fails). They were found by the KS-1937 census and left out of that change by Wednesday's ruling, which asked for ONE ticket for both; the adminConfig line also waits for PR 2019, which edits the same file. Both are pre-existing and neither is a thrown-object leak. **Nothing here is a fix; no code change is proposed or made.**

## What is read (develop `7ad5a8b4bdf7`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src`)

* `routes/certifications.ts:1385`: `logger.info('Certification shared', { certificationId: id, recipientEmail: recipient.email, shareType: recipient.shareType });`. It sits in the share loop right after the share notification is sent, so the person a document is shared with has their address written on every share. That is a third party's address.
* `routes/adminConfig.ts:2123`: `try { logger.error('Demo user seed failed', { email: u.email, error: readableErrorMessage(err) }); } catch {...}`. `u` is an entry of the hard-coded demo-seed account list in the same route; each entry also carries an `id`. KS-913 (archived) records that a real person's email once sat in that list. Whether any address there is personal today is **not measured here**.

## The ruling it follows

Kam's card `secuura-ks1346-logging-thrown-objects-leaks-secrets` = a: "Log what kind of thing was thrown and the NAMES of its fields, never their values." Wednesday's ANSWER of 2026-11-06 on KS-1937 applied it to a recipient address: "A. Log the template only, never the address", for `utils/notificationClient.ts` and `services/email.ts`. This ticket carries the two remaining lines of the same class. Related: KS-1937 (originate's client and email service), KS-1964 (the same pattern in the auth service's `email.ts`).

## How these two were found (the census)

A balanced-parenthesis scan of every log call in `services/originate/src`, tests excluded: 60 files, 303 calls, 12 flagged. Ten are in `notificationClient.ts` (3) and `services/email.ts` (7), covered by the KS-1937 change; these two are the rest. Controls: the 3 known client lines, and the 7 `email.ts` lines that a plain grep found independently (the scanner's first version missed those 7 because it blanked template-literal text, interpolations included; fixed, and both controls now pass). **Limits:** it flags the identifiers `to`, `toEmail`, `email`, `emails`, `recipient*` and `address*` inside a log call's arguments. It does not follow a value held under another name, and it does not read error text that a library forwards, so an SMTP or notification-service error that echoes an address is **not** covered.

## Board search (so nobody files this twice)

Run 2026-11-06 over this team's titles, descriptions and comment bodies, archived included: `Certification shared` 0; `recipient.email` 0; `logs the recipient` 0; `email in the log` 0; `u.email` 2 (KS-1802 and KS-1817, both about how the thrown value is read in that catch, not the address); `Demo user seed failed` 6 (KS-1802, KS-1817, KS-1818, KS-1990, KS-2004, KS-960, all seed-demo-users catches or counts, read by title; none is about the address). Positive control: `notificationClient` returns KS-1937 and KS-1964.

## What is not known, and what would settle it

1. Whether either log reaches a persisted destination, and for how long. Settled by reading the deployment's log configuration.
2. Whether any address in the demo-seed list is a real person's today (KS-913).
3. The shape of the fix is not decided here. KS-1937's shape is the model: log the identifiers, not the address. For the share line `certificationId` and `shareType` already identify the event; for the seed line the entry's `id` identifies the failing row.

## Priority

Medium, as KS-1937 and KS-1964 read on the board.

title: m365: GET /api/onedrive/files interpolates a raw folderId into the Graph path with no type check or encoding
description:
**BLUF:** `GET /api/onedrive/files` in m365-integration builds its Microsoft Graph path from the raw `folderId` query parameter, with no type check and no encoding. No ticket owned this: it sat as an "Also" section inside KS-1673, and KS-1673's PRs do not touch the line. No exploit is measured or claimed.

## Source

KS-1673's description, section "Also from AP1 N5 (same route)", verbatim:

> `GET /api/onedrive/files` interpolates a raw `folderId` into the Graph path (`:1090`: `/me/drive/items/${folderId}/children`), with no type check and no encoding. The handler's `try` → `next` means this cannot crash the process. Path text is passed to [graph.microsoft.com](<http://graph.microsoft.com>) under the connection's token.

## The code, read now

`Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` at develop `2fd6d529573c`, read with `git show`:

* line 1159: `const { connectionId, folderId } = req.query;`
* line 1166: `` const path = folderId ? `/me/drive/items/${folderId}/children` : '/me/drive/root/children'; ``
* the next statement fetches `https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0${path}` with the connection's access token.

KS-1673's ownership check (`ownedMemConnection`) runs before this, so the caller reaches it only with a connection of its own.

Controls on the read: the literal `me/drive/items` is on 3 lines of that file and a nonce on 0. `git blame` dates line 1166 to commit `ccf8961d3651e` (2026-03-26). PRs 1633, 1637 and 1640, the ones attached to KS-1673, change 0 lines carrying `folderId`; the same read shows PR 1633's squash `9207fe336797` is the commit that added the `ownedMemConnection` call in this handler, so the read does see that PR.

## Not measured

* Reachability on any box. No request was sent to any service for this ticket.
* How Graph treats `/`, `../`, `?` or `#` in that path segment.
* What a non-string `folderId` does here (an array form from `req.query`).
* Whether any connection exists on a box today.

## Searched before filing, 2026-11-06

Board search over titles, descriptions and comments, archived included:

* `folderId`: 1 hit, KS-1673.
* `/me/drive/items`: 1 hit, KS-1673.
* `onedrive/files`: 7 open and 6 closed hits. KS-1673 is one. The other 12 name the route in spec, Schemathesis or 503-coverage work: KS-256, KS-591, KS-665, KS-693, KS-716, KS-1364, KS-210, KS-268, KS-423, KS-466, KS-475, KS-499. None of them carries `folderId` or `/me/drive/items`, as the two lines above show.

Controls on the same instrument: `mobile/secuura-app` hit KS-1981 and a random token hit 0.

## Done when

* A red-first cell plants a `folderId` containing `/`, `?` and `..`, and asserts the Graph path is built from an encoded or refused value. It fails on today's code.

title: A bare database serves rights_holders with no RLS and no tenant_id until boot 2: migrations 026 to 028 run before the CORE stage that creates it
description:
## BLUF

On a **bare** database (one where the `docker/init` scripts did not run), the gateway's own migration runner leaves `rights_holders` with **no row-level security, no** `tenant_id` **column and no policy** after boot 1. The table is isolated only after boot 2. Measured at develop `4ccdc3b3e7cf`: as the non-superuser, NOBYPASSRLS app role `secuura_app`, a witness row owned by tenant A was visible with no tenant set and to tenant B after boot 1 (1 / 1), and invisible to tenant B after boot 2 (0) with a positive control (tenant A reads 1). The window is the gap between boot 1 and boot 2. **Medium:** it heals on boot 2, the table is empty on a fresh database, and the window exists only where the compose init scripts did not run.

## What was run (MEASURED, 2026-11-06, Seat C 35th)

* develop `4ccdc3b3e7cf`, fetched by sha; bare databases; a throw-away PostgreSQL 15.19 (Homebrew) on a unix socket only (0 inet sockets by `lsof`, with a positive control that sees 1); the product's own `runStartupMigrations` via tsx (pg 8.23.0 and tsx 4.23.15, the gateway lock's versions); `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` unset.
* Reads as `secuura_app` (`rolsuper` f, `rolbypassrls` f). One transaction per read: witness rows inserted as the owner, counted as `secuura_app`, rolled back (0 left behind, read back). The non-RLS tracker table read 54 after boot 1 and 59 after boot 2 as the control, and the owner saw its witnesses.

| `rights_holders` as `secuura_app` | no tenant set | another tenant | the row's own tenant |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| after boot 1 (RLS off, no `tenant_id`, 0 policies) | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| after boot 2 (RLS on, `tenant_id`, 1 policy) | 0 | 0 | 1 |

After boot 2 the policy `rights_holders_tenant_isolation` keys on `app.tenant_id`, not on `app.current_tenant_id` like the 038/039 set; originate sets it (`services/originate/src/db.ts:337` and `:358`). The boot-2 row is read with that setting.

## Cause

Migrations `026` (add `tenant_id`), `027` (enable RLS and the policy) and `028` (set NOT NULL) fail on boot 1 with `relation "rights_holders" does not exist`. No file migration creates the table. The CORE stage does (`startup-migrations.ts:317`), and it runs after the file stage. A failed file is not recorded, so boot 2 applies all three. Gateway summary: boot 1 `applied 103, failed 5`; boot 2 `applied 53, failed 0`; tracker rows 54 then 59. The five that fail on boot 1 are `006`, `008`, `026`, `027`, `028`; `006` and `008` fail on the same ordering (`svc_webhooks`) and were not assessed here. The KS 1054 fix (migration `038a`) creates the four tables `039` needs before `039` runs, and leaves this table to the CORE stage.

## The window, stated narrowly

* It exists where `docker/init/07-rights-holders.sql` did not run. READ, not run: compose mounts `./docker/init` into Postgres's init directory (`docker-compose.yml:159`), and that file creates `rights_holders` at database init, before any migration. A compose-initialised database should not show the window.
* **No row was written across a real boot gap** by this work. The only rows written were witness rows inside transactions that were rolled back. Whether any real row ever sat in `rights_holders` unprotected is not known.
* Whether any deployed database (Kintsugi, demo, production, a DR restore, CI) was created without those init scripts is **UNMEASURED**. A box read is outside this ticket's filer.
* The module header of `startup-migrations.ts` says the gateway keeps serving after a failed migration (READ), so a stack can take requests between boot 1 and boot 2. Not observed live.

## Also measured, so it is not measured again

* `scripts/run-migrations.sh` alone on a bare database never creates the table: `026` to `028` fail on every boot and the script exits 3 each time (head boot 1 `applied=55 failed=5`; boot 2 `applied=2 failed=3 skipped=55`). Nothing is exposed on that path, because the table is absent.
* Control: at the pre-fix merge-base `0d156d12` the gateway runner leaves `users.tenant_isolation` in the FAIL-OPEN form after boot 1 (a witness row is visible with no tenant set: 1) and fail-closed after boot 2, so the harness shows both states. KS 1054's own defect does not reproduce at the head; the comment on that ticket has the full matrix.
* Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatC-35th/evidence/` (`head_gw_boot1_*`, `head_gw_boot2_*`, `ks1054_matrix.md`).

## Not decided here

Which fix shape is right (for example creating the table in a file migration numbered before `026`, as `038a` did for the `039` tables) is a design choice. Nothing was built.

## Searched before filing

Linear, includeArchived, title and description: `rights_holders` 5 hits (KS 108, KS 109, KS 159, KS 236, KS 2004), `rights holders` 1 (KS 37), `026_rights` 0, `027_rights` 0, `028_rights` 0, `before CORE` 0, `file stage` 3 (KS 1054, KS 1055, KS 1885), `CORE stage` 1 (KS 1054). Read in full: KS 108 (the original RLS fix; no mention of a boot-ordering window), KS 1055 (per-tenant databases; does not mention this table) and KS 1054 (lists `026` to `028` among seven failing files; does not discuss this table).

Related: KS 1054 (open), KS 108 (where migrations `026` to `028` come from).

Found by Seat C 35th during the KS 1054 sweep. Filed on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-11-06.

title: OpenAPI: connectorId is declared on ApiKeyCreateRequest but not on ApiKey or ApiKeyCreateResponse, which now return it
description:
**BLUF:** The published OpenAPI schemas `ApiKey` and `ApiKeyCreateResponse` do not declare `connectorId`, although `POST /api/keys` (the 201 body) and `GET /api/keys` (each list row) return it since PR 1319 (KS-908). An integrator reading the spec cannot learn the field exists. Spec only, Low. Evidence class: READ ONLY (parsed from the file at one commit; nothing was run).

**Where (origin develop** `82d9ef03d795`**, read 2026-11-06 with git show on a fresh scratch fetch):**

* `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`: `ApiKeyCreateRequest` starts at line 9274 and names `connectorId` 3 times (lines 9274 to 9316); `ApiKeyCreateResponse` starts at 9317 and names it 0 times (lines 9317 to 9370); `ApiKey` starts at 9371 and names it 0 times (lines 9371 to 9422, where `ApiKeyListResponse` begins at 9423). The request side is the positive control: the same count over it reads 3, so the count can see the word.
* The code that returns the field: `Blockchain/Dev/services/security/src/index.ts` line 1539 (the 201 body of POST /api/keys) and line 1613 (each row of GET /api/keys).

**Why a ticket and not a note:** KS-908 closes on its read-back scope, which PR 1319 delivered. KS-908's merge comment already names "declaring it is a separate follow-up" and says the response schemas are `.passthrough()`, so the field is tolerated but undocumented. A comment left on KS-908 would go into the archive with it, and nothing else on the board tracks the response side.

**Not covered:** whether the spec generator can emit the field (PR 1319 measured that no spec change was needed for `check:openapi` to pass; it did not try declaring one); the published list body `{keys}` against the handler's `{success,data}` (that drift is KS-1514, a different defect); the Platform S side of the contract.

**Source:** gate 215 (round 1, 2026-11-06), finding F6, re-read at the lines above by Seat S 26th.

**Board search before filing (2026-11-06, Seat S 26th, board_search tool, controls held: a term unique to KS-1379 hit KS-1379 among open tickets, a random token hit 0):** `ApiKeyCreateResponse` returned 1 candidate and 0 literal hits; `connectorId+openapi` returned 36 candidates, open literal hits KS-485, KS-577, KS-772, KS-908, KS-1579 and KS-1696, closed hit KS-1434. KS-1434 (Done) is about the `rotate` field on `ApiKeyCreateRequest`; its text shows the request schema already names `connectorId`. No ticket tracks the response schemas.

title: security: an empty-string connectorId is stored as '' but the key API answers null, so the response and the row disagree
description:
**BLUF:** A key minted with `connectorId: ''` is written to the database as `''`, but the 201 body and the list row answer `null`. For this one value the symptom KS-908 fixed survives: the API says null while the row holds a value. Low. Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME at handler level for the response (in-memory, mocked store); READ ONLY for the store (no real database was run).

**Where**, at origin develop `82d9ef03d795` (read 2026-11-06): `Blockchain/Dev/services/security/src/index.ts` line 476 passes `k.connectorId ?? null` to the INSERT, and `??` keeps `''`. Lines 1539 and 1613 answer `apiKey.connectorId || null` and `k.connectorId || null`, and `||` turns `''` into null.

**Measured by gate 215 (round 1, 2026-11-06), handler level:** mint with `connectorId: ''` answered 201 with `connectorId: null`, and the list row read null (probe output in that gate's runs folder, `runs/probe_ks908.txt`). PR 1319's own merge comment on KS-908 disclosed it as polish: an empty-string connectorId reads back as null, so "" and absent are indistinguishable to a caller.

**NOT measured:** a real PostgreSQL write of `''`; whether any reader treats `''` as a connector; what the COALESCE upsert at line 472 does on a later save of the same key.

**Adjacent ticket, not a duplicate:** KS-1525 (In Progress) records the other half of the same question for the read mapper: `connector_id: ''` reaches callers as `''`, and it leaves "should an empty-string id normalise to absent?" unsettled as a product question. This ticket is the write path and the response echo; the answer on that question settles the fix here.

**Fix shape:** decide first whether `''` is a connector or none; then either refuse `''` at the mint or store null, and make the echo and the mapper agree.

**Board search before filing (2026-11-06, Seat S 26th, board_search tool, controls held):** `connectorId+empty` returned 36 candidates (open literal hits include KS-908 and KS-1525); `dbSaveApiKey` returned 11 candidates (open literal hits KS-577, KS-1370, KS-1377, KS-1569, KS-1732, KS-1868; none about an empty string). No ticket says the store writes `''` while the API answers null.

title: wallet-connector: session DELETE updates the table before it checks the session exists, and a session records no owner
description:
**BLUF:** In the wallet-connector, `DELETE /api/wallets/session/:sessionId` runs its database UPDATE before it checks that the session exists, so a session id this process does not hold in memory is set disconnected in the table and then answered 404. And the service records no owner for a session, so nothing ties it to the user or tenant who created it: any signed-in caller who holds a session id can disconnect it. A third item found while checking this: `svc_wallet_sessions` is defined twice with different columns. Low. Evidence class: READ ONLY throughout, as gate 215 labelled the first two. Nothing was run and none of this is a measurement.

**Where**, at origin develop `82d9ef03d795` (read 2026-11-06 with git show on a fresh scratch fetch):

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/wallet-connector/src/server.ts`, the handler at lines 201 to 226. It looks the session up in memory (line 205), and only if found marks it disconnected and saves it (lines 206 to 210). It then runs `UPDATE svc_wallet_sessions SET connected = false WHERE id = $1` on the id from the URL (line 215, when the database is available), and only after that tests `if (!session)` and answers 404 (lines 221 to 223). A found session is answered 200 with `success: true` (line 225).
* No owner is recorded: the service's own save (lines 62 to 64) writes `id`, `wallet_type`, `address`, `connected` and `connected_at` and nothing about a user or tenant, and the DELETE handler never reads the caller.
* Two definitions of the same table. `Blockchain/Dev/migrations/002_verification-tiers.sql` creates it with `id`, `wallet_type`, `address`, `connected`, `connected_at`, `disconnected_at` (no user column), which is the shape the service's SQL uses. `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts` line 416 also runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for it, with `id`, `user_id TEXT NOT NULL`, `wallet_address`, `wallet_type`, `chain`, `status`, `metadata`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and none of `address`, `connected`, `connected_at`. Both are IF NOT EXISTS, so whichever runs first on a database wins, and the other becomes a no-op. The service's INSERT and UPDATE name columns that exist only in the first.

**Why it matters:** the first point means a 404 does not mean nothing changed. The second means a session cannot be tied to who may end it. The third means that on a database where the gateway's definition won, the service's table writes would fail (errors the code catches and logs at lines 66 and 216), leaving the in-memory map as the only record; on a database where the migration's definition won, the table carries no owner. Which holds on Kintsugi or demo is not known. The gateway answers 401 to an unauthenticated DELETE (recorded on KS-1360 on 2026-11-04), so the open question is the signed-in caller who is not the session's owner.

**Neither the first nor the second comes from PR 1345** (KS-1360), which only added `success: true` to the 200 body.

**NOT measured:** any request to this route; which table definition a given database actually has (no database was read); whether the gateway or the browser flow ever lets one user learn another's session id; whether other routes read the table or only the in-memory map; the GET-by-id sibling route (not examined here).

**Fix shape:** check the session first and update the table only for a session the caller owns; record the owner (user and tenant) when the session is created and bind the UPDATE to it; keep one definition of the table and make the service's SQL match it.

**Source:** gate 215 (round 1, 2026-11-06), "curio, unreplicated", re-read by Seat S 26th at the lines above. The second definition is Seat S 26th's own finding, from reading the api-gateway source; it is not in the gate's verdict, and gate 215's "no owner column" holds only for the first definition.

**Board search before filing (2026-11-06, Seat S 26th, board_search tool, controls held):** `svc_wallet_sessions` returned 100 candidates and 0 literal hits (open or closed); `Session disconnected` returned 100 candidates and 1 open literal hit, KS-1360 itself (its title and the 200 body, not this ordering, the missing owner or the second definition). No ticket says the DELETE updates before it checks the session, that wallet sessions have no owner, or that the table is defined twice.

title: transfer: a valid string signature on POST /api/transfers/:id/reject is accepted and then discarded, never stored or verified
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/transfers/:id/reject` validates an optional string `signature` and then throws it away: the stored rejection has no such field, so a caller who sends a real signature gets 200 and a rejection recorded without it. PR 1408 (KS-1435) made a wrong-typed signature a 400; it did not decide what a valid one is for. Low. Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME at handler level against a mocked database (gate 215, round 1, twice) for the drop; READ ONLY for the lines re-read by Seat S 26th.

**Where**, at origin develop `82d9ef03d795` (read 2026-11-06 with git show on a fresh scratch fetch):

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts`: `rejectTransferSchema` (lines 415 to 423) declares `signature: z.string().optional()` at line 422. The rejection record is built at lines 761 to 767 from `id`, `rejectorId`, `rejectorRole`, `reason` and `rejectedAt` only. `interface TransferRejection` (lines 125 to 131) has no signature field. Approve, by contrast, stores it (`signature: data.signature`, line 695).
* `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` lines 11452 to 11454: the published `TransferRejectRequest` describes the field as "Wallet signature, when the rejection flow requires CIP-8 sign-off".

**Measured by gate 215:** reject with `signature: 'GATE215SIG'` answered 200, and the string appeared in neither the reply, the read-back nor the mock table; measured twice (probe output in that gate's runs folder, `runs/probes2.txt`). The cell in PR 1408 that sends a string signature (TRC1) passes regardless, because it asserts only the status.

**Why its own ticket:** KS-1435's description ends with a "Not checked" line asking whether the signature is consumed later in the reject path ("if it is, the dropped value is also a functional bug"). This is the answer: it is not consumed. PR 1408's body names the harm of an undeclared field ("recorded without the signature it believed it had sent") and that harm remains for valid input. It is outside KS-1435's asked fix, so KS-1435 closes with this ticket cited.

**For the owner to decide:** store the signature, verify it (CIP-8), or drop it from the published request.

**NOT measured:** a real database; a gateway path; whether anything downstream expects a signature on a rejection; the `execute` and `cancel` routes. The caller-check defect on these same two routes (approve and reject) is a different ticket, KS-2038; this is not it.

**Source:** gate 215 (round 1, 2026-11-06), finding F5, re-read by Seat S 26th at the lines above.

**Board search before filing (2026-11-06, Seat S 26th, board_search tool, controls held):** `TransferRejection` returned 0 candidates; `rejectorId` returned 3 candidates, open literal hits KS-1435 and KS-2038, closed hit KS-466. KS-1435 only asks the question in its "Not checked" line; KS-2038 names the signature only to say its own defect is a different one. No ticket says a valid signature on reject is discarded.

title: Schemathesis baseline: two accepted rows describe fixed defects, and the gate does not notice when their tickets close
description:
**BLUF:** The Schemathesis baseline carries two accepted rows whose reasons describe defects that PR 1343 (KS-1371) and PR 1408 (KS-1435) fixed. Both rows expire 2026-12-31. The baseline gate checks that a row has a reason, a ticket and an expiry and nothing about the ticket's state, so closing KS-1371 and KS-1435 raises nothing, and a regression of either defect would be accepted silently until the expiry. Low. Evidence class: READ ONLY (the rows and the gate source read at one commit; the gate was not run).

**Where**, at origin develop `82d9ef03d795` (read 2026-11-06 with git show on a fresh scratch fetch):

* `systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis-baseline.json` line 488, `by_design_input_tolerance_guard::POST /api/status/{id}/unrevoke`, ticket KS-1371. Its reason says unrevoke accepts index -1 with 200. Since PR 1343 the handler refuses it with 400, and PR 1343's cells U1 and U2 pin that (gate 215's mutant with the bound removed turned exactly those two red).
* The same file, line 683, `negative_data_rejection::POST /api/transfers/{id}/reject`, ticket KS-1435. Its reason says a wrong-typed signature is accepted with 200 because the reject schema omits the field, and cites `services/transfer/src/index.ts:408-412`. Since PR 1408 the schema declares it (`Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts` line 422) and cells TR1 and TR2 pin the 400.
* `systemTest/schemathesis/scripts/runner/baseline_gate.py` lines 285 and 289 test for the fields `reason`, `ticket` and `expires` (a missing field is malformed, a past date is expired). The file has 0 occurrences of closed, done, completed, canceled or linear. Control: the same count for `expires` is 6 lines.
* A third row names the reject operation: line 418, `positive_data_acceptance::POST /api/transfers/{id}/reject`, ticket KS-591, a different check. Not examined here.

**Relation to other tickets:** KS-1015 (In Progress) already proposes, as an option in its fix direction, that the gate validate that an entry's ticket is still open ("so closure orphans an entry as loudly as expiry does"), and it lists ten rows whose tickets were Done on 2026-09-08. That structural check stays on KS-1015. This ticket is the two concrete rows whose tickets are closing on 2026-11-06. KS-1511 (In Progress) retires a different row, the audit-log pair; its quoted line number for that row is older than this read.

**Order of work:** retire or re-reason both rows only after a sweep has read them, as KS-1511 asks for its row. Gate 215 notes that a harness false firing is not excluded for unrevoke: a case with two negative components that is still valid on the wire would fail `request_valid_as_sent` at the tip (READ ONLY there). Removing the row could expose that instead of a platform defect. Not run here: the gate, and any sweep.

**Source:** gate 215 (round 1, 2026-11-06), finding F4, re-read by Seat S 26th at the lines above.

**Board search before filing (2026-11-06, Seat S 26th, board_search tool, controls held):** `schemathesis-baseline` returned 92 candidates (14 open literal hits, none about the state of these two rows); `baseline_gate` returned 85 candidates (1 open literal hit, KS-1015). No ticket asks to retire these two rows.

title: Postgres outage behind pgbouncer kills auth, anchoring, api-gateway and tenant-provisioning on an unhandled pg client error
description:
**BLUF:** On a disposable stack, stopping Postgres with pgbouncer still up crash-looped auth and anchoring and restarted api-gateway and tenant-provisioning once each, on an unhandled pg client error. Callers saw 504 then 502, not the designed 503. With pgbouncer stopped too, auth stayed up and answered 503. Anchoring answered 202 nine times during the outage and those anchors have no row after recovery. Nothing here is fixed.

Found by Seat U 16th, 2026-11-06, running KS-1477's owed check, on throw-away stack `u16` built from develop `2fd6d529573c`, `NODE_ENV=development`, compose's own pgbouncer and Postgres, mock anchoring. Not on a box.

## Measured: run 1, requests through nginx and the gateway to auth

Postgres stopped 02:53:43Z, started 02:56:09Z, pgbouncer left running.

* auth: 9 restarts in about 2 minutes, crashing 1 to 2 s after each boot until Postgres came back; 18 `Unhandled 'error' event` lines in its log.
* api-gateway: `Uncaught exception` with `Connection terminated unexpectedly`, then shutdown and restart, once, at 02:55:28Z.
* What callers saw for `POST /api/users/me/verification`: 504 `GATEWAY_TIMEOUT` after 60 s, then 502 `BAD_GATEWAY`. Never the 503.

## Measured: run 2, requests in flight directly to four services

Postgres stopped 03:07:23Z for about 100 s, pgbouncer left running. A short-lived prober on the stack's internal network sent one request to each service every 4 s, bypassing the gateway. The baseline with the database up answered 201, 202, 200 and 200.

| service | restarts | in its log | what the prober saw (25 requests) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| anchoring | **10** | `Unhandled 'error' event` 10, `Connection terminated unexpectedly` 10 | 202 on 9; connection, DNS or socket errors on 16 |
| tenant-provisioning | **1** | `Unhandled 'error' event` 1, `terminating connection due to administrator command` | 500 on 23; connection refused on 2 |
| originate | 0 | none of these | 500 on 25, `Code: 08P01`, `server login has been failing` |
| security | 0 | none of these | 503 on 25 |

* auth and api-gateway had nothing in flight to them in run 2 and did not restart.
* **Anchoring's 202s:** read at 03:10Z, after recovery, `anchor_store` holds 0 rows created after the stop; its newest row is 03:07:22Z, from the baseline, and the 2 baseline rows are there as the control. Its log says `Database unavailable — using in-memory fallback` 9 times. So 9 anchors were accepted with 202 and have no row. Whether that is this defect or its own is not decided here.
* Every service read healthy again within about a minute of Postgres returning.

## Discriminating control

With pgbouncer **and** Postgres stopped, so no established connection can be cut: auth logged 0 crashes and stayed up, including when restarted during the outage (the in-memory fallback line once), and answered 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` every time. Only auth was driven in this arm.

## The stack, verbatim, from auth

```
throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
Error: Connection terminated unexpectedly
    at Connection.<anonymous> (/app/node_modules/pg/lib/client.js:204:73)
Emitted 'error' event on Client instance at:
    at Client._handleErrorEvent (/app/node_modules/pg/lib/client.js:422:10)
```

It holds no application frames.

## A reading, not measured

* It reads as a pg client checked out of a pool when pgbouncer cuts its connection ("server login has been failing"). The pool-level `on('error')` handlers would not cover a checked-out client.
* auth and the gateway died with a request in flight to them in run 1 and did not in run 2. That suggests in-flight work is the trigger; two runs do not establish it.

## UNMEASURED

* The call site in each service.
* Kintsugi and demo. Compose has the same pgbouncer; nothing was tried on a box.
* `NODE_ENV=production`.

title: anchoring answers 202 during a database outage and the anchor has no row after recovery
description:
**BLUF:** In a Postgres outage on a disposable stack, anchoring answered 202 to 9 of 25 `POST /api/anchors` requests, and after recovery `anchor_store` held no row created after the stop. A 202 tells the caller its anchor was accepted. Split out of KS-2045 on Wednesday's ruling, because a crash loop and a 202 with no stored row are separate fixes. Nothing here is fixed.

## Measured

Seat U 16th, 2026-11-06, on throw-away stack `u16` built from develop `2fd6d529573c`, `NODE_ENV=development`, mock anchoring with no wallet. Not on a box. Postgres stopped 03:07:23Z for about 100 s, pgbouncer left running. A prober on the stack's internal network sent one `POST /api/anchors` every 4 s directly to anchoring, with a connector JWT minted on that stack.

* **9 of 25 answered 202.** The other 16 got connection, DNS or socket errors while the process was restarting (KS-2045).
* `anchor_store` **read at 03:11:30Z, about 2 minutes after Postgres was healthy: 0 rows created after the stop.** The newest row is 03:07:22.643Z. The 2 rows created just before the stop are there as the control, and the table holds 15 in all.
* **Anchoring's log in the outage:** `Database unavailable — using in-memory fallback` 9 times, `Anchor created` 9 times (2 more before the stop). The counts match the 9 responses; the prober kept statuses and not ids, so they were not matched one to one.
* **Each of those 9** `Anchor created` **lines is followed by the process crash in KS-2045 within 1 to 4 ms** (03:07:27.904Z to 03:08:42.469Z), so in this run no process that wrote one lived on. The row read is after the last restart.

## Read at source, not run

`Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts` at `2fd6d529573c`, in `dbPersistAnchor`:

* lines 1551 to 1552, a comment: "a failed persist must propagate so the handler returns a 5xx rather than a false 202".
* line 1553: `if (!isDbAvailable()) return { id: anchor.id, payloadTimestamp: payloadTimestampOf(anchor.metadataPayload) };`, which returns with no write.
* line 538: the handler calls it and carries on.

## UNMEASURED

* Whether anything later replays those anchors. The read came about 3 minutes after the last 202, and the stack was torn down at 03:13Z. That is why this ticket says "no row after recovery" and not "lost".
* How long an in-memory copy lives in a process that does not crash. Here each process crashed within 4 ms, so KS-2045 may be hiding what this path does on its own.
* Whether anything reaches a chain. This stack has no wallet, so nothing could from here; on a box, not measured.
* Kintsugi and demo, and `NODE_ENV=production`.
* The 202 bodies, and what a caller does on one. The prober kept statuses only.

title: Pre-push cost: leg 14's 116 shell suites run one after another and are 90 to 92 percent of every push, and no other leg is timed
description:
BLUF: Every push that changes Blockchain/Dev runs all 16 preflight legs inside the push lock. Leg 14, the 116 shell suites, is 90 to 92 percent of it (948 of 1033 s, 990 of 1096 s, 1102 of 1213 s on three pushes read on 2026-11-06), they run strictly one after another, and no other leg is timed, so the other 85 to 111 s of each push is unattributed. At 03:26Z the push queue held 19 live tickets; at about 19 minutes a push that is several hours before the last of them reaches a gate.

One test pass, three items:

1. Per-leg timing. Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh prints one line per leg for all 16 legs at the verdict, in leg order, each marked ran or skipped, with its seconds and a line stating the ratio of legs timed (16/16). The existing PREFLIGHT PASSED and PREFLIGHT FAILED lines, the legs ran count, the exit codes, the skip accounting and the shell suites wall-clock line stay byte-for-byte what they are. A failed run still prints the table.
2. Parallel suites, conditional on a measurement. First measure on this host whether the 116 suites collide when run side by side (fixed ports, shared postgres sockets, fixed names under /tmp) and what the saving is at several worker caps. Only if a safe set exists, Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-shell-suites.sh runs it in parallel under a worker cap with buffered output printed in suite order. Every suite still runs. The pass, fail and skip rule, the empty-run refusal, the git environment clearing, the short TMPDIR substitution and --list and --check-unreached stay as they are; a worker cap of 1 reproduces today's serial output. New assertion: passed plus failed plus skipped must equal the suites reached. INT and TERM stop every running worker. bash 3.2 only. If the saving is small beside the added risk, item 2 is not raised and the numbers go on this ticket.
3. The push rehearsal runs leg 1 under the driver's own TMPDIR, so a hook-only failure like Seat V 24th's (a 121-byte tsx socket path against macOS's 104, lock held 18.6 minutes) shows in a rehearsal. This is a corrected tool copy in the seat's record folder, not part of the PR.

Not in scope: running the preflight outside the lock or pushing with --no-verify (Kam's card secuura-push-queue-prerun-preflight-1106, option a, is open; this work is its default, option b). This work reaches only branches cut after it merges, because the hook and the runner run from each pushing worktree's own tracked copy.

Source: Wednesday's push-queue cost report, 0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_push-queue-cost/report.md (section 1 table and the UNMEASURED list).

Board search before filing (title and description, archived included, Secuura-PK): shell suites wall-clock 0 hits; per-leg timing 0; step() timing 0; worker cap 0; TMPDIR with rehears 0. Positive controls: run-shell-suites 28 hits, push queue 2 hits. Negative control, a nonsense symbol, 0 hits.

title: auth oauth router POST /authorize: a non-string action is taken as approve, and an array client_id passes the charset check
description:
**BLUF:** On the auth service's oauth router, `POST /authorize` compares `action` with the string 'deny' by strict equality, so an array or object `action` never matches and the request takes the approve path; and a one-element array `client_id` passes the client_id charset regex by coercion and reaches `getAppByClientId` as an array. Medium. Priority as ruled by Wednesday (ANSWER 2026-11-06T03:40:16Z). Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME by gate 212 for the route (handler level, doubled lookups); READ ONLY for the lines Seat S 27th re-read; the real database function is not measured.

**Where**, at origin develop `45d2edc73aa9` (read 2026-11-06 by Seat S 27th with git show and git grep in a shallow scratch clone of origin develop `45d2edc73aa9`; nothing was run):

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts`: the handler is `oauthRouter.post('/authorize', ...)`; line 679 is the test `action === 'deny'`. `action` comes straight from `req.body`; the KS-1797 guard just above refuses a non-string `state` or `code_challenge` only.
* Same file, lines 267 to 271: `if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$/.test(clientId))` then `const app = await getAppByClientId(clientId);`. `RegExp.prototype.test` converts its argument to a string, so a one-element array such as \["abc"\] passes the test and the array itself is then handed to the lookup.

**Measured by gate 212** (verdict note N3, pre-existing and unchanged from the base, 0 of 336 rows differ; probe output in that gate's evidence folder, local to the coordinator): `action: ["deny"]` with valid credentials takes the approve path and mints a code; a one-element array `client_id` reached mint as `clientId: ["client-conf"]` with a permissive lookup double and answered invalid_client with a strict double. The gate's own reading: the caller holds the credentials, so nothing is gained over a plain approve, but a deny that mints is wrong. `redirect_uri`, `response_type`, `scope`, `code_challenge_method`, `email`, `password` and `mfaCode` as arrays all answer 400 on the approve path; on deny the credential fields are not read at all.

**For the owner to decide:** refuse any non-string `action` and `client_id` with the same 400 invalid_request envelope the KS-1797 guard uses, before the deny/approve split.

**NOT measured:** what the real `getAppByClientId` does with an array (the gate used doubles); a gateway path (the gate's note N4 says the form-encoded cells reach only the service layer).

**Source:** gate 212 (PR 2023, KS-1797), note N3, re-read by Seat S 27th at the lines above.

**Board search before filing (2026-11-06, Seat S 27th, board_search tool, both controls held: 'msgpackr' hit KS-1379 among open tickets, a random token hit 0):** `getAppByClientId` returned 5 candidates, 0 open literal hits, 1 closed (KS-823, a different defect: the refresh_token grant authenticates no client). No ticket says either point. The Apple sign-in id_token read from the same gate family (gate 211 N5) is not this ticket: KS-1858's description already names it.

title: transfer POST /api/transfers: the initiator names both parties in the body and nothing checks the caller is the current owner
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/transfers` (and `/api/transfers/initiate`) takes `currentOwnerId` and `newOwnerId` from the request body, validates only that each is a GUID, and copies both into the new transfer, so an authenticated caller can open a transfer that names someone else as the owner and themselves as the recipient. High. Priority as ruled by Wednesday (ANSWER 2026-11-06T03:40:16Z). Evidence class: READ ONLY at origin develop; the handler was not run.

**Where**, at origin develop `45d2edc73aa9` (read 2026-11-06 by Seat S 27th with git show and git grep in a shallow scratch clone of origin develop `45d2edc73aa9`; nothing was run):

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts` lines 375 and 376: `currentOwnerId: z.string().guid()` and `newOwnerId: z.string().guid()`. Line 528: `const initiatedBy = ((req as any).user?.userId as string) || data.currentOwnerId;` so the authenticated user feeds only `initiatedBy`, and the body's owner is the fallback. Lines 542 and 543 copy `data.currentOwnerId` and `data.newOwnerId` into the transfer. Lines 602 and 603 mount the handler on both paths. Nothing in the handler compares `currentOwnerId` with the caller or checks who owns `documentId`.
* Lines 580 to 582 create notifications for both named parties, so the named owner receives an approval-required notice for a transfer they did not start.

**Why it matters for KS-2038:** KS-2038 (the transfer routes approve, reject, execute and cancel admit any signed-in caller and take the actor from the body) depends on this ticket: any rule it adopts about who may act on a transfer reads `currentOwnerId` from the stored transfer, and this route lets the initiator set that value freely. The rule itself is not decided here and nothing in this ticket states it; the decision card for it is still open.

**Seat W 29th's reading (relayed in Wednesday's brief; not re-run by Seat S 27th):** binding `currentOwnerId` to the caller turns an existing object-authorization cell red, because that cell creates a transfer with an owner id that is not the caller.

**For the owner to decide:** bind `currentOwnerId` to the authenticated caller (or check ownership of `documentId`) at initiate, and refuse otherwise.

**NOT measured:** the handler at runtime; a real database; a gateway path; whether another service already checks document ownership before the gateway forwards this call.

**Source:** Seat W 29th's QUESTION mail to Wednesday of 2026-11-06T02:47:04Z (section 5, item i), re-read by Seat S 27th at the lines above.

**Board search before filing (2026-11-06, Seat S 27th, board_search tool, both controls held: 'msgpackr' hit KS-1379 among open tickets, a random token hit 0):** `initiateTransferHandler` returned 0 candidates. `currentOwnerId` and `newOwnerId` each returned one open literal hit, KS-1703, which names the two fields as part of the row a GET-by-id route returns; its scope is GET-by-id routes, not the initiate handler. Closed hits KS-466, KS-474 and KS-475 are earlier, different defects.

title: transfer POST /api/delegations: parentDelegationId comes straight from the body and nothing ties it to the caller
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/delegations` takes the delegator from the authenticated user but passes `req.body.parentDelegationId` straight through, and the service checks only that the parent allows sub-delegation, has depth left and holds the permissions asked for; nothing compares the caller with the parent's delegatee, so any signed-in caller who knows a parent delegation id can create a child delegation under it. title: platform tenants table has two tracked definitions that disagree; which one the deployed platform database carries is unknown
description:
**BLUF:** The platform `tenants` table is defined twice in tracked files with different columns and constraints, both as `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so whichever runs first wins and the other silently does nothing; which one the deployed platform database carries has not been established. Low. INFERRED from the two files; READ ONLY. Priority as ruled by Wednesday (ANSWER 2026-11-06T03:40:16Z).

**Where**, at origin develop `45d2edc73aa9` (read 2026-11-06 by Seat S 27th with git show and git grep in a shallow scratch clone of origin develop `45d2edc73aa9`; nothing was run):

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql` lines 21 to 33 (the file compose mounts): `status VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'provisioning'` with `CHECK (status IN ('provisioning','active','suspended','archived'))`, `industry VARCHAR(100)`, `logo_url VARCHAR(512)`, `settings JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`, timestamps `NOT NULL`.

Code written against one shape can fail or silently differ on the other. Whether any application code reads `logo_url`, `test_url` or `live_url` was not checked.

title: governance: an admin in one tenant can set stake and flags on another tenant's existing participant row
description:
**BLUF:** A platform admin in tenant T1 can change the stake, DRep status and committee status of a participant row owned by a user in tenant T2. QA gate 219 measured this at PR 2039 and at the develop before it, so it is not a regression. Nothing is fixed here. It needs a ruling, then a migration.

**Measured by the gate** (real compiled service, real JWT verification and router, real PostgreSQL as secuura_app):

* An admin in T1 on a row owned by a T2 user: 201, and stake, DRep and committee all change.
* One wallet linked in both tenants: the T1 admin binds it to the T1 user, the T2 owner gets 409, and a T2 admin's registration then writes onto the T1 user's row.

**Cause:** svc_governance_participants has no tenant column and no row-level security. Ruling D2 (a) on KS 1951 protects only the first bind, when no row holds the wallet yet. Once a row holds it, the admin path writes without reading a tenant. The comment in db.ts saying an admin in one tenant never binds another tenant's user is true only for a new row.

**What the ruling has to weigh:**

* **Precedent:** Kam's KS 1906 ruling keeps vc-issuer's owner-less credentials with "platform administrators of their tenant". Whether that reaches governance is not ruled.
* **The seeded SYSTEM_ADMIN sits in the default tenant** (userRepo.ts:1420). Today the only way that admin can stake a user in a provisioned tenant is this path: the owner self-registers, then the admin's stake lands on the row. Closing it plainly takes that away, so someone needs a named way to stake those users.
* **Other writers:** this was measured on the register route only. The other governance routes that read this table were not walked for the same shape.

**Fix shape, read only, not tried:** a tenant column on svc_governance_participants, backfilled from users, with row-level security and the same GUC the users read uses. A row whose id is not a user id (a legacy uuid row) has no tenant to backfill from, so it needs its own rule.

**Proposed priority:** High, because it writes vote power across a tenant boundary. The priority is for the humans to set.

title: erasure: an erased user's wallet stays on their users row, and their governance participant row keeps its vote power
description:
**BLUF:** Erasing a user leaves their wallet address on the users row, and leaves any governance participant row they hold in place with its vote power. KS 1951's follow-up only stops new binds to an erased user, so rows that already exist stay counted. Nothing is fixed here.

**What is there:**

* **users.wallet_address is not cleared by either erasure writer.** originate's executeErasure (gdprService.ts) sets status to deleted, and auth's user.erased subscriber (userErasedSubscriber.ts) sets it to deactivated. Neither statement names the column. QA gate 219 ran the auth statement on real PostgreSQL and the wallet stayed. The originate statement is read from source, not run.
* **Governance does not subscribe to user.erased:** 0 hits for USER_ERASED under services/governance. The gate found no other service that touches svc_governance_participants, so the row keeps its wallet, its stake and its share of total vote power.
* **The gate measured the vote power:** a row bound to an erased id added 200000 to total DRep vote power, for an account that can never log in or vote.

**Why it is not simply covered:** KS 1955 is about kyc and wallet-connector steps failing, and names no governance data. It does treat the wallet address as the subject's data. KS 239 is the decision on triggering erasure and names neither.

**What needs deciding:**

* What happens to a participant row with votes cast or proposals created, when its owner is erased: delete it, keep it with the wallet and vote power cleared, or keep it for audit.
* Whether clearing users.wallet_address at erasure is wanted, given the position on on-chain immutability in KS 234.

**Not measured:** how many erased users hold a wallet or a participant row on any box. No box was read.

title: governance: a failed by-address participant read logs the wallet address
description:
**BLUF:** When the database cannot be read, governance logs the wallet address the caller sent. QA gate 219 saw it in the service log on PR 2039 and marked it a note, because it is pre-existing and the new line in that PR does not do it. Nothing is fixed here.

**Where:** dbGetParticipantByAddress in services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts, around line 416: logger.error('DB get participant by address failed', { walletAddress, error: reason }).

**Searched first:** the log line's text, dbGetParticipantByAddress, walletAddress, "logs the wallet", "PII in logs". KS 1732 and KS 1940 touch the same read but are about what it answers, not what it logs.

title: Audit run: a scan that is still failing exits 0 from the second run on, because job 09 fails only on new findings and run-internal-audit.sh exits from the aggregator alone
description:
## BLUF

**A scan that is still failing makes the audit run exit 1 once and then exit 0.** The aggregator (job 09) fails only on findings that are new since the previous run, and [run-internal-audit.sh](<http://run-internal-audit.sh>) takes its exit from the aggregator alone. So "a failed scan is not a clean image" holds for one run only: a persistently broken trivy reads green at the exit-code level from the second run on, with only a "failed: 1" warning line in the summary.

* Medium, proposed. Found by gate 221 on PR 2041 (the KS-1136 fix), finding N1. The gate measured the aggregator half at runtime and read the orchestrator half; I read both in the PR's tree and did not re-run the second-run probe myself.
* Pre-existing as a design. Before PR 2041 the same scan failure was rc 0 on every run, so the fix is better than base but quieter than its title reads.
* A design question for the owner. Not built here; PR 2041 is not changed by it.

## Detail

* Repro (the gate's, real aggregator, two consecutive run directories under one runs/ directory, bash 3.2.57): a job-04 artefact holding one image with an error. Run 1: one high finding "image/scan-failed", rc 1, new 1. Run 2 on the same artefact: rc 0, new 0, "NEW findings: none", while the high total still counts it and it is still listed under all findings.
* Where, at PR 2041's head dfa1c633b329: Blockchain/Testing/jobs/09-aggregate-report.sh computes new as current minus the previous run's fingerprints minus baselined, and exits 1 only when the new, non-baselined findings reach the threshold. Blockchain/Testing/run-internal-audit.sh counts a failed job (FAIL_COUNT) and prints a warning, then exits from the aggregator's status alone (0, 1 or 2).
* This is the aggregator's documented design (it fails on new findings only), which is why it is a design question and not a defect report. KS-1136 recorded the same behaviour as context ("R-1") and PR 2041's cases assert the first run only for that reason.

## Recommendation

Prose only; the owner's call. Either of these, plus a test that pins the second-run behaviour so the choice is recorded:

* have the orchestrator count a job-04 failure toward its own exit; or
* key the scan-failed finding as always-new, for example with a fingerprint that includes the run id, so every run that still fails exits 1.

Priority is the humans' call.

## Searched before filing

Linear literal substring matches over issues (title and description) and comments, archived included, 2026-11-06 about 04:50Z. Control: an absent term returned 0, and "unreadable-artefact" returned the known KS-1136 and KS-878.

* "second run", "new-only", "fails only on new", "rc gate": KS-1136 only among the issues (its own R-1 context item). The two comment hits I read are KS-105 (the TypeScript CI orchestrator's blocking model, a different aggregator, Done) and PS-322 (an accessibility sweep); the many "second run" hits are other subjects and I read none of them beyond their titles.
* "run-internal-audit": KS-1787, KS-1382, KS-923, KS-868 (slot guard, TARGET_BASE default, a stage-2 guard, [orchestrate.sh](<http://orchestrate.sh>)), none about the exit status.
* "scan-failed": KS-1274, KS-1273, KS-1136 (the shapes job 04 turns into scan-failed), none about the second run.
* "AGG_EXIT", "prev_run": 0 hits.
* "09-aggregate-report": KS-1136, KS-878, KS-868, KS-676 (the artefact reads).

title: Security: a demoted or deleted ORG_ADMIN or ISSUER_ADMIN whose token is still live can mint and revoke API keys (tenant-level and own organisation)
description:
## BLUF

A user whose token says ORG_ADMIN or ISSUER_ADMIN, and whose `users` row no longer holds that role or is no longer active, can still mint and revoke API keys: 201 and 200 on every shape measured, tenant-level and own-organisation alike. The key routes read no `users` row for these two roles. It is the same harm as KS-2032, for the two roles a login actually issues. KS-2032's predicate is ADMIN-only and its card rules ADMIN, so it does not reach them. Facts only; nothing is built. Whether the rule extends is Kam's.

## Measured

Seat Y 6th, 2026-11-06. The real `POST /api/keys` and `DELETE /api/keys/:id` on real PostgreSQL 15.19 as the least-privilege app role, on develop `299b9d6a3827` plus the KS-2032 working tree (which does not touch these two roles). Node v26.8.1, not an LTS line. Tokens hand-signed RS256: token role, tenant T, organisation A1, the user's id. Each row is one run of all four calls.

| token role | stored role / status | mint, no organisation | revoke a tenant-level key | mint for own organisation | revoke own organisation's key |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| ORG_ADMIN | org_admin / active (control) | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ORG_ADMIN | user / active | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ORG_ADMIN | verifier / active | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ORG_ADMIN | org_admin / deleted | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ORG_ADMIN | org_admin / suspended | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | issuer_admin / active (control) | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | user / active | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | verifier / active | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | issuer_admin / deleted | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |
| ISSUER_ADMIN | issuer_admin / suspended | 201, key created | 200, key inactive | 201 | 200 |

Instrument control: the same mint with a token for another tenant answers 403.

Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatY-6th/evidence/ks2032/finding2_head.json`; the probe is `tools/ks2032_finding2_probe.integration.test.ts` in that folder. Evidence only, not committed to the repo.

## Read at source, not run

Lines at develop `299b9d6a3827`.

* `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:235`: for an org-bounded role, an unqualified target is allowed same-tenant. Kam's 2026-09-03 ruling for org-less keys.
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:838`: an admin's change to a user revokes that user's sessions only when the new status forbids a credential. So a role-only demotion leaves the session alive.
* `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:672`: the gateway checks the session, not the `users` row, and fails open if the session store is unreachable. So through the gateway, a status shape above should die at 401 while the store is up, and a role-only demotion should not. Not run through the gateway.
* `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:257`: `mapDbRole` issues ORG_ADMIN and ISSUER_ADMIN from stored rows, and has no key for ADMIN. So, by reading, these two roles are the ones real logins carry, and ADMIN is not (KS-2032's PR records that).
* `services/security/src/adminScope.ts:45`: `LIVE_ADMIN_USER_PREDICATE` is ADMIN-only and cannot serve these roles.

## Not measured

* A real demotion through `PATCH /api/users/admin/:id`, or any of this through the gateway.
* The real token lifetime on any box (compose default 1 day, code default 1 hour; the box values are not read).
* Whether any user on a box is in one of these states with a live token.
* Whether a tenant-level key reaches more than an organisation key: KS-2032's open item, still open.

## Open question (a decision, not made here)

Should these two roles also need a live `users` row holding that role at mint and revoke? It would be a new authorisation rule, not KS-2032's predicate, and it costs a database read on these roles' mints and revokes. Wednesday cards it for Kam with this figure.

Filed by Seat Y 6th on Wednesday's ANSWER 2026-11-06T05:02:31Z, from Finding 2 of the KS-2032 design QUESTION. Proposed priority: High. Related: KS-2032, KS-1585, KS-1570.

title: Nothing schedules the base-image watch that the KS-365 ruling relies on: the cron is retired and the replacement script is run by hand
description:
**BLUF:** Kam's card on KS-365 accepts a critical vulnerability (CVE-2025-68121, in the gosu binary of the postgres:15-alpine image) on the strength of "the weekly image watch tells us when it clears". At source nothing runs a weekly watch: the workflow that ran it monthly is retired, and its replacement script is run by hand. Evidence class: READ ONLY. No fix shape is chosen here.

## Evidence

* **The card.** secuura-ks-365-postgres-image-gosu-vulnerability-1106, option a, "Accept until the upstream rebuild; re-scan weekly"; detail, verbatim: "No work; the weekly image watch tells us when it clears." Ruled 2026-11-06T14:59:40+11:00.
* **The workflow.** At develop 038e8ab5ae2d, read in a read-only clone: `.github/workflows/base-image-refresh.yml` opens "THIS WORKFLOW NO LONGER RUNS" and keeps only a workflow_dispatch trigger, with no cron. Its last scheduled run was 2026-08-01 (KS-365 comments db01e8bc and d27de4b7). GitHub Actions is retired for this repository (Kam, 2026-08-27).
* **The replacement.** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/base-image-watch.sh` is run by hand. Its usage line calls the plain run "the monthly run", and KS-365 comment 8fe9efd6 says Wednesday runs it on the 1st of each month from a Secuura session. That is monthly and by hand, not weekly.
* **The last recorded re-scan.** KS-365 comment f00e3aa5 (2026-09-08): digest sha256:fe0737ba... unchanged, the CVE present. KS-365 records no re-scan after that date.
* **Board search**, includeArchived, by symbol (controls fired: the term msgpackr hits KS-1379; a random token hits 0). `base-image-watch`: 3 open literal hits and 3 closed. `base-image-refresh`: 2 open and 1 closed. The open hits are KS-365; KS-1446 (Renovate and EXCLUDED_BASES); KS-1669 (Renovate against the Dependabot ruling); and KS-636 (the node:24-alpine critical that the 2026-08-01 run flagged and nobody read). None of them owns scheduling the watch. KS-636 is the nearest, and was written on 2026-08-14, before Actions was retired.
* **Wednesday's scheduled jobs** were not found to run it, by Wednesday's read of her launchd list and scheduler folder just before her mail of 2026-11-06T05:45:38Z. Her read was a name grep, so it says little about a job under another name.

## UNMEASURED

* Whether anything outside the repository schedules the watch under another name. The instrument that closes it is the list of scheduled jobs read by what each job runs, not by its name.
* Whether the script has run at all since 2026-09-08. KS-365 records no run.
* Whether the hand run that KS-365 comment 8fe9efd6 describes happened on 2026-10-01 or 2026-11-01.

## Related

KS-365 (the ticket whose accepted residual relies on this watch) and KS-636 (the unread-alarm channel for the same watch). Who runs the watch, how often, and where a failure should land are not decided here.

title: Gate 213 on PR 2026 (KS-1539): a throw in the 503 path's log line answers 500, and no cell pins "never the message" past SyntaxError
description:
**BLUF:** Gate 213 raised two findings on PR 2026, the KS-1539 fix, that no ticket carries. F2 (Low): the allow-list catch logs before it answers 503, so a throw inside that log line answers 500 instead. F3 (Info): "never the message" is pinned by a cell for a SyntaxError only. KS-1539 was closed (Done, archived 2026-11-06T05:55Z) without the verdict having been read, so the follow-up is this new ticket. Whether F2 can happen in service is not measured.

## F2 (Low), from the gate 213 verdict, line 52

Verbatim: "The log line precedes the 503, so a throw inside it replaces the answer." Where: `routes/verification.ts:855` at the PR's head, in the catch, before the 503 answer. The gate ran 32 rows on the real router over loopback, base against head:

* Working logger, 12 ordinary thrown shapes plus one Error with a planted `constructor.name` (13 rows): base 503, head 503, byte-identical.
* Working logger, three hostile shapes (an Error with `constructor` undefined, an Error with a throwing `constructor` getter, a revoked Proxy of an Error) (3 rows): base 503, head 500 INTERNAL_ERROR "Failed to create document".
* Throwing logger, all 16 shapes (16 rows): base 503, head 500, the same body.
* Enforcement ran 0 times in all 32 rows, so the create stays refused: a wrong status, not an opening.
* The gate's fix shape: log after the answer, or guard the log and the class read so neither can stop the 503. Its oracle: the cheat fragment says "one log line, nothing else".

## F3 (Info), from the same verdict, line 65

The verdict's words: "Never the message" is pinned only for a SyntaxError. The gate's own tamper logged the error message for every other Error class and left the 6 new cells green. The product code is correct today: across the 13 rows above the message never reached a log line. The stored-bytes reason in the code applies to the SyntaxError, so this is a gap in the cells, not a leak.

## What is NOT known

* Whether F2 can happen in service. The gate says the three hostile shapes are synthetic (JSON.parse and the real ioredis class cannot produce them) and that it did not make the real gateway logger throw.
* Whether a follow-up staged by another seat already holds F2 or F3. The board search below finds none; staged files were not searched.
* Whether F2 and F3 were accepted at the merge. The verdict reads GO WITH NOTES for PR 2026, PR 2026 is merged to develop, and the board search below finds no record of these two notes being accepted or deferred.

## Owed

* F2: decide whether to apply the gate's fix shape given F2 is unmeasured in service; if so, a cell with a throwing logger that still answers 503.
* F3: a cell that fails when any Error class's message reaches a log line.

## Searched before filing (2026-11-06, includeArchived, titles, descriptions and comments)

* Controls: "KS-1539" hit (5 issues, 6 comments); a nonsense symbol returned 0.
* "log line precedes" 0 and 0; "errorClass" 0 and 0; `constructor.name` 0 and 0; "winstonLogger" 0 and 0; "throwing logger" 0 issues, comments on KS-1771, KS-1772 and KS-1818, which fixed the same class of fault at other sites (KS-1771 names the document-types catch at line 1067, not this catch).

title: RLS verify-fail-closed.sh reports PASSED and exits 0 on a database with no rows: every count is 0 and the users definer check is skipped
description:
**BLUF:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/rls/verify-fail-closed.sh`, the KS-458 check that the fail-closed tenant_isolation policy binds, prints "RLS FAIL-CLOSED VERIFICATION PASSED." and exits 0 on a database whose checked tables hold no rows. Every check compares a row count with 0, and the one check that needs a real row is skipped without a line. Found by reading the script at develop c5c26b2835df08e7e6addc1aec30939cf5531377; nothing was run.

## What the script does on an empty database (read, not run)

* Lines 99 and 100: with no tenant context the count must be "0". An empty table gives 0, so it passes.
* Lines 108 to 111: under a wrong tenant the count must be "0". An empty table passes here too.
* Lines 119 to 126: platform scope must see at least as many rows as the default tenant. 0 against 0 passes. Line 132 prints "OK <table> (closed=0, wrong=0, tenant=N, platform=N)", with "closed=0, wrong=0" as literal text rather than the measured counts.
* Lines 156 to 166: the definer check picks a user with `SELECT id FROM users LIMIT 1` under platform scope (line 156). When users is empty, `uid` is empty, the `if [ -n "$uid" ]` block at line 158 is skipped, and no line says so (no SKIP and no FAIL).
* Lines 168 to 173: with `fail` still 0 it prints the PASSED line (169) and exits 0 (173).

So on an empty database the script cannot tell a policy that hides rows from one that hides nothing, and it still reports the run as verified.

## Why it matters, as far as it is known

KS-458's acceptance records two PASSED runs of this script, local and demo. Those comments report counts with the right tenant, which reads as databases that held data; the runs themselves were not re-checked. The exposure is a fresh database: a rebuild, a restore before data, a new slot. There the script would print PASSED without exercising anything.

## What is NOT known

* Whether any run of the script has been done on an empty database. The seat filing this ran nothing.
* Whether the default tenant's row count is ever 0 on the stacks the script is pointed at.

## Owed

A run of the script against an empty database (a fresh compose stack before seeding) to confirm the PASSED line. Then either seed before verifying, or make an all-zero run fail or print an explicit SKIP line, and print a line whenever the definer check is skipped.

title: Audit export CSV: values starting with = + - or @ go out unneutralised, so a spreadsheet can read them as formulas (gate 202 N4)
description:
**BLUF:** The admin audit export (`GET /api/admin/audit/export`) writes CSV through `escapeCSVField`, which quotes a value only when it contains a comma, a double quote or a newline. A value that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` therefore goes out raw, or quoted only by accident, and a spreadsheet can read it as a formula. Gate 202 measured this on PR 2012 (KS-1645) at base and at head and graded it a Note; no ticket carries it. Whether any consumer opens the export in a spreadsheet is not known.

## What the gate measured (gate 202 on PR 2012, finding N4; its G-CSV cells, base and head)

* `escapeCSVField` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts`, lines 90 to 97, unchanged by the PR) quotes only values containing a comma, a double quote or a newline.
* `+1+1`, `-2` and `@SUM(A1)` go out raw.
* `=HYPERLINK(...)` is quoted only because it contains a comma, and it still starts with `=`.
* A bare carriage return is not quoted, at base or at head.
* `userAgent` and `ipAddress` can be set by the caller and were populated at base too. PR 2012 newly fills `action`, `resource` and `timestamp`, which the service sets.
* The gate's grading: a Note, not a hold, "per the commission".

## What is NOT known

* Whether any consumer opens the export in a spreadsheet.

## Owed

Decide the writer's contract for values that start with a formula character, and add a cell that fails when one goes out unneutralised.
