title: observability: npm run down exits 1 with no message when slot 1's redis container is absent, so the stack cannot be stopped
description:
**BLUF:** Peter appended this finding to KS-1388 on 2026-10-07 (comment `9e36fdd5-db2e-4467-94bb-42a548f84531`). It has no fix and no ticket of its own. In `observability/`, `npm run down` exits 1 with no error message while slot 1's Redis container is absent, and the observability stack keeps running. The runtime observation is Peter's, on his Mac; this seat ran nothing. This seat re-read the script at develop `35bcfa000b44`: the Redis password lookup runs at file scope before the action switch, under `set -euo pipefail`, with no guard. Priority Low (4). Facts only, nothing is built.

## What Peter observed (his comment, quoted in substance)

* Peter's Mac, 2026-10-07, observability started from the KS-1445 worktree. Slot 1 had been stopped by another session.
* `npm run down` ran `bash scripts/observability.sh down` and exited 1. All 9 `secuura-obs-*` containers were still up.
* `bash -x` showed the run stopping inside `resolve_redis_password`, called at file scope, after `docker inspect secuura-redis` found no container. The `down)` branch was never reached.
* Workaround he used, from `observability/`: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml --profile phase2 down`. It removed all 9 containers and kept the 3 data volumes.

## What the source shows at develop `35bcfa000b44` (read through the GitHub API, not run)

File `observability/scripts/observability.sh`, 268 lines.

* Line 25: `set -euo pipefail`.
* Lines 132 to 149: `resolve_redis_password` runs `docker inspect "$container" --format '{{json .Config.Cmd}}' 2>/dev/null` into a Python filter. There is no `|| true` or other guard on that pipeline. With `pipefail`, a failing `docker inspect` makes the pipeline fail.
* Line 151: `_redis_pw="$(resolve_redis_password)"` is at file scope, before the action switch. Under `set -e` a failing assignment from a command substitution ends the script.
* Lines 257 to 260: the `down)` branch is only `docker compose ... --profile phase2 down`. It needs neither credential.
* The Postgres lookup differs from what Peter's comment says. His comment names both `secuura-redis` and `secuura-postgres`. At this sha `resolve_pg_dsn` (line 91, called at line 115) runs `docker exec` at line 100 and guards it with `|| creds=""` at line 101, so an absent Postgres container is guarded at that line. His trace stopped in the Redis function. Whether the Postgres path can also abort elsewhere in its function (lines 91 to 112) was not traced by this seat.

## Not known

* Whether current develop reproduces Peter's exit 1: his run was on the script at develop `b280b74ff`, and no one has re-run it since. The reading above is from the source only.
* Which Docker version or shell the exit status depends on.

## Fix direction (Peter's suggestion, quoted, not done)

"Resolve the platform credentials only for the actions that start containers (start / up / phase2), or make the lookups non-fatal for down / status / logs. Stopping the stack should never depend on the platform being up."

## Related

* KS-1388 holds the original comment and the slot-awareness record for `observability/`. It stays open; its priority is not changed by this ticket.

## Searched before filing (board, includeArchived)

Read-only, run 2026-11-06 with controls: a known term hit KS-1379, a random token hit 0, and the non-zero control `KS-1388` gave 3 candidates, 2 open literal hits, 1 closed. Counts are candidates, open literal hits, closed or archived literal hits.

* `npm run down` 100, 1, 0 (KS-1388). `resolve_redis_password` 89, 1, 0 (KS-1388). `resolve_pg_dsn` 100, 1, 0 (KS-1388). The script's file name, `observability/scripts/observability.sh` taken by its last path segment, 100, 4, 1 (open: KS-1381, KS-1388, KS-1550, KS-1558; closed: KS-200).
* The full text of KS-1550, KS-1558, KS-1381, KS-1415 and KS-1388 was read for `npm run down`, "exits 1", the script's file name, `secuura-redis` and `docker inspect`. Only KS-1388 states this finding: in Peter's appended comment, and in KS-1388's newest comment, which records that no commit after PR 1387 names it. The other four name the script only in lists of slot-1 scripts.
* This is "not found by these searches", not proof of absence.

title: No notification service is defined in the stack: originate posts to one, then falls back to SMTP; the gateway keeps them in a Map
description:
**BLUF:** Two statements from Seat E 39th, relayed by the coordinator and checked here in source at develop `35bcfa000b44`, point at one gap: the stack defines no notification service. The originate notification client posts to `http://notification:3008/api/notifications` by default and falls back to direct SMTP; the gateway's notifications routes keep their data in a process-local `Map` under a comment that says it is backed by the notification service in production. Nobody has measured the runtime effect, and this seat ran nothing. Priority Low (4) for that reason. Facts only, nothing is built.

## Item 1: the originate client posts to a service the stack does not define

* `services/originate/src/utils/notificationClient.ts` line 19 to 20: the URL is `process.env.NOTIFICATION_SERVICE_URL` or the default `http://notification:3008/api/notifications`.
* Lines 28 to 33: the doc comment says it sends through the notification service and "falls back to direct SMTP if the notification service is unreachable". Line 35 is the `fetch` to that URL.
* Lines 44 and 60: on a non-OK reply and on an unreachable service the client logs a warning that it is falling back to SMTP. Lines 71 to 73: the fallback skips the notification with an INFO line, "SMTP not configured", when SMTP is not configured.
* So with the default URL and no service behind it, each send is expected to try the `fetch` first, log a warning, then use SMTP if it is configured or skip. That sequence is read from the source, not observed.

## Item 2: the stack defines no such service (read at the same sha)

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` defines 44 services and none has "notif" in its key (control: `staking` is defined, line 1045). Its only mention of notifications is a comment at line 634 about SMTP.
* No other compose file in the tree names "notification" at all (the 14 other compose files in the tree were read for the word, case-insensitive: 0 hits), and none of the 16 files under `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/` with a bicep, shell, YAML or JSON extension names it (all 16 were read for the word; control: 13 of the 16 contain "container", "image" or "resource").
* The tree holds 27 service directories under `Blockchain/Dev/services/` and none starts with "notif".

## Item 3: the gateway's notifications routes are held in a process-local Map

* `services/api-gateway/src/routes/notifications.ts` line 69 is the comment "In-memory store (backed by notification service in production)", and line 72 is `const notifications = new Map<string, Notification[]>();`.
* The router declares six routes: list (line 115), unread count (162), mark one read (183), mark all read (212), delete (240) and create (270). This seat did not read the handlers. If they all use the `Map`, the data is per process and lost on restart; that is not measured.

## Not known

* Whether `NOTIFICATION_SERVICE_URL` is set in any deployed environment (Kintsugi, demo, staging). No compose file sets it; no environment was read.
* Whether any portal shows in-app notifications, and whether SMTP is configured in any deployed environment.
* What a send does at runtime with the default URL when the name `notification` does not resolve.
* A related datum, not interpreted here: KS-256 has a comment of 2026-08-18 that says "the notification service times out under load" for the client's 5000 ms `AbortSignal.timeout` and names it as the trigger of a gateway breaker tripping. It does not say whether a service was running or the host was unreachable.

## Open decision (not made here)

Build the service the client and the route comment assume, or remove the first attempt and state SMTP as the transport, or keep the route data in a store. This ticket does not choose.

## Adjacent, not duplicates

* KS-1937, KS-1964 and KS-2036 are about the recipient's email address written to logs by the originate client and the auth email path. A different defect.
* KS-1868 and KS-256 mention the notification service in passing and do not say it is absent.

## Searched before filing (board, includeArchived)

Read-only, run 2026-11-06 with controls: a known term hit KS-1379 and a random token hit 0. Counts are candidates, open literal hits, closed or archived literal hits.

* `NOTIFICATION_SERVICE_URL` 100, 0, 0. `notification:3008` 79, 0, 0. `backed by notification` 100, 0, 0. `notification service` 100, 3, 0 (KS-256, KS-1868, KS-1937; matched lines read). `notificationClient` 6, 4, 0 (KS-256, KS-1937, KS-1964, KS-2036).
* This is "not found by these searches", not proof of absence.

title: transfer: an approve body carrying action reject is recorded as an approval, because the schema drops the action key
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/transfers/:id/approve` records an approval for a body that says it is a refusal. A named approver who sends their own id with `action: 'reject'` gets 200, `fullyApproved: true` and 0 rejections; `decision: 'rejected'` does the same; a sale owner who sends `action: 'reject'` with `comment: 'I refuse'` gets an approval that carries the comment "I refuse". Medium severity, low likelihood (the gate's grade), and pre-existing: the result is the same at the base and at PR 2048's head. Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME by gate 229 (same result at base and head); the code lines were READ ONLY by me at origin develop `a6cd828e820d`, nothing was run by me.

**Where**, at origin develop `a6cd828e820d69b7a48f9d28d54023bc1a628437` (read 2026-11-06 by Seat S 32nd through the GitHub contents API at that sha), all in `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts`:

* Lines 404 to 415: `approveTransferSchema` is a non-strict `z.object` with `approverId`, `approverRole`, `reason`, `signature`, `walletAddress` and `comment`. It declares no `action` and no `decision`, so zod drops them. The schema's own comment at lines 407 to 410 says that zod's non-strict objects silently drop unknown keys.
* Line 701 parses the body with that schema. Lines 726 to 735 build the approval from the signed-in caller plus `data.signature`, `data.walletAddress` and `data.comment`. Nothing in the handler reads a refusal word.
* The gate read the published request as permitting the extra key (`additionalProperties: {}`); I did not re-read the yaml.
* Line 711 is a code comment from PR 2048: `approverId` stays required so that a body that names nobody, "such as the SDK's { action: 'reject' }", keeps its 400 and is never read as an approval. The hole is the case where `approverId` is present.

**Who could hit it, as the gate read it:** no real caller today, because the SDK and the e2e specs send no approver id and read 400 (gate 229, Question 5). The refusal shape is advertised, though: the gateway's `/api` text says "Approve/reject transfer" (`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:851`, the gate's citation, not re-read by me); the SDK comment at `Blockchain/Dev/sdk/javascript/src/modules/transfers.ts:111` reads "Approve or reject a transfer" and its `approve()` takes `'approve' | 'reject' | 'accept'` (lines 113 to 125, read by me); and `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/api/transfer.api.spec.ts` lines 118 to 132 post `action: 'reject'` to the approve door and expect `status` `rejected` (read by me).

**Why it matters, as the gate put it:** a silent inversion, and on a simple transfer the owner's reject is then gone (the owner's right to reject ends once the recipient has approved, which reads 400).

**For the owner to decide:** the gate's fix-shape is to refuse any `action` other than approve. Declaring the key on the schema or making the schema strict are the other shapes visible in the code; which one, and what the reject path at the approve door should do, is the owner's call.

**NOT measured:** by me, anything at runtime; a gateway path; a real database. PR 2048 merged 2026-11-06T09:30:58Z as squash `bdbb11b21585`; a squash on develop is not a deploy and I have read nothing about a deploy of it.

**Source:** gate 229 verdict, finding F4: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate229-tier1-pr2048-ks2038/verdict.md` (a coordinator-local file). Related: KS-2038 (the PR's ticket, hands-off), KS-2043 (the reject door drops a valid signature, a different door).

title: transfer after PR 2048: no cell pins the executor reject row, the restart proof has no assertion, the cancel summary disagrees
description:
**BLUF:** Three Low items from gate 229 on PR 2048 (KS-2038), none of them a wrong behaviour of the shipped rule: (F6) tampers that remove the executor from the reject row on simple, sale and corporate transfers turn no test cell red, although the spec publishes that clause; (F7) the committed tests stub the authenticator and run with no database, and the one restart proof is an uncommitted tool with no assertion in it, so it cannot go red; (F9) the published cancel summary says "before execution" while the description and the code say draft or pending approval. One ticket for the three, as three items. Low. Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME by gate 229 for F6 (its own tampers); READ ONLY by me for F7's assertion count and F9's lines, at origin develop `a6cd828e820d`, nothing was run by me.

**Item 1, F6: test gaps found by the gate's own tampers** (the gate's record is `evidence/q6/tampers.out` in its folder beside the verdict):

* Survived, and the gate says they matter: G1, G2 and G3 remove the executor from the reject row on simple, sale and corporate transfers: 0 red cells. The spec publishes the clause ("the executor where one is named") and nothing pins it. Seat W 29th had noted this debt. The gate's probes show the current behaviour is right.

* Caught: G4, but only by one unit cell, so no door cell exercises a non-uuid principal and the HTTP test file contains 0 mentions of a connector (the same gap KS-2081 needs a regression cell for); G5, G8 and G9.
* Not counted: G11 was the gate's own mistake (it only reorders a list, an equivalent mutant). Seat W 29th's own set: the gate re-ran 3 sampled tampers, all red in the cells named; W's record reads 61 of 61 with bytes restored.

**Item 2, F7: what the committed proofs leave unproven**

* Seat W 29th's HTTP cells stub the authenticator and run with no database. The gate ran the real authenticator itself; the committed tests still leave unproven the persistence of the recorded actor, a restart, the `ON CONFLICT` upsert and the real token path.
* The restart proof is a tool, not a committed test: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatW-29th/tools/restart_proof_w29.test.ts` (sha256 957e3c6386b9b162378908e9ded26f48a3fe7fb7f80fc8687f75ddd26af0e0ac). I counted its assertions myself: 0 occurrences each of `expect`, `assert`, `toBe`, `toEqual` and `toThrow` in its 130 lines, against 2 `it(` calls and 1 `writeFileSync` as the control that the pattern can match. It records rows, so vitest exits 0 whatever they say; the gate read the rows by eye and found them in agreement with the PR body and the code. The gate also notes it stubs the authenticator by a header. The gate notes its schema source is named (docker/init plus migrations); I did not check that.

**Item 3, F9: published text disagrees with itself on cancel**

title: transfer: the JavaScript SDK and the e2e specs post initiate and approve bodies the transfer validator refuses with 400
description:
**BLUF:** The JavaScript SDK's `transfers.initiate()` and `transfers.approve()`, and the e2e specs that call the transfer doors, send bodies that the transfer service's validators refuse, so those calls answer 400 today. They were already failing before PR 2048 (KS-2038): gate 229's callers table reads 400 at the base and 400 at the head, so this is not a regression of that PR. Low. One coupling matters for whoever fixes it: PR 2048's code comment relies on the SDK's refusal body still reading 400, and fixing the callers alone would turn the SDK's reject into an approval (KS-2082). Evidence class: READ ONLY by me at origin develop `a6cd828e820d` (callers and validators); the 400s are gate 229's table, which I did not re-run, and I ran nothing.

**Where**, at origin develop `a6cd828e820d69b7a48f9d28d54023bc1a628437` (read 2026-11-06 by Seat S 32nd through the GitHub contents API at that sha):

* The validators, `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts`. Lines 373 to 402: `initiateTransferSchema` requires `documentId`, `transferType` (simple, sale, inheritance or corporate), `currentOwnerId` and `newOwnerId` (both guids), `documentHash` (64 hex characters), `documentTitle` and `documentType`. Lines 404 to 415: `approveTransferSchema` requires `approverId` (a guid) and `approverRole`. `POST /api/transfers` and `POST /api/transfers/initiate` are the same handler (lines 604 and 605).
* The SDK, `Blockchain/Dev/sdk/javascript/src/modules/transfers.ts`. Lines 53 to 59 and 87 to 89: `initiate` posts `documentId`, `toUserId` and the optional `reason`, `requiresApproval` and `workflowType` to `/api/transfers/initiate`; it sends none of `transferType`, `currentOwnerId`, `newOwnerId`, `documentHash`, `documentTitle` or `documentType`. Lines 113 to 125: `approve` posts `{ action, comment?, signature? }` to `/api/transfers/:id/approve`; it sends no `approverId` and no `approverRole`.
* The e2e specs, all under `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/`: `api/transfer.api.spec.ts` lines 15 to 21 initiate with `fromUserId`, `toUserId`, `reason` and `requiresApproval` and expect ok (line 28); lines 104 to 110 and 121 to 127 post `{ action: 'approve', signature }` and `{ action: 'reject', reason }` to the approve door and expect ok and `rejected`. `integration/full-certification-flow.api.spec.ts` lines 123 to 127 initiate with `toUserId`; lines 145 to 148 and 161 to 164 post `action: 'approve'` and `action: 'accept'`. `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/full-stakeholder-browser.spec.ts` lines 793 to 800 and `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/local-platform-smoke.spec.ts` lines 318 to 325 post `fromUserId` and `toUserId` to `/api/transfers`.

**Gate 229's callers table** (its Question 5; 400 at base and head for each of these): SDK `initiate` and the two initiate specs with `toUserId`; SDK `approve` and the e2e approve and accept calls with no approver id; the e2e reject-through-approve call with no approver id, which also skips because no transfer is created. The two specs that post `fromUserId` assert only "under 500", so they still pass at 400. SDK `cancel` is the only call that newly fails after PR 2048, and by the ruling.

**The coupling, with KS-2082:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts` line 711 is a PR 2048 comment: `approverId` stays required so that a body that names nobody, "such as the SDK's { action: 'reject' }", keeps its 400 and is never read as an approval. KS-2082 records that a body that does carry `approverId` and `action: 'reject'` is recorded as an approval. So a fix on the caller side that adds `approverId` to the SDK's `approve()` would, with KS-2082 open, make `approve(id, 'reject')` approve. KS-2049 also bears on the initiate side: it records that the handler takes both parties from the body, and what `currentOwnerId` must be is its question.

**For the owner to decide:** change the callers to the shape the validators require, or change the validators and the published contract to accept what the SDK and the specs send; which, and in which order relative to KS-2082 and KS-2049, is the owner's call.

**NOT measured:** by me, any of the 400s at runtime; a gateway path; whether any real integration uses the SDK's transfer module. PR 2048 merged 2026-11-06T09:30:58Z as squash `bdbb11b21585`; a squash on develop is not a deploy and I have read nothing about a deploy of it.

**Source:** Seat W 29th's filing candidate "the SDK and e2e send a body the validator refuses" (its HANDOVER of 2026-11-06, lines 8 and 41), which Wednesday ruled to file Low naming gate 229's callers table: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate229-tier1-pr2048-ks2038/verdict.md` (a coordinator-local file), Question 5. Related: KS-2038 (hands-off), KS-2049, KS-2082.

title: Kintsugi renders FRONTEND_URL as localhost:6882 for m365-integration, kyc and api-gateway, so the M365 connect redirect goes to localhost
description:

No such refusal exists since PR 2053 removed it; line 509 was corrected and lines 330 to 333 annotated, but line 522 was missed, and "below" was already wrong because the function sits above it. 2. F2, Low. The sentence "an unreadable base name is refused" is overbroad. Fix shape: derive the keys from the awk program at run time, or add a cell asserting NON_JS_BASES is assigned only by the loop over the split() list. title: No hook suite proves a red preflight makes the pre-push hook refuse a push: its final exit 1 can become exit 0 with every suite green
description:
**BLUF:** No hook suite proves that a red preflight makes the pre-push hook refuse a push. The final step of `.githooks/pre-push`, the `|| { ...; exit 1; }` after the preflight call, can be changed to `exit 0` and every hook suite that can run on a sparse tree stays green. If that line regressed, every leg of the preflight would become advisory and no suite would say so. Found by gate 228 (tier 1, round 2 of 2, GO WITH NOTES) on PR 2047 (KS-1728) as its finding F3: pre-existing, outside that PR's diff, for routing. The hook is correct at the gate's head, so this is a missing test and not a defect today. Verdict in full: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate228-tier1-pr2047-ks1728/verdict.md, finding F3 from line 51 (gate head 0dbf24bc0ce40135ed98fcff92661d752b95f350).

## What the gate measured (evidence class MEASURED AT RUNTIME)

* Mutant H3 changes that `exit 1` to `exit 0`, placed in the gate's own worktree as the real hook. All 8 hook suites that are green on that sparse tree stayed green, at base and at head where run. The verdict grades F3 Minor, which is its technical grade. The priority here is Medium, set by Wednesday on this ground: one line carries every leg of the preflight, nothing proves it, and a regression would make the whole push gate advisory with no suite saying so. It costs one cell to close.

title: governance castVote counts a delegator's stake twice: the delegator still votes with it and the delegate's vote adds it again
description:
**BLUF:** In the governance service a delegator keeps full voting power after delegating it, and the delegate's vote adds the delegated power on top, so the same stake is counted twice in `votes_for`. Measured on a real compiled service: with one stake of 1000 delegated, `votes_for` reads 3000; in both controls (no delegation, and after the delegation is revoked) it reads 2000. Found in Seat U 17th's walk of the governance service; no fix here.

**Measured (MEASURED AT RUNTIME), Seat U 17th, 2026-11-06:** the real compiled governance service on PostgreSQL 15.19 at develop `b7d433fda83c` on Node v26.8.1; not a box, not Kintsugi, not demo. Evidence file `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatU-17th/evidence/walk/run_base.out`, lines 2 to 5, quoted (a is the delegator, d the delegate, each owns a stake of 1000):

* `4B control no delegation {"a":1000,"d":1000,"status":[200,200],"votesFor":2000}`
* `4B delegate {"s":200,"delegatedPower":1000}`
* `4B delegated {"a":1000,"d":2000,"status":[200,200],"votesFor":3000}`
* `4B after revoke {"a":1000,"d":1000,"votesFor":2000}`

The delegator's own vote was accepted (status 200) and counted 1000; the delegate's vote counted 2000, its own 1000 plus the delegated 1000.

**Where (READ at the same sha):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts`. `castVote` (line 946) gives every voter `voter.votePower` plus `getDelegatedPowerFor(voterId, proposal.category)` (lines 982 and 983) and nowhere checks whether the voter has delegated their own power away. `delegateVote` (line 1193) stores `delegatedPower: delegator.votePower` (line 1224) and leaves the delegator's own `votePower` as it was. `getDelegatedPowerFor` (line 1259) sums `delegatedPower` over the delegate's active delegations. The early-finalise check (lines 1038 to 1045 of the same file) reads `votesFor`, so the doubled figure can decide an outcome.

**Not measured:** a category-scoped delegation (`categories`), several delegators to one delegate, and a proposal whose outcome flips because of the extra power.

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** 0 open and 0 closed literal hits for `getDelegatedPowerFor`, `delegated power` and `votes_for`. `castVote` has 0 open hits and 5 closed ones, none about delegation (KS-450, KS-1940, KS-1942, KS-1950, KS-1951).

**Possible shapes (mine, not a decision):** refuse or zero a delegator's own vote while an active delegation covers the proposal's category, or subtract the delegated-away power in `castVote`; either needs a test cell holding the 2000 and 3000 figures above.

title: governance POST /api/governance/proposals/:id/execute checks no role: any signed-in user of any tenant executes a queued proposal
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/governance/proposals/:id/execute` checks only that the caller is signed in. It checks no role, no proposer or committee membership and no tenant. Measured on a real compiled service: a user of one tenant with the OWNER role executed a queued proposal created by a user of another tenant and got 200 with `status` `executed`. Limit: today execution only logs each action and flags it executed (no contract call), by Seat U 17th's read, so the effect is the proposal's status moving to `executed`. Found in Seat U 17th's walk of the governance service; no fix here.

**Measured (MEASURED AT RUNTIME), Seat U 17th, 2026-11-06:** the real compiled governance service on PostgreSQL 15.19 at develop `b7d433fda83c` on Node v26.8.1; not a box, not Kintsugi, not demo. Evidence file `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatU-17th/evidence/walk/run_base.out`, line 14, quoted (T1 and T2 are the two tenants of the walk):

* `X8 execute a T2 queued proposal as T1 OWNER {"s":200,"t2Status":"executed"}`

A 200 also means the timelock check passed, because the service answers 409 before the proposal's execution time. Sibling routes in the same walk do check the caller: cancel by a non-committee user answered 403 `Only proposer or constitutional committee can cancel` (line 11), and process-expired by an OWNER answered 403 where a SUPER_ADMIN got 200 (line 13).

**Where (READ at the same sha):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts` lines 300 to 315: the handler reads `userId`, answers 401 when it is absent, and calls `governanceService.executeProposal(req.params.id, userId)`. `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts` line 1103: `executeProposal(proposalId: string, _executorId: string)`. The executor id is named `_executorId` and appears nowhere else in the file; the body checks that the proposal exists, is `queued` and is past its timelock, then marks its actions executed and saves.

**Not measured:** a rule in front of the service. The walk's STATUS lists originate, auth, wallet-connector and governance as the compiled services, so whether the api-gateway narrows this path is not measured.

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** 0 open and 0 closed literal hits for `proposals/:id/execute`, `executeProposal` and `_executorId`. The nearest tickets are the same class on other services: KS-1814 (the document anchor route) and KS-2038 (the transfer doors).

**Possible shape (mine, not a decision):** a check like the cancel route's (proposer or committee) or a role set on `execute`, with a cell for the 403.

title: originate publishEvent swallows every Redis failure in an empty catch: a failed user.erased publish is silent and the log says published
description:
**BLUF:** originate publishes `user.erased` through its own `publishEvent`, and the `catch` at lines 143 to 145 of `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/events.ts` is empty. A Redis failure while publishing is therefore silent: the erasure returns success, `gdprService` logs `user.erased event published`, and no stream entry exists, so no downstream service ever erases the subject's copy. With `REDIS_URL` unset the same happens. The `warn` branch in `gdprService` that says the cascade may be incomplete cannot fire on a Redis failure, because `publishEvent` never throws. Found in Seat U 17th's walk of the erasure; no fix here.

**Measured (MEASURED AT RUNTIME), Seat U 17th, 2026-11-06:** the real compiled originate on PostgreSQL 15.19 and redis-server 8.10.3 at develop `b7d433fda83c` on Node v26.8.1; not a box, not Kintsugi, not demo. Evidence file `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-06_seatU-17th/evidence/walk/run_erasure.out`, lines 12 and 13, quoted:

* `E8 dead Redis {"result":{"label":"E8","success":true,"tables":["users","pii_subject_keys"],"ms":89},"warned":false,"newEntries":0,"status":"deleted","walletKept":true}`
* `E9 REDIS_URL unset {"result":{"label":"E9","success":true,"tables":["users","pii_subject_keys"],"ms":95},"saidPublished":true,"newEntries":0}`

Seat U 17th predicted a `warn` for E8 before running it (`predictions_erasure.txt` line 10 in the same folder) and the run showed none: success true after 89 ms, no warn line, 0 stream entries, and the log line `user.erased event published`. Its STATUS of 2026-11-06 about 11:55Z (item W1) records the same.

**Where (READ at the same sha):**

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/events.ts`: `publishEvent` (line 118) returns at once when there is no client (`if (!redis) return;`, line 123); otherwise its `try` runs `xadd` and the `catch` at lines 143 to 145 holds only the comment `// Fire-and-forget — never let event publishing break the service`. `initEventBus` warns once at start-up when `REDIS_URL` is unset (line 62); no later erasure says anything.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/services/gdprService.ts`: lines 962 to 981 wrap `await publishEvent(EventTypes.USER_ERASED, ...)` in a `try`, log `user.erased event published — downstream services will cascade` after it (line 970) and log `Failed to publish user.erased event (cascade may be incomplete)` in the `catch` (line 980). That `catch` is unreachable for a Redis failure.
* What does not happen when the entry is missing, per the same run: auth deactivating the user (E3) and wallet-connector deleting the wallet's session rows (E4); per KS-1955, kyc's deletes. KS-1955 also says originate marks the data-subject request completed at step 12, before the publish at step 13.

**Not measured:** a Redis failure that appears only after the `xadd` is accepted, and the running Kintsugi or demo originate (neither was touched).

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** 0 open and 0 closed literal hits for `originate/src/events.ts` and `event published`. `user.erased` has 7 open hits, none about the publisher: KS-239, KS-485, KS-772, KS-1868, KS-1931, KS-1955, KS-2060. KS-1955 (Backlog, High, 0 comments) is the handler half: a failed kyc or wallet-connector handler after the bus, and its text does not name `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/events.ts` or `publishEvent`. KS-2004 is an empty catch in the demo user seed, a different file. `publishEvent` appears in KS-1651 (the `ownership_transferred` payload) and `initEventBus` in KS-1868 (unguarded thrown-value reads); neither covers this empty catch.

**Possible shapes (mine, not a decision):** have `publishEvent` return whether the entry was added, or log inside the catch with the event type and the error message, and make the `gdprService` info line depend on that result so the existing `warn` can fire.

title: Both portals print Block 0 for a document with no block: the verifier's Block Height row and the issuer's Block card
description:
**BLUF:** Two portal screens show "0" as a block number for a document that has no block, so the claim of a block 0 survives on screen even where the API now answers `null`. The verifier portal prints `Block Height 0` for a pending document. The issuer portal prints `Block 0` for every real anchor, even a confirmed one, because it never carries the height through. Neither is a regression and neither is cured by PR 2054 (KS-1509); gate 238 asked for both to be ticketed. Evidence class: READ ONLY (not run in a browser).

**F4, the verifier portal (READ ONLY at develop** `90b500e19883`**):** `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/verifier/src/components/ResultPage.tsx`. The "Blockchain Proof" card shows when `result.verified && (result.blockchain || result.anchor)` (line 449). Its "Block Height" row (lines 495 to 498) prints `(result.blockchain?.blockHeight || result.anchor?.blockNumber || 0).toLocaleString()` (line 497), so an unknown height prints 0. `verified` is true for a pending row. Gate 238 records the same lines at the PR head and that the card sits beside a failing "Anchored on blockchain" check. Fix shape (gate 238's): hide the row when there is no height.

**F5, the issuer portal (READ ONLY at develop** `90b500e19883`**):** `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/issuer/src/components/DocumentDetail.tsx` lines 185 to 192 build the anchor from `raw.blockchain` with `id`, `status`, `network`, `txHash` and `anchoredAt` and no height; gate 238 records that GET document returns no `anchors` key, so line 120 (`blockNumber: anchor.blockHeight || anchor.block_height || 0`) always falls to 0. The card shows when the proof has a hash (line 490), and `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/issuer/src/components/blockchain/BlockchainCard.tsx` line 195 prints `proof.blockNumber.toLocaleString()`, so any anchor with a hash shows 0, including one confirmed at a real height. Gate 238 did not read whether the row sits behind a collapsed section. Fix shape (gate 238's): carry `blockHeight` through and hide the row when it is null.

**Source:** gate 238 verdict, grade MODERATE for both, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate238-tier1-pr2054-ks1509/verdict.md`, findings F4 and F5 (Wednesday's gate; read whole by this seat). The lines above were re-read by this seat at develop `90b500e19883` through the GitHub API; nothing was run.

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** `BlockchainCard.tsx` and `blockHeight || blockNumber`: 0 hits. `ResultPage.tsx`: 1 open hit, KS-735 (the verify result shows nothing about what was registered; a different defect in the same file). `DocumentDetail.tsx`: 1 open hit, KS-1831 (the sign route). `Block Height`: 5 open hits (KS-485, KS-772, KS-1384, KS-1509, KS-1809). KS-1509 was read: it covers the API's height defaults and PR 2054 and does not name either portal screen. No open ticket tracks these two screens.

description:
**BLUF:** `GET /api/documents/:id` answers `blockchain.anchored: true` for a document whose anchoring is only pending and that has no transaction hash. `anchored` is true for any blob that is not `anchor_failed`, so a pending blob reads as anchored. title: Public API examples show blockHeight as a string ("4615780"); a client typed as a number would fail to read it
description:
**BLUF:** Two public examples show a transaction's `blockHeight` as a string, `"blockHeight": "4615780"`. A client typed as a number would fail to read it. Gate 238 read Platform S's `long?` height with its JSON options in a June snapshot and found no number-from-string handling, so its verify page would fall to "temporarily unavailable" on such a body. Pre-existing and docs only; gate 238 grades it MINOR. Evidence class: READ ONLY (the deserialisation was not run).

**Where (READ at develop** `90b500e19883`**):** `Blockchain/Dev/docs/VERIFICATION.md` line 64 and `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/docs/developer-portal.html` line 202, the same example wrapped in HTML. Both sit inside a `blockchain` object with `"network": "preprod"` and a `txHash`.

**Platform S side (gate 238, READ from a June snapshot, not run):** `CardanoAnchorService.cs` lines 19 to 23 hold the JSON options with no number-from-string handling, and the verify page's fallback text is at lines 332 to 340. The deployed Platform S has moved since that snapshot (gate 238, finding F2), so what it does today is not known.

**Related, read in KS-1129 (In Progress):** anchoring's `block_number` leaves `buildResponse` as a string because `pg` returns BIGINT as a string, and a healed document can carry that string into the public verify answer; KS-1628 ruled that the successor verify accepts a positive-integer digit string as well as a number. So the example may show real output and not only a docs slip, which is why the contract (number, or number or digit string) comes before the wording. **Not measured by this seat:** which routes answer a string today. PR 2054 (KS-1509) moves the stored height toward a number or null, which gate 238 reads as the right direction.

**Source:** gate 238 verdict, finding F10, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-06_gate238-tier1-pr2054-ks1509/verdict.md`.

**Board search (2026-11-06, includeArchived, paginated):** `docs/VERIFICATION.md` and `4615780`: 0 hits. `developer-portal.html`: 5 open hits (KS-485, KS-772, KS-967, KS-1473, KS-1651) and 3 closed, none about the height example (KS-1473 is the undocumented verify-batch route). `blockHeight`: 8 open and 16 closed hits; the nearest is KS-1129 (In Progress): anchoring's raw `pg` BIGINT block number reaches readers as a string.

**Possible shape (mine, not a decision):** settle the height's contract with KS-1129 first, then make both examples match it; a Platform S owner should say whether the deployed reader accepts a string.

title: Pre-push hook leg 14 refused a push on 4 failed controls of the slot-literals suite, which passes 11 of 11 alone (one occurrence)
description:

title: PR 2056 residues: a failed SMTP send still logs the recipient address, a contact email at INFO, cells blind to a partial leak
description:
**BLUF:** PR 2056 (KS-1937, merged 2026-11-06 11:51:28Z as `90b500e19883`) took the recipient address out of ten originate log lines, but a failed SMTP send can still log it, because the line prints the error text and an SMTP server echoes the address in its refusal. Two smaller residues from the same gate: a third-party verifier's contact email is logged at INFO, and the PR's 12 cells stay green when the log line carries the recipient's domain. Item 1 is MEDIUM (MEASURED AT RUNTIME); items 2 and 3 are MINOR. Found by QA gate 235 (round 1); no fix here.

**Item 1, MEDIUM, MEASURED AT RUNTIME (gate 235, a loopback stub SMTP server with real nodemailer 10.2.1):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/services/email.ts` line 210 (read again at develop `90b500e19883`) is `` console.error(`[Email/SMTP] Failed to send: ${error.message}`) ``. Gate 235 also read nodemailer's `smtp-connection/index.js` line 1221, which builds `'Invalid recipient ' + JSON.stringify(address)`. The PR's tests forward the text `ks1937 smtp boom` and so prove nothing about what a server echoes. Same class, not measured: the ACS error object (line 164 of the same file at the PR head), `err?.message` (line 167), `String(err)` in the WARN lines of `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/utils/notificationClient.ts`, and its `body.substring(0,200)` of the notification service's reply. The ruling behind it is Kam's card `secuura-ks1346-logging-thrown-objects-leaks-secrets` (a: never their values) and Wednesday's KS-1937 answer (log the template, never the address). Fix shape (gate 235's): log the error's class and code (`error.code`, `error.responseCode`) instead of its message, or strip the recipient first; test with a stub server that echoes the address.

**Item 2, MINOR, READ ONLY:** the PR's fragment says a scan of every log call flags the two sites in KS-2036 and nothing else. `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/thirdPartyVerifiers.ts` line 87 (read again at `90b500e19883`) is `logger.info('Third-party verifier registered', { id, organizationName, contactEmail })`: a contact address, not a recipient, but an address in an INFO line, and not in KS-2036's list.

**Item 3, MINOR, MEASURED AT RUNTIME (gate 235 tamper X):** with the allow-list refusal line changed to print the recipient's domain, `...refusing to send: ${options.to.split("@")[1]}`, all 12 cells stay green: they look only for the full address. The ACS path's "the address still reaches the mailer" is also unpinned (cells E1 to E3 never check the arguments of `beginSend`); only the SMTP path pins `mockSendMail.mock.calls[0][0].to` (cell E6). Tampers Y (full address on the SMTP Sent line), Z (address back on the client fallback INFO line) and W (blank SMTP `to`) were each caught by exactly one cell. Tests: `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1937-email-service-logs-never-carry-the-recipient-address.test.ts` and `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1937-notification-client-logs-the-template-never-the-recipient-address.test.ts`.

title: PR 2057 forged-tenant cells stay green if the tenant resolver falls back to the token's tenant claim: a blind spot, not a defect
description:

title: PR 2076 (KS-2058 follow-up), gate 242: five wording and test-cell notes in a code comment, two fragments, a docstring and cell R3
description:
**BLUF:** PR 2076 (KS-2058 follow-up, head `8ce56b0f9a86`, open and not merged when this was filed) changes comments and two documentation fragments, and adds one test cell. Compiled with comments removed, the two product files are byte-identical to the base. QA gate 242 returned GO WITH NOTES with five notes, H1 to H5: four Low and one Info, all about words or one test cell, none a code defect. This ticket carries them as items, one test pass. Wednesday decided on 2026-11-08 that PR 2076 gets no new round: its text stays as it is and is corrected under this ticket. Evidence class for all five: READ ONLY (gate 242 read the code against the words; it ran no PostgreSQL and did not re-run the seat's mutants).

**H1 (Low, words).** Where: `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/db.ts`, the two new lines 236 and 237 at the PR head. Found: the comment says "with one disabled holder and one live one, the admin's request binds the live one." That holds on the owner-read path, which `registerParticipant` reaches only when `dbGetParticipantByAddress` finds no row for the wallet (`Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts`, around lines 630 to 637). If the disabled holder already has a participant row for the wallet, the request lands on that row and the owner read never runs. The enclosing docstring scopes itself to "a new row", so the sentence is not false in context, but it stands alone as a "Stated limit". The cheat fragment's "What to know" row is scoped to "wallet with no row" and is fine. Fix shape: scope the sentence to a wallet with no row.

**H2 (Low, words).** Where: the flow fragment, row "The retry's own save", `Projects Documents/fragments/flow/KS-2058-an-erased-user-is-not-a-wallets-owner-and-an-omitted-did-keeps-what-the-row-holds.html`. Found: it says "In nature it is vanishingly rare" and "my driver reproduces that". The first is a frequency claim; the only measurement behind it is forced timing (10 of 10 under forced interleaving) and no rate in nature was measured, so a reader may take it as a measured bound. The second is first person in a document a Secuura reader sees, and names a tool that is not in the PR. Fix shape (gate 242): drop the phrase, or say "not measured outside forced timing"; drop the first person. Both phrases stand in the tree for now, by Wednesday's decision above.

**H3 (Low, words).** Where: the cheat fragment, row "Not measured here", `Projects Documents/fragments/cheat/KS-2058-an-erased-user-is-not-a-wallets-owner-and-an-omitted-did-keeps-what-the-row-holds.html`. Found: it gains the G1 limit but not the two limits the flow fragment and the `registerParticipant` docstring now state: "the 201 can differ from the row on the did", and "an omitted flag is written from the default, which can lose a flag or grant one". Its "What to know" row says "An omitted did keeps what the row holds when the write lands", which a reader can take as covering the response body too. Evidence: gate 242 read both fragments against the code (`asStored`, lines 640 to 649; the upsert, lines 182 to 197, writes `is_drep` and `is_constitutional_committee` from EXCLUDED).

**H4 (Low, test).** Where: `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/__tests__/ks2058-an-erased-owner-is-not-an-owner-and-a-read-miss-keeps-the-did.test.ts`, the new cell at the end (about lines 551 to 565), named `control ks2058 R3 the did changes between the holder read and the retry's save: the newer did stays`. Found: the cell checks status 201 and the row's did. The comment in the code says the 201 can name the older did; R3 pins the fix (the row keeps the newer did) and says nothing about the stated limit (the response names the older). Not wrong, but the "state the limit" half of the PR has no cell. Gate 242's own planted defect shows other cells cover the re-read of the holder.

title: anchoring: an empty or null 2xx reply from a configured chain client reads ABSENT, which can lead to a second fee-paying transaction
description:
**BLUF:** with a configured chain client, a 2xx reply with an empty body or a JSON `null` counts as the chain answering and reads ABSENT in the anchoring confirmation poller, and a body of `{}` reads confirmed with no block hash. A false ABSENT lets guard 3 schedule the ordinary retry, which is a second fee-paying Cardano transaction; its fee and its on-chain record cannot be undone. QA gate 248 found it while gating PR 2081 (KS-1171 8k). It is older than that PR, which cannot add the outcome (1,364 attempt sequences, 0 widened). Kam's card `secuura-anchoring-second-fee-on-empty-reply-1107` = a, "Merge PR 2081, and fix the empty reply before anchoring next deploys (recommended)", ruled 2026-11-08 at 20:31:42 +11:00; its detail: "Two tickets by a board seat, High for the empty reply and Medium to measure the mint on an image. A build seat fixes the empty reply next, tier 1 gate. Anchoring's deploy stays held for your word." This is the High ticket. The Medium half is carried on KS-562, whose gate 70 comment already records the open question, "whether the anchoring image's install layout reproduces the split in a built container". Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME for the client and the poller result, with the real client and poller; guard 3's retry from this input follows from an existing cell's path (cell C1) and was not driven end to end.

**Measured (gate 248):** the real blockfrost-js 6.1.1 on a loopback listener returns an empty string for an empty 200 and for a 204, `null` for a body of `null`, and `{}` for a body of `{}`. HTML on a 200 throws; a 404 and a 502 throw with their status. The real provider and the real poller on the production schedule, at develop and at the PR 2081 head, with the transaction lookup resolving each body: an empty string and `null` give `polled` 30 and `definitelyAbsent` true; `{}` gives `confirmed` true with no block hash.

**Why it matters (gate 248):** the code's own comment defines an answer as "the transaction or not found". An empty 200 is neither. It is the same second-fee harm that PR 2081 closes for the no-client case, on the configuration that really pays fees, where 8k itself has no route. PR 2081's sentence "An empty 200 is '', so it still counts as an answer, as it does today" is true, but nothing there says it reaches guard 3.

**Likelihood (gate 248):** low. It needs an upstream or a proxy answering 2xx with no body. Not seen in service; no box was read.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/cardano/confirmation.ts`, lines 94 to 103 at the PR 2081 head (gate 248's tree). On develop `a65ae7ed1d60` the same polling logic starts near line 81, where the `polled` counter is incremented. Gate 248's probes are in the evidence folder next to its verdict.

**Fix shape (gate 248, for the owner):** decide whether the poller counts only `null` and a real transaction as answers, and pin it. That touches the 2026-09-25 definition of "answered" (card `secuura-ks1171-when-is-an-anchor-absent` = c); Kam's ruling above sends it to a build seat under a tier 1 gate. Anchoring's deploy stays held for Kam's word.

**Not measured:** a real Blockfrost, a real node or a real unreachable chain; any box, image or gateway path; guard 3's retry end to end from this input; how often a provider sends an empty 2xx.

title: governance castVote: a lock-free read, change and whole-row save loses a concurrent vote's tally and can write back an erased wallet address
description:
**BLUF:** In governance, `castVote` reads a proposal, changes it in memory and writes the whole row back with no row lock and no transaction. So two votes on one proposal at the same moment lose one tally, and a vote in flight during an erasure can write back the wallet address the erasure has just blanked. Evidence class: READ, not measured. Nobody has driven two concurrent requests, and the window has not been timed.

What I read, at develop `14ac61bd1a4c854c17539f1cd0f518631f998fbb`, in `Blockchain/Dev/services/governance/src/services/governanceService.ts` (1357 lines):

* Line 952: `castVote` starts with `dbGetProposal(proposalId)`. `dbGetProposal` (line 329) is a plain `SELECT * FROM svc_proposals WHERE id = $1`: no `FOR UPDATE`, no transaction.
* Lines 998 to 1011: the vote is pushed onto `proposal.votes`, `proposal.voterCount` is incremented, and `votesFor`, `votesAgainst` or `votesAbstain` grows by the voter's power. All of it in memory.
* Line 1013: `dbSaveProposal(proposal)` (defined at line 144) upserts the whole row. Its `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE` sets `votes_for`, `votes_against`, `votes_abstain`, `voter_count` and `votes` from the in-memory object (lines 153 to 157).
* Line 989: each stored vote carries `voterAddress: voter.walletAddress`, so the `votes` array holds wallet addresses.

What follows from that reading:

1. Two requests that read the same row each add their own vote to their own copy. The second upsert replaces the first, so one vote and its tally are gone, although the first request has already answered success.
2. An erasure that blanks a wallet address inside `svc_proposals.votes` while a vote on that proposal sits between its read (line 952) and its write (line 1013) is overwritten by the vote's pre-erasure copy. The address is back in the row.

The same read-then-whole-row-save shape stands at the `submitProposal` call sites (lines 883 and 910) and the `finalizeProposal` call sites (lines 1052 and 1096) in the same file. I read the call sites only, not those function bodies.

Not claimed: no concurrent run, no measurement of the window, no read of the erasure handler (it is Seat U 18th's local commit for KS-2060, not pushed when this was filed).

Related:

* KS-2060 (the erasure work). Seat U 18th's finding file says KS-2060 states the in-flight vote as a limit.
* KS-2058 (the co-owner limit).
* KS-2092 (`castVote` counts a delegator's stake twice): a different defect in the same function.
* KS-1950 (Done): the same class on the participant row. The code comment at line 1014 says the voter row now gets a counter-only update.

Source of the finding: Seat U 18th, finding 1 of "Two findings for you to route" in `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-11-08_seatU-18th/drafts/02_q_ks2059_order.txt`, marked there "Read, not measured". I re-read the lines above myself at the develop sha named.

Duplicate search before filing (board account, includeArchived, open tickets read with all comments): `castVote`, `dbSaveProposal`, the full path of the service file, "votes array", "lose one tally", "row lock" with "vote", "concurrent" with "vote", "lost update". No open ticket describes this race; the closest hits are KS-2092 (open) and KS-1950 (Done), both under Related. Priority: Medium, a default set by the board seat because the finding gives none. A raise is Wednesday's call.

title: Admin Settings page pollutes Object.prototype on save when a stored settings category is named `__proto__`
description:
**BLUF:** If the stored platform-settings document holds a category named `__proto__`, the admin Settings page's save grouping writes that category's fields onto `Object.prototype` in the admin's browser. This is pre-existing: the same at develop `cfb6c1573ba9` and at the head of PR 2058 (`527d67b1852e`), which did not introduce it. Gate 256 measured it on both, and by its model any admin caller of the settings PUT can store such a key. It found no gadget and looked for none. Medium is Wednesday's default; the gate graded it minor to medium.

Source: gate 256 (Secuura / Blockchain, PR 2058, KS-1231 portal half, tier 1, round 2 of 2), finding N5, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-08_gate256-tier1-pr2058-r2/verdict.md`, lines 52 to 56. The code lines below I read myself, at the shas named.

1. What was measured. Evidence class: MEASURED by the gate (tsx; the head module against develop's grouping logic copied out). It planted the wire document `{"settings":{"general":{...},"__proto__":{"g256polluted":"yes"}}}` (the contents of `general` are elided as in the verdict); `JSON.parse` makes `__proto__` an own key. A control read before each run gave `({}).g256polluted` as undefined. After one save build it was `"yes"` at both the head and develop. The save request body itself did not carry the key.
2. The line on develop. Evidence class: READ at `cfb6c1573ba9`. `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/admin/src/pages/Settings.tsx` lines 63 to 71 group the form values by category: `if (!updates[category]) { updates[category] = {}; }` (lines 67 to 69), then `updates[category][field] = formValues[key];` (line 70). For the name `__proto__`, `updates[category]` is not empty (it is the object prototype), so the branch is skipped and line 70 assigns onto `Object.prototype`. That last step is my reading of the two lines; the gate's run is what measured it.
3. The line at PR 2058's head. Evidence class: READ at `527d67b1852e`. `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/admin/src/lib/settingsSavePayload.ts` line 84 is `const target = (updates[category] ??= {}) as Settings;` and line 85 assigns `target[field] = value`. That file exists only on the PR's head (it is absent from develop at `cfb6c1573ba9`); the same reading applies, because `??=` keeps a value that is not null or undefined.
4. Whether such a key can be stored. Evidence class: MEASURED by the gate on a model of the gateway's spread (it keeps an own `__proto__` key), plus READ at `cfb6c1573ba9`. In `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts`, the PUT validates only `integrations[].config.allowedDocumentTypes` (lines 1169 to 1179) and line 1200 is the merge `{ ...PLATFORM_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS, ...existing, ...body }`; I found no check on category names between line 1164 and line 1200. So, by that measurement and that read, an admin caller of the PUT can store the key, and every admin who then opens and saves the page is affected. Not run against a real gateway.

Fix shapes (the gate's): skip `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` categories, or build the body on `Object.create(null)`, and refuse the key at the gateway.

Not claimed: no gadget (none found, none looked for); no browser run of the real page with such a stored key; no run against a real gateway; and the head-side file is on an unmerged PR, so a change there is that PR's round, not this ticket's.

Related: KS-1231 (PR 2058's ticket; this ticket is separate and the head-side file is its PR's). KS-1197 shows the same mechanism at another site, a stored `__proto__` value resolved through a plain-object lookup in the auth service, per its text; different site and effect. KS-1998 and KS-1256 are the settings store, another subject.

Priority: Medium, Wednesday's default in the brief; a raise is hers.

title: Connector-key rotate answers rotated true with no warning while an older organisation key with no connector id still validates
description:
**BLUF:** The connector-key rotate (register-connector with rotate on) answers `rotated: true`, a count of 1 and no warning while an older key of the same organisation, one that carries no connector id, still validates. It happens on the retry after a count of 0, and also on the first call when the organisation holds both kinds of key, so no 0 is needed. The cause is in security's retire, which matches only the connector id; the gateway cannot see the older key. Gate 257 measured it on real PostgreSQL. It is old behaviour that PR 2073 narrows (the 0 itself is now honest) and does not remove. Priority High is Wednesday's call; the gate graded the finding Medium. Wednesday's ruling on the fix direction, under Kam's card `secuura-ks-1152-rotate-says-rotated-when-old-key-lives-1106` = b ("Keep rotating, but answer 'rotated: false' and say why", ruled 2026-11-06 15:00:34 AEDT, read with `tools/decision_queue.sh show`): the fix extends that honest answer to these keys; it does NOT retire them.

Source: gate 257, tier 1, round 2 of 2, PR 2073 (KS-1152 R-880-1), finding F1 and the section "For Kam, at the top", `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-08_gate257-tier1-pr2073-r2/verdict.md`, lines 17 to 34 and 40 to 49. Wednesday's ADDENDUM to the board seat, 2026-11-08 11:39:30Z, orders this filing. Seat Y 8th had recorded the retry case first (its probe P2, in its entry in `5_Project_History/history.md`) and proposed a distinct code for Kam's and Stuart's monthly agenda.

1. What was measured. Evidence class: MEASURED by gate 257 on real PostgreSQL 15 (the gate's own cluster), through a real gateway route over real security, at PR 2073's head `2684a29d8f576ff74634f07ad6576af5bd00370b` and again on the develop merge.
   * G2a, the first call with a count of 0: 200, `rotated` false, `priorKeysRevoked` 0, `PRIOR_KEY_STILL_ACTIVE`. The older key and the new key both validate.
   * G2b, the retry: 200, `rotated` true, count 1, no warning. The older key is still valid; the key the 0 call returned is no longer valid.
   * G3, an organisation that holds both an older key with no connector id and a key with the connector id, first call: 200, `rotated` true, count 1, no warning. The older key is still valid; the connector key is retired.
2. Where. Evidence class: READ. `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts` at PR 2073's head, line 979: `rotated: rotate && existing.rows.length > 0 && priorKeysRetired && priorKeysRevoked >= 1`. `Blockchain/Dev/services/security/src/index.ts` at develop `abd044f63a9dd5673f1b9ff7a2b1e42e1c26de82` (the file is not changed by PR 2073), lines 239 and 246: both retire statements end `WHERE connector_id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2::uuid AND id <> $3 AND is_active = true`, so a key with no connector id is never matched.
3. Why it is old behaviour. By the gate's reading, develop answers `rotated: true` on the 0 itself, on the retry and on G3. PR 2073 makes the 0 honest and leaves the retry and G3 as they were.
4. The fix direction. Ruled by Wednesday (ADDENDUM 11:39:30Z): extend the honest answer, `rotated: false` with a reason, to these keys; do not retire them. The gate's two fix shapes were that security reports how many active keys of the organisation remain after the retire, or that the retire also takes the organisation's keys that have no connector id. The first fits the ruling; the second is what the ruling excludes. A regression test the owner should add (the gate): G3's shape, asserting that `rotated` is not true while the older key validates. If this behaviour stays for now, the gate asks for one sentence each in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md` and in the spec: "`rotated: true` says nothing about an older key with no connector id; a retry after a 0 answers `rotated: true` with that key still active."
5. The cost the gate names in Wednesday's ruling A2. One code now carries two instructions, so a client that reads only the code retries after a 0 and lands in G2. The PR body calls that retry "futile, not harmful"; the gate disagrees, because the retry ends in a false all-clear. The gate leaves that trade-off to Kam.
6. Who reads `rotated`. By the gate: rotation is platform-admin only (its GUARDRAIL 1), so a K admin reads the reply; whether Platform S reads `rotated` is unknown; the only code reader is systemTest, which stops at `rotated: true`. The contract Stuart's team reads says a retry does not help but not that the retry answers `rotated: true`, and it does not mention G3.

Not claimed: how many keys with no connector id exist on any box (the gate did not measure it); whether Platform S reads `rotated`; any run by me. PR 2073 is not merged: the line numbers for `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts` are at its head and may shift when it merges.

title: KS-1152 follow-up: nothing pins rotated to an existing organisation; the gate removed that check and 0 of 25 cells failed
description:
**BLUF:** Round 2 of PR 2073 made `rotated` read false for a count of 0, and the cell that covers a new organisation runs only with a count of 0, so nothing now pins `rotated` to an existing organisation. Gate 257 planted the removal of `existing.rows.length > 0 &&` from the `rotated` expression and 0 of 25 cells failed. In round 1 the same cell caught that plant (gate 245's "rotated on a new org", 1 red); under `>= 1` a count of 0 reads false either way. It is a test gap that round 2 created, not a runtime defect: the code as shipped answers `rotated: false` for a new organisation. Medium is Wednesday's call in the ADDENDUM; the gate graded it minor.

Source: gate 257, tier 1, round 2 of 2, PR 2073 (KS-1152 R-880-1), finding F2, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-08_gate257-tier1-pr2073-r2/verdict.md`, lines 51 to 54. Evidence class: MEASURED by gate 257 (a planted copy, run twice, each restoration checked by sha256): T5, drop `existing.rows.length > 0 &&` from `rotated` at `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts` line 979. 0 of 25 cells failed. The other six plants (T1 to T4, T6, T7) were each caught by assertion.
2. The cells, READ at the head. In `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1152-register-connector-says-when-the-old-key-lives.test.ts`, line 270 is the new-organisation cell, `control ks1152 C3 a rotate on a new organisation with a count: 201, rotated false, no warning`, and it replies with `{ priorKeysRevoked: 0 }` only. The existing-organisation count cell C1 (line 253) runs counts 1 and 3. A comment at line 252 records that the count-0 row was removed from C1 in round 2.

title: KS-1152 follow-up: the spec and the cheat fragment say a count of 0 carries a warning; a new organisation gets none
description:
**BLUF:** Three sentences in PR 2073's published text are untrue for a NEW organisation. On a rotate of a new organisation with a count of 0 or more, the reply is 201, `rotated` false and no warning; the spec's `rotated` and `rotationWarning` descriptions and the cheat fragment say a 0 always carries `PRIOR_KEY_STILL_ACTIVE`, or that a rotate that did not retire a prior key carries it. The code is right and the PR body's table is right; only the three sentences are unqualified. Low is Wednesday's call in the ADDENDUM; the gate graded it minor.

Source: gate 257, tier 1, round 2 of 2, PR 2073 (KS-1152 R-880-1), finding F3, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-08_gate257-tier1-pr2073-r2/verdict.md`, lines 56 to 62. Wednesday's ADDENDUM to the board seat, 2026-11-08 11:39:30Z, orders this filing. The text below I read myself at PR 2073's head `2684a29d8f576ff74634f07ad6576af5bd00370b`; the PR is not merged, so line numbers may shift when it merges.

1. What was measured. Evidence class: MEASURED by gate 257 as G5 (a count of 0) and G6 (a count of 1): a rotate of a new organisation answers 201, `rotated` false and no `rotationWarning`. Cell C3 pins it.
2. The three sentences. Evidence class: READ at the head.
   * The spec's `rotated` description, `Blockchain/Dev/services/tenant-provisioning/src/tenant-provisioning.openapi.ts` line 756: "A count of 0 answers false, with PRIOR_KEY_STILL_ACTIVE and a message saying no prior key was retired". It is unqualified; the 0 warning is for an existing organisation only.
   * The spec's `rotationWarning` description, the same file, line 765: "Present when a rotate did not retire a prior key". For a new organisation with a count of 0 nothing was retired and there is no warning.
   * The cheat fragment, `Projects Documents/fragments/cheat/KS-1152-rotate-says-when-the-old-key-lives.html`, line 2: "Otherwise, with status 200 or 201 and the new key still returned: `rotated: false` and `rotationWarning.code` `PRIOR_KEY_STILL_ACTIVE`".
3. What is right. The gate read the PR body's table ("new organisation, a count | 201 | false | the count | absent") and the contract paragraph in `Blockchain/Dev/docs/S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md` ("on an existing organisation") as correct.

Fix (the gate's): add "on an existing Organisation" to the three sentences. The spec change is a published-spec edit, so `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, which the PR regenerates from the spec source, needs the regeneration; the gate found that regeneration deterministic and, today, a no-op on the merge with PRs 2072 and 2077, and says whichever PR merges second should still run it. I did not read the yaml's lines.

Not claimed: no run by me; the yaml's matching text is the gate's statement, not my reading.
